yoruba: Àgbéré àwòdì ní ńní òun ó jẹ ìgbín.
english_literal: It is an overreaching kite that proposes to eat snails.
interpretation_gold: Know your limits.
deepseek_translation: The kite's talon says it will eat the snail.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against making empty boasts or threats without the ability to carry them out.
claude_translation: The kite that carries snails says it will eat the snail.
claude_interpretation: Someone who has access to or control over something will inevitably take advantage of it for their own benefit.
gemini_translation: The hawk's foolishness is that it thinks it will eat a snail.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to attempt something impossible or to underestimate the difficulty of a task.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The hawk's foolishness is that it thinks it will eat a snail.", "interpretation": "It is foolish to attempt something impossible or to underestimate the difficulty of a task."}
mistral_translation: The kite boasts that it will eat the snail.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against overconfidence in one's ability to overcome a seemingly weaker opponent.
llama_translation: The snail shell is what the snail eats.
llama_interpretation: One's circumstances or resources can be the source of one's sustenance or survival.

yoruba: A kì í kórira ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n ká finá bọ ahéré.
english_literal: One does not so hate the bush rat that one sets one's farm hut alight.
interpretation_gold: One should not destroy oneself simply to get at one's enemy.
deepseek_translation: We do not hate the grinding stone and use fire to burn the mortar.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not destroy something useful while expressing dislike for another.
claude_translation: One does not hate a wasp so much as to use fire to drive it from a calabash.
claude_interpretation: The cure should not be worse than the problem itself.
gemini_translation: One does not hate the buffalo so much as to set fire to the hut.
gemini_interpretation: One should not cause greater harm to oneself or others in an attempt to harm an enemy.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not hate the buffalo so much as to set fire to the hut.", "interpretation": "One should not cause greater harm to oneself or others in an attempt to harm an enemy."}
mistral_translation: We do not gather dry twigs to set a hut on fire
mistral_interpretation: One should not deliberately create or escalate problems that will harm others or their own community.
llama_translation: We do not use a single rope to tie a bundle of sticks
llama_interpretation: Unity and cooperation are necessary to achieve a common goal.

yoruba: A kì í bọ òrìṣà lójú ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n; bó bá dalẹ́ a máa tú pẹpẹ.
english_literal: One does not sacrifice to a god in the presence of a house rat; otherwise, when night falls it invades the rafter shelves.
interpretation_gold: Do not do things that might constitute temptation to others.
deepseek_translation: We do not worship the deity in the presence of the deaf; when it gets dark, we will whisper.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises discretion and the importance of choosing the right time and place for sensitive matters.
claude_translation: One does not worship a deity in the presence of a baboon; if it falls down, it will scatter the shrine.
claude_interpretation: Sacred or important activities should not be performed in the presence of those who lack respect or understanding, as they may disrupt or desecrate what is holy.
gemini_translation: One does not worship an Orisha in the open; when it gets dark, it will scatter the altar.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to perform sacred rituals or reveal sensitive matters publicly, as they may be exposed to disrespect or disruption.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not worship an Orisha in the open; when it gets dark, it will scatter the altar.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to perform sacred rituals or reveal sensitive matters publicly, as they may be exposed to disrespect or disruption."}
mistral_translation: We do not worship the deity in the presence of a lazy person; if night falls, we will surely light a lamp
mistral_interpretation: Laziness hinders progress, but persistence and effort will eventually lead to success or enlightenment
llama_translation: We do not worship the god of the forest in the open field; if we do, we will be ridiculed.
llama_interpretation: One should respect the norms and conventions of a particular setting or community.

yoruba: Àrí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, baálé ilé yọkun lémú.
english_literal: Something-seen-but-unmentionable, the man of the house walks around with mucus dripping from his nose.
interpretation_gold: When a venerable person acts like a fool, few dare tell him so.
deepseek_translation: The one who says 'I must not speak', the landlord's house collapses silently.
deepseek_interpretation: Silence in the face of wrongdoing can lead to unnoticed destruction.
claude_translation: The one who must not be spoken against, the head of the house removes the yoke from the neck.
claude_interpretation: A respected authority figure has the power to free others from burdens and oppression.
gemini_translation: The one who sees but must not speak, the head of the house has a runny nose.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes a situation where one is aware of a problem but is powerless or forbidden to address it, leading to a sense of frustration or helplessness.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who sees but must not speak, the head of the house has a runny nose.", "interpretation": "This proverb describes a situation where one is aware of a problem but is powerless or forbidden to address it, leading to a sense of frustration or helplessness."}
mistral_translation: The one who must not be scolded, the head of the household has mucus in his nose
mistral_interpretation: A person who is above reproach often has hidden flaws or vulnerabilities that others tolerate.
llama_translation: The one who does not listen to advice, the owner of the house will sell the house and run away
llama_interpretation: Disregarding advice can lead to loss and chaos.

yoruba: Àwòrò tí a ò bá lù kì í luni.
english_literal: A priest one does not hit does not hit one.
interpretation_gold: A person who wants to be respected must respect others.
deepseek_translation: The hoe that is not used does not have an owner.
deepseek_interpretation: Unused resources or tools are neglected and lose their value.
claude_translation: The plate that is not beaten does not make sound.
claude_interpretation: If you don't take action or make an effort, you won't get results or attention.
gemini_translation: A priest that we do not beat does not beat us.
gemini_interpretation: One should not provoke or antagonize others if they wish to avoid conflict.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A priest that we do not beat does not beat us.", "interpretation": "One should not provoke or antagonize others if they wish to avoid conflict."}
mistral_translation: A drummer that one does not pay does not play for free.
mistral_interpretation: People expect compensation or appreciation for their efforts and services.
llama_translation: The dawn that we did not greet will not greet us.
llama_interpretation: One must acknowledge and respect the beginning of a new phase or opportunity in order to benefit from it.

yoruba: Àpárá ńlá, ìjà ní ńdà.
english_literal: Excessive ribbing unfailingly leads to a fight.
interpretation_gold: Jokes should know limits.
deepseek_translation: A big hoe, trouble is brewing.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that excessive or improper use of power or resources can lead to conflict or trouble.
claude_translation: Big buttocks, it is trouble that it causes.
claude_interpretation: Having prominent or attractive physical features can lead to unwanted attention and problems.
gemini_translation: A big mouth causes a fight.
gemini_interpretation: Speaking excessively or boastfully often leads to conflict.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A big mouth causes a fight.", "interpretation": "Speaking excessively or boastfully often leads to conflict."}
mistral_translation: The big bat, it is fighting that it is doing
mistral_interpretation: A person who appears strong or intimidating is often the one causing unnecessary conflict or trouble
llama_translation: A big axe, a fight is what it causes.
llama_interpretation: A powerful tool or resource can often lead to conflict or strife.

yoruba: À-jẹ-tán, à-jẹ-ì-mọra, ká fi ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá jẹun ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
english_literal: Eating-absolutely-everything, eating-with-abandon, eating with all ten fingers is unworthy of human beings.
interpretation_gold: People should not be slaves to food.
deepseek_translation: Neither eating to satisfaction nor eating with moderation, using all ten fingers to eat is not proper for a human child.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the importance of moderation and self-control in all aspects of life.
claude_translation: Having eaten to satisfaction, having eaten to fullness, to use ten fingers to eat is not befitting of a human being
claude_interpretation: Good manners and self-control should be maintained even when one has abundance or plenty.
gemini_translation: Eating completely, eating without restraint, that one eats with all ten fingers is not befitting of a human being.
gemini_interpretation: It is improper and uncivilized to eat without moderation or self-control, especially by using all ten fingers.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Eating completely, eating without restraint, that one eats with all ten fingers is not befitting of a human being.", "interpretation": "It is improper and uncivilized to eat without moderation or self-control, especially by using all ten fingers."}
mistral_translation: After eating excessively, after eating without restraint, using ten fingers to eat is not proper for a human being.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive or greedy behavior is unbecoming and should be avoided.
llama_translation: We eat in the morning, we eat in the afternoon, but we do not use our hands to eat our own children.
llama_interpretation: One should not harm or destroy one's own kind or family members.

yoruba: Aláṣejù, pẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ńtẹ́; àṣéjù, baba àṣetẹ́.
english_literal: The immoderate person easily finds disgrace; immoderation is the father of disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation brings disgrace.
deepseek_translation: The one who acts excessively, the ground is swallowing; the excessive one, father of the one who acts hastily.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against excessive behavior, as it leads to negative consequences and hastiness.
claude_translation: The one who does too much, it is slowly that follows; doing too much is the father of doing wrongly.
claude_interpretation: Excessive haste or overdoing things leads to mistakes and poor outcomes.
gemini_translation: The one who overdoes it, will be disgraced; overdoing it, is the father of disgrace.
gemini_interpretation: Excessive actions or behaviors inevitably lead to negative consequences and public shame.
mistral_translation: Excessiveness, it is the grasshopper that suffers for it; excess, the father of regret.
mistral_interpretation: Excess in any form leads to negative consequences and regret.
llama_translation: The one who is not yet a king, is being called; the one who is already a king, is being begged.
llama_interpretation: Those who are not yet in power are often courted and flattered, while those who are already in power are often appeased and placated.

yoruba: Arọ̀lẹ̀kẹ̀ ò rọ bàtà; gbẹ́dó-gbẹ́dó ò rọ ojúgun.
english_literal: The bead maker cannot fashion a shoe; the mortar carver cannot manufacture a shinbone.
interpretation_gold: People should stick to what they are qualified to do.
deepseek_translation: The lazy person does not wear shoes; the sluggard does not wear armor.
deepseek_interpretation: Laziness leads to unpreparedness and vulnerability.
claude_translation: The lazy person does not mend shoes; the careless person does not mend inheritance.
claude_interpretation: Negligence and laziness lead to the deterioration of both material possessions and valuable legacy.
gemini_translation: The one with a swollen ankle cannot wear shoes; the one with a swollen knee cannot wear a battle garment.
gemini_interpretation: One's physical condition or limitations can prevent them from performing certain actions or fulfilling specific roles.
mistral_translation: The one who wears a colorful wrapper does not mend shoes; the one who wears rags does not mend bones.
mistral_interpretation: People often specialize in work that aligns with their social status or appearance, reflecting societal roles and expectations.
llama_translation: The messenger does not wear shoes; the messenger's message is not for the road.
llama_interpretation: A messenger's role is to deliver a message, not to indulge in personal interests or get distracted along the way.

yoruba: A kì í gbọ́n tó Báyìí-ni-ngó-ṣe-ǹkan-àn-mi.
english_literal: One cannot be as wise as “Thus-will-I-do-my-thing.”
interpretation_gold: Never impose your preferences on other people in their own affairs.
deepseek_translation: One cannot be wiser than Bayii-ni-ngose-nkan-an-mi.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the limits of human wisdom, suggesting that no one can surpass the ultimate wisdom of a mythical or proverbial figure.
claude_translation: One cannot be wiser than 'This-is-how-I-do-my-things'
claude_interpretation: No one can be wiser than someone who is set in their ways and insists on doing things their own particular method.
gemini_translation: One is not as wise as 'This is how I will do my thing.'
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to be overly confident or boastful about one's plans, as circumstances can change unexpectedly.
mistral_translation: We do not become wise enough to say 'This is how I will do my thing.'
mistral_interpretation: One should remain humble and open to learning, as no one is ever too wise to seek guidance or adapt their ways.
llama_translation: We do not hear the one who says 'I am the one who does everything for me'.
llama_interpretation: One who boasts of self-sufficiency will not receive help or support from others.

yoruba: A-bèèrè kì í ṣìnà.
english_literal: He who asks the way does not lose his way.
interpretation_gold: One should admit one's weaknesses.
deepseek_translation: Asking does not lead to straying.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that seeking guidance or asking questions prevents mistakes and missteps.
claude_translation: One who asks questions does not lose their way
claude_interpretation: Asking for guidance and information prevents mistakes and helps one stay on the right path in life.
gemini_translation: One who asks does not get lost.
gemini_interpretation: Seeking guidance or information prevents one from making mistakes or going astray.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who asks does not get lost.", "interpretation": "Seeking guidance or information prevents one from making mistakes or going astray."}
mistral_translation: A question does not lead one astray.
mistral_interpretation: Asking questions is a reliable way to gain clarity and avoid mistakes.
llama_translation: The one who is not patient does not eat ripe fruit.
llama_interpretation: Patience is necessary to achieve desirable outcomes.

yoruba: À ńgé e lọ́wọ́, ó ḿbọ òrùka.
english_literal: His hand is being severed, yet he is slipping on a ring.
interpretation_gold: The person has been judged undeserving of a hand; it is an affront, therefore, for him or her to adorn his or her fingers-an indication of heedlessness.
deepseek_translation: When you cut off the finger, the ring falls off.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that when the source or foundation is removed, what depends on it will inevitably fail or collapse.
claude_translation: We are cutting it from the hand, it is removing the ring.
claude_interpretation: When solving one problem, you may inadvertently create or reveal another problem.
gemini_translation: We are cutting off his hand, he is putting on a ring.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who is oblivious or indifferent to a serious problem or danger they are facing.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We are cutting off his hand, he is putting on a ring.", "interpretation": "This proverb describes someone who is oblivious or indifferent to a serious problem or danger they are facing."}
mistral_translation: You are stretching out your hand, but the ring is slipping off
mistral_interpretation: It warns against overreaching or attempting something beyond one's capacity, as it may lead to failure or loss.
llama_translation: We are going to the market, but the road is blocked by a tree.
llama_interpretation: This proverb teaches that sometimes, obstacles can hinder progress or achievement of goals.

yoruba: Àjàjà ṣoge àparò, abàyà kelú.
english_literal: The uncharacteristically spruced up partridge swells its chest.
interpretation_gold: The nouveau riche always goes to extremes in consumption.
deepseek_translation: The kite perches like the guinea fowl, the abdomen is different.
deepseek_interpretation: Outward appearances can be deceiving; true nature lies beneath the surface.
claude_translation: The dog barks at the partridge, the coward enters the town
claude_interpretation: While the brave confront challenges directly, cowards avoid conflict and seek safety in numbers or familiar territory.
gemini_translation: The one who struts proudly is the partridge, the one with a chest like a city wall.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who is boastful or arrogant, comparing their proud demeanor to the puffed-up chest of a partridge.
mistral_translation: The cowrie shell is too heavy for the kite, it is a burden for the hawk
mistral_interpretation: A task or responsibility that is too difficult for one person may also be unsuitable for another.
llama_translation: The dog that is fed at the backyard will not be known at the front
llama_interpretation: One who is not properly acknowledged or recognized will not be valued or respected.

yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ sọ̀rọ̀ méjì, ọ́ fìkan purọ́; ó ní nígbàtí òún lu ọmọ òun lábàrá, òún já a léèékánná pàtì.
english_literal: The leper said two things, one of them being a lie; he said after he had struck his child with his palm, he also pinched him severely with his nails.
interpretation_gold: One fools only oneself when one claims to have done the impossible.
deepseek_translation: The two-headed palm nut is difficult to crack; it says when it hits its child on the chest, it breaks into two pieces.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that internal conflicts or divided loyalties can lead to self-destruction.
claude_translation: The liar spoke two things, one of them was false; he said that when he beat his child on the shoulder, he tore it into eleven parts.
claude_interpretation: Liars often contradict themselves and make exaggerated claims that reveal their dishonesty.
gemini_translation: A leper said two things, he lied about one; he said when he slapped his child, he also scratched him with his fingernails.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb highlights the tendency of some people to exaggerate or embellish their stories, even when the initial statement is already impactful.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A leper said two things, he lied about one; he said when he slapped his child, he also scratched him with his fingernails.", "interpretation": "The proverb highlights the tendency of some people to exaggerate or embellish their stories, even when the initial statement is already impactful."}
mistral_translation: The king spoke two words, he lied with one; he said when he slapped his child in anger, he only did it once in a long while.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb illustrates how people often justify their wrongdoings with excuses or half-truths to appear reasonable.
llama_translation: A crown is worn by two people, it is not exclusive; when it is worn by a child, it is worn with the consent of the elders.
llama_interpretation: Decision-making and leadership require the involvement and approval of elders and experienced individuals.

yoruba: Àrífín ilé ò jẹ́ ká jẹ òròmọ adìẹ.
english_literal: Fear of losing face within one's home dissuades one from eating day-old chicks.
interpretation_gold: A person who would retain his esteem among his peers must not act beneath himself or herself.
deepseek_translation: The dust of the house does not allow us to eat the chick of the hen.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that minor issues or distractions can prevent us from achieving greater goals.
claude_translation: The wise person of the house does not allow us to eat chicken eggs
claude_interpretation: A knowledgeable elder prevents wasteful consumption that would harm future prosperity.
gemini_translation: Disrespect in the house prevents us from eating a young chicken.
gemini_interpretation: Internal conflict or disrespect within a family or community can prevent them from enjoying the benefits or rewards that are rightfully theirs.
mistral_translation: The owner of the house does not eat the chicken's offspring
mistral_interpretation: One should not take advantage of their position to exploit those under their care or responsibility.
llama_translation: The owner of the house does not eat the chicken of the orphan.
llama_interpretation: One should not take advantage of the vulnerable or those in a weaker position.

yoruba: Àbúrò rẹ ńdáṣọ fún ọ, o ní o ò lo elékuru; ta ní ńlo alákàrà?
english_literal: Your junior brother (or sister) buys clothing for you, and you say you will not wear anything with bean-grits patterns; who has the right to opt for clothing with a bean-fritter patterns?
interpretation_gold: One should act in accordance to one's station in life.
deepseek_translation: Your younger sibling is sewing clothes for you, you say you don't eat elékuru; who then eats alákàrà?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against ingratitude and rejecting kindness, as it may lead to losing all forms of goodwill.
claude_translation: Your younger sibling is dyeing cloth for you, you say you don't wear bean cake seller's cloth; who then wears the bean fritter seller's cloth?
claude_interpretation: Don't be ungrateful or look down on help from those close to you, as you may not be as important as you think you are.
gemini_translation: Your younger sibling is sewing clothes for you, and you say you don't use eko (corn pudding); who uses akara (bean cake)?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the absurdity of rejecting a generous offer based on a trivial or irrelevant comparison, implying that one should appreciate the gesture rather than finding fault.
mistral_translation: Your younger sibling is sewing clothes for you, and you say you are not going to eat elékuru; who is going to eat àkàrà?
mistral_interpretation: Do not reject a small or indirect benefit from someone, as it may be all they can offer.
llama_translation: His friend is making a dress for him, he says he doesn't wear agbada; who wears a wrapper?
llama_interpretation: One should appreciate the efforts of others, even if the outcome may not be exactly what one wants.

yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ olè, aboyún ńdáhùń; odiidi èèyàn ló gbé pamọ́.
english_literal: We speak of stealing and a pregnant woman intervenes; she herself is concealing a whole person.
interpretation_gold: Her condition makes her guilty of concealment.
deepseek_translation: The thief is making noise, the pregnant woman is silent; the multitude of people is hiding it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that public outcry often distracts from hidden truths or silent suffering.
claude_translation: We are talking about a thief, a pregnant woman is responding; she is the very person who hid it.
claude_interpretation: Those who react defensively or speak up when not directly accused often reveal their own guilt.
gemini_translation: We are talking about a thief, and a pregnant woman is answering; she has hidden a whole person.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb implies that someone who is overly defensive or quick to respond to an accusation might be guilty of the offense being discussed.
mistral_translation: While we are talking about the thief, the pregnant woman is giving birth; it is a human being that is hidden.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights that people often focus on the wrong things while ignoring what truly matters or is hidden in plain sight.
llama_translation: We are searching for a thief, the owner is sleeping; it is the foolish person that will be caught.
llama_interpretation: This proverb warns that one should not be deceived by appearances, as the true culprit may be hiding in plain sight.

yoruba: A kì í peni lákọ ẹran ká ṣorí bòró.
english_literal: One does not enjoy the designation “He Goat” and yet sport a smooth (horn-less) head.
interpretation_gold: A person should live up to his/her billing.
deepseek_translation: One does not ask a goat for permission to slaughter it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that sometimes decisions must be made unilaterally for the greater good, without seeking consent from those who would naturally oppose it.
claude_translation: One does not kill a person with a piece of meat and then use the head to cover a pot.
claude_interpretation: You cannot harm someone and then expect them to help you or serve your purposes.
gemini_translation: One does not call someone the head of an animal and then have a small head.
gemini_interpretation: A leader or person of importance is expected to possess qualities that match their esteemed position.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not call someone the head of an animal and then have a small head.", "interpretation": "A leader or person of importance is expected to possess qualities that match their esteemed position."}
mistral_translation: We do not tie a person to a piece of meat and then climb a palm tree.
mistral_interpretation: Do not create a problem for someone and then abandon them to deal with it alone.
llama_translation: We do not throw a stone at a frog on a rock
llama_interpretation: One should not take action that might cause unintended harm or consequences.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà kì í ṣe lágbalàgba.
english_literal: An elder should not behave in an unbecoming manner.
interpretation_gold: One should behave according to one's status.
deepseek_translation: An elder does not act like an elder.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that elders should behave with wisdom and dignity befitting their status.
claude_translation: An elder does not act carelessly or recklessly
claude_interpretation: Mature people are expected to behave with wisdom and restraint, not act foolishly like children.
gemini_translation: An elder does not act like an elder.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb is a critique of an elder who fails to exhibit the expected wisdom, maturity, and responsible behavior associated with their age and status.
mistral_translation: An elder does not act childishly.
mistral_interpretation: Elders are expected to behave with maturity and wisdom, setting an example for others.
llama_translation: The elderly are not the ones who are old
llama_interpretation: Age is not the sole determinant of wisdom or maturity.

yoruba: A kì í mọ́ egbò fúnra ẹni ká sunkún.
english_literal: One does not treat one's own sore and yet cry from the pain.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's own pain threshold.
deepseek_translation: One does not cry for one's own death in advance.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not worry excessively about future misfortunes that may never happen.
claude_translation: One does not know the medicine for oneself and then cry
claude_interpretation: You shouldn't complain about problems when you already know the solution but refuse to apply it.
gemini_translation: One does not treat one's own wound and cry.
gemini_interpretation: It is difficult to objectively assess or address one's own problems, as self-pity or bias can hinder effective solutions.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not treat one's own wound and cry.", "interpretation": "It is difficult to objectively assess or address one's own problems, as self-pity or bias can hinder effective solutions."}
mistral_translation: One does not know the extent of their own wound to start crying for others
mistral_interpretation: Focus on solving your own problems before worrying about others' troubles.
llama_translation: We don't know the depth of a well for someone to draw water
llama_interpretation: One should not assume they know the extent of someone's problem or challenge.

yoruba: Àbọ̀ ejò kì í gbé isà.
english_literal: Half a snake does not live in a burrow.
interpretation_gold: One should act according to one's circumstances.
deepseek_translation: The snake's head does not carry poison.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that the source of a problem is often harmless or inconspicuous.
claude_translation: Half of a snake does not live in a hole.
claude_interpretation: Incomplete or half-hearted efforts cannot achieve lasting success or survival.
gemini_translation: The snake's shed skin does not remain in the hole.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot return to a past state or situation once it has been left behind.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The snake's shed skin does not remain in the hole.", "interpretation": "One cannot return to a past state or situation once it has been left behind."}
mistral_translation: A snake's skin does not carry a load.
mistral_interpretation: One should not take on responsibilities or burdens that are not theirs to bear.
llama_translation: The one who is not a farmer does not carry a hoe.
llama_interpretation: One should not interfere in matters that are not their concern or area of expertise.

yoruba: Aláǹgbá kì í lérí àti pa ejò.
english_literal: A lizard does not boast that it will kill a snake.
interpretation_gold: People should not propose what they cannot accomplish.
deepseek_translation: The lizard does not have a neck and yet it swallows a snake.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that one should not underestimate others based on appearances, as even the seemingly weak can achieve great things.
claude_translation: A lizard does not have the head to kill a snake
claude_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks that are beyond their capabilities or resources.
gemini_translation: The lizard does not boast of killing a snake.
gemini_interpretation: One should not boast about achieving something that is beyond their capabilities or is inherently dangerous.
mistral_translation: The lizard does not boast and kill a snake
mistral_interpretation: One should not claim abilities or achievements beyond what they can truly accomplish
llama_translation: The one who is not strong does not know how to wrestle
llama_interpretation: One must be prepared and capable before taking on a challenge.

yoruba: A kì í fi gbèsè sọ́rùn ṣọ̀ṣọ́.
english_literal: One does not carry debt around one's neck and live like a dandy.
interpretation_gold: One should discharge one's obligations before one indulges in extravagance.
deepseek_translation: We do not use debt to tie the neck tightly.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against the burdens and consequences of being in debt.
claude_translation: One does not use debt to adorn the neck beautifully
claude_interpretation: It is unwise to use borrowed money or resources to create a false appearance of wealth or status.
gemini_translation: One does not adorn the neck with debt.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to take on debt for frivolous or non-essential things.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not adorn the neck with debt.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to take on debt for frivolous or non-essential things."}
mistral_translation: We do not use debt to make the neck comfortable (i.e., to adorn the neck with beads).
mistral_interpretation: One should not incur debt to finance luxury or non-essential expenses.
llama_translation: We do not use a debt to pay a debt
llama_interpretation: One problem or debt should not be solved by creating another.

yoruba: Ajá kì í gbó níbojì ẹkùn.
english_literal: A dog does not bark in the leopard's lair.
interpretation_gold: One must defer to one's superiors.
deepseek_translation: A dog does not bark where the leopard is.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not challenge or provoke those who are clearly more powerful or dangerous.
claude_translation: A dog does not bark in the shadow of a leopard.
claude_interpretation: One should know when to remain silent in the presence of someone more powerful or dangerous.
gemini_translation: A dog does not bark in the leopard's den.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to challenge or provoke a powerful authority in their own domain.
mistral_translation: A dog does not hear the roar of a leopard in the same way.
mistral_interpretation: Different people perceive the same situation or threat differently based on their nature or position.
llama_translation: A dog does not hear where a leopard is.
llama_interpretation: One should be aware of potential dangers lurking around.

yoruba: Aṣiwèrè èèyàn ní ńsọ pé irú òun ò sí; irúu rẹ̀-ẹ́ pọ̀ ó ju ẹgbàágbèje lọ.
english_literal: Only an imbecile says there is no one else like himself; the likes of him are many more than several thousands.
interpretation_gold: There is no one the likes of whom the world has never seen.
deepseek_translation: A mad person is saying there is no one like him; his kind are more than two thousand.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against arrogance and the illusion of uniqueness, emphasizing that no one is truly alone or without peers.
claude_translation: A foolish person says there is no one like them; their type is more than nine hundred.
claude_interpretation: Foolish people think they are unique when in reality there are countless others just like them.
gemini_translation: A foolish person is the one who says their type does not exist; their type is numerous, more than twenty thousand.
gemini_interpretation: A foolish person believes they are unique or exceptional, but in reality, many others share similar characteristics or situations.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A foolish person is the one who says their type does not exist; their type is numerous, more than twenty thousand.", "interpretation": "A foolish person believes they are unique or exceptional, but in reality, many others share similar characteristics or situations."}
mistral_translation: A mad person swears that his own kind does not exist; his own kind are more than fourteen thousand in number
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns against hypocrisy or denial of one's own flaws while criticizing others for the same faults.
llama_translation: The foolishness of a person is what shows that there is no one like him; his foolishness surpasses that of a madman.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the uniqueness and extremity of an individual's foolish behavior.

yoruba: Àáyá yó níjọ́ kan, ó ní ká ká òun léhín ọ̀kánkán.
english_literal: The Colobus monkey ate its fill one day, and asked that his front teeth be knocked out.
interpretation_gold: Excessive happiness made the animal careless.
deepseek_translation: The squirrel will have a day, it says we should count it behind the squirrel.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that everyone, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem, will eventually have their moment of importance or success.
deepseek_raw: {"translation": "The squirrel will have a day, it says we should count it behind the squirrel.", "interpretation": "This proverb teaches that everyone, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem, will eventually have their moment of importance or success."}
claude_translation: The wife said one day, she said we should count her behind the husband.
claude_interpretation: A wife's proper place and role is to support and follow her husband's leadership in the household.
gemini_translation: The monkey that is full one day says we should pluck its teeth one by one.
gemini_interpretation: When one is in a state of comfort or abundance, they may make requests or demands that are impractical or foolish.
mistral_translation: The chest will have its day; it says we should massage it after every meal
mistral_interpretation: One should take care of their health consistently to prevent future problems
llama_translation: The mother says one thing, and she says another thing is behind it.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the complexity of human communication, suggesting that people often say one thing but mean another.

yoruba: Àgbà tí kò lẹ́sẹ̀ nílẹ̀ a lọ́gbọ́n nínú.
english_literal: An elder that has no substance should have cunning.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limitations and how to compensate for them.
deepseek_translation: The elder who has no legs at home uses wisdom inside.
deepseek_interpretation: Even in physical limitation, wisdom remains a valuable asset.
claude_translation: An elder who has no feet on the ground has wisdom inside
claude_interpretation: True wisdom and experience matter more than physical presence or mobility.
gemini_translation: An elder who does not have feet on the ground has wisdom within.
gemini_interpretation: Even if an elder is physically frail or unable to move, their accumulated life experience still provides valuable wisdom.
mistral_translation: An elder who cannot rest his legs on the ground walks with wisdom inside.
mistral_interpretation: True wisdom comes from experience and humility, not just age or authority.
llama_translation: An elder who is not at home is the one we consult in a foreign land.
llama_interpretation: Respect and seek guidance from those who have experience and wisdom, even if they are not physically present.

yoruba: A-wọ̀lú-má-tẹ̀ẹ́, ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀ ló mọ̀.
english_literal: One-who-enters-a-town-and-maintains-his/her-reputation does because he/she knows his/her place.
interpretation_gold: Self-knowledge guarantees one's reputation.
deepseek_translation: The one who bathes but does not dry properly, their own body knows.
deepseek_interpretation: The consequences of one's actions are ultimately felt by oneself.
claude_translation: The one who enters the palace without prostrating, only he knows his own measure
claude_interpretation: Only the person who acts disrespectfully in a sacred or important place truly understands their own audacity and the consequences they're willing to face.
gemini_translation: One who enters a town and does not stumble, knows their own body's measure.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that a person who navigates a new or challenging situation successfully does so because they understand their own capabilities and limitations.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who enters a town and does not stumble, knows their own body's measure.", "interpretation": "This proverb suggests that a person who navigates a new or challenging situation successfully does so because they understand their own capabilities and limitations."}
mistral_translation: The one who pounds yam without tiring, it is their own strength that they know
mistral_interpretation: One’s true capabilities or endurance are only fully understood by oneself.
llama_translation: The one who does not know the road, it is the people of the town who know it.
llama_interpretation: Local knowledge and expertise are essential for navigating unfamiliar territories.

yoruba: Àbá ni ikán ńdá; ikán ò lè mu òkúta.
english_literal: The termite is only striving; it can never eat a rock.
interpretation_gold: Termites may make their tunnels on a rock; the rock will be safe.
deepseek_translation: The arm is where the shrimp builds; the shrimp cannot carry a stone.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should recognize and work within their limitations.
claude_translation: The termite creates according to its ability; the termite cannot carry a stone.
claude_interpretation: Everyone should work within their capabilities and not attempt tasks beyond their natural limits or strength.
gemini_translation: It is a wish that the termite makes; a termite cannot drink a stone.
gemini_interpretation: One's aspirations or desires, no matter how strong, are limited by the realities of what is physically possible or achievable.
mistral_translation: It is a trap that a rat sets; the rat cannot lift a stone
mistral_interpretation: One who sets a trap for others may lack the strength to escape it themselves
llama_translation: The palm tree is the one that produces palm nuts; palm nuts cannot produce palm trees.
llama_interpretation: A superior being or entity is the source of something lesser, and the lesser cannot produce the superior.

yoruba: A kì í fi pàtàkì bẹ́ èlùbọ́; ẹní bá níṣu ló ḿbẹ́ ẹ.
english_literal: One does not come by yam-flour because of one's importance; only people who have yams can make yam flour.
interpretation_gold: One cannot eat one's importance.
deepseek_translation: We do not use importance to wrap pounded yam; it is the person who has soup that follows it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that true value lies in substance (like soup for pounded yam) rather than superficial appearances or claims of importance.
claude_translation: One does not beg the yam flour seller with importance; whoever has yam is the one who begs for it
claude_interpretation: Those who have what others need hold the power in any transaction or relationship.
gemini_translation: One does not peel yam flour with importance; it is the one who has yam that peels it.
gemini_interpretation: One should not prioritize or dedicate significant effort to something that is not inherently valuable or important, but rather focus on what truly matters.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not peel yam flour with importance; it is the one who has yam that peels it.", "interpretation": "One should not prioritize or dedicate significant effort to something that is not inherently valuable or important, but rather focus on what truly matters."}
mistral_translation: One does not use an important thing to cut cassava; whoever has yam is the one who holds the knife.
mistral_interpretation: Authority or decision-making power belongs to those who possess the necessary resources or qualifications.
llama_translation: We don't use a big mortar to pound locust beans; it's the one who has beans that knows how to pound them.
llama_interpretation: One must be mindful of the resources and abilities of others when assigning tasks or making demands.

yoruba: Àgbàrá ba ọ̀nà jẹ́, ó rò pé òún tún ọ̀nà ṣe.
english_literal: The rain flood ruins the path believing that it is repairing it.
interpretation_gold: Ignorance or incompetence in tackling a task often leads to unintended results.
deepseek_translation: The fire burns the road, it thinks it is repairing the road.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against actions that cause harm under the guise of helping.
claude_translation: The pothole spoiled the road, it thinks it repaired the road.
claude_interpretation: Those who cause problems often delude themselves into believing they are actually helping or solving issues.
gemini_translation: The flood spoils the road, thinking it is repairing the road.
gemini_interpretation: Actions intended to help can sometimes cause more harm than good.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The flood spoils the road, thinking it is repairing the road.", "interpretation": "Actions intended to help can sometimes cause more harm than good."}
mistral_translation: When the flood blocks the road, it thinks it is repairing the road
mistral_interpretation: It warns against mistaking destruction or disruption for improvement or progress.
llama_translation: The elder does not know the road, he says the road knows itself.
llama_interpretation: Experience and age are not the only determinants of wisdom or knowledge.

yoruba: Àìsí-ńlé ẹkùn, ajá ńgbó.
english_literal: The leopard being away from home, the dog barks.
interpretation_gold: When the master is away the minion will strut.
deepseek_translation: When the leopard is absent, the dog barks.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights how people may act boldly or disrespectfully when those in authority or more powerful individuals are not present.
claude_translation: In the absence of the leopard, the dog barks loudly
claude_interpretation: People become bold and boastful when those they fear or respect are not present.
gemini_translation: Absence of the leopard, the dog barks.
gemini_interpretation: When a powerful authority figure is absent, those of lesser status may act boldly or assume control.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Absence of the leopard, the dog barks.", "interpretation": "When a powerful authority figure is absent, those of lesser status may act boldly or assume control."}
mistral_translation: Without the leopard on the ground, the dog barks loudly
mistral_interpretation: People often act boldly or arrogantly only when a stronger authority is absent or not present to check them
llama_translation: The dead body of a leopard is eaten by a dog
llama_interpretation: Even the mighty can fall and be taken advantage of by the weak.

yoruba: Àgbààgbà ìlú ò lè péjọ kí wọn ó jẹ ìfun òkété, àfi iyán àná.
english_literal: The elders of the town will not assemble and eat the intestines of a bush-rat, only stale pounded yams.
interpretation_gold: People should behave in ways that befit their station.
deepseek_translation: The elders of the town cannot gather together to eat the intestines of the bush rat, except for yesterday's pounded yam.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that certain actions or behaviors are only acceptable under specific, often past, circumstances.
claude_translation: The elders of the town cannot gather together to eat the intestines of a grass-cutter, except yesterday's pounded yam.
claude_interpretation: Important people will not come together for trivial matters, unless there is something substantial or worthwhile involved.
gemini_translation: Elders of the town cannot gather and eat the intestines of a giant rat, except for yesterday's pounded yam.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate for elders to engage in undignified or petty acts, as their status demands respect and decorum.
mistral_translation: The elders of the town cannot gather to eat the intestines of a giant rat, except yesterday's pounded yam
mistral_interpretation: Elders should not waste time on trivial matters that do not benefit the community, focusing instead on meaningful actions.
llama_translation: The elders of the town cannot gather to eat the intestines of a rat, except with pounded yam.
llama_interpretation: Important people or elders require a certain level of dignity and respect in their gatherings and activities.

yoruba: Ahọ́n ni ìpínnlẹ̀ ẹnu.
english_literal: The tongue is the border of the mouth.
interpretation_gold: There is a limit to everything.
deepseek_translation: The mouth is the bottom of the calabash.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that words spoken carelessly can lead to trouble, just as a calabash with a weak bottom cannot hold its contents.
claude_translation: The tongue is the divider of the mouth.
claude_interpretation: The tongue has the power to create division and conflict through speech.
gemini_translation: The tongue is the state of the mouth.
gemini_interpretation: The tongue is the most important part of the mouth, as it dictates what comes out of it.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The tongue is the state of the mouth.", "interpretation": "The tongue is the most important part of the mouth, as it dictates what comes out of it."}
mistral_translation: The tongue is the boundary of the mouth
mistral_interpretation: One should be mindful of their words, as they can limit or define their circumstances
llama_translation: The tongue is the pillar of the mouth
llama_interpretation: One's words have the power to support or destroy their reputation.

yoruba: Aláṣọ-kan kì í ná ànárẹ.
english_literal: A person who has only one set of clothing does not bargain until he is wet.
interpretation_gold: A person with meagre resources should husband them judiciously.
deepseek_translation: A person with one piece of cloth does not burn the mat.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises against destroying what little one has, emphasizing prudence and resourcefulness.
claude_translation: One who has only one cloth does not lend it out
claude_interpretation: People who have limited resources are naturally cautious about sharing them because they cannot afford to lose what little they have.
gemini_translation: One who has only one cloth does not tear it for a feast.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to sacrifice your only essential resource for a temporary pleasure or event.
mistral_translation: A single piece of cloth does not strangle the leper.
mistral_interpretation: One person alone cannot overcome a problem that requires collective effort or support.
llama_translation: One cloth does not dress the body.
llama_interpretation: No single person or thing can solve all problems or meet all needs.

yoruba: Àgbà tó bú ọmọdé fi èébú-u rẹ̀ tọrọ.
english_literal: An elder who insults a youth makes a present of his own insult.
interpretation_gold: Only those who show respect for others may expect respect in return.
deepseek_translation: The elder who abuses the child uses his own abuse to beg.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that elders should lead by example, as their actions influence the behavior of the younger generation.
claude_translation: An elder who insults a child uses his insult to buy trouble.
claude_interpretation: When elders behave inappropriately toward children, they invite problems and conflict upon themselves.
gemini_translation: An elder who curses a child asks for their curse in return.
gemini_interpretation: Elders should not curse younger people, as their words carry weight and can be reciprocated negatively.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An elder who curses a child asks for their curse in return.", "interpretation": "Elders should not curse younger people, as their words carry weight and can be reciprocated negatively."}
mistral_translation: An elder who curses a child uses his own bad character as an example.
mistral_interpretation: An elder should not criticize a younger person for a fault that the elder also possesses.
llama_translation: An elder who beats a child uses his walking stick
llama_interpretation: Experience and wisdom are essential in handling delicate situations.

yoruba: Aláàńtètè: ó jí ní kùtùkùtù ó ní òun ó dàá yànpọ̀n-yànpọ̀n sílẹ̀.
english_literal: The cricket arises in the morning and vows to perform wonders.
interpretation_gold: The puny person's boasts are always empty.
deepseek_translation: The lazy person: he wakes up early and says he will stretch leisurely.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes laziness and procrastination, highlighting how the lazy make excuses to avoid work.
claude_translation: The early riser: he woke up very early and said he would defecate scattered droppings on the ground
claude_interpretation: Being early or first doesn't guarantee quality results if one lacks proper preparation or skill.
gemini_translation: The early riser: he woke up early and said he would cause a commotion.
gemini_interpretation: Waking up early with a mischievous intent suggests that some people are inherently inclined to cause trouble, regardless of the circumstances.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The early riser: he woke up early and said he would cause a commotion.", "interpretation": "Waking up early with a mischievous intent suggests that some people are inherently inclined to cause trouble, regardless of the circumstances."}
mistral_translation: The early riser: he wakes up very early and says he will spread out various mats outside
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the importance of taking early action to secure opportunities before others do
llama_translation: The one who is always in a hurry: he eats in a hurry, he also walks hastily to the market.
llama_interpretation: Haste can lead to mistakes and accidents.

yoruba: Adìẹ funfun ò mọ ara ẹ̀ lágbà.
english_literal: The white chicken does not recognize itself as an elder.
interpretation_gold: One should act one's age always.
deepseek_translation: The white chicken does not know itself to be old.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against self-deception or lack of self-awareness regarding one's limitations or age.
claude_translation: The white chicken does not know itself as an elder.
claude_interpretation: People often fail to recognize their own wisdom, experience, or status that others can clearly see.
gemini_translation: A white fowl does not know itself to be old.
gemini_interpretation: One's appearance does not always reflect their true age or experience.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A white fowl does not know itself to be old.", "interpretation": "One's appearance does not always reflect their true age or experience."}
mistral_translation: The white chicken does not know its own age.
mistral_interpretation: One should not be arrogant or forgetful of their origins and limitations.
llama_translation: White cloth does not know the body is big
llama_interpretation: One's appearance or status does not necessarily reflect one's true nature or abilities.

yoruba: Àgbà tó fi ara-a rẹ̀ féwe lèwe ḿbú.
english_literal: It is an elder who delivers himself unto youths that the youth will insult.
interpretation_gold: If one wants to be respected, one should respect oneself.
deepseek_translation: The elder who behaves childishly is playing with fire.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that elders should act with maturity and dignity, as childish behavior can lead to trouble or disrespect.
claude_translation: An elder who compares himself to a leaf is what the leaf respects
claude_interpretation: When elders humble themselves and show modesty, they earn genuine respect from those younger than them.
gemini_translation: An elder who makes himself a child will be insulted by children.
gemini_interpretation: Elders should maintain their dignity and not behave childishly, or they risk losing the respect of younger generations.
mistral_translation: An elder who uses his body to shade a leaf from the sun for a young plant.
mistral_interpretation: It highlights the selfless care and protection elders provide to nurture the younger generation.
llama_translation: An elder who uses his body to play with a child will get tired
llama_interpretation: One should not engage in activities that are beneath their age or status.

yoruba: Àlémú ò yẹ àgbà; àgbà kì í ṣe ohun àlémú.
english_literal: To be pursued does not become an elder; an elder does not cause himself to be pursued.
interpretation_gold: Elders should always behave in ways that would cause them no disgrace.
deepseek_translation: The young palm frond does not surpass the old one; the old one is not a thing of the young palm frond.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the respect and value due to elders, as their wisdom and experience cannot be matched by the youth.
claude_translation: Disgraceful behavior does not befit an elder; an elder does not do disgraceful things.
claude_interpretation: Elders are expected to maintain dignity and avoid shameful conduct that would diminish their respected status in society.
gemini_translation: A joke does not suit an elder; an elder does not do things that are jokes.
gemini_interpretation: Elders are expected to maintain a dignified and serious demeanor, avoiding frivolous behavior that could diminish their respect and authority.
mistral_translation: A child's action is not suitable for an elder; an elder does not do a child's thing
mistral_interpretation: Each person should act according to their age, status, and responsibility in society
llama_translation: The young one does not greet the elder; the elder does not do the work of the young one.
llama_interpretation: Respect and responsibility are tied to one's age and social status.

yoruba: Ajá rí epo kò lá; ìyá-a rẹ̀ẹ́ ṣu ihá bí.?
english_literal: The dog sees palm-oil but does not lick it; did its mother excrete palm-nut pericarp?
interpretation_gold: One should not be unreasonably squeamish.
deepseek_translation: The dog saw palm oil; can its mother lick salt?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the inevitability of influence or behavior passed down from parent to child.
claude_translation: The dog sees palm oil but cannot lick it; did its mother give birth to it in vain?
claude_interpretation: One should not waste opportunities or fail to take advantage of good fortune when it presents itself.
gemini_translation: A dog saw palm oil and did not lick it; did its mother excrete a thorny fruit?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions why someone would reject something inherently desirable or beneficial, implying that such an action is unnatural or unexpected.
mistral_translation: Does a dog that sees palm oil not lick it; will its mother then chew the bone for it?
mistral_interpretation: One should take responsibility for their own opportunities rather than expecting others to do so on their behalf.
llama_translation: The dog sees the palm oil but does not lick it; what is the mother's concern?
llama_interpretation: One should not be concerned about what is not their problem or responsibility.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà akàn tó kó sí garawa yègèdè, ojú tì í.
english_literal: The elderly crab that enters into a bucket; it is thoroughly disgraced.
interpretation_gold: One should avoid potentially disgraceful actions.
deepseek_translation: The old crab that enters the basket of yègèdè, its eyes are closed.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that experienced individuals should not feign ignorance when faced with familiar situations.
claude_translation: An elder who puts yam flour in a calabash feels ashamed
claude_interpretation: When someone of high status or experience does something beneath their dignity or makes a basic mistake, they feel embarrassed.
gemini_translation: An old crab that falls into a shallow bucket is ashamed.
gemini_interpretation: It is shameful for an experienced person to make a foolish or easily avoidable mistake.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An old crab that falls into a shallow bucket is ashamed.", "interpretation": "It is shameful for an experienced person to make a foolish or easily avoidable mistake."}
mistral_translation: An elder who has gathered enough wisdom to fill a calabash of melon seeds, yet still has eyes to see.
mistral_interpretation: True wisdom in elders is shown by their continued openness to learning and observing, no matter how much knowledge they already possess.
llama_translation: The elderly person who carries a load to the market, the eyes are not enough
llama_interpretation: Experience and wisdom are not enough to accomplish a task without physical effort.

yoruba: Abùléra ọ̀fọ́n-ọ̀n; ó ní ọjọ́ tí ológbò-ó ti bí òun ò ìtí-ì dá a ní báríkà.
english_literal: Mouse-that-does-not-know-its-place; it says that since the day the cat delivered (a baby) it has not gone to offer congratulations.
interpretation_gold: Never forget your vulnerabilities and limitations.
deepseek_translation: The house rat is small; it says the day the wild rat gave birth to it, it did not resemble a squirrel.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches humility by reminding people not to boast about their origins or status, as everyone has humble beginnings.
claude_translation: The foolish rat; it says the day the cat gave birth to it, it did not give it whiskers.
claude_interpretation: A foolish person blames others for their natural disadvantages instead of accepting their limitations and working with what they have.
gemini_translation: The chameleon is a fool; it says the day the cat gave birth to it, it has not yet congratulated it.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the foolishness of someone who denies their origins or fails to acknowledge those who brought them into being.
mistral_translation: The cat does not forget; it says the day the kitten was born it did not receive a blessing from it.
mistral_interpretation: This proverb warns against ingratitude, reminding people that those who help or nurture others may remember if they are later disrespected or unappreciated.
llama_translation: The compound is not a forest; it says the day the elephant gave birth to it, it was not as big as this.
llama_interpretation: A person's greatness is not solely determined by their current circumstances, but by their potential and future prospects.

yoruba: A-ṣe-bọ̀rọ̀kìnní-má-kìíyè-sábíyá, gbogbo abíyá dọ́ṣẹ.
english_literal: He-who-lives-in-style-but-pays-no-attention-to-his-armpits, both armpits are taken over with foamy filth.
interpretation_gold: Attention to detail is integral to good character or breeding.
deepseek_translation: One who acts hastily does not inquire about the mother's name, all mothers are guilty.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against hasty actions without proper consideration, as they often lead to blame and regret.
claude_translation: One who performs rituals carelessly without proper reverence for the sacred, all the rituals become ineffective
claude_interpretation: Spiritual practices require genuine respect and proper intention to be meaningful and effective.
gemini_translation: One who acts like a wealthy person but does not pay attention to the midwives, all the midwives become angry.
gemini_interpretation: Those in positions of power or wealth must acknowledge and appreciate the contributions of others, especially those who provide essential services, to avoid resentment.
mistral_translation: The one who prepares to be a leader does not lack wisdom, all wise people make mistakes
mistral_interpretation: No matter how wise or prepared a leader is, they are still human and can make errors.
llama_translation: The one who does not know how to greet in the morning will not know how to greet in the evening, all children will be confused.

deepseek_translation: The bride's wrapper is pulled gently; if it is pulled and it does not come off, she says what is holding it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises patience and gentleness in handling delicate matters, as force may reveal underlying issues.
claude_translation: A bride is something that must be pulled gently; if you pull her and she doesn't yield, she has her reasons.
claude_interpretation: Patience and understanding are required when dealing with people, as resistance often has valid underlying causes.
gemini_translation: Reluctance is for the wife; if we pull her and she doesn't budge, she has something bothering her.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that a woman's apparent reluctance or resistance often indicates an underlying issue or concern that needs to be addressed.
mistral_translation: The bride is like a pulled thread; if you pull it and it does not stretch, it will make the noise of what it is doing.
mistral_interpretation: A person’s true nature or hidden flaws will eventually reveal themselves under pressure or scrutiny.
llama_translation: The one who does not have a husband is not a wife; if we do not have a husband and yet we are not a wife, it means there is something wrong with us.
llama_interpretation: A person's worth or identity is not solely defined by their relationship status.

yoruba: Àkísà-á mọ ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀, ó gbé párá jẹ́.
english_literal: The rag knows its place; it remains quietly on the rafters.
interpretation_gold: A person of low standing should not call attention to himself or herself.
deepseek_translation: The cripple knows his size, he carried a load and it broke.
deepseek_interpretation: One should recognize their limitations and act accordingly to avoid failure.
claude_translation: The grasshopper does not know its own measure, it swallowed a locust.
claude_interpretation: People who don't understand their own limitations often attempt things beyond their capacity.
gemini_translation: The rag knows its own measure, it stays on the heap.
gemini_interpretation: One should understand their limitations and not overstep their boundaries.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The rag knows its own measure, it stays on the heap.", "interpretation": "One should understand their limitations and not overstep their boundaries."}
mistral_translation: The rag knows its own size, it covers only a part
mistral_interpretation: One should recognize their own limitations and not overreach beyond their capacity
llama_translation: The tortoise knows the size of its own stomach, it eats accordingly.
llama_interpretation: One should be mindful of their limitations and not overextend themselves.

yoruba: A kì í gbọ́n tó “Èmi-lóni-í.”
english_literal: One cannot be as wise as “I-am-the-owner.”
interpretation_gold: One should not presume to know as much about something as the owner.
deepseek_translation: One cannot be wiser than 'I am the one today.'
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against excessive pride or arrogance, as no one is superior to fate or circumstance.
claude_translation: One cannot be wiser than 'I-am-the-one-today.'
claude_interpretation: No one can outsmart someone who is currently in power or control of a situation.
gemini_translation: One is not as wise as 'I am the owner of today.'
gemini_interpretation: No one is wise enough to predict or control the events of the future.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One is not as wise as 'I am the owner of today.'", "interpretation": "No one is wise enough to predict or control the events of the future."}
mistral_translation: We do not become wise enough to say 'It is I who owns this.'
mistral_interpretation: No one should be so arrogant as to claim absolute ownership or authority over anything, as humility is a valued virtue.
llama_translation: We do not hear the one who says 'I am the owner of today.'
llama_interpretation: One should not boast about being in a position of power or authority, as it can be fleeting.

yoruba: Àgbà ajá kì í bàwọ̀jẹ́.
english_literal: A grown dog does not deface its skin.
interpretation_gold: Decorum goes with age.
deepseek_translation: The old dog does not bark in vain.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that experienced people do not act without reason; their actions are based on wisdom and knowledge.
claude_translation: An elder dog does not eat excrement
claude_interpretation: Experience and maturity prevent one from engaging in degrading or foolish behavior.
gemini_translation: An old dog does not spoil the hunt.
gemini_interpretation: Experience and wisdom gained over time are valuable and contribute positively to endeavors.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An old dog does not spoil the hunt.", "interpretation": "Experience and wisdom gained over time are valuable and contribute positively to endeavors."}
mistral_translation: An old dog does not prostrate to greet.
mistral_interpretation: Elders or experienced individuals are not obligated to show excessive deference to others due to their wisdom and status.
llama_translation: The elder dog does not get lost.
llama_interpretation: Experience and age bring wisdom and guidance.

yoruba: Àgbà-ìyà tí ńmùkọ ọ̀níní, ó ní nítorí omi gbígbóná orí-i rẹ̀ ni.
english_literal: Worthless elderly person who is eating corn gruel worth one tenth of a penny, he says he only wants the hot water on top of it.
interpretation_gold: One should act according to the demands of one's status.
deepseek_translation: The old suffering that befriends wealth says it is because of hot water on its head.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that enduring hardship (like scalding water) can lead to prosperity and respect.
claude_translation: The elder who is teaching the young person says it is because of the hot water on his head.
claude_interpretation: Experience and wisdom come from enduring hardships and challenges in life.
gemini_translation: The old woman who drinks cold pap says it is because of the hot water on her head.
gemini_interpretation: People often attribute their actions or choices to external circumstances, even if those reasons are not directly related or are a convenient excuse.
mistral_translation: The old calabash that leaks today says it is because the water it carries is too hot for its head
mistral_interpretation: People often blame their current failures or shortcomings on past difficulties or hardships rather than taking responsibility.
llama_translation: An elderly woman who is a gossip, she says because the water has touched her head
llama_interpretation: Old age does not necessarily bring wisdom or discretion.

yoruba: We saw other trees in the bush before we settled on ọ̀mọ̀
interpretation_gold: One should never presume to be the only possible answer to every challenge.
deepseek_translation: We saw other trees in the bush before we settled on the child
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that careful consideration and comparison were made before making a final choice or decision.
claude_translation: We saw other trees in the bush before we settled on ọ̀mọ̀
claude_interpretation: One should carefully consider all available options before making a final decision, as the choice made reflects deliberate selection after proper evaluation.
gemini_translation: We saw other trees in the bush before we settled on ọ̀mọ̀
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to explore all available options before making a final decision.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We saw other trees in the bush before we settled on ọ̀mọ̀", "interpretation": "It is wise to explore all available options before making a final decision."}
mistral_translation: We saw other trees in the forest before we chose the ọ̀mọ̀ tree
mistral_interpretation: One carefully considers all available options before making a final decision or commitment.
llama_translation: We saw other trees in the bush before we settled on ọ̀mọ̀
llama_interpretation: One should consider all options before making a final decision.

yoruba: Àgbà tí kò nítìjú, ojú kan ni ìbá ní; ojú kan náà a wà lọ́gangan iwájú-u rẹ̀.
english_literal: An elder without self-respect might as well have only one eye, that one eye being in the center of his forehead.
interpretation_gold: Shamelessness does not become an elder.
deepseek_translation: An elder who is not blind has one eye; the other eye is in front of him.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that elders possess wisdom and foresight, seeing beyond the obvious.
claude_translation: An elder who has no shame would have one eye; that same one eye would be located in the middle of his forehead.
claude_interpretation: A shameless elder is like a cyclops with poor vision, unable to see clearly or judge situations properly due to their lack of moral awareness.
gemini_translation: An elder who has no shame would have only one face; that one face would be right in front of them.
gemini_interpretation: A truly shameless person would not care about public opinion or the need to present different faces to different people, as their lack of shame would be openly displayed for all to see.
mistral_translation: An elder who has no shame will have one eye; that same eye will be looking sideways into his future.
mistral_interpretation: A person without shame or self-respect will face consequences that hinder their progress and future.
llama_translation: An elder who is not respected, one eye is the one that is blind; that same one eye is the one that is looking at his future.
llama_interpretation: A person who is not respected in their old age will have a bleak future.
llama_raw: {"translation": "An elder who is not respected, one eye is the one that is blind; that same one eye is the one that is looking at his future.", "interpretation": "A person who is not respected in their old age will have a bleak future."}

yoruba: A kì í yàgò fún “Mo gun ẹṣin rí o!”
english_literal: One does not get out of the way for “I used to ride a horse!”
interpretation_gold: People should not expect to live on past glory.
deepseek_translation: One does not make excuses for "I rode a horse and saw it!"
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that firsthand experience or direct knowledge does not require justification or excuses.
claude_translation: One does not make way for 'I have ridden a horse before!'
claude_interpretation: Past achievements or experiences do not automatically command present respect or special treatment.
gemini_translation: One does not make way for 'I have ridden a horse before!'
gemini_interpretation: Past achievements or experiences do not automatically grant present authority or respect.
mistral_translation: We do not prepare a stable for 'I rode a horse and saw you!'
mistral_interpretation: One should not make unnecessary preparations or assumptions based on mere boasts or empty claims.
llama_translation: We don't shout for 'I see a horse!'
llama_interpretation: One should not make a big deal out of something insignificant or obvious.

yoruba: A kì í mọ ọ̀nà ọgbà ju ọlọ́gbà lọ; ẹní múni wá là ńtẹ̀lé.
english_literal: One does not presume to know the way to or around a garden better than the owner of the garden; one always follows the person who brought one.
interpretation_gold: Never presume to have a better knowledge of a matter than has the person most intimately involved.
deepseek_translation: We cannot know the way to the farm better than the farmer; it is the one who brought us that we follow.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes respecting and following the guidance of those with more experience or knowledge.
claude_translation: One cannot know the path to the farm better than the farm owner; we follow the one who brought us.
claude_interpretation: Always follow the guidance of those with direct experience and authority in their domain, as they know best how to navigate their own territory.
gemini_translation: One does not know the garden path better than the gardener; we follow the one who brought us.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to defer to the expertise of those who are more knowledgeable or experienced in a particular domain, especially when they are guiding you.
mistral_translation: We do not know the path of the garden more than the gardener; it is the one who leads us that we follow.
mistral_interpretation: Respect the wisdom and guidance of those with more experience or authority in a matter.
llama_translation: One does not know the path of the forest more than the hunter; it is the owner who shows us the way.
llama_interpretation: Experience and knowledge are not enough; guidance from those in authority or with deeper understanding is necessary for success.

yoruba: Àì-kúkú-joye, ó sàn ju, “Ẹnuù mi ò ká ìlú” lọ.
english_literal: Not-assuming-the-position-of-ruler-at-all is far better than, “My word is not heeded by the people.”
interpretation_gold: A person who does not assume a responsibility is better off than a person who takes it on and fails to fulfill it.
deepseek_translation: It is better to endure hunger than to say, 'My mouth has betrayed the town.'
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the value of discretion and loyalty, emphasizing that personal suffering is preferable to betraying trust or revealing secrets.
claude_translation: Not becoming a chief at all is better than saying 'My mouth cannot rule a town'
claude_interpretation: It is better to never attempt leadership than to accept a position and then claim incompetence or inability to fulfill the responsibilities.
gemini_translation: Not becoming a chief at all is better than saying, 'My mouth cannot control the town.'
gemini_interpretation: It is better to decline a position of leadership than to accept it and fail to fulfill its responsibilities effectively.
mistral_translation: Not dying suddenly is better than saying, 'My mouth will not taste the town.'
mistral_interpretation: It is wiser to endure temporary hardship than to boast prematurely about avoiding future suffering.
llama_translation: The one who does not die does not know the value of life, he says, “My mouth does not know the town”
llama_interpretation: One must experience hardship or loss to truly appreciate the value of life.

yoruba: A sìnkú tán, alugbá ò lọ́ ó fẹ́ ṣúpó ni?
english_literal: The funeral is over, but the calabash beater does not take his leave; does he want to inherit a wife?
interpretation_gold: This proverb has the same import as, A kúnlẹ̀, a pàgbò . . .
deepseek_translation: When the rat dies, does the trap go to the funeral?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against expecting loyalty or gratitude from those who only benefit from you when you are useful to them.
claude_translation: After we finish burying the dead, the grave digger doesn't leave, does he want to cook soup?
claude_interpretation: People who linger unnecessarily after completing their assigned task may have ulterior motives.
gemini_translation: We have finished the burial, will the calabash drummer not want to marry a successor?
gemini_interpretation: Even after a period of mourning or a significant event, life continues and people will eventually move on to new relationships or endeavors.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We have finished the burial, will the calabash drummer not want to marry a successor?", "interpretation": "Even after a period of mourning or a significant event, life continues and people will eventually move on to new relationships or endeavors."}
mistral_translation: After the burial is over, does the one who carries the corpse refuse to take the soup bowl?
mistral_interpretation: One should not refuse a well-deserved reward or benefit after fulfilling a difficult or unpleasant task.
llama_translation: We are crying together, who is the one that will console us?
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of having someone to turn to for comfort in times of collective suffering.

yoruba: Àkíìjẹ́ mú òrìṣà níyì.
english_literal: Refusal-to-acknowledge-salutations enhances the god's dignity.
interpretation_gold: Distancing oneself from ordinary people lends one prestige.
deepseek_translation: The stubbornness of the crab disrespects the deity.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that persistent defiance can lead to disrespect or downfall, even towards revered figures.
claude_translation: Greetings bring honor to the deity
claude_interpretation: Showing proper respect and courtesy through greetings brings dignity and reverence to spiritual forces and authority figures.
gemini_translation: One does not take a deity for granted.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to show respect and reverence to those in positions of authority or power, as well as to sacred things.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not take a deity for granted.", "interpretation": "It is important to show respect and reverence to those in positions of authority or power, as well as to sacred things."}
mistral_translation: One does not take pride away from a deity.
mistral_interpretation: Respect and honor due to those in authority or positions of reverence should not be diminished.
llama_translation: The tortoise swallows the deity
llama_interpretation: Even the weak can overpower the strong through cunning and strategy.
