yoruba: Aládàá lo làṣẹ àro.
english_literal: It is the owner of the machete who exercises authority over mutual laborers.
interpretation_gold: One yields authority to one's host, or the owner of the property.
deepseek_translation: The owner of the dye pit knows the depth of the dye.
deepseek_interpretation: Only the person involved in a situation truly understands its intricacies.
claude_translation: The one with a cutlass is the one who commands the dye.
claude_interpretation: Those who possess the tools or power are the ones who control the process and make the decisions.
gemini_translation: The one who cuts is the one who has authority over the inheritance.
gemini_interpretation: The person who initiates or controls a process ultimately determines its outcome or distribution.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who cuts is the one who has authority over the inheritance.", "interpretation": "The person who initiates or controls a process ultimately determines its outcome or distribution."}
mistral_translation: It is the dyer who owns the indigo dye.
mistral_interpretation: Those who possess a skill or resource have the authority to decide how it is used.
llama_translation: The one who has a wrapper is the one who has a cloth
llama_interpretation: Having a little is better than having nothing at all.

yoruba: Akú, nkò ní omitooro-o rẹ̀ ẹ́ lá; àìkú, nkò níí pè é rán níṣẹ́.
english_literal: Dead, I will not eat its broth; alive, I will not send it on an errand.
interpretation_gold: One needs pay no mind to a person who can in no way affect one's fortune.
deepseek_translation: Death, it does not announce its coming; death, it does not send a messenger ahead.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that death comes unexpectedly and without warning, emphasizing life's unpredictability.
claude_translation: Death, I will not call upon your helper to break it; not dying, I will not send it on an errand
claude_interpretation: One should neither wish for death nor take life for granted, but accept whatever fate brings without trying to manipulate it.
gemini_translation: If you die, I will not lick your soup; if you don't die, I will not send you on an errand.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb expresses a complete disassociation from someone, indicating a desire to have no dealings with them, whether in life or death.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If you die, I will not lick your soup; if you don't die, I will not send you on an errand.", "interpretation": "This proverb expresses a complete disassociation from someone, indicating a desire to have no dealings with them, whether in life or death."}
mistral_translation: If it is death, I will not plead for its delay; if it is immortality, I will not call it to come and work.
mistral_interpretation: One should accept fate without complaint, whether it brings hardship or ease, as destiny cannot be altered by mere words.
llama_translation: Death, it is the one who takes the owner of the house away; life, it is the one who calls him to work.
llama_interpretation: Life is a call to work and responsibility, while death is a force that can suddenly take one away from those responsibilities.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà tó ńgun ọ̀pẹ, bó bá já lulẹ̀ ó dọ̀run.
english_literal: An elder who climbs palm-trees: if he crashes from the tree he will find himself in heaven.
interpretation_gold: An elder should know better than to climb palm-trees; one should not court danger.
deepseek_translation: An old man climbing a palm tree, if he falls, he falls heavily.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that the consequences of failure are more severe for those who take on risky endeavors beyond their capacity.
claude_translation: An elder who climbs a palm tree, if he falls down he goes to heaven.
claude_interpretation: When experienced people take unnecessary risks at their age, the consequences can be fatal.
gemini_translation: An elder who climbs a palm tree, if he falls, he goes to heaven.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb humorously implies that an elder engaging in risky activities might face severe consequences, highlighting the importance of caution and wisdom in old age.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An elder who climbs a palm tree, if he falls, he goes to heaven.", "interpretation": "This proverb humorously implies that an elder engaging in risky activities might face severe consequences, highlighting the importance of caution and wisdom in old age."}
mistral_translation: An elder who is climbing a palm tree, if he falls to the ground, he will go to heaven.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the respect for elders, suggesting that even in failure, their dignity and wisdom remain intact.
llama_translation: An elderly person who is beating a palm tree, if he is not careful, he will fall
llama_interpretation: One should be mindful of their actions, lest they suffer the consequences of their own doing.

yoruba: Àì-lápá làdá ò mú; bí a bá lápá, ọmọ owú to-o gégi.
english_literal: It is a deficiency of biceps that blunts the machete; if one has strong biceps one can cut trees with a cudgel.
interpretation_gold: One should not blame one's deficiencies on one's tools.
deepseek_translation: The knife without a handle is not taken; if it has a handle, the child of the cotton tree cuts the tree.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of preparation and having the right tools or support to achieve success.
claude_translation: Not having arms is why the cutlass cannot be held; if one has arms, cotton thread can cut wood.
claude_interpretation: Having the right tools or abilities makes even seemingly impossible tasks achievable, while lacking them makes even simple tasks impossible.
gemini_translation: It is because one has no arm that the cutlass does not cut; if one has an arm, a child of owu can cut wood.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that perceived limitations often stem from a lack of ability or effort, and with the right tools or capabilities, even seemingly difficult tasks can be accomplished by anyone.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It is because one has no arm that the cutlass does not cut; if one has an arm, a child of owu can cut wood.", "interpretation": "The proverb emphasizes that perceived limitations often stem from a lack of ability or effort, and with the right tools or capabilities, even seemingly difficult tasks can be accomplished by anyone."}
mistral_translation: It is the one without a cutlass that the machete does not touch; if one has a cutlass, the child of the cotton plant that is too stubborn gets cut
mistral_interpretation: Those who are unprepared or lack the means to defend themselves often avoid trouble, while the reckless or overconfident invite consequences
llama_translation: The one who does not have a hoe does not farm; if you have a hoe, the child of a farmer will not be lazy.
llama_interpretation: Having the right tools or resources is essential for productivity and success.

yoruba: A kì í gbé sàráà kọjá-a mọ́ṣáláṣí.
english_literal: One does not carry alms beyond the mosque.
interpretation_gold: Excess brings disgrace.
deepseek_translation: One does not carry a load and pass by the palm wine tapper unnoticed.
deepseek_interpretation: Your actions and responsibilities are visible to those around you.
claude_translation: One does not carry a prayer mat past the mosque.
claude_interpretation: Don't miss opportunities when they present themselves right in front of you.
gemini_translation: One does not carry alms past the mosque.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to give to those in need, especially when the opportunity or designated place for such giving is present.
mistral_translation: We do not carry a prayer mat past a mosque.
mistral_interpretation: It is unnecessary to show off or overdo something that is already well-known or commonly practiced in a particular place.
llama_translation: We don't take a calabash to fetch water beyond the river
llama_interpretation: One should not seek help or solutions from a source that is already overwhelmed or insufficient.

yoruba: A kì í fini joyè àwòdì ká má lè gbádìẹ.
english_literal: One cannot be given the title “eagle” and yet be incapable of snatching chickens.
interpretation_gold: One should be able to live up to expectations.
deepseek_translation: One does not aspire to the hawk's title without being able to soar like an eagle.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not seek a position or honor if you lack the requisite skills or ability.
claude_translation: One is not given the chieftaincy title of the hawk without being able to catch a chick
claude_interpretation: Authority or position must be earned through demonstrated competence and ability to fulfill the responsibilities that come with it.
gemini_translation: One is not made a chief of hawks and be unable to seize a chicken.
gemini_interpretation: One should be capable of fulfilling the responsibilities and expectations that come with their position or authority.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One is not made a chief of hawks and be unable to seize a chicken.", "interpretation": "One should be capable of fulfilling the responsibilities and expectations that come with their position or authority."}
mistral_translation: We do not first install the vulture as a chief and then fail to be able to pluck a chicken
mistral_interpretation: One should not appoint someone to a position of authority without ensuring they have the necessary competence or resources to fulfill their duties
llama_translation: We do not learn the art of being a king from a pawn.
llama_interpretation: One must learn from those who have achieved greatness, not from those who are still struggling.

yoruba: Aláṣejù, baba ojo.
english_literal: The immoderate person, greatest of cowards.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation is a cloak for cowardice.
deepseek_translation: Excessiveness, father of rain.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that excessiveness (greed, wastefulness) leads to ruin, just as too much rain can cause floods.
claude_translation: The one who does too much is the father of trouble
claude_interpretation: Excessive actions or overdoing things leads to problems and complications.
gemini_translation: Excessiveness, father of rain.
gemini_interpretation: Too much of anything, even a good thing, can lead to negative consequences.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Excessiveness, father of rain.", "interpretation": "Too much of anything, even a good thing, can lead to negative consequences."}
mistral_translation: The excessive one is the father of rain.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive behavior or overindulgence often leads to negative consequences.
llama_translation: The one who clears the road, father of the journey.
llama_interpretation: Those who pave the way for others are considered the true leaders or pioneers.

yoruba: Aṣọ tó kuni kù ní ńjẹ́ gọgọwú.
english_literal: Whatever clothing one is left with is one's best.
interpretation_gold: One makes the most of what one has.
deepseek_translation: The cloth that is short is what causes the itch.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that inadequacy or lack often leads to discomfort or problems.
claude_translation: The cloth that is left over after cutting is what becomes rags.
claude_interpretation: What remains or is discarded often becomes useful for humble purposes later.
gemini_translation: The cloth that is too big for one is called 'gogowu'.
gemini_interpretation: Something that is too large or ill-fitting for a person is considered cumbersome or inappropriate.
mistral_translation: The cloth that is left after being cut is what is used to make a patch.
mistral_interpretation: One should make the best use of whatever resources or opportunities remain available, no matter how small or insignificant they may seem.
llama_translation: A cloth that is not sold is being worn by a madman.
llama_interpretation: Something that is not valued or appreciated by others may still be useful or beneficial to someone else.

yoruba: À-sẹ́-kú làgbàlagbà ńsẹ́ ọ̀ràn.
english_literal: Denying-until-death is the way a venerable person denies a matter.
interpretation_gold: One must never admit to doing something unworthy of one's position.
deepseek_translation: The elder is doing things as if there is no death.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against the arrogance or recklessness of elders who act as if they are immune to death or consequences.
claude_translation: It is 'let it not die' that the elder is doing to the matter
claude_interpretation: Elders work to preserve and sustain important matters or traditions to prevent them from being forgotten or lost.
gemini_translation: The elder settles a dispute to the point of death.
gemini_interpretation: Elders are expected to resolve conflicts thoroughly and definitively, even if it requires significant effort or sacrifice.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The elder settles a dispute to the point of death.", "interpretation": "Elders are expected to resolve conflicts thoroughly and definitively, even if it requires significant effort or sacrifice."}
mistral_translation: It is by not dying that an elder handles matters
mistral_interpretation: The wisdom and experience of elders are invaluable in resolving issues, as they have lived long enough to understand life's complexities
llama_translation: The one who does not die does not know the value of life.
llama_interpretation: Appreciation for life comes from experiencing its fragility and impermanence.

yoruba: À-gbàbọ̀-ọ ṣòkòtò, bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a ṣoni; rẹ́múrẹ́mú ni ohun ẹni ḿbani mu.
english_literal: Borrowed trousers: if they are not too tight around the legs, they will be too loose; one's own things fit one exactly.
interpretation_gold: Borrowed articles are never like one's own.
deepseek_translation: The one who wears trousers, if it does not cover the legs, it covers the waist; persistence is what sustains one's livelihood.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of perseverance and adaptability in overcoming challenges to sustain one's livelihood.
claude_translation: A borrowed trouser, if it doesn't give you legs it will disgrace you; gently is how one's own thing holds one
claude_interpretation: It's better to use what belongs to you, even if modest, than to borrow something that may not fit properly and cause embarrassment.
gemini_translation: The borrowed trousers, if they don't pinch the legs, they will tear; one's own things are what one enjoys using.
gemini_interpretation: It is always better to rely on one's own resources and possessions than to depend on borrowed ones, which often come with complications or limitations.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The borrowed trousers, if they don't pinch the legs, they will tear; one's own things are what one enjoys using.", "interpretation": "It is always better to rely on one's own resources and possessions than to depend on borrowed ones, which often come with complications or limitations."}
mistral_translation: The one who sews trousers for a hunchback, if it does not fit the legs, it will fit the waist; what belongs to someone will eventually be theirs to use
mistral_interpretation: No effort is truly wasted, as what is meant for someone will eventually serve them in some way
llama_translation: The farmer's farm is not far from his house, but the lazy person's farm is far from his house; what one does not want to do is what one will be forced to do.
llama_interpretation: One's laziness can lead to a life of hardship and struggle.

yoruba: Àpárá ńlá ni iná ńdá; iná ò lè rí omi gbéṣe.
english_literal: The fire is being most overbearing; there is nothing fire can do to water.
interpretation_gold: This entry has the same application as the preceding one.
deepseek_translation: A big fire is what fire starts; fire cannot carry water to perform rituals.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that those who cause problems cannot be trusted to solve them.
claude_translation: Fire creates a big flame; fire cannot borrow water.
claude_interpretation: One cannot seek help from their natural enemy or opposite, as fundamental differences make cooperation impossible.
gemini_translation: A big boast is what fire makes; fire cannot see water and act.
gemini_interpretation: One should not make empty boasts, as true power or authority will always reveal the limits of such claims.
mistral_translation: The big log is what the fire burns; the fire cannot see the water that will extinguish it
mistral_interpretation: A person may be powerful or successful now, but they cannot foresee the challenges or forces that will eventually overcome them
llama_translation: A large axe is what gives fire; fire cannot see the water's edge.
llama_interpretation: One's strength or ability is what gives one power or influence.

yoruba: Ajá kì í rorò kó ṣọ́ ojúlé méjì.
english_literal: A dog is never so fierce that it can guard two doorways.
interpretation_gold: One cannot serve two masters simultaneously.
deepseek_translation: A dog does not get so fat that it owns two houses.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not become so successful or wealthy that they forget their roots or responsibilities.
claude_translation: A dog does not bark and guard two compounds at once.
claude_interpretation: One cannot effectively serve two masters or divide their loyalty and attention between competing interests.
gemini_translation: A dog cannot be fierce and guard two compounds simultaneously.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot effectively manage or dedicate oneself to two demanding tasks or responsibilities at the same time.
mistral_translation: A dog does not grow so fierce that it urinates in two compounds.
mistral_interpretation: No matter how powerful or arrogant someone becomes, they should not overstep their bounds or disrespect others.
llama_translation: A dog does not get tired of going to two markets.
llama_interpretation: One should not be deterred from pursuing multiple opportunities or sources of livelihood.

yoruba: Agbára wo ló wà lọ́wọ́ igbá tó fẹ́ fi gbọ́n omi òkun?
english_literal: What strength does the calabash have at its disposal that makes it attempt to scoop up all the water in the ocean?
interpretation_gold: People should not overreach.
deepseek_translation: What strength is in the hand of the calabash that it wants to use to scoop the ocean water?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against overestimating one's abilities or attempting impossible tasks.
claude_translation: What power does a calabash have that it wants to use to scoop ocean water?
claude_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks that are far beyond their capacity or resources.
gemini_translation: What power does a calabash have that it wants to scoop the ocean water?
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to attempt a task that is clearly beyond one's capabilities.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "What power does a calabash have that it wants to scoop the ocean water?", "interpretation": "It is foolish to attempt a task that is clearly beyond one's capabilities."}
mistral_translation: What strength is there in the hands of the calabash that wants to measure the depth of the ocean?
mistral_interpretation: It highlights the futility of attempting a task beyond one's capacity or resources.
llama_translation: Who is strong enough to fetch water from the ocean with a calabash?
llama_interpretation: One should not attempt a task that is beyond one's capability or strength.

yoruba: A-dìtan-mọ́ èsúó; ó ní èkùlù ló bí ìyá òun.
english_literal: The red-flanked duiker, desperate to claim relationship, says that its mother was born of a crested duiker.
interpretation_gold: Never make preposterous claims of kinship.
deepseek_translation: The one who is mocking the cripple; he says it is the hunchback that gave birth to his mother.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against mocking others' flaws, as one may unknowingly share similar or worse imperfections.
claude_translation: The one who knows how to deceive the yam; he says it was the earthworm that gave birth to his mother.
claude_interpretation: A skilled deceiver will tell outrageous lies, claiming impossible things like a small creature being ancestor to a larger one.
gemini_translation: The one who is too familiar with the goat; he says the bushbuck gave birth to his mother.
gemini_interpretation: Over-familiarity can lead to disrespect and the fabrication of false claims to diminish another's status.
mistral_translation: I thought the rope was a snake; it said it was a millipede that gave birth to it
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights how misjudgments can arise from fear or misunderstanding, leading to absurd or exaggerated conclusions.
llama_translation: We asked the tortoise about its mother; it said its mother was a snail.
llama_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one's origin or background can influence their behavior or characteristics.

yoruba: À ḿbáni mú adìẹ à ńforúnkún bó; bọ́wọ́ bá ba òkókó, a ò ní fún aládìẹ?
english_literal: One helps to catch a chicken and scrapes one's knees; having laid one's hands on the chick will one not hand it over to the owner?
interpretation_gold: One should not be overzealous in helping others, especially when no benefit will accrue to one from the effort.
deepseek_translation: When we catch the chicken, we rejoice loudly; if the hawk catches it, won't we give it to the owner of the chicken?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against premature celebration over gains that may not be secure or rightfully yours.
claude_translation: We help someone catch a chicken and we cover it with a basket; if our hand touches the chicken, won't we give it to the chicken owner?
claude_interpretation: When you help someone accomplish a task, you deserve some recognition or benefit from your contribution.
gemini_translation: We are helping to catch a chicken, and we are kneeling; if our hands touch the chick, won't we give it to the chicken owner?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the temptation to take advantage of a situation when given an opportunity, even if it means betraying trust or acting against the common good.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We are helping to catch a chicken, and we are kneeling; if our hands touch the chick, won't we give it to the chicken owner?", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the temptation to take advantage of a situation when given an opportunity, even if it means betraying trust or acting against the common good."}
mistral_translation: If I hold a chicken and it is puffing up its neck feathers; if the neck were a wooden pestle, would we not give it to the chicken owner?
mistral_interpretation: One should not take responsibility for problems caused by someone else's property or actions.
llama_translation: We are asking the chicken to take care of the eggs; if the chicken is careless, who will take care of the eggs?
llama_interpretation: One should be mindful of the responsibility entrusted to them, lest they compromise the very thing they are supposed to protect.

yoruba: Ajá ò gbọdọ̀ dé mọ́ṣáláṣí ìkókò ṣàlùwàlá.
english_literal: A dog dares not go to a wolf's mosque to make ablutions.
interpretation_gold: One should not exceed one's station.
deepseek_translation: The dog does not reach the market square without a reason.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that every action has a purpose or motive behind it.
claude_translation: A dog must not reach the mosque's cooking pot carelessly
claude_interpretation: One should not approach sacred or important places without proper respect and caution.
gemini_translation: A dog must not perform ablution with a cooking pot.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to use sacred or valuable items for mundane or disrespectful purposes.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A dog must not perform ablution with a cooking pot.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate to use sacred or valuable items for mundane or disrespectful purposes."}
mistral_translation: A dog must not arrive at the same time as the soup ladle on the pot's lid.
mistral_interpretation: One should avoid being present or involved in situations where their presence could lead to suspicion or trouble.
llama_translation: A dog does not enter the house of a Moslem to eat the meat of a cow.
llama_interpretation: One should not intrude into a situation where they are not welcome or do not belong.

yoruba: Àfòpiná tó fẹ́ paná-a súyà: ẹrán pọ̀ sí i.
english_literal: The moth (that) tries to put out the barbecue fire: the meat becomes more plentiful.
interpretation_gold: A person who foolishly attempts dangerous tasks courts destruction.
deepseek_translation: The stubborn fly that wants to die: the fire is hot.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against stubbornness in the face of obvious danger.
claude_translation: The fire-blower who wants to extinguish the suya fire: there is more meat on it.
claude_interpretation: One should not destroy something that still has value or potential benefit remaining.
gemini_translation: The fire extinguisher that wants to put out a suya fire: there is more meat in it.
gemini_interpretation: Attempting to solve a problem with an inadequate solution will only exacerbate the issue.
mistral_translation: The firewood that wants to roast meat: the meat is too much for it.
mistral_interpretation: One should not take on more than they can handle or manage effectively.
llama_translation: The one who is afraid of a palm tree will not get a palm kernel: a coward will not get meat.
llama_interpretation: One must be brave and take risks to achieve success or gain rewards.

yoruba: Àgbéré laáyán gbé tó ní òun ó jòó láàárín adìẹ.
english_literal: The cockroach overreaches itself when it says it will dance in the company of chickens.
interpretation_gold: The chickens will eagerly peck it to death.
deepseek_translation: The millipede is long but it says it will dance among the chickens.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against overconfidence or underestimating challenges despite one's abilities.
claude_translation: The hawk that perched and said it would sit peacefully among the chickens
claude_interpretation: A predator cannot claim to have peaceful intentions among its natural prey, as one's true nature will eventually reveal itself.
gemini_translation: It is foolishness that the cockroach exhibits when it says it will dance among chickens.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish and dangerous to put oneself in a situation where one is clearly at a disadvantage or in danger.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It is foolishness that the cockroach exhibits when it says it will dance among chickens.", "interpretation": "It is foolish and dangerous to put oneself in a situation where one is clearly at a disadvantage or in danger."}
mistral_translation: It is the lame-legged one who boasts that he will dance in the midst of chickens
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns against overconfidence or boasting about one's ability to succeed where others are clearly more capable or better suited.
llama_translation: The one who is carrying a load on his head is the one who knows its weight in the middle of the night.
llama_interpretation: Only the person experiencing a problem truly understands its severity.

yoruba: A kì í pe ìyàwó kó kan alárẹnà.
english_literal: One does not summon the wife and so involve the go-between.
interpretation_gold: People should mind their own business.
deepseek_translation: We do not call a bride to share the burden of the carrier.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not involve inexperienced or unprepared individuals in difficult tasks.
claude_translation: We do not call a wife to touch/handle a leper
claude_interpretation: One should not expose loved ones to danger or harmful situations that could bring them harm.
gemini_translation: One does not call the bride and it concerns the matchmaker.
gemini_interpretation: One should not interfere in matters that do not directly concern them.
mistral_translation: We do not call a bride to light the way for a visitor.
mistral_interpretation: It is improper to assign a new bride tasks that should be handled by others, as she should be respected and not burdened.
llama_translation: One does not call the wife to join the husband's creditor.
llama_interpretation: A person's personal problems should not be imposed on their partner or family.

yoruba: A-ṣúra-mú ò tẹ́ bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: A person who is mindful of his/her image is not easily disgraced.
interpretation_gold: People take one as one presents oneself.
deepseek_translation: The one who acts hastily does not reach the market.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the importance of patience and careful planning to achieve success.
claude_translation: One who takes without permission does not step on soap
claude_interpretation: A thief or dishonest person cannot afford to be careless or slip up, as they must always be cautious to avoid being caught.
gemini_translation: One who is careful does not fall into a ditch.
gemini_interpretation: Carefulness and foresight prevent one from encountering misfortune or problems.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who is careful does not fall into a ditch.", "interpretation": "Carefulness and foresight prevent one from encountering misfortune or problems."}
mistral_translation: The one who gathers ants does not step on a millipede
mistral_interpretation: Being cautious in one's actions prevents unexpected harm or trouble
llama_translation: The one who is not present does not get a share of the meat.
llama_interpretation: Those who are absent or not actively involved will not benefit from the opportunities or rewards.

yoruba: A kì í dákẹ́ ká ṣìwí; a kì í wò sùn-ùn ká dáràn.
english_literal: One does not keep quiet and yet misspeak; one does not silently contemplate the world and yet get into trouble.
interpretation_gold: A careful and cautious person seldom gets into trouble.
deepseek_translation: One does not keep quiet and speak; one does not look at a trap and get caught.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that actions have consequences and one cannot engage in contradictory or dangerous behavior without facing the inevitable outcome.
claude_translation: We do not keep quiet and become foolish; we do not look at sleep and become wicked.
claude_interpretation: One should not remain silent when action is needed, nor should one be idle when there is work to be done.
gemini_translation: One does not keep silent and then accuse; one does not watch quietly and then commit a crime.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of speaking up against wrongdoing when it occurs, as silence can be interpreted as complicity or lead to future accusations.
mistral_translation: One does not keep quiet to speak; one does not sleep soundly to snore.
mistral_interpretation: Actions or words should serve a purpose rather than being done carelessly or without thought.
llama_translation: We don't use a knife to cut a yam; we don't use a razor to shave a calabash.
llama_interpretation: One should use the right tool or approach for a task to achieve the desired result.

yoruba: Àjàpá ní òun tí ìbá só ló sùn yí, bẹ́ẹ̀ni ẹní bá sùn kì í só.
english_literal: Tortoise argues that it that might have farted is sound asleep, and, surely, those that sleep do not fart!
interpretation_gold: Some defenses are so transparent as to be frivolous.
deepseek_translation: The tortoise says that whoever sleeps next to it will not wake up, and indeed whoever sleeps does not wake.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns about associating with deceitful people, as their negative traits may influence or harm you.
claude_translation: The tortoise says if it had spoken, it would have slept this way, likewise whoever sleeps does not speak
claude_interpretation: It is better to remain silent and avoid trouble than to speak carelessly and face consequences.
gemini_translation: Tortoise said that what he would have done, he slept over it, and indeed, whoever sleeps does not do.
gemini_interpretation: Procrastination, like sleeping instead of acting, prevents one from achieving their goals.
mistral_translation: It is the tortoise who said that if he had been the one to roll over in his sleep, likewise anyone who sleeps does not roll over
mistral_interpretation: One should not blame others for faults they themselves are guilty of or make excuses for their own shortcomings.
llama_translation: The leopard is the one whose spots are on its body, if someone else has spots, it is not the leopard's
llama_interpretation: One's true identity cannot be taken by another, no matter how similar they may appear.

yoruba: A kì í ní agbára kékeré ṣe èkejì.
english_literal: One does not offer to second a combatant in spite of one's negligible strength.
interpretation_gold: Never attempt more than you have the power to accomplish.
deepseek_translation: We do not have small strength as a second option.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that even small efforts or resources should not be underestimated or dismissed as secondary.
claude_translation: One does not have little strength to be second
claude_interpretation: Being in second place or a supporting role still requires significant strength and capability.
gemini_translation: One does not have little strength to do a second thing.
gemini_interpretation: It is difficult to undertake a second task when one's resources or energy are already depleted from the first.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not have little strength to do a second thing.", "interpretation": "It is difficult to undertake a second task when one's resources or energy are already depleted from the first."}
mistral_translation: One does not have small strength and be second.
mistral_interpretation: True ability or strength is demonstrated by one's ability to lead or excel, not just participate.
llama_translation: We do not have the power to make a second heaven
llama_interpretation: One should be content with what they have and not try to recreate or surpass what is already perfect.

yoruba: Ajá kì í lọ ságinjù lọ ṣọdẹ ẹkùn.
english_literal: A dog does not go into the wild to hunt a leopard.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt feats one is unqualified to accomplish.
deepseek_translation: A dog does not go beyond the hunter's leash.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches the importance of knowing one's limits and respecting boundaries.
claude_translation: A dog does not go into the deep forest to hunt leopards
claude_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks that are far beyond their capabilities or venture into situations where they are clearly outmatched.
gemini_translation: A dog does not go to the jungle to hunt a leopard.
gemini_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks that are beyond their capabilities or inherently dangerous for them.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A dog does not go to the jungle to hunt a leopard.", "interpretation": "One should not attempt tasks that are beyond their capabilities or inherently dangerous for them."}
mistral_translation: A dog does not go hunting recklessly where a leopard hunts
mistral_interpretation: One should avoid unnecessary competition or confrontation with those far stronger or more capable
llama_translation: A dog does not go to the forest to play with a leopard.
llama_interpretation: One should not engage in a confrontation or competition with someone who is more powerful or formidable.

yoruba: A kì í ní ọ̀kánjúwà ká mọ̀; ará ilé ẹni ní ńsọ fúnni.
english_literal: One does not know that one has covetousness; it is one's kin who so inform one.
interpretation_gold: Often, only those close to one can recognize one's flaws and alert one to them.
deepseek_translation: One does not have foresight and still be ignorant; it is one's household members that inform one.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of heeding advice from those close to you, as they often have your best interests at heart.
claude_translation: One does not have a spy to know; it is one's own household members who tell on one
claude_interpretation: Betrayal and exposure of secrets often come from those closest to us, not from outsiders or enemies.
gemini_translation: One does not know they are greedy; it is one's family members who tell one.
gemini_interpretation: People are often unaware of their own flaws, and it is those closest to them who can provide honest feedback.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not know they are greedy; it is one's family members who tell one.", "interpretation": "People are often unaware of their own flaws, and it is those closest to them who can provide honest feedback."}
mistral_translation: We do not have haste to know; it is one's own family member that lies for one.
mistral_interpretation: People often deceive or mislead those closest to them, rather than strangers.
llama_translation: We do not know the sorrow of the heart; it is the owner of the house who knows the one who is suffering
llama_interpretation: Only the person experiencing a problem truly understands its depth and complexity.

yoruba: Àjàpá ńlọ sájò, wọ́n ní ìgbà wo ni yó dèé, ó ní ó dìgbàtí òún bá tẹ́.
english_literal: Tortoise set out on a journey and it was asked when it would return; it replied that it would be after it had earned disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Certain people will not change course until they are disgraced.
deepseek_translation: Tortoise is going on a journey, they asked when he will arrive, he said it is when he gets there.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches patience and the understanding that some things cannot be rushed or predicted.
claude_translation: Tortoise is going to market, they asked when he will arrive, he said he will arrive when he steps there.
claude_interpretation: One should focus on taking action and making progress rather than making promises about timing or outcomes.
gemini_translation: Tortoise is going on a journey, they asked when he would return, he said he would return when he is disgraced.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that some individuals are so stubborn or set in their ways that they will only change or return from a path when faced with significant failure or humiliation.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Tortoise is going on a journey, they asked when he would return, he said he would return when he is disgraced.", "interpretation": "This proverb suggests that some individuals are so stubborn or set in their ways that they will only change or return from a path when faced with significant failure or humiliation."}
mistral_translation: The tortoise was going to the market, they asked when he would return, he said he would return when he stepped on something
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that some people avoid giving direct answers or commitments to avoid accountability.
llama_translation: The tortoise is going to the market, they asked him when he would return, he said when his buttocks would be cool
llama_interpretation: One should not rush to make promises or set deadlines without considering one's own limitations or circumstances.

yoruba: Afọ́jú tó dijú, tó ní òún sùn, ìgbàtí kò sùn ta ló rí?
english_literal: The blind person who shuts his eyes and says he is asleep, when he was not asleep whom did he see?
interpretation_gold: The deceiver deceives him/herself.
deepseek_translation: The blind person who claims to sleep, when they did not sleep, who saw them?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against pretending to have knowledge or experience one does not actually possess, as the truth will eventually be revealed.
claude_translation: A blind person who opens their eyes and says they are sleeping, what did they see when they were not sleeping?
claude_interpretation: This proverb exposes the contradiction in someone's false claims by questioning their ability to make such claims given their obvious limitations.
gemini_translation: The blind person who closed their eyes and claimed to be asleep, when they were not asleep, who saw them?
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to pretend to be something you are not, especially when the pretense is easily exposed or irrelevant to your true condition.
mistral_translation: The blind person who is in darkness, who claims to be sleeping, when he did not sleep, what did he see?
mistral_interpretation: A person who pretends to be ignorant or unaware cannot truly claim to have missed what happened.
llama_translation: A cloth that is not worn, that has not been washed, when will it get worn out?
llama_interpretation: One cannot experience the consequences of a situation they have not been in.

yoruba: Amùrín ò sunwọ̀n, ó yí sáró.
english_literal: The lizard is not good-looking to start with, and it slips into indigo dye.
interpretation_gold: A person who has enough flaws should not seek ways to add to them.
deepseek_translation: The one who does not sleep well turns around constantly.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that lack of proper rest leads to discomfort and unrest in one's life.
claude_translation: The mute person is not beautiful, he turned to madness.
claude_interpretation: When someone cannot express themselves or communicate effectively, it can lead to frustration and irrational behavior.
gemini_translation: The chameleon is not beautiful, it has turned blue.
gemini_interpretation: Appearances can be deceiving, as something that seems unattractive might simply be in a temporary state or perceived differently.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The chameleon is not beautiful, it has turned blue.", "interpretation": "Appearances can be deceiving, as something that seems unattractive might simply be in a temporary state or perceived differently."}
mistral_translation: The palm kernel does not become round, it turns into a calabash.
mistral_interpretation: Change or transformation is a natural process, and one should adapt to new circumstances rather than resist them.
llama_translation: The one who is not patient will not eat ripe fruit.
llama_interpretation: Patience is necessary to achieve desired outcomes.

yoruba: Aáyán ati eèràá ṣígun, wọ́n ní àwọ́n ńlọ mú adìẹ àlọ la rí, a ò rábọ̀.
english_literal: Cockroach and ant make ready for war and say they are off to capture chicken; we see their departure, but not their return.
interpretation_gold: Never forget your limitations.
deepseek_translation: The spider and the ant went to war, they said they were going to bring the hen without feathers, we did not see them.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against engaging in futile conflicts that yield no tangible results.
claude_translation: The cockroach and the ant went to war, they said they were going to capture the chicken but we saw them return without success.
claude_interpretation: Small or weak entities should not attempt tasks that are clearly beyond their capabilities, as they will inevitably fail.
gemini_translation: The cockroach and the ant went to war, they said they were going to catch a chicken. We saw them go, we did not see them return.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb warns against embarking on a task that is clearly beyond one's capabilities, as it will likely lead to failure or disappearance.
mistral_translation: The squirrel and the ground squirrel fought, they said they were going to catch a wild chicken, but we did not see any sacrifice
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the futility of making grand plans without taking the necessary steps or preparations to achieve them.
llama_translation: The tortoise and the lizard are friends, they said they are going to the farm to meet the hen, but they did not meet.
llama_interpretation: This proverb teaches that some friendships are based on ulterior motives or hidden agendas.

yoruba: Ajá mọ ìgbẹ́; ẹlẹ́dẹ̀-ẹ́ mọ àfọ̀; tòlótòló mọ ẹni tí yó yìnbọn ìdí sí.
english_literal: A dog knows excrement; a pig knows a mud pit; a turkey knows to whom to direct its fart.
interpretation_gold: People should know who are their peers and who are not.
deepseek_translation: The dog knows the bush; the pig knows the mud; the turkey knows who will twist its tail.
deepseek_interpretation: Each creature understands its own environment and potential threats.
claude_translation: The dog knows the forest; the pig knows the muddy place; the turkey knows who will pluck its tail feathers.
claude_interpretation: Every creature instinctively knows its natural environment and the dangers that threaten it.
gemini_translation: The dog knows the bush; the pig knows the muddy wallow; the turkey knows who will shoot its behind.
gemini_interpretation: Each creature, and by extension each person, instinctively understands its own environment, needs, or potential threats.
mistral_translation: The dog knows the bush; the pig knows the swamp; the turkey knows who will tie its anus.
mistral_interpretation: Each individual understands their own circumstances and challenges best.
llama_translation: The dog knows the bush; the lizard knows the rock; the tortoise knows the one who has pounded its head.
llama_interpretation: Everyone knows their own troubles and challenges best.

yoruba: Aláṣejù tí ńpọkọ ní baba.
english_literal: Overzealous wife that calls her husband “father.”
interpretation_gold: The wife who calls her husband “father” carries respect beyond reasonable limits; one should not be overzealous in one's observance of proprieties.
deepseek_translation: The one who excessively gathers is the father of lack.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against greed and hoarding, as it ultimately leads to scarcity and loss.
claude_translation: The one who does too much calls a hunchback father
claude_interpretation: Excessive behavior or going overboard in actions leads to undesirable consequences or associations.
gemini_translation: The one who overdoes it calls the penis 'father'.
gemini_interpretation: Excessive flattery or subservience, often for personal gain, can lead to undignified behavior.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who overdoes it calls the penis 'father'.", "interpretation": "Excessive flattery or subservience, often for personal gain, can lead to undignified behavior."}
mistral_translation: The one who is too much in a hurry ends up as a stepfather.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive haste or impatience can lead to unfavorable or unintended consequences.
llama_translation: The one who is lazy will meet his father
llama_interpretation: One's laziness will ultimately lead to a confrontation with the consequences of one's actions.

yoruba: Alákòró kì í sá fógun.
english_literal: A wearer of a battle-helmet does not flee from war.
interpretation_gold: A warrior does not run from battle.
deepseek_translation: The owner of the corn does not run from the cornfield.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not fear or avoid responsibilities tied to their possessions or roles.
claude_translation: A leper does not run for twenty years
claude_interpretation: Someone with limitations or disabilities cannot sustain strenuous activities for extended periods.
gemini_translation: The one who wears the akoro (a type of crown/headgear) does not run from war.
gemini_interpretation: Those in positions of leadership or responsibility are expected to face challenges and fulfill their duties with courage.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who wears the akoro (a type of crown/headgear) does not run from war.", "interpretation": "Those in positions of leadership or responsibility are expected to face challenges and fulfill their duties with courage."}
mistral_translation: The cripple does not run from a war medicine (charm).
mistral_interpretation: One should not avoid challenges or responsibilities simply because they seem difficult or beyond one's ability.
llama_translation: The drummer does not get burned by the fire.
llama_interpretation: One who is skilled in their profession or familiar with a situation is unlikely to be harmed by it.

yoruba: Afínjú-u póńpólà, ogé kun osùn láìwẹ.
english_literal: Unusual-fashionable-person, the preener anoints herself with camwood without taking a bath.
interpretation_gold: Cleanliness should be more than a matter of appearance.
deepseek_translation: The blind man carries a heavy load, the vulture perches on the soap.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony and imbalance in life where those who are incapable bear heavy burdens while those who could help do nothing.
claude_translation: The one who looks intently at the palm kernel, the calabash is full of camwood without washing
claude_interpretation: While focusing too intensely on small matters, one neglects more important tasks that require attention.
gemini_translation: The neat person is a dandy, the vain person applies camwood without bathing.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb criticizes superficiality, highlighting that true cleanliness and beauty come from within, not just outward appearance.
mistral_translation: The refined person is many, but elegance fills the camwood without measure
mistral_interpretation: True refinement and elegance are rare qualities, even if many claim to possess them
llama_translation: The one who is not patient will not be able to pound the yam with the mortar
llama_interpretation: Patience is necessary to achieve success in any endeavor.

yoruba: A rí èyí rí ni tonílé; a ò rí èyí rí ni tàlejò; bónílé bá ní ká jẹ ẹ́ tán, àlejò a ní ká jẹ ẹ́ kù.
english_literal: “Its likes have been seen before,” is what the host says; “No one has ever seen its likes before,” is what the guest says; if the host says that we should empty the plate, the guest should argue for leaving a little.
interpretation_gold: A host might minimize his hospitality, but the guest should praise it; if the host is lavish, the guest should not be greedy.
deepseek_translation: What we see at home is for today; what we don't see is for visitors; if the household says we should finish it, visitors will say we should leave some.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches the importance of hospitality and saving resources for unexpected guests.
claude_translation: We have seen this and that says the host; we have not seen this and that says the guest; if the host says let us finish it all, the guest will say let us leave some remaining.
claude_interpretation: Hosts and guests have different perspectives and interests, with hosts being more generous while guests tend to be more conservative about consumption.
gemini_translation: What the host has seen, the host says; what the guest has not seen, the guest says; if the host says we should finish eating it, the guest will say we should leave some.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the differing perspectives and priorities between a host and a guest, often due to their respective familiarity and comfort with a situation.
mistral_translation: We see what we see at home; we do not see what we see in another's house; when the host says we should finish eating it, the guest says we should leave some.
mistral_interpretation: People often judge others by different standards than they apply to themselves or their own situations.
llama_translation: We see the one at home with our eyes; we don't see the one outside with our eyes; when the one at home is eating, we join to eat; when the one outside is eating, we don't join to eat.
llama_interpretation: One should prioritize and appreciate what they have at home rather than envying or seeking what others have outside.

yoruba: A-dá-má-lè-ṣe àdàbà tí ńdún bẹ̀m̀bẹ̀.
english_literal: Start-something-it-cannot-finish dove that makes bombastic noises.
interpretation_gold: Bombast often masks fickleness.
deepseek_translation: The dove that sings softly does not fall.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that humility and gentleness prevent downfall.
claude_translation: The one who fails to do good is like a dove that sounds sweet
claude_interpretation: Someone who appears gentle or pleasant but fails to act righteously is deceptive, as true goodness requires both good appearance and good deeds.
gemini_translation: The one who promises but fails to deliver is like the dove that coos 'bèm̀bè'.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb criticizes those who make promises they do not keep, comparing their empty words to the repetitive, unfulfilled sound of a dove's coo.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who promises but fails to deliver is like the dove that coos 'bèm̀bè'.", "interpretation": "This proverb criticizes those who make promises they do not keep, comparing their empty words to the repetitive, unfulfilled sound of a dove's coo."}
mistral_translation: The farmer does not eat the pigeon that coos sweetly
mistral_interpretation: One should not destroy or consume what brings joy or value, even if it seems tempting or harmless
llama_translation: One who does not know how to dance will say the drum is bad.
llama_interpretation: It highlights the tendency to blame external circumstances for one's own incompetence or lack of skill.

yoruba: Àgó tó gbó ṣáṣá, ẹ̀bìtí pa á, áḿbọ̀sì olóósè a-bara-kùọ̀kùọ̀.
english_literal: The nimble, sprightly rat fell victim to the trap, how much more the sluggish, sickly mouse.
interpretation_gold: If the green wood is consumed, the dry wood has no prayer.
deepseek_translation: The trap that makes noise suddenly, the rat kills it, the silent trap of the hunter catches plenty.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the value of silence and discretion in achieving success, contrasting noisy failure with quiet effectiveness.
claude_translation: The bell that rang clearly, rust killed it, the ambassador of the owner who touches here and there.
claude_interpretation: Even things that once functioned well can deteriorate through neglect, and those who meddle in everything may contribute to such decline.
gemini_translation: A basket that is old and worn out, a trap catches it, let alone the one with a weak body.
gemini_interpretation: If something strong and resilient can fall victim to a challenge, then something inherently weak or vulnerable stands no chance.
mistral_translation: The debt that roars loudly, the creditor kills it, but the debtor who keeps dodging remains unharmed
mistral_interpretation: A problem openly confronted is resolved, while one avoided through evasion persists without consequence for the evader
llama_translation: A drum that sounds loudly, the drummer breaks it, yet the drummer is not tired of beating.
llama_interpretation: One should not be deterred by obstacles or setbacks in pursuing a goal or activity.

yoruba: Àpárá ńlá nikán ńdá; ikán ò lè mu òkúta.
english_literal: The termite is being most overbearing; a termite cannot eat a rock.
interpretation_gold: Certain people do not know their place; certain people are beyond the reach of their adversaries.
deepseek_translation: Only the big squirrel digs; the squirrel cannot carry a stone.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not attempt tasks beyond their capability.
claude_translation: Only a big machete can cut; a small one cannot break a stone.
claude_interpretation: Difficult tasks require adequate tools and strength, as insufficient resources cannot accomplish challenging goals.
gemini_translation: Only the big termite mound stands; termites cannot consume a stone.
gemini_interpretation: Some things are inherently resistant to decay or destruction, just as termites cannot destroy a stone.
mistral_translation: Only a big stone cracks; a single ant cannot move a rock
mistral_interpretation: Strength or success often comes from collective effort rather than individual struggle
llama_translation: A large calabash does not break itself; it is the stone that breaks it.
llama_interpretation: External factors can cause the downfall of even the strongest among us.

yoruba: À ḿbẹ̀rù alájá, ajá ṣebí òun là ḿbẹ̀rù.
english_literal: One shows deference to the dog's owner, and the dog thinks the deference is to it.
interpretation_gold: A person who has a powerful patron mistakenly believes that the respect he enjoys from others is due to his or her own qualities, whereas it is reflected from the patron.
deepseek_translation: He who fears the dog, the dog barks as if he is the one it fears.
deepseek_interpretation: Fear often attracts the very thing one is afraid of.
claude_translation: We fear the dog owner, but the dog thinks it is the one we fear
claude_interpretation: People often mistake the respect or fear shown to their superiors as being directed at themselves personally.
gemini_translation: We fear the dog owner, the dog thinks it is him we fear.
gemini_interpretation: People often misinterpret the source of respect or fear directed towards them, believing it is due to their own power rather than the influence of those associated with them.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We fear the dog owner, the dog thinks it is him we fear.", "interpretation": "People often misinterpret the source of respect or fear directed towards them, believing it is due to their own power rather than the influence of those associated with them."}
mistral_translation: If I fear the dog's owner, the dog itself claims I fear it.
mistral_interpretation: People often misinterpret your caution towards a powerful figure as fear of them, even when they are not the primary concern.
llama_translation: We are looking for the owner of the dog, the dog is looking at its owner.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the absurdity of searching for something that is already present or obvious.

yoruba: Aaka ò gbé ọ̀dàn; igbó ní ńgbé.
english_literal: The hedgehog does not live in the grassland, only in the forest.
interpretation_gold: Certain things are proper; certain things are not.
deepseek_translation: The crab does not inhabit the grassland; the forest is its home.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that everyone has their natural place or role where they truly belong.
claude_translation: The hoe does not live in the open field; it lives in the forest.
claude_interpretation: Tools and resources belong in their proper place of storage and care, not left abandoned where they are used.
gemini_translation: The aardvark does not live in the savanna; it lives in the forest.
gemini_interpretation: One should not expect someone to be in a place or situation that is not natural or suitable for them.
mistral_translation: The hawk does not perch in the savannah; it perches in the forest.
mistral_interpretation: People naturally gravitate toward environments or situations that suit their nature or abilities.
llama_translation: The stick does not support the load; the forest supports it.
llama_interpretation: Collective effort is more effective than individual strength.

yoruba: Àgbà tí kò mọ ìwọ̀n ara-a rẹ̀ lodò ńgbé lọ́.
english_literal: It is an elder who does not know his limitations that is washed away by a river.
interpretation_gold: Elders who cannot swim will be cautious near rivers.
deepseek_translation: An elder who does not know the size of his body is the one the river carries away.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that lack of self-awareness or overestimating one's abilities can lead to downfall.
claude_translation: An elder who does not know their own measure is what the river carries away.
claude_interpretation: Those who lack self-awareness and overestimate their abilities will face consequences or downfall.
gemini_translation: An elder who does not know their own measure is carried away by the river.
gemini_interpretation: It is important for individuals, especially those in positions of authority, to understand their limitations and capabilities to avoid detrimental consequences.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An elder who does not know their own measure is carried away by the river.", "interpretation": "It is important for individuals, especially those in positions of authority, to understand their limitations and capabilities to avoid detrimental consequences."}
mistral_translation: An elder who does not know the measure of his own strength is carried away by the river.
mistral_interpretation: Overconfidence or lack of self-awareness, especially in elders, can lead to failure or downfall.
llama_translation: An elder who does not know the way will ask a child to lead the way
llama_interpretation: It is okay to seek guidance from someone younger or less experienced if it means finding the right path.

yoruba: A kì í bẹ̀rù ikú bẹ̀rù àrùn ká ní kí ọmọ ó kú sinni.
english_literal: One does not so fear death and disease that one asks that one's child die before one.
interpretation_gold: One should not be more concerned with saving oneself than with saving one's dependents.
deepseek_translation: One does not fear death, fear illness so that the child does not die in sleep.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that neglecting health (a preventable issue) is more dangerous than fearing inevitable death.
claude_translation: We do not fear death and fear sickness only to let a child die in the grave.
claude_interpretation: It is contradictory to worry about lesser dangers while allowing greater harm to occur to those we should protect most.
gemini_translation: One does not fear death and fear sickness and then wish for a child to die and bury them.
gemini_interpretation: It is contradictory to fear death and sickness while simultaneously wishing for a child to die before oneself, as children are expected to bury their parents.
mistral_translation: We do not fear death and fear sickness only to wish our child dies before us.
mistral_interpretation: It is hypocritical to fear misfortune yet wish it upon others, especially one's own children.
llama_translation: We do not mourn death, we mourn illness so that the child does not die in vain.
llama_interpretation: It is the suffering and pain caused by illness that is mourned, not the death itself, as death is a natural part of life.

yoruba: A kì í fi ìka ro etí, ká fi ro imú, ká wá tún fi ta ehín.
english_literal: One does not use one's finger to clean one's ear passages, use it to pick one's nose, and then use it to pick one's teeth.
interpretation_gold: One should always behave with decorum.
deepseek_translation: We do not use a finger to clean the ear, then use it to clean the nose, and then use it again to crack the teeth.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against reusing the same solution for different problems, as it may lead to unintended consequences.
claude_translation: One does not use the finger to pick the ear, then use it to pick the nose, and then use it to pick the teeth.
claude_interpretation: Maintain proper hygiene and cleanliness by not transferring dirt or germs from one part of the body to another.
gemini_translation: One does not use a finger to clean the ear, then use it to clean the nose, and then use it to pick the teeth.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to maintain proper hygiene and avoid cross-contamination, especially when dealing with different body parts.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not use a finger to clean the ear, then use it to clean the nose, and then use it to pick the teeth.", "interpretation": "It is important to maintain proper hygiene and avoid cross-contamination, especially when dealing with different body parts."}
mistral_translation: We do not use wickedness to scratch the ear, then use it to scratch the nose, and then try to use it to lick the teeth
mistral_interpretation: One should not use harmful or deceitful means to solve problems, as it will eventually backfire or harm oneself.
llama_translation: We do not use a cutlass to cut a tree, we use it to cut the head, and we come to use it to cut the tail.
llama_interpretation: One should use the right tool or approach for the task at hand to avoid unnecessary complications.

yoruba: Àgbéré lẹyẹ ńgbé; kò lè mu omi inú àgbọn
english_literal: The bird only attempts the impossible; it cannot drink the milk in a coconut.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limits.
deepseek_translation: The chicken is dancing; it cannot drink the water in the calabash
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against engaging in futile efforts or distractions that do not lead to meaningful results.
claude_translation: The hornbill lives in luxury; it cannot drink water from inside a coconut
claude_interpretation: Despite having advantages or status, some people lack the practical skills to access basic necessities or opportunities available to them.
gemini_translation: The bird lives in the air; it cannot drink the water inside the coconut.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot achieve what is beyond their natural capabilities or reach.
mistral_translation: The bird perches on the raffia palm; it cannot drink water from the coconut
mistral_interpretation: One should recognize their limitations and not attempt what is beyond their capacity or nature.
llama_translation: The calabash floats on the surface; it cannot drink water from the bottom
llama_interpretation: One cannot benefit from an opportunity if they are not fully immersed or committed to it.

yoruba: À ńjá ìbàǹtẹ́ ẹ̀ lẹ́hìn, ó ńjá tará iwájú.
english_literal: His loincloth is being stripped from behind, yet he is stripping those of the people ahead of him.
interpretation_gold: Attacks on him do not stop him from belaboring his enemies.
deepseek_translation: While wrestling the mat from behind, it is wrestling itself in front.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against focusing on minor issues while neglecting more significant problems that require attention.
claude_translation: We are fighting the battle behind, while fighting the battle in front.
claude_interpretation: One cannot effectively handle multiple conflicts or challenges simultaneously from different directions.
gemini_translation: One is tearing his loincloth from behind, he is tearing the one in front.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who is oblivious to their own self-destructive actions while focusing on external matters.
mistral_translation: One fights the back's scar today, and fights the front's scar tomorrow
mistral_interpretation: People often repeat the same mistakes or conflicts without learning from past experiences.
llama_translation: We are running in the backyard, he is running in the front yard.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the difference in pace and progress between those who are proactive and those who are reactive.

yoruba: Àpọ́nlé ni “İyá-a Káà”; ìyá kan ò sí ní káà tí kò lórúkọ.
english_literal: Calling a person “Mother of the Compound” is only a mark of respect; there is no mother in the compound who does not have a name.
interpretation_gold: People in a position of respect should not forget that respect can be withdrawn.
deepseek_translation: The floor mat is called "Mother Káà"; there is no mother called Káà that does not have a name.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that everything has its own identity and purpose, even if it seems insignificant.
claude_translation: It is a nickname that 'Mother So-and-so'; there is no mother in the neighborhood who does not have a name.
claude_interpretation: Every person, no matter how they may be casually referred to, has their own distinct identity and proper name that deserves recognition.
gemini_translation: Praise name is 'Mother of the Káà'; there is no mother in the Káà who has no name.
gemini_interpretation: Every individual, regardless of their status or role, possesses a unique identity and significance.
mistral_translation: The bag of the mother is 'Let's go home'; there is no mother in the town square who does not have a name
mistral_interpretation: Every person, no matter how seemingly insignificant, has a distinct identity and purpose.
llama_translation: The one who is called 'Mother of the Kite' is not the one who has a kite; it is the one whose name is Kite.
llama_interpretation: A person's reputation or name can be misleading, as it may not reflect their true nature or circumstances.

yoruba: A gbé gàárì ọmọ ewurẹ ńrojú; kì í ṣe ẹrù àgùntàn.
english_literal: We lift a saddle and the goat (kin) scowls; it is no burden for a sheep.
interpretation_gold: The goat has no cause to scowl, because no one will condescend to ride it anyway.
deepseek_translation: The goat's child carries garri on its head; it is not the sheep's load.
deepseek_interpretation: Each person has their own responsibilities and burdens to bear.
claude_translation: We carry cassava flour, the young goat is hopeful; it is not the load of a sheep.
claude_interpretation: People often have misplaced expectations or hopes about situations that don't actually concern them or benefit them.
gemini_translation: We carry the kid of a goat and it complains; it is not the burden of a sheep.
gemini_interpretation: Some people complain about minor tasks, while others endure much greater burdens without complaint.
mistral_translation: One carries gari on the head of a goat's child; it is not the burden of a sheep
mistral_interpretation: The responsibility or burden one carries should be appropriate for the individual's capacity or status, not imposed unfairly.
llama_translation: We carry the load of a goat's child on our head; it is not the load of a leopard's child.
llama_interpretation: One should not take on a burden that is beyond their capacity or strength.

yoruba: Àjàpá ní kò sí oun tó dà bí oun tí a mọ̀ ọ́ṣe; ó ní bí òún bá ju ẹyìn sẹ́nu, òun a tu èkùrọ́ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: Tortoise says there is nothing quite like expertise in one's calling; it says if it puts a palm-fruit into its mouth, it spits out a palm-nut.
interpretation_gold: Nothing succeeds like expertise.
deepseek_translation: The tortoise says there is nothing as good as what he knows; he says if he puts more than a palm nut in his mouth, he will spit out the kernel.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the value of contentment and knowing one's limits.
claude_translation: The tortoise says there is nothing as good as what one knows how to do; he says if he throws his back into his mouth, he will release palm kernel oil.
claude_interpretation: Everyone should focus on and take pride in their own unique skills and abilities rather than envying others.
gemini_translation: Àjàpá (Tortoise) says there is nothing like what one knows how to do; he says if he throws a palm kernel into his mouth, he will spit out the palm kernel shell.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the value of expertise and skill, suggesting that one's proficiency in a particular task makes it seem effortless and effective.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Àjàpá (Tortoise) says there is nothing like what one knows how to do; he says if he throws a palm kernel into his mouth, he will spit out the palm kernel shell.", "interpretation": "The proverb emphasizes the value of expertise and skill, suggesting that one's proficiency in a particular task makes it seem effortless and effective."}
mistral_translation: The tortoise says there is no one like him who knows how to perform rituals; he says if he surpasses the snail in entering its shell, he will leave the kernel behind.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against overestimating one's abilities while underestimating others, as pride can lead to failure.
llama_translation: The tortoise does not have a mate as big as the one we know; if it grows bigger than its shell, it will break its back.
llama_interpretation: One should not overextend oneself beyond one's capabilities.

yoruba: Àgbà kì í ṣorò bí èwe.
english_literal: An elderly person does not perform rituals like a youth.
interpretation_gold: The elder's performance should be commensurate with his station and status.
deepseek_translation: An elder does not speak like a youth.
deepseek_interpretation: It teaches that elders are expected to be more thoughtful, measured, and wise in their speech than the young.
deepseek_raw: {"translation": "An elder does not speak like a youth.", "interpretation": "It teaches that elders are expected to be more thoughtful, measured, and wise in their speech than the young."}
claude_translation: An elder does not speak like a child.
claude_interpretation: Maturity and experience should be reflected in one's speech and behavior, with elders expected to demonstrate wisdom and restraint in their words.
gemini_translation: An elder does not behave like a youth.
gemini_interpretation: Elders are expected to exhibit maturity and wisdom, unlike the impulsiveness often associated with youth.
mistral_translation: An elder does not make noise like a child.
mistral_interpretation: Elders are expected to exhibit maturity, wisdom, and composure, unlike children who may act impulsively.
llama_translation: The elder does not argue like a leaf
llama_interpretation: Respect and dignity are expected from those in positions of authority and age.

yoruba: Àgùnbánirọ̀ ní ńfojúdini.
english_literal: It is the person taller than another who shows no respect for the other.
interpretation_gold: Even in a company, each person should know his/her relative station.
deepseek_translation: The one who climbs the palm tree is the one who knows where the nuts are.
deepseek_interpretation: Experience and effort are necessary to achieve success.
claude_translation: The vulture is the one that looks downward.
claude_interpretation: Those who are always looking for opportunities to benefit from others' misfortunes or failures will naturally focus on negative situations.
gemini_translation: The one who climbs with you is the one who looks down on you.
gemini_interpretation: Those closest to you, especially those who have risen with you, are often the ones who show disrespect or disdain.
mistral_translation: It is the owner of the snail that is searching for it in the bush.
mistral_interpretation: The responsibility to find or resolve an issue lies with the person who owns or is directly affected by it.
llama_translation: The one who is patient will see the back of the problem
llama_interpretation: Patience is necessary to overcome challenges and see a resolution.

yoruba: Abùlàǹgà kì í ṣasán; bíyàá ò lọ́rọ̀, baba a lówó lọ́wọ́.
english_literal: The arrogant person is not arrogant for nothing; if his mother is not wealthy, his father must be rich.
interpretation_gold: There is, or should be, some basis for one's strutting.
deepseek_translation: The wealthy does not show off; if the child lacks money, the father has money in hand.
deepseek_interpretation: True wealth is discreet and reliable, ensuring support is available when needed.
claude_translation: A poor person does not work in vain; if the mother has no words, the father will have money in hand.
claude_interpretation: Hard work by those in need will eventually be rewarded, and when one parent cannot provide guidance or support, the other will step in with resources.
gemini_translation: A cripple is not useless; if the mother has no words, the father has money in hand.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that every individual, regardless of their perceived limitations, possesses some form of value or contribution, and that different family members can compensate for each other's shortcomings.
mistral_translation: A lazy person does not prosper; if the child does not go to the farm, the father will have money in hand.
mistral_interpretation: Hard work and personal effort are essential for success, as relying on others may not yield the desired outcome.
llama_translation: The lazy person does not have a farm; when the child is crying, the father is the one who is crying.
llama_interpretation: A person who does not take responsibility for their own life will shift the burden to others.

yoruba: Ajá tún padà sí èébì-i rẹ̀.
english_literal: The dog returns to its vomit.
interpretation_gold: To accept what one has once rejected is to lose face.
deepseek_translation: The dog has returned to its vomit.
deepseek_interpretation: It warns against reverting to old, harmful habits despite knowing better.
claude_translation: The dog returns to its vomit.
claude_interpretation: People tend to go back to their bad habits or harmful behaviors despite knowing better.
gemini_translation: The dog returns to its vomit.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who reverts to old, bad habits or behaviors they had previously abandoned.
mistral_translation: The dog has returned to its vomit.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against repeating foolish or shameful actions after having abandoned them.
llama_translation: The dog returns to its vomit.
llama_interpretation: One who has not learned from past mistakes will repeat them.

yoruba: Àì-lè-jà ni à ńsọ pé “Ojúde baba-à mi ò dé ìhín.”
english_literal: It is inability to fight that prompts one to say, “My father's front yard does not extend this far.”
interpretation_gold: A coward will find any excuse to avoid a just fight.
deepseek_translation: It is the one who cannot fight that says, "The back of my father's head does not resemble the front."
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes making excuses or blaming others when one lacks the ability or courage to face a challenge.
claude_translation: It is because one cannot fight that one says 'My father's presence did not reach here.'
claude_interpretation: People make excuses about lacking protection or support when they are actually just avoiding confrontation due to their own weakness or cowardice.
gemini_translation: It is because one cannot fight that one says, “My father’s compound does not extend this far.”
gemini_interpretation: People often use excuses or feign powerlessness to avoid confrontation or responsibility.
mistral_translation: It is laziness that makes one say 'My father's courtyard has not reached here.'
mistral_interpretation: The proverb criticizes those who make excuses instead of taking responsibility or putting in effort.
llama_translation: It is not a traveler that tells you that the road to your father's house is not good.
llama_interpretation: One should not rely on outsiders to criticize or speak ill of one's own family or heritage.

yoruba: Àfi ohun tí a kì í tà lọ́jà lẹrú kì í jẹ.
english_literal: The only thing a slave cannot eat is something not available in the market.
interpretation_gold: A slave has no choice.
deepseek_translation: Except what cannot be sold in the market, a slave does not eat.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that one must make use of every available opportunity or resource, no matter how small.
claude_translation: Except for what is not sold in the market, a slave does not eat
claude_interpretation: One must work or contribute something of value to earn their sustenance and place in society.
gemini_translation: It is only what is not sold in the market that a slave does not eat.
gemini_interpretation: A slave is deprived of everything except what is not available for purchase, highlighting their complete lack of autonomy and ownership.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It is only what is not sold in the market that a slave does not eat.", "interpretation": "A slave is deprived of everything except what is not available for purchase, highlighting their complete lack of autonomy and ownership."}
mistral_translation: Except for what is not sold in the market, a slave does not eat it.
mistral_interpretation: One should not expect or take what is not rightfully theirs or beyond their means.
