llama_translation: We do not sell what we do not have in the market of lies
llama_interpretation: One should not pretend to have what they do not possess.

yoruba: Àṣá kì í rà kádìẹ gbé kòkòrò dání.
english_literal: When a kite hovers, a chicken does not hang on to an insect.
interpretation_gold: When a great danger threatens, one does not wait for small favors.
deepseek_translation: The hawk does not buy a chicken to feed the worm.
deepseek_interpretation: One does not go out of their way to provide for those who can fend for themselves.
claude_translation: The hawk does not buy a squirrel to carry insects in its mouth.
claude_interpretation: One should not pay for something that naturally comes with what they already possess or can easily obtain.
gemini_translation: The hawk does not perch to pick up a chick while holding a worm.
gemini_interpretation: One should focus on the primary goal and not be distracted by lesser opportunities.
mistral_translation: A hawk does not buy a chicken to keep insects for itself
mistral_interpretation: One does not undertake a task solely for the benefit of another without personal gain or intention
llama_translation: A hawk does not pick up a tortoise and carry it on its head.
llama_interpretation: One should not take on a burden that is beyond one's strength or capability.

yoruba: A-binú-fùfù ní ńwá oúnjẹ fún a-binú-wẹ́rẹ́-wẹ́rẹ́.
english_literal: A volatile-tempered person secures food for a mild-tempered person.
interpretation_gold: Whatever good fortune might have been meant for the volatile person will wind up in the lot of the mild-mannered person.
deepseek_translation: The one who is angry slowly looks for food for the one who is angry quickly.
deepseek_interpretation: Patience and calmness are necessary to resolve conflicts caused by those who act hastily in anger.
claude_translation: The one who gets angry and sulks is the one looking for food for the one who gets angry and goes crazy
claude_interpretation: Those who react with quiet resentment often end up serving or appeasing those who express their anger more dramatically.
gemini_translation: The one with a soft stomach is the one who seeks food for the one with a rumbling stomach.
gemini_interpretation: Those who are compassionate and understanding are often the ones who provide for those in need.
mistral_translation: The easily angered one is searching for food for the quick-tempered one.
mistral_interpretation: People with similar negative traits often seek each other out or reinforce each other's behavior.
llama_translation: The one who is afraid of the ant-hill will not be given food by the one who is afraid of the anthill.
llama_interpretation: Those who are timid or fearful will not be able to help or support one another.

yoruba: À-bí-ì-kọ́; à-kọ́-ì-gbà; òde ló ti ńkọ́gbọ́n wálé.
english_literal: A-child-that-was-never-taught-how-to-behave; a-child-that-was-taught-but-that-refused-to-heed-instruction; it is from outside the home that he will learn wisdom.
interpretation_gold: Look well to your child's upbringing.
deepseek_translation: The one who refuses to learn; the one who learns but refuses to accept; it is from outside that wisdom enters the home.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against stubbornness in learning and accepting wisdom, emphasizing that wisdom often comes from external sources.
claude_translation: One who is born but not taught; one who is taught but does not accept; it is from outside that wisdom is being brought home.
claude_interpretation: True wisdom often comes from external sources when people fail to learn from their birth family or reject local teachings.
gemini_translation: One who is taught but does not learn; one who learns but does not accept; it is from outside that they bring wisdom home.
gemini_interpretation: True wisdom is not merely acquired through instruction but through practical experience and application, often learned outside formal settings.
mistral_translation: The one who gives birth does not teach; the one who teaches does not receive; it is the outsider who brings wisdom home.
mistral_interpretation: True wisdom or guidance often comes from external sources rather than those closest to us.
llama_translation: We don't know the day; we don't know the night; it is the road that teaches the traveler.
llama_interpretation: Experience and challenges are the best teachers in life.

yoruba: Àì-mọ̀-kan, àì-mọ̀-kàn ní ḿmú èkúté-ilé pe ológbò níjà.
english_literal: It is severe ignorance that prompts a mouse to challenge a cat to a fight.
interpretation_gold: Never taunt an adversary you cannot handle.
deepseek_translation: Not knowing one, not knowing two is what makes the house rat call the cat a fighter.
deepseek_interpretation: Ignorance leads to underestimating danger or overestimating one's abilities.
claude_translation: Not knowing one, not knowing the other is what makes the house rat challenge the cat to a fight
claude_interpretation: Ignorance of one's limitations and opponent's strengths leads to foolish confrontations with disastrous consequences.
gemini_translation: Not knowing one, not knowing two is what makes the house rat challenge the cat to a fight.
gemini_interpretation: Ignorance of one's limitations or the strength of an opponent can lead to foolish and dangerous actions.
mistral_translation: Not knowing one, not knowing another is what makes the house-rat think the cat is a wrestler
mistral_interpretation: Ignorance or lack of experience can lead one to underestimate a more knowledgeable or powerful opponent
llama_translation: No one knows, no one knows is what the owner of the house says when he is fighting
llama_interpretation: A person's true character is revealed in times of conflict or crisis.

yoruba: Àlejò kì í pìtàn ìlú fónílé.
english_literal: The visitor does not recount the history of the town for the host.
interpretation_gold: Never presume to know more than the custodian of knowledge.
deepseek_translation: A visitor does not tell the history of the town to the homeowner.
deepseek_interpretation: One should respect the knowledge and authority of those who are native to a place.
claude_translation: A visitor does not tell the history of a town to its inhabitants.
claude_interpretation: Outsiders should not presume to teach locals about their own affairs or culture.
gemini_translation: A visitor does not narrate the history of a town to the homeowner.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate and presumptuous for an outsider to claim more knowledge or authority than those who are native or experienced in a particular context.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A visitor does not narrate the history of a town to the homeowner.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate and presumptuous for an outsider to claim more knowledge or authority than those who are native or experienced in a particular context."}
mistral_translation: A visitor does not recount the history of the town in another's house
mistral_interpretation: It is disrespectful to discuss the affairs of one household while in another's home, as it shows poor manners and lack of discretion
llama_translation: A stranger does not tell the story of the town's interior
llama_interpretation: Outsiders should not interfere with or speak about the internal affairs of a community.

yoruba: A di gàárì sílẹ̀ ewúrẹ́ ńyọjú; ẹrù ìran rẹ̀ ni?
english_literal: We prepare the saddle, and the goat presents itself; is it a burden for the lineage of goats?
interpretation_gold: Goats that know their place do not offer their backs to be saddled.
deepseek_translation: When the goat is eating the leftover gari, where is the fear of its lineage?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that neglecting one's responsibilities can lead to disgrace for oneself and one's family.
claude_translation: We pour garri on the ground and the goat is happy; is it the burden of its generation?
claude_interpretation: People often rejoice over small favors without realizing they may be accepting the consequences of deeper systemic problems or generational burdens.
gemini_translation: A saddle is placed down, and a goat appears; is it carrying its own load?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the appropriateness or readiness of someone for a task or position, implying they are ill-suited or unprepared.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A saddle is placed down, and a goat appears; is it carrying its own load?", "interpretation": "This proverb questions the appropriateness or readiness of someone for a task or position, implying they are ill-suited or unprepared."}
mistral_translation: When gari is poured on the ground, the goat rejoices; is that its family's fear?
mistral_interpretation: One should not mistake another's temporary gain or joy for a permanent solution to their own problems.
llama_translation: A dog is tied to the leg of a goat; what is the purpose of the rope?
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the futility of attempting to control or restrain someone who is already being controlled or restrained by circumstances.

yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ rí wèrè, ó kán lùgbẹ́.
english_literal: The leper sees a mad person and dashes into the bush.
interpretation_gold: A person who should be ostracized ostracizes others.
deepseek_translation: The madman saw a fool, he started dancing.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against mocking others' flaws when you have similar or worse shortcomings yourself.
claude_translation: The crown-wearer saw a mad person and touched the drum
claude_interpretation: Even those in positions of authority can be moved to act impulsively or inappropriately when confronted with unusual situations.
gemini_translation: A leper saw a mad person, and he jumped into the bush.
gemini_interpretation: Even those who are themselves afflicted can be startled or frightened by a more severe or unusual affliction.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A leper saw a mad person, and he jumped into the bush.", "interpretation": "Even those who are themselves afflicted can be startled or frightened by a more severe or unusual affliction."}
mistral_translation: The madman's crown sees madness, it only knocks on the side
mistral_interpretation: Those who are foolish or misguided often fail to recognize their own faults and instead criticize others.
llama_translation: The one who knows the madman is the one who ties him up.
llama_interpretation: Only those who understand a problem or situation can effectively address it.

yoruba: Ara-àìbalẹ̀, olórí àrùn.
english_literal: Restlessness, father of all diseases.
interpretation_gold: No disease is greater than hyper-action.
deepseek_translation: The restless body, the head of disease.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that constant restlessness or lack of peace can lead to illness or trouble.
claude_translation: A restless body is the head of illness
claude_interpretation: Lack of rest and constant agitation leads to sickness and poor health.
gemini_translation: Restlessness/anxiety, the chief of ailments.
gemini_interpretation: Anxiety and worry are often the root causes or major contributors to various illnesses and problems.
mistral_translation: The lazy person, the head of sickness
mistral_interpretation: Laziness leads to or invites suffering and misfortune.
llama_translation: The body of a lazy person is the head of illness
llama_interpretation: Laziness can lead to physical and mental suffering.

yoruba: A fi ọ́ jọba ò ńṣàwúre o fẹ́ jẹ Ọlọ́run ni?
english_literal: You have been crowned a king, and yet you make good-luck charms; would you be crowned God?
interpretation_gold: Being crowned a king is about the best fortune a mortal could hope for.
deepseek_translation: You are not yet king and you are making decrees, do you want to be God?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against arrogance and overstepping one's bounds before attaining the proper authority or position.
claude_translation: We made you king but you are not showing gratitude, do you want to be God?
claude_interpretation: Those elevated to positions of power should remain humble and grateful rather than becoming arrogant and forgetting their human limitations.
gemini_translation: You who were made king, you are still making sacrifices for good fortune, do you want to become God?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the insatiable desire for power and control, implying that even those in positions of authority should not overstep their bounds or seek to usurp divine power.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "You who were made king, you are still making sacrifices for good fortune, do you want to become God?", "interpretation": "This proverb questions the insatiable desire for power and control, implying that even those in positions of authority should not overstep their bounds or seek to usurp divine power."}
mistral_translation: Is it because one is ruling that one forgets to pray to God?
mistral_interpretation: Success or power should not make one forget their dependence on God or neglect gratitude.
llama_translation: We are asking for a king, who will we worship as God?
llama_interpretation: This proverb cautions against seeking power or authority that rivals or supersedes the divine.

yoruba: A kì í bínú ààtàn ká dalẹ̀ sígbẹ̀ẹ́.
english_literal: One does not get angry with the rubbish dump and discard one's rubbish into the bush.
interpretation_gold: One should not act in unreasonable and harmful ways because of anger.
deepseek_translation: One does not get angry at a goat and then sleep in its pen.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not hold grudges against those you must continue to live or work with.
claude_translation: One does not get angry at the firefly and then lie down in the grass.
claude_interpretation: Don't let minor irritations cause you to put yourself in a worse or more dangerous situation.
gemini_translation: One does not get angry at the refuse dump and then throw dirt into the bush.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to harm oneself or a larger community due to anger at a specific, often minor, issue.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not get angry at the refuse dump and then throw dirt into the bush.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to harm oneself or a larger community due to anger at a specific, often minor, issue."}
mistral_translation: We do not get angry at the rubbish heap and then go to bed on it.
mistral_interpretation: It is foolish to let anger over a minor issue lead you to harm yourself or make a bad situation worse.
llama_translation: We do not use the heat of the fire to roast a snail
llama_interpretation: One should not use excessive force or energy to accomplish a task that requires gentleness or subtlety.

yoruba: Àjànàkú ò tu lójú alájá; o-nígba-ajá ò gbọdọ̀ tọ́pa erin.
english_literal: The elephant does not break and run at the sight of dogs; a person with two hundred dogs dares not stalk an elephant.
interpretation_gold: Two hundred dogs are no match for an elephant.
deepseek_translation: The elephant does not get lost in the presence of the dog; the one who has the dog must not shoot the elephant.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against underestimating or disrespecting those who are more powerful or influential, as it can lead to dire consequences.
claude_translation: The elephant does not dissolve in the eyes of the dog owner; the dog owner must not challenge the elephant's path.
claude_interpretation: One should not challenge or confront those who are far more powerful or superior in status.
gemini_translation: The elephant does not get lost in the presence of the dog owner; the owner of two hundred dogs must not track an elephant.
gemini_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks that are beyond their capabilities or resources, especially when facing a superior force.
mistral_translation: The elephant does not trip in the presence of the dog; when it is time for the dog, it must not meet the elephant already passed by
mistral_interpretation: One should not underestimate others, as everyone will have their own moment to shine or prove their worth
llama_translation: The hunter does not look at the dog's face; the dog that is about to catch a lion does not listen to the hunter's command.
llama_interpretation: One should not be distracted or swayed by external opinions when focused on a critical task or goal.

yoruba: A kì í jẹ oyè ẹnu ọ̀nà kalẹ́.
english_literal: One does not bear the title of gatekeeper even until night time.
interpretation_gold: As one advances in age, so should one's responsibilities advance in gravity and importance.
deepseek_translation: One does not eat the chieftaincy title by the roadside.
deepseek_interpretation: Achieving honor or high status requires effort and cannot be obtained casually.
claude_translation: One does not eat the title of the mouth of the road and swallow it
claude_interpretation: Empty titles or positions without substance should not be accepted or valued.
gemini_translation: One does not eat the chieftaincy title of the doorway and go home.
gemini_interpretation: One should not accept a position or responsibility without being prepared to fully commit to its duties and implications.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not eat the chieftaincy title of the doorway and go home.", "interpretation": "One should not accept a position or responsibility without being prepared to fully commit to its duties and implications."}
mistral_translation: We do not eat the chieftaincy title of the roadside at night
mistral_interpretation: One should not pursue risky or ill-timed ambitions that could lead to harm or failure.
llama_translation: We do not eat the title of the road's elder
llama_interpretation: One should not take advantage of a position or title without putting in the necessary effort or responsibility.

yoruba: A pè ọ́ lọ́mọ erín-màgbọn ò ńyọ̀; ìwọ pàápàá ló mì í?
english_literal: You are described as the child of the elephant that swallows coconuts, and you rejoice; are you the one who swallows coconuts?
interpretation_gold: The description honors the father, not the person being addressed.
deepseek_translation: They say the wise one does not laugh; are you the one laughing?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against arrogance by questioning whether one truly possesses the wisdom they claim.
claude_translation: We call you a child of the elephant-wise one and you don't rejoice; are you the one who gave birth to it?
claude_interpretation: One should appreciate and be grateful for the honor and recognition given to them rather than acting ungrateful or entitled.
gemini_translation: You are called the child of a chewing elephant and you are smiling; did you yourself swallow it?
gemini_interpretation: One should not be pleased by a reputation or accusation that implies wrongdoing, especially if they are not directly involved.
mistral_translation: You call it a baby elephant that does not rejoice; is it only you that I know?
mistral_interpretation: The proverb questions why someone assumes they are the only person of value or importance, reminding them that others exist and matter just as much.
llama_translation: We are calling the elephant's child, but it is not responding; who is calling me?
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of respecting those in positions of authority or power.

yoruba: Àbúrò kì í pa ẹ̀gbọ́n nítàn.
english_literal: The younger person does not give the older person history lectures.
interpretation_gold: One should not exceed one's station.
deepseek_translation: A younger sibling does not inherit disgrace.
deepseek_interpretation: Each person is responsible for their own actions and should not be judged by the mistakes of their elders.
claude_translation: A younger sibling does not tell lies about an elder sibling
claude_interpretation: Younger family members should show respect and loyalty to their elders by not speaking falsely against them.
gemini_translation: A younger sibling does not tell an older sibling a tale.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate for a younger person to lecture or correct an older person, as respect for elders is paramount in Yoruba culture.
mistral_translation: A younger sibling does not kill an elder sibling with a story.
mistral_interpretation: One should not use words or tales to undermine or cause harm to those who are older or more experienced.
llama_translation: A friend does not kill a friend in a dream.
llama_interpretation: True friends do not harm each other, even in a hypothetical or imagined situation.

yoruba: À-tẹ́-ẹ̀-ká ni iyì ọlọ́lá; sálúbàtà ni iyì ọlọ̀tọ̀; bá a bá gbéra lágbèéjù ọba ni wọ́n ńfini íṣe
english_literal: Spreading-the-mat-without-rolling-it-back-up is the mark of the wealthy; sandals are the mark of the illustrious; if one sings one's praise too loudly one is liable to be made a king.
interpretation_gold: People take one as one presents oneself.
deepseek_translation: The honor of the wealthy is their expensive cloth; the honor of the poor is their sandals; when we gather at the king's courtyard, they are judged by their deeds
deepseek_interpretation: Material possessions may differ, but true worth is measured by one's actions and character.
claude_translation: Stepping carefully is the dignity of the wealthy; slippers are the dignity of the poor; if we carry ourselves with pride in the palace, they make us a king
claude_interpretation: How you conduct yourself determines the respect and position you receive in society, regardless of your background.
gemini_translation: Spreading out is the honor of the rich; slippers are the honor of the distinct one; if we carry ourselves with dignity, we are treated like royalty.
gemini_interpretation: One's demeanor and self-respect dictate how others perceive and treat them, regardless of their social standing.
mistral_translation: The wrapper of the wealthy is honor; the sandals are the honor of the poor; if you surpass the king's palace in extravagance, they will investigate your deeds
mistral_interpretation: One should not live beyond their means or pretend to be wealthier than they are, as it invites scrutiny and potential trouble.
llama_translation: The one who has a hat is the friend of the king; the one who has a shoe is the friend of the farmer; when we get to the palace, it is the one who has a horse that they will ask for help
llama_interpretation: One's usefulness is determined by the situation and the resources they possess.

yoruba: Afínjú wọ ọjà ó rìn gbẹndẹ́kẹ ọ̀bún wọ ọjà ó rìn ṣùẹ̀ṣùẹ̀; ọ̀bùn ní ó ru ẹrù afínjú relé.
english_literal: The fashionable person enters the market and walks in a leisurely manner; the filthy person enters the market and walks in a sluggish manner; it is the filthy person that will carry the fashionable person's load to the house for him or her.
interpretation_gold: Good breeding confers great advantages.
deepseek_translation: The blind man goes to the market and returns safely; the sighted man goes to the market and returns with trouble; the blind man carries the sighted man's load home.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that wisdom and caution often outweigh physical ability or advantage.
claude_translation: The albino enters the market walking proudly, the hunchback enters the market walking quietly; it is the hunchback who carries the albino's load home.
claude_interpretation: Quiet, humble people often do the real work while those who make a show of themselves contribute little of substance.
gemini_translation: The neat person enters the market and walks gracefully, the dirty person enters the market and walks sloppily; it is the dirty person who will carry the neat person's load home.
gemini_interpretation: One's character and presentation, whether good or bad, ultimately determine their fate and how they are perceived and treated by others.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The neat person enters the market and walks gracefully, the dirty person enters the market and walks sloppily; it is the dirty person who will carry the neat person's load home.", "interpretation": "One's character and presentation, whether good or bad, ultimately determine their fate and how they are perceived and treated by others."}
mistral_translation: The neat person enters the market and walks with a straight posture; the dirty person enters the market and walks with a stooped gait; it is the dirty one who carries the neat person's load home.
mistral_interpretation: Those who appear careless or irresponsible often end up burdened with the consequences of the actions of those who are meticulous or prudent.
llama_translation: The one who sells firewood at the market walks with a bent back, the one who sells ivory at the market walks with a straight back; it is the ivory that makes the firewood seller come to the ivory seller's house.
llama_interpretation: Those who possess valuable resources or knowledge have more power and influence than those who do not.

yoruba: A kì í mú oko lọ́nà ká ṣèmẹ́lẹ́; tajá tẹran ní ḿbúni.
english_literal: One does not farm a plot by the road and neglect its care; every dog and goat would ridicule one.
interpretation_gold: Never expose yourself to insult by behaving badly in public view.
deepseek_translation: One does not carry a hoe on the road and stumble; it is the bush and grass that trip one.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that one should be mindful of their actions and surroundings to avoid preventable mishaps.
claude_translation: One does not take a hoe on a journey to go and farm; it is the hunter and the meat seller that bring us meat
claude_interpretation: People should focus on their own expertise and rely on specialists for other needs rather than trying to do everything themselves.
gemini_translation: One does not take a farm to the road and be lazy; both dogs and livestock will insult one.
gemini_interpretation: When one's work is publicly visible, laziness will lead to public ridicule and scorn.
mistral_translation: We do not take a hoe on the road to use as a walking stick; it is the butcher who knows the cow's joints.
mistral_interpretation: One should rely on the expertise of those skilled in a particular task rather than attempting it without proper knowledge.
llama_translation: We don't take a farm to the road to make it fertile; it's the road that is blocked by the farm.
llama_interpretation: One's problems or responsibilities should not be imposed on others or taken to where they don't belong.

yoruba: Àgbéré-e ṣìgìdì tó ní ká gbé òun sójò; bí apá ti ńya nitan ńya; kidiri orí ò lè dá dúró.
english_literal: The overreaching mud idol that asked to be put in the rain; as the arms fell off, so did the thighs; the rounded head could not support itself.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's limitations.
deepseek_translation: The crab with stiff legs that says we should carry it to the river; as the hand is stretching, it is stretching; the whirlwind on the head cannot stand still.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against hypocrisy and pretending to need help while actually being capable or unwilling to change.
claude_translation: The carved wooden figure that says we should take it to the rain; as the arm keeps breaking off; the head cannot stand firm.
claude_interpretation: A person who insists on being placed in situations they cannot handle will inevitably fall apart and lose their dignity.
gemini_translation: The foolish masquerade that asks to be placed in the rain; as the arms are getting wet, so are the thighs; the head cannot stand alone.
gemini_interpretation: A person who invites trouble will inevitably experience its full consequences, as problems rarely remain isolated.
mistral_translation: The cripple who says we should carry him to the market; as the arm that has been aching keeps aching; the head with a boil cannot stand still
mistral_interpretation: One should not make unreasonable demands or expect help when their own persistent problems make it impossible for others to assist effectively.
llama_translation: The calabash that is not strong enough to carry itself, if it is carried on the head, it will break; if it is carried on the back, it will break; it cannot stand upright on its own.
llama_interpretation: A weak or incompetent person cannot handle responsibility or independence.

yoruba: Aláṣọ-kan kì í ṣeré òjò.
english_literal: A person who has only one set of clothing does not play in the rain.
interpretation_gold: See the preceding entry.
deepseek_translation: A one-clothed person does not play in the rain.
deepseek_interpretation: One should avoid unnecessary risks when unprepared or vulnerable.
claude_translation: One who has only one cloth does not play in the rain
claude_interpretation: A person with limited resources must be more careful and cautious than those who have abundance.
gemini_translation: One who has only one cloth does not play in the rain.
gemini_interpretation: People with limited resources must be cautious and avoid risks that could lead to further loss.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who has only one cloth does not play in the rain.", "interpretation": "People with limited resources must be cautious and avoid risks that could lead to further loss."}
mistral_translation: A single piece of cloth does not play with rain
mistral_interpretation: One should not face challenges or hardships alone without support or preparation
llama_translation: One cloth does not dry the body
llama_interpretation: No single person can solve all problems or meet all needs.

yoruba: Aṣọ à-fọ̀-fún ò jẹ́ ká mọ olówó.
english_literal: Clothes washed clean make identifying the rich person impossible.
interpretation_gold: A poor person who looks to his or her appearance looks rich.
deepseek_translation: Tattered clothes do not allow us to know the rich.
deepseek_interpretation: Outward appearances can be deceiving and do not always reflect a person's true wealth or status.
claude_translation: Clothes that are given freely do not let us know who has money
claude_interpretation: When people receive things for free, it becomes difficult to distinguish between those who are wealthy and those who are not.
gemini_translation: A cloth that is too white to wash prevents us from knowing the rich person.
gemini_interpretation: It is difficult to distinguish the truly wealthy from those who merely appear so when everyone presents themselves immaculately.
mistral_translation: Clothes that are blown about by the wind do not let us know the wealthy person
mistral_interpretation: Outward appearances can be deceptive and should not be relied upon to judge someone's true status or character
llama_translation: Clothes that are given out freely do not last long for the owner.
llama_interpretation: Things acquired easily or without effort are often not valued or taken care of.

yoruba: A ní ká wá ẹni tó lẹ́hìn ká fọmọ fún, abuké ní òun rèé; ti gànnàkù ẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀ là ńwí?
english_literal: One seeks a person with a prominent back as suitor for one's daughter, and the humpback presents himself; who spoke of protruding back?
interpretation_gold: The expression that translates as “prominent back” is an idiom meaning a proud pedigree. The humpback makes a rather embarrassing mistake.
deepseek_translation: We said let us look for someone to follow, the hunchback said he is the one; is it his hunch we are talking about?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against blindly following those who are unfit or unqualified to lead.
claude_translation: We said we should find someone with a back to carry a child for, the hunchback said he is ready; are we talking about that kind of back?
claude_interpretation: Not everyone who volunteers for a task is actually suitable or qualified for it.
gemini_translation: We said to find someone with a strong back to give a child to, the hunchback says he is the one; are we talking about his hunch?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of understanding the true nature of a request or problem before offering a solution, as superficial appearances can be misleading.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We said to find someone with a strong back to give a child to, the hunchback says he is the one; are we talking about his hunch?", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the importance of understanding the true nature of a request or problem before offering a solution, as superficial appearances can be misleading."}
mistral_translation: Someone says we should seek someone who is behind to bear a child for us, but it is the hunchback who says it is his turn; who are we referring to when we speak of someone with a very short back?
mistral_interpretation: This proverb criticizes those who make unreasonable demands or shift blame while ignoring their own flaws or limitations.
llama_translation: We are looking for someone to lean on and rest, the tortoise is the one we are looking for; what is the meaning of the back of the tortoise?
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of seeking help and support from those who are strong and reliable.

yoruba: À-wín-ná-wó ò yẹni; à-gbà-bọ̀-ọ ṣòkòtò ò yẹ ọmọ èèyàn; bí kò fúnni lẹ́sẹ̀ a dòrògí; ohun ẹni ní ńyẹni.
english_literal: Borrowing-money-to-spend does not speak well of one; borrowed trousers do not become a person; if it is not tight around the legs it is difficult to remove; it is one's thing that fits one.
interpretation_gold: One should not live beyond one's means.
deepseek_translation: The one who dances with fire does not suit anyone; the one who wears trousers does not suit a human child; if it does not give one legs, it becomes a walking stick; one's own thing is what suits one.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of individuality and self-acceptance, suggesting that what is suitable for one person may not be for another.
claude_translation: Borrowing money does not suit one; wearing borrowed trousers does not suit a human being; if it does not fit one's feet, one becomes lame; one's own things are what suit one.
claude_interpretation: Using what belongs to others or living beyond one's means brings discomfort and problems, while being content with what you own brings true satisfaction and dignity.
gemini_translation: Spending borrowed money does not suit one; wearing borrowed trousers does not suit a person; if it doesn't fit the leg, it becomes baggy; one's own things suit one.
gemini_interpretation: It is always better to use what is genuinely yours and within your means, as borrowed things often come with discomfort or unsuitability.
mistral_translation: The firewood does not fit one; the loincloth does not fit another; if it does not reach one's feet, one drags it; what belongs to someone is what fits them.
mistral_interpretation: People should be content with what is suitable or meant for them rather than forcing what does not fit their circumstances.
llama_translation: The one who is not at home does not know; the one who is not in the forest does not know the forest's secret; if one does not enter the forest, one does not know the forest's depth; what one has is what one knows.
llama_interpretation: Personal experience is the best teacher, and one can only truly know something by experiencing it firsthand.

yoruba: A kì í gbọ́ “Lù ú” lẹ́nu àgbà.
english_literal: One never hears “Beat him/her up” in the mouth of an elder.
interpretation_gold: Elders resolve disputes; they do not goad disputants on.
deepseek_translation: One does not hear 'Beat' in the mouth of an elder.
deepseek_interpretation: Elders are wise and avoid advocating violence or conflict.
claude_translation: One does not hear 'Beat him' from the mouth of an elder.
claude_interpretation: Elders are expected to show wisdom and restraint by not inciting violence or encouraging harmful actions against others.
gemini_translation: One does not hear 'Hit him/it' from the mouth of an elder.
gemini_interpretation: Elders are expected to promote peace and reconciliation, not incite violence.
mistral_translation: We do not hear 'Beat the drum' from an elder's mouth
mistral_interpretation: An elder should not engage in or encourage reckless or inappropriate behavior.
llama_translation: We don't hear 'Lù ú' from an elder's mouth
llama_interpretation: Elders are expected to speak with wisdom and decorum, not utter nonsense or foolish words.

yoruba: Akórira ò ní ǹkan; ọ̀dùn ò sunwọ̀ fún ṣòkòtò.
english_literal: An overly squeamish person owns nothing; raffia cloth is no good for trousers.
interpretation_gold: Excessive squeamishness renders one helpless and destitute.
deepseek_translation: The crab has no head; the year is not favorable for the lazy.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that laziness leads to unfavorable outcomes, as the crab's lack of a head symbolizes aimlessness and the year's disfavor represents consequences.
claude_translation: The impatient person has nothing; the year does not move closer for trousers.
claude_interpretation: Patience is essential for success, as rushing or being impatient will not make things happen faster than their natural time.
gemini_translation: The one who hates has nothing; a hole is not good for trousers.
gemini_interpretation: Hate is destructive and offers no benefit, just as a hole ruins the usefulness of trousers.
mistral_translation: The miser has nothing; the year does not sew trousers for the poor.
mistral_interpretation: Hardship and poverty are not temporary conditions that will resolve themselves without personal effort or divine intervention.
llama_translation: The farmer has no problem; the year does not wait for the lazy person.
llama_interpretation: One must be diligent and take timely action to achieve success.

yoruba: A kì í jayé ọba ká ṣu sára.
english_literal: One does not so luxuriate in one's majesty that one shits on oneself.
interpretation_gold: Lack of moderation and decorum will bring disgrace to even the most elevated person.
deepseek_translation: One does not eat the king's food and defecate on his body.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not repay kindness with disrespect or harm.
claude_translation: One does not enjoy the king's reign and still carry loads on one's head
claude_interpretation: You cannot benefit from a position of privilege or authority while still engaging in menial tasks or maintaining a lowly status.
gemini_translation: One does not enjoy the king's life and then defecate on oneself.
gemini_interpretation: One should not abuse or disrespect the privileges and benefits bestowed upon them.
mistral_translation: We do not enjoy the king's reign and then roast yam peels
mistral_interpretation: One should not waste or misuse the benefits of a good situation or leadership.
llama_translation: We do not go to the king's palace to play
llama_interpretation: One should be serious and respectful when interacting with those in positions of authority.

yoruba: Adití ò gbọ́, “Yàgò!”
english_literal: The deaf does not hear,“Make way!”
interpretation_gold: Cautionary words are lost on reckless people.
deepseek_translation: The deaf does not hear, "Yàgò!"
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that some people are impervious to warnings or advice due to their stubbornness or inability to listen.
claude_translation: The deaf person does not hear 'Get out of the way!'
claude_interpretation: Someone who refuses to listen to advice or warnings will inevitably face the consequences of their stubbornness.
gemini_translation: A deaf person does not hear, "Get out of the way!"
gemini_interpretation: It is futile to warn someone who is incapable of understanding or responding to the warning.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A deaf person does not hear, \"Get out of the way!\"", "interpretation": "It is futile to warn someone who is incapable of understanding or responding to the warning."}
mistral_translation: Aditi did not hear, 'Run away!'
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns against ignoring clear warnings or advice, leading to avoidable misfortune.
llama_translation: The deaf one did not hear, “Yàgò!”
llama_interpretation: A person who refuses to listen or heed advice will ultimately face the consequences.

yoruba: À-rí-ì-gbọdọ̀-wí, baálé ilé ṣu sápẹ.
english_literal: Something-seen-but-unmentionable, the man of the house shits in the sauce-pan.
interpretation_gold: When an illustrious person does the unmentionable, no one dares speak.
deepseek_translation: He who sees the guinea fowl, the house owner shoots it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against taking advantage of opportunities that belong to others, as it may lead to conflict.
claude_translation: What-is-seen-must-not-be-spoken, the head of the house has defecated on a mat.
claude_interpretation: Some shameful family matters should be kept private and not discussed publicly, even when they are obvious to household members.
gemini_translation: That which is seen but must not be spoken, the head of the house defecated in a plate.
gemini_interpretation: Some shameful acts, especially by those in authority, are best kept secret to preserve their dignity and the family's reputation.
mistral_translation: One who sees and does not warn, the owner of the house is already soaked in the rain
mistral_interpretation: It is irresponsible to witness danger and fail to alert others, as the consequences will eventually affect everyone.
llama_translation: The one who knows the depth of the river, the owner of the house will not wade
llama_interpretation: One should respect and seek guidance from those with deeper knowledge or experience in a particular matter.

yoruba: Aáyán fẹ gẹṣin; adìẹ ni ò gbà fún un.
english_literal: The cockroach would ride a horse; it is the chicken that does not allow.
interpretation_gold: A cockroach that stirs in the presence of a chicken is as good as dead.
deepseek_translation: The woodcarver wants to carve a horse; the chicken is what he was given.
deepseek_interpretation: One must make the best of what is available, even if it falls short of one's desires.
claude_translation: The cockroach wants to mount a horse; it is the chicken that will not allow it.
claude_interpretation: Those who attempt things beyond their capacity often face opposition from those only slightly above them rather than from those far superior.
gemini_translation: The cockroach wanted to ride a horse; the chicken did not allow it.
gemini_interpretation: One's aspirations can be thwarted by a more powerful or dominant entity.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The cockroach wanted to ride a horse; the chicken did not allow it.", "interpretation": "One's aspirations can be thwarted by a more powerful or dominant entity."}
mistral_translation: The squirrel wants to ride a horse; it is the chicken that refuses to give it one
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the folly of desiring something beyond one's capacity or status while blaming others for not enabling the impossible.
llama_translation: The tortoise wants a drum; it is a calabash that it got.
llama_interpretation: One may desire something, but end up with something entirely different.

yoruba: Aáyán kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ erin; èèyàn kì í yán ẹsẹ̀ irò.
english_literal: A cockroach does not trip an elephant; a human being does not trip a chimpanzee.
interpretation_gold: One should not take on adversaries one cannot match.
deepseek_translation: The sculptor does not carve the foot of an elephant; a person does not carve the foot of an ant.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks beyond their capability or expertise.
claude_translation: A cockroach does not choose the elephant's foot; a person does not choose the foot of a lie.
claude_interpretation: One should not associate with or align themselves with falsehood or deceit, just as the weak should avoid confronting the powerful.
gemini_translation: The cockroach does not choose the elephant's leg; a person does not choose the leg of a rumor.
gemini_interpretation: One should not involve themselves in matters that are too powerful or dangerous for them to handle, just as a cockroach cannot dictate to an elephant, and a person cannot control the spread of a rumor.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The cockroach does not choose the elephant's leg; a person does not choose the leg of a rumor.", "interpretation": "One should not involve themselves in matters that are too powerful or dangerous for them to handle, just as a cockroach cannot dictate to an elephant, and a person cannot control the spread of a rumor."}
mistral_translation: The woodpecker does not count the elephant's toes; a person does not count the locust's toes.
mistral_interpretation: One should not concern oneself with matters that are beyond their capability or irrelevant to their position.
llama_translation: The tortoise does not walk the path of the elephant; the human being does not walk the path of the antelope.
llama_interpretation: Each person should follow their own path and not try to imitate or follow the path of another.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà tó wẹ̀wù àṣejù, ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó fi rí.
english_literal: An elder who wears the garment of immoderation will find disgrace because of it.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation brings disgrace.
deepseek_translation: An elder who dresses excessively will be ridiculed.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against excessive behavior that contradicts one's age or status.
claude_translation: An elder who wears excessive clothing will be seen with disgrace
claude_interpretation: Moderation and appropriateness in behavior and appearance are essential for maintaining dignity and respect, especially for those in positions of authority or age.
gemini_translation: An elder who wears excessive clothes will find disgrace.
gemini_interpretation: Excessive display or behavior, even by a respected person, can lead to shame or ridicule.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An elder who wears excessive clothes will find disgrace.", "interpretation": "Excessive display or behavior, even by a respected person, can lead to shame or ridicule."}
mistral_translation: An elder who wears excessive clothing will end up seeing lice
mistral_interpretation: Excess in behavior or appearance often leads to unforeseen negative consequences
llama_translation: An elderly person who sees a masquerade, it is with the corner of the eye that he sees it.
llama_interpretation: Elderly people should be cautious and humble in their interactions, avoiding direct confrontation or boldness.

yoruba: A kì í kọ ẹlẹ́ṣin ká tún lọ fẹ́ ẹlẹ́sẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not divorce a horse rider and go marry a pedestrian.
interpretation_gold: One should ever progress, never regress.
deepseek_translation: One does not teach a horse rider and then go to teach a pedestrian.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not waste time teaching those who already know or are unwilling to learn.
claude_translation: One does not reject a horse rider and then go to desire a foot walker
claude_interpretation: You should not reject something of higher value only to later settle for something of lesser value.
gemini_translation: One does not reject a horse rider and then go on to marry a pedestrian.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to reject a superior option only to settle for an inferior one.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not reject a horse rider and then go on to marry a pedestrian.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to reject a superior option only to settle for an inferior one."}
mistral_translation: We do not teach the horse-rider how to mend the foot-traveler's path.
mistral_interpretation: One should not interfere in matters where others are more knowledgeable or experienced.
llama_translation: We do not learn the ways of the horse to go and ride the donkey
llama_interpretation: One should not apply the skills or methods of one situation to a completely different situation.

yoruba: A kì í pẹ̀lú ọ̀bọ jáko.
english_literal: One does not join a monkey in roaming the bush.
interpretation_gold: Do not join others in their madness.
deepseek_translation: One does not wrestle with a gorilla.
deepseek_interpretation: Avoid engaging in conflicts with those who are clearly stronger or more powerful than you.
claude_translation: One does not stay long with a monkey and learn to jump
claude_interpretation: Bad company inevitably corrupts good character through prolonged association.
gemini_translation: One does not accompany a monkey to the farm.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to associate with those who are known to cause trouble or destruction, as their actions will inevitably lead to negative consequences for you.
mistral_translation: One does not clap with one hand.
mistral_interpretation: Cooperation and mutual effort are essential for success or resolving issues.
llama_translation: We do not call a child a thief
llama_interpretation: One should not prematurely judge or label someone based on a single action or behavior.

yoruba: Àkùkọ̀ adìẹ́ fi dídájí ṣàgbà; ó fi ṣíṣu-sílẹ̀ ṣèwe.
english_literal: The rooster shows its maturity by its early rising; it shows its lack of maturity by defecating on the floor.
interpretation_gold: Nobody is free of some blemish.
deepseek_translation: The rooster proves its maturity by crowing; it proves its youth by scratching the ground.
deepseek_interpretation: Actions reveal a person's true nature and stage in life.
claude_translation: The rooster shows maturity by crowing; it shows youth by scratching the ground.
claude_interpretation: People demonstrate their level of maturity or experience through their actions and behavior.
gemini_translation: The rooster becomes old by crowing early; it becomes young by laying eggs.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb highlights that one's actions and contributions, rather than age, determine their status or perceived value within a community.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The rooster becomes old by crowing early; it becomes young by laying eggs.", "interpretation": "The proverb highlights that one's actions and contributions, rather than age, determine their status or perceived value within a community."}
mistral_translation: The chicken that the hen uses to grow old; it leaves the yam seedlings for the young ones.
mistral_interpretation: Elders should nurture the young by passing on responsibilities and opportunities to ensure continuity and growth.
llama_translation: The cockerel uses its beak to teach the elder; it uses its comb to decorate itself.
llama_interpretation: One should not pretend to be wiser than those who are older or more experienced.

yoruba: Àgbàlagbà kì í yọ ayọ̀-ọ kí-ló-báyìí-wá?
english_literal: An elder does not rejoice in a manner that would provoke, “What brought all this about?”
interpretation_gold: Moderation and decorum in everything.
deepseek_translation: Does an elder not know the way to this place?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb questions the wisdom of elders, implying they should know better due to their experience.
claude_translation: An elder does not rejoice and ask 'what has brought this joy?'
claude_interpretation: Elders should maintain composure and wisdom by understanding the reasons behind events before expressing emotions.
gemini_translation: An elder does not ask, 'What brought this joy?'
gemini_interpretation: An elder, having experienced much, understands that joy is often fleeting or comes with its own challenges, and therefore does not question its arrival.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An elder does not ask, 'What brought this joy?'", "interpretation": "An elder, having experienced much, understands that joy is often fleeting or comes with its own challenges, and therefore does not question its arrival."}
mistral_translation: Does an elder ever dance the 'ayo-ọ' game to the extent of saying 'how did this come about?'
mistral_interpretation: Elders should maintain composure and wisdom, not behaving inappropriately or losing control in public.
llama_translation: Will the elderly not remove the ayo game from the one who is playing it?
llama_interpretation: Respect your elders and yield to their authority when necessary.

yoruba: À-jókòó-àì-dìde, à-sọ̀rọ̀-àì-gbèsì, ká sinni títí ká má padà sílé, àì-sunwọ̀n ní ńgbẹ̀hìn-in rẹ̀.
english_literal: Sitting-without-getting-up, speaking-without-waiting-for-responses, walking people on their way and not turning back, unpleasantness is what they breed.
interpretation_gold: Excess and self-forgetfulness in anything bring unpleasant results.
deepseek_translation: One who sits without standing, talks without listening, let us sit until we return home, they are not behind him.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against arrogance and neglecting others' perspectives, as it leads to isolation.
claude_translation: Sitting without getting up, talking without taking action, staying out until we don't return home, inappropriateness follows behind it.
claude_interpretation: Excessive idleness, empty talk, and staying away from home too long lead to improper behavior and negative consequences.
gemini_translation: Sitting without standing up, speaking without being answered, being escorted all the way without returning home, it is ill-fated that follows it.
gemini_interpretation: Unnatural or incomplete actions and situations often lead to negative outcomes.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Sitting without standing up, speaking without being answered, being escorted all the way without returning home, it is ill-fated that follows it.", "interpretation": "Unnatural or incomplete actions and situations often lead to negative outcomes."}
mistral_translation: Sitting without rising, speaking without responding, let us serve him until we never return home, it is regret that follows him
mistral_interpretation: Laziness and poor communication in service lead to lifelong regret and unfulfilled potential.
llama_translation: We do not sleep, we do not wake up, we do not rest until we return home, we do not hear the voice of the one who is behind us.
llama_interpretation: One should not rest or be complacent until they have achieved their goal or returned to a place of safety.

yoruba: it is a sagacious person that eats kolanut; it is someone not squeamish about what he eats that eats awùsá.
interpretation_gold: People are what they eat; each to his/her own taste.
deepseek_translation: it is a wise person that eats kolanut; it is someone not picky about food that eats awùsá.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that wisdom and adaptability are essential qualities for navigating life's challenges and opportunities.
claude_translation: It is a sagacious person that eats kolanut; it is someone not squeamish about what he eats that eats awùsá.
claude_interpretation: Different foods require different levels of wisdom and discernment to consume appropriately.
gemini_translation: It is a sagacious person that eats kolanut; it is someone not squeamish about what he eats that eats awùsá.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb highlights that discerning individuals make wise choices, while those less particular might accept anything.
mistral_translation: It is a wise person who eats kolanut; it is someone who is not picky about what they eat that eats awùsá
mistral_interpretation: Wisdom involves discernment and openness to experiences, even those that may seem unconventional or challenging.
llama_translation: It is a wise person that eats kolanut; it is someone not squeamish about what he eats that eats awùsá.
llama_interpretation: A wise person is discerning about what they consume, while a careless person will eat anything.

yoruba: Àfòpiná tó ní òun ó pa fìtílà, ara ẹ̀ ni yó pa.
english_literal: The moth that attempts to kill (put out) the oil lamp will kill itself.
interpretation_gold: It is unwise to take on an adversary one knows can destroy one.
deepseek_translation: The rope that says it will hang the flag, it will hang itself.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that those who plot harm against others may ultimately bring harm upon themselves.
claude_translation: The match that says it will kill the lamp wick will kill itself.
claude_interpretation: Those who plot to destroy others often end up destroying themselves in the process.
gemini_translation: The moth that says it will extinguish the lamp will destroy itself.
gemini_interpretation: Those who attempt to harm something powerful or established will ultimately bring about their own downfall.
mistral_translation: The lamp-wick that says it will extinguish the lamp will extinguish itself
mistral_interpretation: Those who plot harm against others often end up harming themselves in the process
llama_translation: The one who has a razor to shave the head, it is the body that will shave
llama_interpretation: One's own actions or circumstances can ultimately lead to their downfall.

yoruba: Àì-jọnilójú lọ́sàn-án ní ḿmúni jarunpá luni lóru.
english_literal: Lack of regard for a person during the day makes one kick the person during the night as one tosses restlessly in sleep.
interpretation_gold: Familiarity breeds contempt.
deepseek_translation: Not being watchful is what makes the thief steal one's belongings.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that negligence or lack of vigilance invites theft or misfortune.
claude_translation: Not being cautious in the daytime is what makes one stumble over a log at night
claude_interpretation: Carelessness during safe or clear times leads to problems when conditions become difficult or dangerous.
gemini_translation: Not being satisfied in the daytime is what makes one fight with a leopard at night.
gemini_interpretation: Unresolved issues or dissatisfaction during the day can lead to dangerous confrontations or problems later on.
mistral_translation: It is the lack of mutual understanding that causes a bat to be caught in the afternoon
mistral_interpretation: Miscommunication or lack of agreement between people can lead to unexpected and unfavorable outcomes for all involved
llama_translation: It is the eyes that are not looking that are being used to count the number of people in the crowd
llama_interpretation: One should not underestimate the power of observation and awareness, even when not directly looking.

yoruba: Ajá tó ńlépa ẹkùn, ìyọnu ló ńwá.
english_literal: A dog that chases a leopard is seeking trouble.
interpretation_gold: One should not overreach oneself.
deepseek_translation: The dog chasing the leopard is doing so out of anger.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against acting out of anger or recklessness, as it can lead to dangerous consequences.
claude_translation: A dog that chases a leopard is looking for trouble.
claude_interpretation: One should not challenge or confront those who are far more powerful, as it will only lead to disaster.
gemini_translation: A dog that chases a leopard is looking for trouble.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish and dangerous to pursue something far beyond one's capabilities or to challenge a superior force.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A dog that chases a leopard is looking for trouble.", "interpretation": "It is foolish and dangerous to pursue something far beyond one's capabilities or to challenge a superior force."}
mistral_translation: The dog that chases the leopard is looking for trouble
mistral_interpretation: One who provokes or challenges a stronger opponent is inviting unnecessary harm or danger
llama_translation: A dog that is chasing a leopard is the one that will get tired.
llama_interpretation: One should not take on a task that is beyond their strength or capability.

yoruba: Ayọ̀ àyọ̀jù làkèré fi ńṣẹ́ nítan.
english_literal: It is excessive rejoicing that breaks the frog's thigh.
interpretation_gold: Immoderate happiness breeds unhappiness.
deepseek_translation: The joy that exceeds is what the crab uses to tell stories.
deepseek_interpretation: Excessive joy can lead to careless behavior or boasting.
claude_translation: It is excessive joy that the squirrel uses to fall from the tree
claude_interpretation: Excessive excitement or overconfidence can lead to one's downfall.
gemini_translation: Excessive joy is what makes the frog burst its thigh.
gemini_interpretation: Uncontrolled excitement or overindulgence can lead to self-destruction or negative consequences.
mistral_translation: It is with excessive joy and pride that the frog tells its story
mistral_interpretation: Overconfidence or arrogance often leads to one's downfall or embarrassment
llama_translation: Joy is not used to buy a second wife.
llama_interpretation: One should not use happiness or pleasure as a basis for making important decisions.

yoruba: Àgbà tí yó tẹ̀ẹ́, bó fárí tán, a ní ó ku járá ẹnu.
english_literal: An elder courting disgrace, after his head has been shaved he says, “Now, how about shaving the beard (as a gratuity)?”
interpretation_gold: One should know how far one may go before one suffers disgrace.
deepseek_translation: The elder who will fall, when they finish falling, we say they have leftover mouth foam.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that even respected elders can make mistakes, and people will talk about their failures.
claude_translation: An elder who will defecate, after he has shaved his head, we say he should remove the hair from his mouth
claude_interpretation: When someone is preparing to do something shameful or undignified, they should complete all aspects of their preparation thoroughly to avoid additional embarrassment.
gemini_translation: An elder who will be disgraced, after shaving his head, he says there is still the beard around the mouth.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb signifies that someone destined for disgrace will always find an excuse or reason to prolong their downfall, even after addressing initial issues.
mistral_translation: When an elder is about to defecate, even if it is smooth, we say it will leave a stain on the mouth
mistral_interpretation: No matter how carefully an elder acts, their mistakes are often noticed and criticized by others.
llama_translation: An elder who is being roasted, is being roasted by the fire, he says it is the smoke that is disturbing him.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the tendency for people to deny or downplay their own mistakes or wrongdoing.

yoruba: Alátiṣe ní ḿmọ àtiṣe ara-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: The person who must settle his/her affair knows best how he/she plans to go about doing so.
interpretation_gold: One should not second guess others, or try to make their decisions for them.
deepseek_translation: The one who lacks the ability to do something is the one who knows how to do it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb讽刺地指出，那些没有实际能力的人往往是最喜欢对他人指手画脚的。
claude_translation: The one who has experience knows his own capability
claude_interpretation: Only someone with practical experience truly understands their own abilities and limitations.
gemini_translation: The one who knows how to do it knows how to do their own thing.
gemini_interpretation: People are best equipped to handle their own affairs and responsibilities.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who knows how to do it knows how to do their own thing.", "interpretation": "People are best equipped to handle their own affairs and responsibilities."}
mistral_translation: The one who blames others is also blaming themselves.
mistral_interpretation: Criticizing others often reveals one's own flaws or hypocrisy.
llama_translation: The one who is lazy is lazy with his own body
llama_interpretation: One's laziness ultimately affects oneself.

yoruba: Without having a wife a person spares oóyọ́
interpretation_gold: The vegetable is used in stews, and stews are for wives to cook.
deepseek_translation: Without having a wife a person spares oóyọ́
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the idea that those without responsibilities (like a wife) may appear to have fewer burdens or expenses.
claude_translation: Without having a wife a person spares oóyọ́
claude_interpretation: A bachelor avoids the expenses and responsibilities that come with marriage and family life.
gemini_translation: Without having a wife a person spares oóyọ́
gemini_interpretation: A person without a spouse avoids the expenses and responsibilities associated with marriage.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Without having a wife a person spares oóyọ́", "interpretation": "A person without a spouse avoids the expenses and responsibilities associated with marriage."}
mistral_translation: Without having a wife, a person saves oóyọ́ (a type of expense or financial burden)
mistral_interpretation: Marriage or family responsibilities often come with unavoidable financial costs.
llama_translation: Without having a wife a person spares oóyọ́
llama_interpretation: A person without a partner or family responsibilities has more freedom and resources.

yoruba: Àgbà kì í ṣerée kí-ló-bá-yìí-wá?
english_literal: An elderly person does not engage in the type of play that provokes the comment, “What brought all this about?”
interpretation_gold: Elders should show decorum.
deepseek_translation: An elder does not engage in frivolity, what brought this about?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that elders should act with dignity and wisdom, questioning any behavior that seems out of character.
claude_translation: An elder does not play and ask 'what brought this about?'
claude_interpretation: Elders should act with wisdom and foresight, understanding the consequences of their actions rather than behaving carelessly and then wondering about the results.
gemini_translation: An elder does not play the game of 'what did you bring with this?'
gemini_interpretation: Elders are expected to act with wisdom and maturity, not with childish or petty demands for gifts or favors.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "An elder does not play the game of 'what did you bring with this?'", "interpretation": "Elders are expected to act with wisdom and maturity, not with childish or petty demands for gifts or favors."}
mistral_translation: An elder does not run a race to come here and ask, 'What brought me here?'
mistral_interpretation: Elders act with purpose and foresight, not recklessly or without consideration of consequences.
llama_translation: Will an elder not know the way to the farm?
llama_interpretation: Experience and age should bring wisdom and knowledge.

yoruba: A kì í yàgò fún ẹlẹ́ṣin àná.
english_literal: One does not get out of the way for a person who rode a horse yesterday.
interpretation_gold: Past glory avails little in the present.
deepseek_translation: We do not build a stable for yesterday's horse.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not waste effort on things that are no longer relevant or useful.
claude_translation: One does not step aside for yesterday's horseman
claude_interpretation: Past achievements or former status do not command present respect or deference.
gemini_translation: One does not make way for yesterday's horse rider.
gemini_interpretation: One should not give undue respect or deference to someone whose power or influence has waned.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not make way for yesterday's horse rider.", "interpretation": "One should not give undue respect or deference to someone whose power or influence has waned."}
mistral_translation: We do not make a stable for yesterday's horse-rider.
mistral_interpretation: One should not waste resources preparing for what has already passed or is no longer relevant.
llama_translation: We do not make a road for a stubborn horse.
llama_interpretation: One should not go out of their way to accommodate someone who is being obstinate or uncooperative.

yoruba: Àṣejù baba àṣetẹ́; ẹ̀tẹ́ ní ńgbẹ̀hìn àṣejù; àgbàlagbà tó wẹ̀wù àṣejù ẹ̀tẹ́ ni yó fi rí.
english_literal: Lack of moderation is the father of disgrace; disgrace comes of immoderation; a grown person who clothes himself in immoderation will find disgrace.
interpretation_gold: Immoderation leads to disgrace.
deepseek_translation: Excess is the father of moderation; moderation follows excess; an elder who wears excess will see moderation.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that experiencing excess leads to the wisdom of moderation.
claude_translation: Excess is the father of deception; deception follows behind excess; an elder who wears the garment of excess will find deception.
claude_interpretation: Excessive behavior leads to dishonesty and ultimately brings shame and downfall to those who indulge in it.
gemini_translation: Excess is the father of disgrace; disgrace follows excess; an elder who wears the garment of excess will surely find disgrace.
gemini_interpretation: Moderation is key, as overindulgence or extremism, especially in an elder, inevitably leads to shame and dishonor.
mistral_translation: Excess is the father of regret; regret follows excess; an elder who dresses in excess will be mocked by regret.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive behavior leads to negative consequences and should be avoided to prevent future regret.
llama_translation: The one who eats the leftover of the leftover is the one who eats the leftover of the leftover; the elder who sees the leftover of the leftover is the one who eats it.
llama_interpretation: Those who are patient and humble will ultimately benefit from the leftovers of others.

yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀ẹ́ ní òun ò lè fún wàrà, ṣùgbọ́n òún lè yí i dànù.
english_literal: The leper says he may not be able to squeeze out milk, but he can spill it.
interpretation_gold: Even feckless people can cause some damage.
deepseek_translation: Adete cannot give milk, but he can spill it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes those who cannot contribute positively but are quick to destroy or waste what others have provided.
claude_translation: The leper says he cannot give milk, but he can spill it
claude_interpretation: Those who claim they cannot help or contribute positively often have the ability to cause harm or destruction.
gemini_translation: The leper says he cannot give milk, but he can spill it.
gemini_interpretation: Even those who cannot contribute positively can still cause harm or destruction.
mistral_translation: Adẹtẹ says he cannot give butter, but he can make it disappear.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights hypocrisy or deception, where someone claims inability to help but secretly undermines or wastes the very thing they refuse to share.
llama_translation: The one who has a crown cannot give it to a monkey, but he can remove it from his head.
llama_interpretation: A leader or person of authority should not relinquish their power or position to someone unworthy or unqualified.

yoruba: A-báni-gbé kì í yáná; a-bọ̀rìṣà kì í sun òtútù; ẹyin gẹ́gẹ́ kì í gbé àwùjọ́; ilé kannáà ni wọ́n kọ́ fún àwọn mẹ́tẹ̀ẹ̀ta.
english_literal: A guest does not warm himself by the fire; a priest or priestess does not sleep in the cold; a delicate egg does not live in a crowd; the same house was built for all three.
interpretation_gold: Know yourself and your place.
deepseek_translation: The one who carries a corpse does not stagger; the one who carries a deity does not feel cold; the eggs of the guinea fowl do not hatch in public; the same house was built for the three of them.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that those entrusted with sacred or important duties must perform them with dignity and discretion, regardless of challenges.
claude_translation: One who helps others carry burdens does not lack support; one who serves the gods does not sleep in cold; eggs in a basket do not carry the community; the same house was built for all three.
claude_interpretation: Those who serve others and the divine receive protection and support in return, but individual efforts alone cannot sustain a whole community - we all share the same fundamental shelter and interdependence.
gemini_translation: One who lives with us does not make a fire; one who worships an idol does not sleep in the cold; a fragile egg does not stay in a crowd; the same house was built for all three of them.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that certain individuals or things are inherently incompatible with specific situations or environments, suggesting that their nature dictates their appropriate place or behavior.
mistral_translation: One who carries a load does not walk with a torch; a worshipper of the gods does not sleep in the cold; geese do not live together in a group; it is the same house they built for all three.
mistral_interpretation: Despite individual differences or circumstances, people often share the same fundamental conditions or outcomes in life.
llama_translation: The one who doesn't want to be carried doesn't cry; the one who doesn't want to be worshipped doesn't make a shrine; the one who doesn't want to be a chief doesn't build a palace; it is the house that is built for the one who is destined to be a king.
llama_interpretation: One's destiny is predetermined and cannot be forced or fabricated.

yoruba: Àgbá òfìfo ní ńpariwo; àpò tó kún fówó kì í dún.
english_literal: It is an empty barrel that is noisy; a sack full of money makes no sound.
interpretation_gold: Empty barrels make the most noise.
deepseek_translation: The empty barrel makes the loudest noise; a full purse does not rattle.
deepseek_interpretation: Those who are truly knowledgeable or wealthy do not boast, while the ignorant or empty often make the most noise.
claude_translation: An empty elder makes noise; a bag full of money does not make sound.
claude_interpretation: Truly wealthy or knowledgeable people are quiet and humble, while those with little substance make the most noise.
gemini_translation: An empty barrel makes a lot of noise; a full money bag does not make a sound.
gemini_interpretation: Those who are truly wealthy or knowledgeable often do not boast, while those who lack substance tend to be loud and showy.
mistral_translation: The empty barrel makes the most noise; a bag full of money does not make a sound
mistral_interpretation: Those who lack substance or wisdom often speak the loudest, while the truly knowledgeable or wealthy remain quiet and unassuming
llama_translation: The elderly one is not a fool; the bag that is full does not make noise
llama_interpretation: Wisdom and knowledge are not measured by how much one boasts or shows off.

yoruba: A kì í mọ̀-ọ́ rò bí ẹlẹ́jọ́.
english_literal: One never knows how to present it like the owner of the case.
interpretation_gold: No one can know better than the person itself where it hurts most and what relief is needed.
deepseek_translation: We do not know how to dance like the owner of the drum.
deepseek_interpretation: One cannot match the skill or expertise of the person who truly owns or understands something.
claude_translation: One does not know matters like a witness
claude_interpretation: A witness or someone who has experienced something firsthand has deeper knowledge than those who only hear about it secondhand.
gemini_translation: One does not know how to argue it like the owner of the case.
gemini_interpretation: People are most knowledgeable and passionate about their own experiences and concerns.
mistral_translation: We do not know the thoughts of a plaintiff (litigant) as if we were the one in dispute.
mistral_interpretation: One cannot fully understand another person's perspective or motives, especially in a conflict, without being in their position.
llama_translation: We do not know the depth of a river like the fish.
llama_interpretation: One who is deeply involved in a situation has a better understanding of it than an outsider.

yoruba: A kì í dàgbà má làáyà; ibi ayé bá báni là ńjẹ ẹ́.
english_literal: One does not become an adult and yet lack courage; one lives life as it finds one.
interpretation_gold: One should do what is fitting for one's station in life.
deepseek_translation: One does not grow up without scars; wherever life touches one, it leaves a mark.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that life's challenges and experiences inevitably shape and leave lasting impacts on a person.
claude_translation: One does not grow old without having courage; wherever life meets us is where we eat it.
claude_interpretation: Maturity brings the wisdom and courage to face life's challenges wherever they arise, adapting to circumstances rather than avoiding them.
gemini_translation: One does not grow old without having a chest; one eats where life meets them.
gemini_interpretation: One must adapt and make the best of their circumstances as they age and life unfolds.
mistral_translation: One does not grow old and remain cowardly; where life places you is what you eat
mistral_interpretation: Courage is expected to develop with age, and one must adapt to life's circumstances to survive or thrive.
llama_translation: We don't grow old in the market; it's at home we grow old and eat it.
llama_interpretation: One's true character is revealed in the comfort of their own home, not in public.

yoruba: A kì í dá ọwọ́ lé ohun tí a ò lè gbé.
english_literal: One does not lay one's hands on a load one cannot lift.
interpretation_gold: One should not overreach.
deepseek_translation: One does not place a hand on what one cannot carry.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not attempt what is beyond your capability.
claude_translation: One does not put hands on what one cannot carry
claude_interpretation: Don't attempt tasks or take on responsibilities that are beyond your capacity or ability to handle.
gemini_translation: One does not put their hand on what they cannot lift.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to undertake tasks or responsibilities that are beyond one's capabilities.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not put their hand on what they cannot lift.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to undertake tasks or responsibilities that are beyond one's capabilities."}
mistral_translation: We do not place our hand on something we cannot carry
mistral_interpretation: One should not take on responsibilities or burdens beyond their capacity
llama_translation: We do not put our hands on what we cannot carry
llama_interpretation: One should not take on more responsibility than they can handle.

yoruba: À ńwá ẹni tí a ó fọmọ fún, olòṣì ńyọjú.
english_literal: We seek a person to give a child to (in marriage) and a worthless person presents himself.
interpretation_gold: People should know their place and not over-rate themselves.
deepseek_translation: We are searching for someone to marry, the leper is grinning.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against settling for unsuitable partners out of desperation.
claude_translation: We are looking for someone to give a child to, the poor person is showing interest
claude_interpretation: Those who lack resources are often the most eager to take on responsibilities they cannot handle.
gemini_translation: We are looking for someone to give a child to, the poor person is showing their face.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony of someone seeking a benefit or opportunity when they are clearly unsuitable or ill-equipped for it.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We are looking for someone to give a child to, the poor person is showing their face.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the irony of someone seeking a benefit or opportunity when they are clearly unsuitable or ill-equipped for it."}
mistral_translation: We are searching for someone to adopt a child, while the poor person is rejoicing.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the irony of overlooking those in need while seeking help from others who may not be as willing or suitable.
