gemini_interpretation: People tend to gravitate towards and thrive in environments that are conducive to their nature or needs.
mistral_translation: The place where salt is applied is where it stings.
mistral_interpretation: One often feels the consequences of their actions most where they have caused harm or offense.
llama_translation: The place where we throw away yam peels is where they sprout.
llama_interpretation: One's careless or discarded actions can still have unintended consequences.

yoruba: Ilé kì í jó kí baálé ilé tàkakà.
english_literal: A house does not burn while the landlord lounges with indifference.
interpretation_gold: One must not ignore matters of grave concern to one.
deepseek_translation: A house does not burn down and leave the owner of the house destitute.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes resilience and the idea that one will always find a way to recover from misfortune.
claude_translation: A house does not burn while the head of the house is present and alert
claude_interpretation: A responsible leader prevents disaster through vigilance and proper oversight of their domain.
gemini_translation: A house does not burn while the head of the house stands akimbo.
gemini_interpretation: A leader or person in charge must take immediate and active responsibility when a crisis occurs.
mistral_translation: A house does not burn so that the owner of the house can warm his hands
mistral_interpretation: Misfortune is not wished upon someone just to benefit from their suffering
llama_translation: A house does not collapse until the owner of the house is exhausted
llama_interpretation: A person's strength and resilience can hold together a difficult situation, but once they are exhausted, the situation may collapse.

yoruba: Idà ńwó ilé ara ẹ̀ ó ní òún ḿba àkọ̀ jẹ́.
english_literal: The sword is destroying its own home, and it says it is ruining the scabbard.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person whose actions will eventually recoil on him/her, even though the person thinks that he/she is hurting others.
deepseek_translation: The sword in the house of another does not say it helps the cutlass to eat.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not interfere in matters that do not concern them.
claude_translation: The sword is destroying its own house yet it claims to be eating with the sheath
claude_interpretation: One cannot claim to be at peace or in harmony while simultaneously causing destruction to their own foundation or family.
gemini_translation: The sword is destroying its own sheath, yet it says it is spoiling the scabbard.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb means that one is harming themselves while blaming or believing they are harming another.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The sword is destroying its own sheath, yet it says it is spoiling the scabbard.", "interpretation": "This proverb means that one is harming themselves while blaming or believing they are harming another."}
mistral_translation: The sword boasts of the house of its owner, saying it will make charcoal of it
mistral_interpretation: A tool or weapon should not take credit for its owner's achievements or bring harm to the one who wields it.
llama_translation: A sword in the house of a madman is not a plaything.
llama_interpretation: Dangerous things should be handled with care and caution.

yoruba: Ìgbà wo ni Mákùú ò níí kú? Mákùú ò mọ awo ó ḿbú ọpa; Mákùú ò mọ ìwẹ̀ ó ḿbọ́ sódò.
english_literal: When will (or how can) Maku avoid the danger of dying? Maku does not know the mysteries of the cult yet he joins in its vows; Maku does not know how to swim and yet he jumps into the river.
interpretation_gold: A person who will not cooperate in safeguarding himself/herself frustrates the efforts of others.
deepseek_translation: When will Makuu not die? Makuu does not know swimming but enters the water; Makuu does not know rafting but boards the canoe.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against engaging in activities beyond one's knowledge or ability, as it leads to inevitable failure or danger.
claude_translation: When will Makuu not die? Makuu does not know divination yet carries a divination staff; Makuu does not know how to swim yet goes to the river.
claude_interpretation: A person who pretends to have skills they lack will eventually face consequences that expose their incompetence.
gemini_translation: When will the foolish person not die? The foolish person does not know the secret and is insulting the staff; the foolish person does not know how to swim and is jumping into the river.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the self-destructive nature of ignorance and recklessness, suggesting that those who act without knowledge or caution will inevitably face negative consequences.
mistral_translation: When will Makuu not die? Makuu does not know the secret of the medicine that wards off the staff; Makuu does not know the book that blocks the river.
mistral_interpretation: Ignorance and refusal to learn or seek wisdom will inevitably lead to failure or downfall.
llama_translation: When did Makùú die? Makùú did not know the secret, he died of a gunshot; Makùú did not know the medicine, he died of a boil.
llama_interpretation: One who lacks knowledge or understanding of a situation will suffer the consequences.

yoruba: Ìjọba ńpè ọ́ o ní ò ḿmu gààrí lọ́wọ́; ta ní ni ọ́, ta ní ni omi tí o fi ḿmu gààrí?
english_literal: The government summons you and you say you are busy eating cassava grains soaked in water; who owns you, and who owns the water with which you are eating the cassava?
interpretation_gold: When the law summons, one has no option but to heed the summon.
deepseek_translation: The government is calling you that you don't carry cassava in your hand; who are you, who is the water you use to carry cassava?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes those who blame others while ignoring their own role in a problem.
claude_translation: The government is calling you but you say you are drinking garri; who owns you, who owns the water you use to drink garri?
claude_interpretation: When authority calls, one should not make excuses using things that ultimately belong to or are controlled by that same authority.
gemini_translation: The government is calling you, and you say you are holding gari; who are you, and who is the water with which you are drinking gari?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the audacity of someone who prioritizes a trivial personal activity over a significant and urgent call to duty or authority.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The government is calling you, and you say you are holding gari; who are you, and who is the water with which you are drinking gari?", "interpretation": "This proverb questions the audacity of someone who prioritizes a trivial personal activity over a significant and urgent call to duty or authority."}
mistral_translation: The government calls you saying you did not buy gari with the money; whose is it, whose is the water used to soak the gari?
mistral_interpretation: The proverb critiques those in power who blame others for misusing resources while ignoring their own role in enabling or benefiting from the misuse.
llama_translation: The king calls you and you say you are going to the stream; who is it that calls you, who is it that calls the water that you are going to fetch?
llama_interpretation: One should not ignore or disrespect those who have authority or power over them.

yoruba: The likeness of an elephant is not scarce in Alọ.
interpretation_gold: Nobody is one of a kind.
deepseek_translation: The likeness of an elephant is not scarce in Alọ.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that what is being sought after or discussed is common and easily found in the referenced place (Alọ).
claude_translation: The likeness of an elephant is not scarce in Alọ.
claude_interpretation: Where something is abundant or common, it loses its special value or significance.
gemini_translation: The likeness of an elephant is not scarce in Alọ.
gemini_interpretation: Something that is common or easily found in its natural habitat is not considered rare or special.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The likeness of an elephant is not scarce in Alọ.", "interpretation": "Something that is common or easily found in its natural habitat is not considered rare or special."}
mistral_translation: The image of an elephant is not rare in Alọ
mistral_interpretation: This proverb highlights that something or someone of great importance or reputation is well-known and easily recognized in a particular place.
llama_translation: The likeness of an elephant is not scarce in Alọ
llama_interpretation: Even in a small or seemingly insignificant place, one can find something remarkable or impressive.

yoruba: Ibi tí a ti ńpìtàn ká tó jogún, ká mọ̀ pé ogún ibẹ̀ ò kanni.
english_literal: Where one must recite genealogies in order to establish one's claim to inheritance, one should know that one really has no claim to patrimony there.
interpretation_gold: One need not go to great lengths to establish one's claim if it is legitimate.
deepseek_translation: Where we tell stories before inheriting, let us know that the inheritance there is not enough.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against premature celebration or counting on unsecured benefits.
claude_translation: Where we are telling stories before we inherit, we should know that the inheritance there is not for us
claude_interpretation: When there are delays or complications in receiving what should rightfully be yours, it's a sign that it may not be meant for you.
gemini_translation: Where we are narrating history before inheriting, let us know that the inheritance there does not concern us.
gemini_interpretation: If you have to recount a long history to justify your claim to an inheritance, it likely means you are not the rightful heir.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Where we are narrating history before inheriting, let us know that the inheritance there does not concern us.", "interpretation": "If you have to recount a long history to justify your claim to an inheritance, it likely means you are not the rightful heir."}
mistral_translation: Where we have been telling stories before inheriting, we should know that the war there is not small.
mistral_interpretation: One should be aware of the challenges or conflicts in a place before committing to it or claiming its benefits.
llama_translation: The place where we were playing has become a forest, let's go and see if the forest is still the same
llama_interpretation: Change is inevitable, and one must adapt to new circumstances.

yoruba: Ìpéǹpéjú ò ní enini; àgbàlagbà irùngbọ̀n ò ṣe òlòó.
english_literal: The eyelashes do not make dew; a venerable old beard does not behave like an ingenue.
interpretation_gold: Some habits are fitting for one's station, while others are not.
deepseek_translation: A small pot does not have an owner; an old, cracked pot is not useful.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that things of little value or in poor condition are often neglected or discarded.
claude_translation: Haste has no owner; an elder does not act carelessly
claude_interpretation: Wisdom and maturity require patience and careful consideration rather than rushing into decisions.
gemini_translation: The eyelid has no dew; a bearded elder is not a fool.
gemini_interpretation: Just as the eyelid is naturally dry, a person's appearance, like a beard, does not inherently indicate their wisdom or foolishness.
mistral_translation: The young palm fruit has no sap; the elder with a walking stick does not act like a rich person
mistral_interpretation: Youthful inexperience and elderly humility both prevent one from pretending to have what they do not possess
llama_translation: The one who has a boil does not have a skin; the elder does not make a calabash from a gourd.
llama_interpretation: One should not expect someone with their own problems to help solve yours.

yoruba: Ìsáǹsá ò yọ ẹ̀gún; ìsáǹsá kì í káwo ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: The fugitive does not stop to pull a thorn “from his/her feet”; the fugitive does not stop to clear dinner dishes.
interpretation_gold: A person who has committed a crime would not wait around to be caught.
deepseek_translation: The squirrel does not peel the yam; the squirrel does not stir the soup.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not interfere in matters that do not concern them or are beyond their responsibility.
claude_translation: Running away does not remove thorns; running away does not wash hands of soup.
claude_interpretation: Avoiding problems or responsibilities does not make them disappear or absolve you of accountability.
gemini_translation: The runaway does not remove thorns; the runaway does not stir soup.
gemini_interpretation: A person who avoids their responsibilities will not contribute to solving problems or achieving success.
mistral_translation: The pepper does not outlast the locust bean; the pepper does not season the soup.
mistral_interpretation: A person or thing of lesser value or influence cannot surpass or replace one of greater importance.
llama_translation: The needle does not sew the thread; the needle does not sew the cloth.
llama_interpretation: One must know one's limitations and not attempt to do what is beyond one's capabilities.

yoruba: Ibi tí ayé bá ẹni ni a ti ńjẹ ẹ̀.
english_literal: Where life catches up with one, there one lives it.
interpretation_gold: One lives according to the conditions one finds oneself in.
deepseek_translation: Where the world meets one is where one eats.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb means that one must adapt to the circumstances they find themselves in to survive or thrive.
claude_translation: Where life meets one is where one eats it
claude_interpretation: One must accept and make the best of whatever circumstances life presents to them.
gemini_translation: Where life meets one, there one eats it.
gemini_interpretation: One must adapt and make the best of whatever circumstances life presents.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Where life meets one, there one eats it.", "interpretation": "One must adapt and make the best of whatever circumstances life presents."}
mistral_translation: Wherever the world takes you is where you will eat.
mistral_interpretation: One must adapt to and accept the circumstances or opportunities life presents, as they determine one's sustenance and success.
llama_translation: Where the world has caught up with someone, that is where we eat the corn.
llama_interpretation: One's circumstances or challenges in life are what ultimately define their reality.

yoruba: Ìwà ní ńjọ oníwà lójú.
english_literal: Character is always remarkable (or good) in the opinion of its owner.
interpretation_gold: One naturally approves of one's own character.
deepseek_translation: Character is what judges the owner of character in the face.
deepseek_interpretation: One's behavior ultimately determines how they are perceived and judged by others.
claude_translation: Character is what makes the person of good character beautiful in the eyes.
claude_interpretation: A person's good character and behavior is what makes them truly attractive and respected by others.
gemini_translation: Character is what resembles the owner of the character in the eyes.
gemini_interpretation: A person's character is a reflection of who they truly are.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Character is what resembles the owner of the character in the eyes.", "interpretation": "A person's character is a reflection of who they truly are."}
mistral_translation: Character is what judges the owner of character in the face.
mistral_interpretation: A person's true nature will eventually reveal and reflect their actions and reputation.
llama_translation: Character is what recognizes a person of character
llama_interpretation: A person of good character can recognize and appreciate the good character of others.

yoruba: Ibi tí a fi ara sí lara ńgbé.
english_literal: Wherever one situates the body, there it inhabits.
interpretation_gold: One should confine oneself and one's activities to the appropriate spheres.
deepseek_translation: The place where we place ourselves is where we live.
deepseek_interpretation: Your choices determine your circumstances.
claude_translation: Where one places oneself is where the body lives
claude_interpretation: A person's circumstances and experiences are determined by the choices and positions they take in life.
gemini_translation: Where one puts their body, there the body rests.
gemini_interpretation: One's well-being and comfort are found where they choose to settle or dedicate themselves.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Where one puts their body, there the body rests.", "interpretation": "One's well-being and comfort are found where they choose to settle or dedicate themselves."}
mistral_translation: The place where one uses oneself as a tool is where one carries oneself.
mistral_interpretation: One must take personal responsibility and rely on one's own efforts to achieve success.
llama_translation: The place where we use our body to lean is where we rest
llama_interpretation: One should find comfort and rest in the support of family and loved ones.

yoruba: Ìwọ̀fà ní ḿmú ìwọ̀fà jó.
english_literal: A pawned person always dances with a pawned person.
interpretation_gold: People should know who share their station and confine their dealings with them.
deepseek_translation: The debtor is the one who makes the debtor dance.
deepseek_interpretation: The person in debt is often at the mercy of the creditor's demands.
claude_translation: A debtor makes another debtor dance.
claude_interpretation: Those who are in similar difficult situations often exploit or manipulate each other instead of showing compassion.
gemini_translation: A pawn makes a pawn dance.
gemini_interpretation: Those who are indebted or in a similar predicament often influence or control others in the same situation.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A pawn makes a pawn dance.", "interpretation": "Those who are indebted or in a similar predicament often influence or control others in the same situation."}
mistral_translation: The creditor is the one who dances with the creditor's debt.
mistral_interpretation: The person who owes a debt is the one who suffers the consequences or burden of it.
llama_translation: The thread of a needle is where the needle is used.
llama_interpretation: One's usefulness is often tied to their specific role or purpose.

yoruba: Ìrẹ́jẹ ò sí nínúu fọ́tò; bí o bá ṣe jókòó ni o ó bàá ara-à rẹ.
english_literal: There is no cheating in photography; it is just as you sit that you will find your image.
interpretation_gold: One's public perception depends ultimately on one's self-presentation.
deepseek_translation: There is no dancing in a pit; if you sit down, you will meet yourself.
deepseek_interpretation: One must face the consequences of their actions or inactions.
claude_translation: There is no adjustment in a photograph; however you sit is how you will remain with yourself.
claude_interpretation: Your actions and choices become permanent records that you must live with, so conduct yourself wisely from the beginning.
gemini_translation: There is no cheating in a photograph; as you sit, so you will find yourself.
gemini_interpretation: A photograph captures reality as it is, just as one's actions and choices determine their outcomes.
mistral_translation: There is no profit in a muddy puddle; if you sit in it, you will only dirty yourself.
mistral_interpretation: Avoid situations or associations that offer no benefit and will only bring harm or disgrace to you.
llama_translation: There is no profit inside a photograph; if you sit on it, it will only tear your cloth.
llama_interpretation: One should not expect tangible benefits from something that is merely a representation or appearance.

yoruba: Ìjàkùmọ̀ kì í rin ọ̀sán, ẹni a bí ire kì í rin òru.
english_literal: The wild cat never roams in daylight; a well-bred person does not wander around in the night time.
interpretation_gold: People who care about their reputation should stay away from questionable actions.
deepseek_translation: The bat does not walk in the daytime, the one born with good fortune does not walk at night.
deepseek_interpretation: Those blessed with good fortune avoid danger or unfavorable circumstances.
claude_translation: A bat does not walk in the daytime, a person born for good does not walk at night.
claude_interpretation: Good people avoid situations and times that could lead them into trouble or compromise their reputation.
gemini_translation: A leopard does not walk in the daytime, a well-born person does not walk at night.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that individuals of good character or status avoid engaging in activities or behaviors that are considered inappropriate or dangerous, just as certain animals have specific times for their activities.
mistral_translation: The grasshopper does not walk in the afternoon; one born to good fortune does not walk at night
mistral_interpretation: A person destined for success avoids unnecessary risks or dangerous situations
llama_translation: The one who is not a farmer does not go to the farm, the one who is not born for good fortune does not sleep in the morning.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on their own destiny and not interfere with or envy the fortunes of others.

yoruba: Jẹ́jẹ́ leégún àgbà ńjó.
english_literal: Sedately is the way an elderly masquerader dances.
interpretation_gold: Grown-up people should behave in a decorous manner.
deepseek_translation: The elder's bones are dancing.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that disrespecting elders can lead to unforeseen consequences, as their wisdom and influence remain powerful even in old age.
claude_translation: Gently is how the adult masquerader dances.
claude_interpretation: Wisdom and maturity are demonstrated through calm, measured actions rather than rushed or aggressive behavior.
gemini_translation: Gently the elder's masquerade dances.
gemini_interpretation: Elders approach matters with caution and wisdom, avoiding haste or recklessness.
mistral_translation: Let the masquerade of the elder dance gently.
mistral_interpretation: Respect and caution should be shown when dealing with elders or those in positions of authority.
llama_translation: It is the elderly who dance with the masquerade
llama_interpretation: Respect and deference should be given to elders, as they have the wisdom and experience to handle complex situations.

yoruba: Kò rà, kò lówó lọ́wọ́, ó ńwú tutu níwájú onítumpulu.
english_literal: He does not buy, he has no money, yet he sits sulkily before the seller of bean fritters.
interpretation_gold: Said of people reluctant to accept the fact that they cannot have what they wish.
deepseek_translation: He does not buy, he does not have money in hand, he is sweating in front of the seller.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes those who pretend to have resources they lack, leading to unnecessary stress or embarrassment.
claude_translation: He doesn't buy, he has no money in hand, yet he dies of cold in front of the blanket seller
claude_interpretation: People sometimes suffer unnecessarily by failing to seek help or solutions that are readily available to them.
gemini_translation: He did not buy, he does not have money, yet he is swelling up in front of the palm wine tapper.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who is boastful or acts important despite lacking the means or justification to do so.
mistral_translation: He did not buy, he has no money in his hand, yet he is fanning himself cool in front of the peanut seller
mistral_interpretation: It warns against pretending to have what one lacks or acting beyond one's means to impress others.
llama_translation: No rags, no tattered clothes, yet he is shivering in front of the fire
llama_interpretation: One's appearance or circumstances do not always reflect their true state or feelings.

yoruba: Kékeré lọ̀pọ̀lọ́ fi ga ju ilẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: The toad is only slightly taller than the earth.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who behave as though they are superior to others while they have little reason to believe so.
deepseek_translation: The small antelope surpasses the ground in height.
deepseek_interpretation: Even the smallest or weakest can achieve greatness with effort.
claude_translation: It is by being small that the frog jumps higher than the ground
claude_interpretation: Small size or humble beginnings can be an advantage that enables one to achieve great things.
gemini_translation: It is by being small that the toad is taller than the ground.
gemini_interpretation: Even the smallest or seemingly insignificant can possess a unique advantage or perspective that elevates them above others.
mistral_translation: It is with small steps that the antelope surpasses the ground.
mistral_interpretation: Consistent small efforts lead to significant achievements over time.
llama_translation: A small ant can carry a heavy load to the ground.
llama_interpretation: Even the smallest or seemingly insignificant person can accomplish great things with determination and effort.

yoruba: Kò sí ẹni tó dùn mọ́ àfi orí ẹni.
english_literal: There is no one pleased “by one's success” except one's head.
interpretation_gold: Few people genuinely wish that one should succeed.
deepseek_translation: There is no one sweet to another except one's own head.
deepseek_interpretation: People prioritize their own interests above others'.
claude_translation: There is no one who is sweet/pleasant to know except one's own head.
claude_interpretation: No one understands or cares for you better than yourself.
gemini_translation: There is no one as sweet as one's own head.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of self-reliance and the inherent value of one's own efforts and individuality.
mistral_translation: There is no one who tastes sweeter than one's own head.
mistral_interpretation: One should value and prioritize their own well-being and interests above others'.
llama_translation: There is no one who is sweet like oneself
llama_interpretation: One's own interests and well-being are always a priority.

yoruba: Kí ni orí ńṣe tí èjìká ò lè ṣe? Èjìká ru ẹrù ó gba ọ̀ọ́dúnrún; orí ta tiẹ̀ ní ogúnlúgba.
english_literal: What can the head do that the shoulder cannot do? The shoulder carried a load and earned three hundred cowries; the head sold its own for two hundred and twenty cowries.
interpretation_gold: If a person has more power and standing than one, one should not be foolish enough to think the person cannot accomplish what one has accomplished.
deepseek_translation: What is the head doing that the shoulders cannot do? The shoulders carry loads and bear the yoke; the head sells caps in the marketplace.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the importance of each person's unique role and contributions, emphasizing that everyone has their own strengths and responsibilities.
claude_translation: What is the head doing that the shoulder cannot do? The shoulder carries a load and receives twenty cowries; the head sells itself for only twenty-five.
claude_interpretation: Hard work and practical contribution are often more valuable and better rewarded than mere status or position.
gemini_translation: What is the head doing that the shoulder cannot do? The shoulder carried a load and received three hundred; the head sold its own for two hundred thousand.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the disparity in value or reward for different types of effort or contributions, suggesting that some roles are inherently more valued or lucrative than others, even if both involve labor.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "What is the head doing that the shoulder cannot do? The shoulder carried a load and received three hundred; the head sold its own for two hundred thousand.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the disparity in value or reward for different types of effort or contributions, suggesting that some roles are inherently more valued or lucrative than others, even if both involve labor."}
mistral_translation: What is the head doing that the shoulder cannot do? The shoulder carries the load and takes sixty; the head that owns it gets one hundred and twenty.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights that leadership or responsibility often comes with greater rewards, even if others share the burden.
llama_translation: What can the head do that the foot cannot do? The foot kicks the ball and scores a goal; the head butts the ball in a corner kick.
llama_interpretation: Everyone has their unique role and contribution to make, regardless of their perceived importance or status.

yoruba: Kí ni ó yá àpọ́n lórí tó fiṣu síná tó ńsúfèé pé “bí a ti ńṣe ni inú ḿbí wọn”?
english_literal: What has the bachelor to feel superior about, such that while he is roasting yams he is whistling the song, “What one does fills them with jealousy”?
interpretation_gold: Said of people who are arrogant even though they have no basis for pride.
deepseek_translation: What is it that the pot on the fire is murmuring about, saying 'this is how we do it in our own place'?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against blindly following traditions or customs without understanding their purpose or relevance.
claude_translation: What made the bachelor so bold that he put yam on fire and is blowing on it saying 'this is how we do it, it makes them angry'?
claude_interpretation: Someone who lacks experience or proper knowledge should not act with overconfidence and pretend to be an expert.
gemini_translation: What made the bachelor put yam in the fire and whistle, saying, 'As we are doing it, they are getting angry'?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the reason for someone's boastful and provocative behavior, especially when it seems unwarranted or aimed at causing envy.
mistral_translation: What is the use of a bag on the head that roasts yams and then complains, 'They are doing this inside me'?
mistral_interpretation: It warns against causing one's own problems and then blaming others for the consequences.
llama_translation: What is the cloth on the head of the one who is urinating and saying 'this is how we do it in our house'?
llama_interpretation: One should not pretend to be doing something correctly when in fact they are not.

yoruba: Ká wí ogún, ká wí ọgbọ̀n, “Ng ò fẹ́, ng ò gbà” laṣiwèré fi ńpẹ̀kun ọ̀ràn.
english_literal: Whether one speaks twenty times or speaks thirty times, “I do not like it, and I will not accept it” is how the imbecile ends the discussion.
interpretation_gold: The incorrigible person will never listen to reason.
deepseek_translation: To say twenty, to say thirty, "I don't want, I don't accept" is how the madman ends a matter.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that stubborn refusal to compromise or listen to reason leads to foolish outcomes.
claude_translation: Whether we speak of medicine or wisdom, 'I don't want it, I don't accept it' is how a fool ends every matter.
claude_interpretation: A foolish person rejects all advice and help offered to them, regardless of its value or necessity.
gemini_translation: To say twenty, to say thirty, 'I don't want, I don't accept' is how a foolish person ends a matter.
gemini_interpretation: A foolish person's stubborn refusal to compromise or consider other options prematurely ends discussions and opportunities.
mistral_translation: Whether we say twenty or thirty, it is the one who says 'I don’t want it, I don’t accept it' that eventually compounds the issue
mistral_interpretation: Stubborn refusal to cooperate or accept reasonable offers often leads to greater problems or complications
llama_translation: We said war, we said fight, “I neither want nor accept” is the name the lazy person gives to a matter.
llama_interpretation: A person who is unwilling to take action or make a decision will often claim to be neutral or uninterested.

yoruba: Ká ríni sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ò dàbí-i ká sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ká gbà.
english_literal: Having people to advise one is nothing like knowing how to take advice.
interpretation_gold: Nobody can help anyone who will not help himself or herself.
deepseek_translation: To have teeth and chew for someone is not like chewing for someone to swallow.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that true help involves enabling others to help themselves rather than doing everything for them.
claude_translation: To see something and speak to us about it is not the same as speaking to us so we can receive/accept it
claude_interpretation: There is a significant difference between merely informing someone about something and actually persuading them to accept or believe it.
gemini_translation: To see someone and speak to them is not like speaking to someone and they accept it.
gemini_interpretation: Direct communication does not guarantee acceptance or understanding of the message.
mistral_translation: It is better to discuss something for us than to discuss us and accept it
mistral_interpretation: It is wiser to involve people in decisions that affect them rather than making choices for them without their input.
llama_translation: We should not make noise to wake the sleeping one, lest the sleeping one wakes and catches us.
llama_interpretation: One should not provoke or disturb a potentially powerful person or situation unnecessarily.

yoruba: Ká ríni lóde ò dàbí-i ká báni délé.
english_literal: To see a person in the streets is not the same as going home with the person.
interpretation_gold: To really know a person one must see the person where he/she lives.

claude_translation: To see something outside is not like bringing it home
claude_interpretation: There is a significant difference between merely observing or knowing about something and actually possessing or experiencing it firsthand.
gemini_translation: To see someone outside is not like meeting them at home.
gemini_interpretation: True understanding and connection with a person are best achieved in their personal space, not in public.
mistral_translation: Let us see what is outside does not resemble what we find at home
mistral_interpretation: Appearances or external impressions can be deceiving and should not be trusted without verification.
llama_translation: We do not know the way to the farm, we do not know the way home.
llama_interpretation: One should be prepared for the consequences of one's actions, as they can affect both the journey and the return.

yoruba: Kò-sí-nílé kì í jagun ẹnu tì.
english_literal: He-was-not-at-home never fails to prove his valor with his mouth.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person who vows that had he been around when something happened he would have performed wonders.
deepseek_translation: A person without a home does not engage in a verbal fight.
deepseek_interpretation: One who lacks stability or security should avoid unnecessary conflicts.
claude_translation: One who has nothing at home does not fight a war with mouth closed
claude_interpretation: A person with nothing to lose will speak boldly and take risks because they have no possessions or status to protect.
gemini_translation: Absence does not fight a verbal battle.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot defend themselves or their reputation when they are not present to address accusations or gossip.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Absence does not fight a verbal battle.", "interpretation": "One cannot defend themselves or their reputation when they are not present to address accusations or gossip."}
mistral_translation: There is no household that does not have a mouth war (quarrel).
mistral_interpretation: Every family or community experiences disagreements or conflicts at some point.
llama_translation: One who has no home does not fight with the mouth
llama_interpretation: A person without a stable foundation or resources should not engage in unnecessary conflicts or arguments.

yoruba: Ká wí fún ẹni ká gbọ́; ká sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ká gbà; kà bèrè ọnà lọ́wọ́ èrò tó kù lẹ́hìn kàyè baà lè yẹni.
english_literal: If one is spoken to one should listen; if one is advised one should heed the advice; one should seek direction from straggling wayfarers in order than one's life might be pleasant.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to heed advice, and it is wise to seek direction from those who have greater experience than one does.
deepseek_translation: To speak to someone and they listen; to advise someone and they accept; to ask the way from the remaining thoughts behind life so that one may be guided.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of listening, accepting advice, and seeking wisdom to navigate life successfully.
claude_translation: Let us speak to someone and listen; let us talk to someone and accept; let us ask for directions from the traveler who remains behind so that we may not be disgraced in the world.
claude_interpretation: We should seek advice from experienced people and be willing to listen and accept guidance to avoid making mistakes in life.
gemini_translation: To tell someone to listen; to speak to someone to accept; to ask for directions from a traveler who is behind so that life may be good for one.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to seek advice and learn from others, even those seemingly less experienced, to navigate life successfully.
mistral_translation: Let us speak to someone so they may hear; let us talk to them so they may accept; let us ask for the way from the remaining wisdom left behind so life may be favorable to us.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of seeking and heeding wise counsel to navigate life successfully.
llama_translation: Tell it to the person and let them hear; tell it to the wall and let it receive; but the road that leads to the town of the deaf is not far from the town of the dumb.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of choosing the right audience when communicating, as some people may not listen or understand.

yoruba: Ká wí ká gbà ló yẹ ọmọ èèyàn.
english_literal: To heed advice is what best becomes a human being.
interpretation_gold: One should heed advice.
deepseek_translation: To speak and to listen is proper for a human child.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of both speaking wisely and listening attentively as essential qualities for a well-rounded person.
claude_translation: To speak and to listen is what befits a human being
claude_interpretation: True humanity requires both the ability to express oneself and the wisdom to listen to others.
gemini_translation: To be told and to accept is what befits a human being.
gemini_interpretation: It is proper for a person to listen to advice and accept it.
mistral_translation: Let us say it and let it be accepted as befits a human being.
mistral_interpretation: One should speak respectfully and reasonably so that others may accept their words without offense.
llama_translation: It is the saying that is accepted that is good for a person.
llama_interpretation: A person's reputation is built on the good things that are said about them.

yoruba: Kàkà kí àgbò ké, àgbò a kú.
english_literal: Rather than cry out, the ram will die.
interpretation_gold: A grown man must know how to hide his pain.
deepseek_translation: Rather than the goat bleating, the goat dies.
deepseek_interpretation: It is better to endure hardship silently than to complain and face worse consequences.
claude_translation: Rather than the ram bleating, the ram will die
claude_interpretation: It is better to remain silent in dangerous situations than to speak out and face severe consequences.
gemini_translation: Rather than for the ram to bleat, the ram will die.
gemini_interpretation: It is better to suffer in silence or endure hardship than to complain or reveal weakness.
mistral_translation: Instead of the ram bleating, the ram will die
mistral_interpretation: It is better to speak up or act early to prevent a greater loss or disaster
llama_translation: The ram's horn is not yet dry, the ram has died.
llama_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one's legacy or impact can outlive them.

yoruba: Kí ni apárí ńwá ní ìsọ̀ onígbàjámọ̀?
english_literal: What does a bald man want in the stall of the barber?
interpretation_gold: One should stay out of places where one has no business.
deepseek_translation: What is the bald head looking for in the comb's house?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb humorously points out the futility of seeking something one does not need or cannot use.
claude_translation: What is a bald person looking for in the shop of a barber?
claude_interpretation: Don't seek what you don't need or waste time in places that offer nothing relevant to your situation.
gemini_translation: What is a bald person looking for in a barber's shop?
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to seek something from a place or person that cannot provide it.
mistral_translation: What is the bat searching for in the midst of the lizards?
mistral_interpretation: It warns against meddling in affairs where one does not belong or where one's presence is inappropriate.
llama_translation: What is the meaning of a hat on a deaf person?
llama_interpretation: Something is useless or meaningless if it is not appreciated or utilized by the intended recipient.

yoruba: Kí ni ìbá mú igún dé ọ̀dọ̀-ọ onídìrí?
english_literal: What would take the vulture to the stall of the hair dresser?
interpretation_gold: One should stay away from places where one has no business.
deepseek_translation: What did the vulture bring to the owner of the palm tree?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb questions the motives behind unsolicited favors or gifts, implying they may come with hidden expectations.
claude_translation: What would bring a vulture to the pepper seller?
claude_interpretation: This questions why someone would go where they clearly don't belong or have no business being.
gemini_translation: What would make a vulture go to a barber?
gemini_interpretation: It is unusual for someone to seek help from a professional whose services are irrelevant to their needs.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "What would make a vulture go to a barber?", "interpretation": "It is unusual for someone to seek help from a professional whose services are irrelevant to their needs."}
mistral_translation: What would have made the vulture arrive at the riverbank of the one who has a walking stick?
mistral_interpretation: It warns against unnecessary interference in matters that do not concern you or where you lack authority.
llama_translation: What is it that the vulture uses to arrive at the place of the one who has died?
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the inevitability of death, suggesting that death is a universal fate that awaits everyone.

yoruba: Kàkà ká dọ̀bálẹ̀ fún Gàm̀bàrí, ká rọ́jú ká kú.
english_literal: Rather than prostrate oneself in homage or obeisance to a Hausa person, one should rather die.
interpretation_gold: An expression of Yoruba superciliousness towards the Hausa.
deepseek_translation: Rather than prostrate for Gambari, let us look ahead and die.
deepseek_interpretation: It is better to face hardship with dignity than to submit to oppression.
claude_translation: Rather than prostrate for Gambari, let us lift our faces and die
claude_interpretation: It is better to die with dignity than to submit to humiliation or oppression.
gemini_translation: Rather than prostrating to a Gambari, let us endure and die.
gemini_interpretation: It is better to suffer or die with dignity than to submit to an enemy or oppressor.
mistral_translation: Instead of prostrating for the king, we chose to strain ourselves until we die
mistral_interpretation: It warns against stubbornly refusing wise counsel or proper respect, leading to self-destruction.
llama_translation: The dog is rejoicing for Gambari, the head will die.
llama_interpretation: One's joy can be short-lived if it is rooted in the misfortune of another.

yoruba: Kàkà kí iga akàn ó padà sẹhìn, a kán.
english_literal: Rather than bend backwards, the crab's claws will break.
interpretation_gold: Death is to be preferred to retreat.
deepseek_translation: Rather than the millipede goes backward, it breaks.
deepseek_interpretation: It is better to face challenges head-on than to retreat and suffer greater consequences.
claude_translation: Rather than the crab's claw turning backward, it breaks.
claude_interpretation: It is better to break or fail completely than to retreat or go backward from one's principles or position.
gemini_translation: Rather than the crab's claw going backward, it breaks.
gemini_interpretation: It is better to face challenges head-on and suffer consequences than to retreat or compromise one's principles.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Rather than the crab's claw going backward, it breaks.", "interpretation": "It is better to face challenges head-on and suffer consequences than to retreat or compromise one's principles."}
mistral_translation: Instead of the crab walking backwards, it goes forward
mistral_interpretation: It is better to move forward and face challenges directly rather than retreat or avoid them
llama_translation: When the tortoise's leg is broken, it returns to its shell.
llama_interpretation: One should retreat to a safe place when faced with adversity or danger.

yoruba: Kí ni onígbá ńṣe tí aláwo ò lè ṣe?
english_literal: What is the calabash owner doing that the china plate owner cannot do?
interpretation_gold: Whatever one can accomplish, those better placed or better endowed than one can accomplish also.
deepseek_translation: What is the farmer doing that the diviner cannot do?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the limitations of diviners compared to the practical skills of farmers.
claude_translation: What is the calabash owner doing that the plate owner cannot do?
claude_interpretation: People with different resources or tools can often accomplish the same goals, so one should not feel inferior based on what they possess.
gemini_translation: What is the owner of the calabash doing that the owner of the plate cannot do?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the perceived superiority or exclusivity of one person's actions or abilities over another's, suggesting that similar tasks can often be performed by different individuals.
mistral_translation: What is the potter doing that the diviner cannot do?
mistral_interpretation: Everyone has unique skills and limitations; no one is superior in all things.
llama_translation: What is the Ifá priest doing that the divination tray cannot do?
llama_interpretation: No one is indispensable, as others can perform the same tasks.

yoruba: Kíjìpá laṣọ ọ̀lẹ; òfì laṣọ àgbà; àgbà tí ò ní tòfì a rọ́jú ra kíjìpá.
english_literal: Durable hand-woven cloth is the material for shiftless people; loom-woven cloth is the material for the elders; whichever elder cannot afford loom-woven cloth should strive for durable hand-woven cloth.
interpretation_gold: If one cannot have the perfect thing, one should strive to have at least something.
deepseek_translation: The crab walks sideways; the tortoise walks slowly; the elder who does not walk slowly will walk like the crab.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb advises elders to act with patience and wisdom, as haste can lead to undignified behavior.
claude_translation: Torn cloth is the garment of the lazy person; fine cloth is the garment of the elder; an elder who has no fine cloth will be ashamed to buy torn cloth.
claude_interpretation: People should strive to maintain standards appropriate to their status and age, as falling below expectations brings shame.
gemini_translation: Kijipa is the cloth of the lazy person; ofi is the cloth of the elder; an elder who does not have ofi will reluctantly buy kijipa.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of diligence and preparation, suggesting that those who fail to plan or work hard will eventually have to settle for less desirable alternatives.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Kijipa is the cloth of the lazy person; ofi is the cloth of the elder; an elder who does not have ofi will reluctantly buy kijipa.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the importance of diligence and preparation, suggesting that those who fail to plan or work hard will eventually have to settle for less desirable alternatives."}
mistral_translation: A thief's wrapper is a mere strip of cloth; an elder's wrapper is fine woven cloth; an elder who has no fine woven cloth should be ashamed to wear a mere strip of cloth.
mistral_interpretation: Elders should uphold dignity and responsibility, as their status demands proper conduct and appearance.
llama_translation: The cloth of the poor is torn; the cloth of the elder is tattered; an elder whose cloth is not tattered is a poor person.
llama_interpretation: True wealth and status are not measured by material possessions or appearance.

yoruba: Kí ni àǹfàníi kẹ̀tẹ̀kẹ̀tẹ̀ lára kẹ́tẹ́kẹ́tẹ́ à-gùn-fẹsẹ̀-wọ́lẹ̀?
english_literal: What is the point of bragging on account of an ass which when one rides on it one's feet drag on the ground?
interpretation_gold: It is pointless to make too much of a virtually worthless thing.
deepseek_translation: What is the benefit of a long neck on a kneeling camel?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb questions the usefulness of an advantage that cannot be utilized in a given situation.
claude_translation: What benefit does a small donkey get from a donkey that steps its feet on the ground?
claude_interpretation: Being associated with someone who shares your limitations or weaknesses brings no advantage or improvement to your situation.
gemini_translation: What is the benefit of a donkey on a donkey that is ridden until its feet touch the ground?
gemini_interpretation: There is no benefit in having something that is useless or ineffective for its intended purpose.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "What is the benefit of a donkey on a donkey that is ridden until its feet touch the ground?", "interpretation": "There is no benefit in having something that is useless or ineffective for its intended purpose."}
mistral_translation: What is the use of the smallness of a small bicycle to a bicycle with legs that touch the ground?
mistral_interpretation: Small advantages are meaningless when compared to someone with far greater capabilities or resources.
llama_translation: What is the benefit of a small bird in the midst of birds that are not afraid to fly?
llama_interpretation: It highlights the importance of being bold and taking risks in order to achieve greatness.

yoruba: Kò sí mi lájọ àjọ ò kún: ara ẹ̀ ló tàn jẹ.
english_literal: Without-me-in-an-assembly-the-assembly-is-not-complete deceives only himself/herself.
interpretation_gold: Whoever thinks he or she is indispensable is self-deceived.
deepseek_translation: There is no me in the gathering: the body is the one that ate it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against blaming others for one's own actions or mistakes.
claude_translation: There is no me in a gathering that is not full: it is yourself that you deceived.
claude_interpretation: When you exclude yourself from a group or gathering, you only harm yourself by missing out on the benefits of collective participation.
gemini_translation: I am not in the gathering, the gathering is not complete: it is his body that deceived him.
gemini_interpretation: One who believes their absence makes a group incomplete is deluding themselves, as the group will continue without them.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "I am not in the gathering, the gathering is not complete: it is his body that deceived him.", "interpretation": "One who believes their absence makes a group incomplete is deluding themselves, as the group will continue without them."}
mistral_translation: There is no me in a group journey that is not full: it is one's own body that suffers the loss
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that in a failed collective effort, the individual bears the consequences alone, emphasizing personal responsibility in shared endeavors
llama_translation: There is no one to wake me up for a meeting, yet I wake up early: it is my body that is in pain
llama_interpretation: One's body suffers the consequences of one's own actions.

yoruba: Kí ẹrú mọ ara ẹ̀ lẹ́rú; kí ìwọ̀fà mọ ara ẹ̀ níwọ̀fà; kí ọmọlúwàbí mọ ara ẹ̀ lẹ́rú Ọlọ́run ọba.
english_literal: Let the slave know him/herself as a slave; let the pawn know him/herself as a pawn; let the well born person know him/herself as the child of God.
interpretation_gold: Everybody should know himself/herself and his/her station in the scheme of things.
deepseek_translation: Let the slave know he is a slave; let the freeborn know he is freeborn; let the child of God know he is God's slave.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes recognizing one's true identity and status, whether earthly or divine.
claude_translation: Let the slave know himself as a slave; let the indentured servant know himself as an indentured servant; let the well-born know himself as a slave of God the King.
claude_interpretation: Regardless of one's social status, everyone should remember they are ultimately subject to God's authority.
gemini_translation: Let the slave know himself as a slave; let the indentured servant know himself as an indentured servant; let the noble person know himself as a slave of God the king.
gemini_interpretation: Everyone should understand and accept their true position and responsibilities, with even the most esteemed recognizing their ultimate subservience to God.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Let the slave know himself as a slave; let the indentured servant know himself as an indentured servant; let the noble person know himself as a slave of God the king.", "interpretation": "Everyone should understand and accept their true position and responsibilities, with even the most esteemed recognizing their ultimate subservience to God."}
mistral_translation: Let the slave know his fellow slave; let the pawn know his fellow pawn; let the well-brought-up child know that he is a slave to God the King.
mistral_interpretation: Everyone, regardless of status, is ultimately subject to a higher authority or divine will.
llama_translation: Let the slave know his body is a slave; let the apprentice know his body is an apprentice; let the child of character know his body is a slave to God the king.
llama_interpretation: One's status or profession should not make them forget their place or responsibilities.

yoruba: Kó-tán-kó-tán lajá ńlá omi.
english_literal: Swiftly-consumed-swiftly-consumed is the way a dog laps up water.
interpretation_gold: Said of people who attack good things with excessive greed.
deepseek_translation: The big fish swims with its mouth open and shut.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that wisdom involves knowing when to speak and when to remain silent.
claude_translation: Drop by drop is how a dog laps water
claude_interpretation: Great achievements are accomplished through small, consistent efforts over time.
gemini_translation: It is 'finish-finish' that a dog drinks water.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of completing a task thoroughly and without leaving anything undone.
mistral_translation: Little by little, the dog drinks the big water
mistral_interpretation: Consistent small efforts over time lead to the accomplishment of great tasks
llama_translation: The big dog is not a match for the small dog in the water.
llama_interpretation: Even the mighty can be humbled in unfamiliar or challenging environments.

yoruba: Ká wí fúnni ká gbọ́; ká sọ̀rọ̀ fúnni ká gbà; à-wí-ìgbọ́, à-gbọ́-ìgbà ní ńfi igbá àdánù bu omi mu.
english_literal: If one is spoken to one should listen; if one is advised one should accept the advice; refusal to listen to speech and refusal to accept advice leads to using the calabash of deprivation as a drinking cup.
interpretation_gold: Refusal to heed advise leads to deprivation.
deepseek_translation: Tell someone to listen; tell someone to understand; the one who listens but does not understand is like a bat drinking water.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that merely hearing words without comprehending their meaning is futile, like a bat's ineffective attempt to drink water.
claude_translation: Let us speak to someone and they listen; let us talk to someone and they accept; the one who speaks without listening, the one who listens without accepting, uses a broken calabash to fetch and drink water.
claude_interpretation: Effective communication requires both speaking and listening with mutual respect and acceptance, otherwise efforts become futile like trying to use broken tools.
gemini_translation: To tell one to hear; to speak to one to accept; not-telling-to-hear, not-hearing-to-accept is what uses the calabash of loss to drink water.
gemini_interpretation: Refusing to listen to advice or instruction leads to negative consequences and regret.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "To tell one to hear; to speak to one to accept; not-telling-to-hear, not-hearing-to-accept is what uses the calabash of loss to drink water.", "interpretation": "Refusing to listen to advice or instruction leads to negative consequences and regret."}
mistral_translation: Let us speak to you so you may hear; let us talk to you so you may accept; the one who refuses to hear, the one who hears too late, uses the calabash of the bat to drink water.
mistral_interpretation: Those who ignore advice or delay in heeding it will face unnecessary hardship or regret.
llama_translation: We tell the deaf to hear; we tell the lame to walk; the deaf and the lame are the ones who use the calabash of the deaf to scoop water.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the absurdity of expecting someone who lacks the ability or capacity to perform a task to do so.

yoruba: Kàkà kí bàbá ran ọmọ ní àdá bọ oko, oníkálukú a gbé tiẹ̀.
english_literal: Rather than the father carrying the son's cutlass home from the farm, each will carry his own.
interpretation_gold: People may withhold their respect from one, but one should not abet their insolence.
deepseek_translation: Rather than the father giving the child a cutlass to farm, the lazy one has carried a hoe.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes laziness and inefficiency, suggesting that some people avoid the right tools or methods to evade hard work.
claude_translation: Rather than father sending child with cutlass to the farm, each person should carry their own
claude_interpretation: Everyone should take responsibility for their own work and duties instead of relying on others to do what they should do themselves.
gemini_translation: Rather than the father sending the child with a cutlass to the farm, everyone carries their own.
gemini_interpretation: It is better for each person to take responsibility for their own tasks and burdens rather than relying on others.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Rather than the father sending the child with a cutlass to the farm, everyone carries their own.", "interpretation": "It is better for each person to take responsibility for their own tasks and burdens rather than relying on others."}
mistral_translation: Instead of a father sharpening a machete for his child to clear the farm, each person carries their own
mistral_interpretation: Everyone must take personal responsibility for their own tasks rather than relying on others to prepare for them
llama_translation: Before the father sells the child to the farmer, the vulture has already carried the share.
llama_interpretation: This proverb warns that a person's downfall can be orchestrated by those close to them before external enemies even get involved.

yoruba: Kì í dọwọ́-ọ baba kó ló di ọwọ́ ọmọ.
english_literal: Responsibility does not devolve on the father only for him to say it is his son's duty.
interpretation_gold: An elder must do his/her duty and not shove it on the youth.
deepseek_translation: It does not take long for a father's hand to become a child's hand.
deepseek_interpretation: Children often inherit or take over their parents' roles or possessions quickly.
claude_translation: It is not the father's hand that becomes the child's hand
claude_interpretation: Each person must develop their own skills and abilities rather than simply inheriting or depending on their parent's talents.
gemini_translation: It does not become the father's hand and then become the child's hand.
gemini_interpretation: A child cannot inherit or take over their parent's responsibilities or status without first growing into them.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It does not become the father's hand and then become the child's hand.", "interpretation": "A child cannot inherit or take over their parent's responsibilities or status without first growing into them."}
mistral_translation: One does not collect the father's debt and it becomes the child's debt
mistral_interpretation: Unresolved responsibilities or debts of parents can burden their children, emphasizing the importance of addressing obligations promptly
llama_translation: What is not learned from the father will be learned from the child.
llama_interpretation: One will eventually learn a lesson or skill from a younger or inexperienced person if not learned from an elder or experienced one.

yoruba: Kí ni wọ́n ti ńṣe Àmọ́dù nÍlọrin? Ewúrẹ́ ńjẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
english_literal: What use do the people of Ilorin have for Ahmadu? Even goats are so named.
interpretation_gold: Said to express the overabundance of some commodity being discussed.
deepseek_translation: What are they doing with Amodu in Ilorin? The goat is eating like that.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the futility of unnecessary interference in matters that do not concern one.
claude_translation: What are they doing to Amodu in Ilorin? The goat is eating leaves.
claude_interpretation: People often feign ignorance or act indifferent when they know exactly what wrongdoing is happening around them.
gemini_translation: What are they doing to Àmọ́dù in Ilorin? The goat is eating like that.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb is a rhetorical question highlighting a situation where someone is being exploited or taken advantage of, much like a goat freely eating without consequence.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "What are they doing to Àmọ́dù in Ilorin? The goat is eating like that.", "interpretation": "This proverb is a rhetorical question highlighting a situation where someone is being exploited or taken advantage of, much like a goat freely eating without consequence."}
mistral_translation: What is it that the people of Amodu in Ilorin are doing? The goat is saying the same.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the tendency to follow or imitate others without questioning, even when it may not be appropriate.
llama_translation: What are they doing at Amodu's house in Ilorin? Goat is eating its own beard.
llama_interpretation: This proverb warns against self-destruction or harming one's own interests.

yoruba: Kàkà kí kìnìún ṣe akápò ẹkùn, ọlọ́dẹ a mú ọdẹ ẹ̀ ṣe.
english_literal: Rather than the lion serving as carrier for the leopard, each will hunt separately.
interpretation_gold: One would rather leave a company that remain in it and be subordinate to those one considers inferior.
deepseek_translation: Rather than the lion becoming the leopard's keeper, the hunter will kill the leopard.
deepseek_interpretation: It is better to eliminate a potential threat than to try to control or manage it.
claude_translation: Rather than a lion becoming a leopard's bag carrier, a hunter will make it his prey.
claude_interpretation: It is better to maintain one's dignity and face consequences than to accept a demeaning position beneath one's status.
gemini_translation: Rather than a lion being a leopard's bag-carrier, the hunter will take his own game.
gemini_interpretation: It is better to maintain one's dignity and independence, even if it means facing a difficult outcome, than to submit to a subservient role.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Rather than a lion being a leopard's bag-carrier, the hunter will take his own game.", "interpretation": "It is better to maintain one's dignity and independence, even if it means facing a difficult outcome, than to submit to a subservient role."}
mistral_translation: Instead of the lion becoming the leopard's companion, the hunter catches the other hunter.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against trusting those who share the same harmful intentions as your enemies, as they may turn against you.
llama_translation: When the tortoise is about to be caught, the hunter is already holding the rope
llama_interpretation: Preparation is key to success, as one must be ready before the opportunity arises.

yoruba: Labalábá fi ara ẹ̀ wẹ́yẹ, kò lè ṣe ìṣe ẹyẹ.
english_literal: The butterfly likens itself to a bird, but it cannot do what a bird can do.
interpretation_gold: Attempts to emulate those better endowed and qualified than oneself always prove futile.
deepseek_translation: The butterfly uses itself to cover the bird, it cannot do the bird's work.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks beyond their capability or role.
claude_translation: A butterfly adorns itself with feathers, but it cannot do the work of a bird
claude_interpretation: Mere imitation or superficial appearance cannot substitute for genuine ability or natural talent.
gemini_translation: The butterfly compares itself to a bird, but it cannot act like a bird.
gemini_interpretation: It is futile to imitate others when one lacks their inherent abilities or characteristics.
mistral_translation: The butterfly wraps itself in feathers, it cannot do the work of a bird.
mistral_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks beyond their natural abilities or role.
llama_translation: The butterfly uses its body to play, it cannot do the work of a bird.
llama_interpretation: One should not pretend to be what they are not, as they will not be able to fulfill the responsibilities that come with it.

yoruba: Lékèélékèé ò yé ẹyin dúdú; funfun ni wọ́n ńyé ẹyin wọn.
english_literal: Cattle egrets never lay black eggs; only white eggs do they lay.
interpretation_gold: Only certain types of behavior are suitable for people in certain positions.
deepseek_translation: The white part of the egg does not understand the yolk; it is the white that they understand their own.
deepseek_interpretation: People often misunderstand or are unaware of the struggles of others, focusing only on their own experiences.
claude_translation: Speckled does not suit black eggs; they lay white eggs.
claude_interpretation: People should embrace their natural qualities rather than trying to imitate others who are fundamentally different from them.
gemini_translation: The wagtail does not lay black eggs; they lay white eggs.
gemini_interpretation: One should not expect a person to act against their inherent nature or established patterns.
mistral_translation: The speckled one does not suit the black egg; it is the white one that suits their eggs
mistral_interpretation: People should associate with or choose what naturally aligns with their own nature or circumstances
llama_translation: The blacksmith's children are black; white is what they use to clean their children.
llama_interpretation: Those who are closest to a problem or situation often appear to be the most affected by it.

yoruba: fara wé àgbàdo.
english_literal: Ash mixed with water likens itself to indigo dye, but it cannot do what the dye can do; the large red bean likens itself to corn.
interpretation_gold: One should know better than to attempt to overreach one's capabilities.
deepseek_translation: roll with the corn cob.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb advises adapting to circumstances or making the best of a situation.
claude_translation: Use your body to touch corn.
claude_interpretation: One must be willing to work hard and get personally involved to achieve success or obtain what they need.
gemini_translation: Be like corn.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb encourages resilience and growth, as corn grows tall and strong despite challenges.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Be like corn.", "interpretation": "This proverb encourages resilience and growth, as corn grows tall and strong despite challenges."}
mistral_translation: scrubbing corn with soap
mistral_interpretation: It is foolish to waste effort on something that cannot be improved or changed.
llama_translation: yam is not cooked by an elder
llama_interpretation: Respect and authority do not guarantee success or achievement.
llama_raw: {"translation": "yam is not cooked by an elder", "interpretation": "Respect and authority do not guarantee success or achievement."}

yoruba: Lágbájá ìbá wà a di ìjímèrè; ẹni tó bá níwájú di oloyo?
english_literal: Were So-and-So alive he would transform himself into a brown monkey; did the person who preceded him ever transform himself into any kind of monkey?
interpretation_gold: One should not make excessive claims when there is no basis for them.
deepseek_translation: If Lagbaja were present, he would become Ijimere; whoever is in front becomes the leader?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that leadership or prominence is situational and depends on who is present at the time.
claude_translation: If so-and-so were present it would become a gathering; who then would be at the front to become the leader?
claude_interpretation: Too many potential leaders in one place can create confusion about who should actually take charge.
gemini_translation: If so-and-so were to become a monkey; would the one in front become a baboon?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the logic of assuming a direct and equal transformation or consequence based on a hypothetical change in another, highlighting that outcomes are not always parallel or predictable.
mistral_translation: If Lagbaja were to exist, he would become a fool; who that has foresight becomes a spendthrift?
mistral_interpretation: A wise person plans ahead and avoids reckless behavior that could lead to ruin.
llama_translation: The one who is being pursued by Lágbájá is already in a hurry; what about the one who is in front?
llama_interpretation: Those who are already struggling to keep up will be overtaken by those who are ahead.

yoruba: One does not wear ẹtù
interpretation_gold: Not every person is made for greatness.
deepseek_translation: One does not wear a raffia skirt
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises against engaging in behavior or taking on roles that are inappropriate or beneath one's status.
claude_translation: One does not wear ẹtù
claude_interpretation: Some things are too sacred, dangerous, or inappropriate to be used casually or worn as ordinary items.
gemini_translation: One does not wear guinea fowl.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb is incomplete and therefore lacks a clear meaning or lesson without additional context.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not wear guinea fowl.", "interpretation": "This proverb is incomplete and therefore lacks a clear meaning or lesson without additional context."}
mistral_translation: One does not wear ẹtù (a type of expensive, prestigious cloth)

llama_translation: One does not wear ẹtù
