mistral_interpretation: Guests often incur expenses or obligations, but the host ultimately bears the responsibility and consequences
llama_translation: The eyes of a stranger are eating debt; his back is paying for it.
llama_interpretation: A person who borrows or takes things without permission will eventually face the consequences.

yoruba: Orogún ìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dáṣọ fún ọ o ní kò balẹ̀; mélòó nìyá ẹ-ẹ́ dá fún ọ tó fi kú?
english_literal: Your mother's co-wife made a garment for you and you complain that it is not long enough; how many did your mother make for you before she died?
interpretation_gold: People dependent on charity should rather be grateful than difficult to please.
deepseek_translation: Your mother's enemy who gave you clothes did not prostrate; how many did your mother give you that you died?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against ingratitude and emphasizes valuing the sacrifices of those who truly care for you.
claude_translation: Your mother's twenty medicines that she prepared for you, you said they were not effective; how many did your mother prepare for you that caused you to die?
claude_interpretation: One should not dismiss or complain about a mother's care and remedies, as her intentions are always for healing and protection, never harm.
gemini_translation: Your mother's rival gave you clothes and you said they didn't touch the ground; how many did your mother give you that you wore until they tore?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the ingratitude of someone who criticizes a gift from an outsider while overlooking the greater generosity and sacrifice of a close relation.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Your mother's rival gave you clothes and you said they didn't touch the ground; how many did your mother give you that you wore until they tore?", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the ingratitude of someone who criticizes a gift from an outsider while overlooking the greater generosity and sacrifice of a close relation."}
mistral_translation: The debt of a mother is not enough to clothe you; how many mothers' debts did you collect before you died?
mistral_interpretation: One should not rely excessively on the sacrifices of others, especially parents, as no amount of gratitude can fully repay their efforts.
llama_translation: The mother's curse is not a curse that one can escape; how many curses of the mother can one bear?
llama_interpretation: A mother's curse is considered particularly potent and inescapable in Yoruba culture.

yoruba: Oǹpè ní ńfa ọlá; òjípè kì í fa ọlá.
english_literal: It is the person who does the summoning that assumes airs; the person subject to summons does not assume airs.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's place, especially in the company of more illustrious people.
deepseek_translation: The one who is called does not bring wealth; the one who calls does not bring wealth.
deepseek_interpretation: Wealth is not determined by titles or names, but by one's actions and efforts.
claude_translation: Patience attracts honor; impatience does not attract honor.
claude_interpretation: Those who are patient and wait for the right time will gain respect and success, while those who are hasty will not achieve lasting honor.
gemini_translation: The one who calls (invites) brings honor; the one who answers a call does not bring honor.
gemini_interpretation: It is more prestigious to be the one who extends an invitation or initiates an action than to be the one who merely responds to it.
mistral_translation: The palm-wine tapper draws wealth; the one who taps too late does not draw wealth.
mistral_interpretation: Timing and effort are crucial to achieving success or prosperity.
llama_translation: The one who is patient gets wealth; the impatient one does not get wealth.
llama_interpretation: Patience is a necessary virtue for achieving success and prosperity.

yoruba: Ó di ọjọ́ alẹ́ kábuké tó mọ̀ pé iké kì í ṣọmọ.
english_literal: It will not be until the end of days before the humpback realizes that a hump is not a child.
interpretation_gold: People seldom learn wisdom until it is too late.
deepseek_translation: It became the evening of the day Kabuke realized that strength does not belong to a child.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that wisdom and experience, not mere physical strength, are the true marks of maturity.
claude_translation: It was evening before the hunchback knew that a hump does not bear children
claude_interpretation: Some people only realize their limitations or the futility of their expectations when it's too late to make meaningful changes.
gemini_translation: It is on the evening of the hunchback that he knows that the hump is not a child.
gemini_interpretation: One only realizes the true nature or burden of a situation when it becomes critical or too late.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It is on the evening of the hunchback that he knows that the hump is not a child.", "interpretation": "One only realizes the true nature or burden of a situation when it becomes critical or too late."}
mistral_translation: It has become evening for the hunchback who thought a knot could not have a child.
mistral_interpretation: One should not underestimate others or assume their limitations, as unexpected outcomes can challenge such assumptions.
llama_translation: It is the night that reveals the true nature of a hen that we know it does not crow
llama_interpretation: One's true character is revealed in times of crisis or adversity.

yoruba: Ojú baba ara; awọ́n bí ojú; aṣòró dà bí àgbà.
english_literal: The eye, father of the body; nothing is as valuable as the eye; nothing is as difficult to achieve as the status of elder.
interpretation_gold: The status of elder is most precious, and most difficult to achieve.
deepseek_translation: The father's eye; they resemble the eye; the young resembles the elder.
deepseek_interpretation: Children often inherit the traits or behaviors of their parents.
claude_translation: The eye of the father is the body; children are like eyes; it is difficult to be like an elder.
claude_interpretation: A father's watchful care over his children is as essential as eyes are to the body, and achieving the wisdom and responsibility of true eldership is challenging.
gemini_translation: The father's eye is the body; they are like the eye; a difficult person is like an elder.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of respecting elders and those in authority, as their wisdom and guidance, even if seemingly strict, are crucial for well-being and societal order.
mistral_translation: The father's face is a mirror; the faces of the young resemble it; the elder's speech is profound like an elder's.
mistral_interpretation: Children often inherit and reflect the traits, behaviors, or wisdom of their parents or elders.
llama_translation: The father's eyes are many; the children are like the eyes; the cloth is as wide as the elder.
llama_interpretation: A community's collective wisdom and experience are more valuable than individual perspectives.

yoruba: Onífunra àlejò tí ńtètè ṣe onílé pẹ̀lẹ́.
english_literal: The excessively attentive visitor “who” extends hospitality greetings to the host.
interpretation_gold: One should not assume other people's functions.
deepseek_translation: The landlord who hastily builds a house for a visitor will soon become a tenant.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against making hasty decisions that may lead to one's own detriment.
claude_translation: A selfish guest who quickly greets the host.
claude_interpretation: Someone who appears polite and respectful on the surface but is actually self-serving and manipulative in their intentions.
gemini_translation: A suspicious guest who quickly greets the host.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes a person who, despite being a guest, acts with an unusual and perhaps insincere eagerness to please, suggesting ulterior motives or a lack of genuine respect.
mistral_translation: The hasty guest who acts like the owner of the house greets the real owner carelessly.
mistral_interpretation: Overstepping one's bounds or acting presumptuously in unfamiliar situations can lead to embarrassment or disrespect.
llama_translation: The stranger who is always visiting is not a tenant of a small house.
llama_interpretation: Frequent visitors should not be mistaken for permanent residents.

yoruba: Ojú kì í pọ́n òkú ọ̀run kó ní kí ará ayé gba òun.
english_literal: A dead person cannot be so desperate as to appeal to a living person for deliverance.
interpretation_gold: However bad one's circumstances might be, one should use good sense in determining where one can turn for help.
deepseek_translation: The eye does not swell at the death of a person in heaven so that the earthly people can mourn him.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not grieve excessively for those who have lived a good life and passed on honorably, as their transition to the afterlife is a natural and dignified process.
claude_translation: The eye does not wink at a dead person in heaven for the living on earth to accept them
claude_interpretation: One cannot claim divine approval or heavenly endorsement without proper evidence or authority that others can verify.
gemini_translation: The eyes of a dead person in the afterlife do not become red and ask the people of the world to help them.
gemini_interpretation: One should not expect help from those who are no longer in a position to offer it, especially after their passing.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The eyes of a dead person in the afterlife do not become red and ask the people of the world to help them.", "interpretation": "One should not expect help from those who are no longer in a position to offer it, especially after their passing."}
mistral_translation: The eyes do not gather the corpse of heaven to ask the people of the world to receive it
mistral_interpretation: One should not interfere in matters that are beyond their control or responsibility, especially those that belong to the divine or spiritual realm.
llama_translation: The eye does not see the death of heaven, yet the world says it has happened.
llama_interpretation: One should not claim to know or judge something beyond one's knowledge or experience.

yoruba: Òtòlò-ó jẹ, òtòlò-ó mu, òtòlò-ó fẹsẹ̀ wé ẹsẹ̀ erin.
english_literal: The water-buck ate, the water-buck drank, the water-buck compared its limbs to an elephant's.
interpretation_gold: Satiation leads to excess.
deepseek_translation: The mushroom eats, the mushroom drinks, the mushroom attempts to wipe the feet of the elephant.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against overestimating one's abilities or attempting tasks beyond one's capacity.
claude_translation: The mudfish eats, the mudfish drinks, the mudfish rubs its feet against the elephant's feet.
claude_interpretation: Even the smallest or most humble creature can find ways to benefit from or associate with the mighty and powerful.
gemini_translation: The guinea fowl eats, the guinea fowl drinks, the guinea fowl compares its leg to the elephant's leg.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish and dangerous to compare oneself to someone far superior in power or status.
mistral_translation: The otolo (a small bird) eats, the otolo drinks, the otolo uses its legs to wash the elephant's legs
mistral_interpretation: A small or seemingly insignificant person can unexpectedly perform a great or important task.
llama_translation: The tortoise eats, the tortoise drinks, the tortoise throws away the foot of the elephant.
llama_interpretation: One should not waste or reject something that is valuable or useful to others.

yoruba: Ohun tí à ńtà là ńjẹ; kì í ṣe ọ̀rọ̀ oní-kẹrosíìnì.
english_literal: What one sells is what one eats; that does not apply to the kerosene seller.
interpretation_gold: One should be mindful of the peculiarities of one's situation.
deepseek_translation: What we sell is what we eat; it is not the matter of the kerosene seller.
deepseek_interpretation: One should focus on their own affairs and not meddle in others' business.
claude_translation: What we are selling is what we are eating; it is not the matter of the kerosene seller.
claude_interpretation: People should focus on their own business and livelihood rather than interfering in matters that don't concern them.
gemini_translation: What is being sold is what is eaten; it is not the concern of the kerosene seller.
gemini_interpretation: People should focus on their own affairs and not meddle in the business of others.
mistral_translation: It is what we sell that we eat; it is not the business of the one who merely watches.
mistral_interpretation: One benefits only from their own efforts and not from merely observing others.
llama_translation: What we are looking for is what we are eating; it is not the talk of the kerosene seller.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on solving the problem at hand rather than just talking about it.

yoruba: Oníbàjẹ́ ò mọra; oníbàjẹ́ ńlọ sóko olè ó mú obìnrin lọ; ọkọ́ kó akọṣu, ìyàwó kó ewùrà.
english_literal: The shameless person does not know what is fitting; the shameless person is off to raid a farm, and he takes his wife along; the husband steals staple yams, the wife steals wateryams.
interpretation_gold: A man who involves his family in his questionable ventures has sunk to the lowest depths.
deepseek_translation: The spoilt child does not know himself; the spoilt child goes to the farm, the thief takes the woman; the husband gathers firewood, the wife gathers locust beans.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that lack of discipline and indulgence can lead to recklessness and undesirable consequences in life.
claude_translation: The destroyer does not know himself; the destroyer goes to the lazy man's farm and takes a woman along; the husband carries a hoe, the wife carries a goat.
claude_interpretation: A troublemaker lacks self-awareness and involves others in questionable ventures where roles and responsibilities become confused or inappropriate.
gemini_translation: The one who spoils things doesn't know themselves; the one who spoils things goes to the thief's farm and takes a woman along; the husband takes yams, the wife takes water yams.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes the self-destructive and often oblivious nature of someone who causes trouble, highlighting how their actions can lead to further complications and even involve others in their wrongdoing.
mistral_translation: The debauchee does not know the way; the debauchee goes to the thief's farm and takes another man's wife; the husband gathers thorns, the wife gathers okra.
mistral_interpretation: A reckless or immoral person brings trouble upon themselves and others through their thoughtless actions.
llama_translation: The debtor doesn't know; the debtor is going to the farm, the debtor takes the wife; the husband takes the hoe, the wife takes the basket.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of cooperation and division of labor in a marriage.

yoruba: Oòrùn, kó tìẹ wọ̀ ká má bàá Ọlọ́jọ́ wí.
english_literal: Sun, go set so one does not blame the owner of the day.
interpretation_gold: Subordinates should not behave in a manner that would bring their superior to disrepute.
deepseek_translation: Sun, do not shine so we can see the rainbow.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that sometimes we must endure temporary discomfort or sacrifice to achieve greater beauty or rewards.
claude_translation: Sun, let it not set so we don't have to speak with the Owner of the Day
claude_interpretation: It's better to avoid confrontation or difficult conversations with those in authority by preventing situations that would necessitate such encounters.
gemini_translation: Sun, do not set so that we do not blame God.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb expresses a desire for a favorable situation to continue, implying that its cessation would lead to hardship or regret.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Sun, do not set so that we do not blame God.", "interpretation": "This proverb expresses a desire for a favorable situation to continue, implying that its cessation would lead to hardship or regret."}
mistral_translation: The sun, may it not set for us to be caught speaking ill of the owner of the day
mistral_interpretation: It is unwise to speak ill of someone in a position of power or authority while still under their influence or jurisdiction.
llama_translation: The sky, do not look at it and think it is far from the sun
llama_interpretation: Do not underestimate the power or influence of someone just because they seem distant or uninvolved.

yoruba: Olówó jẹun jẹ́jẹ́; òtòṣì jẹun tìpà-tìjàn; òtòṣì tí ḿbá ọlọ́rọ̀ rìn, akọ ojú ló ńyá.
english_literal: The rich man eats slowly and at leisure; the poor person eats fast and with anxiety; the poor man who keeps company with a wealthy man is exceeding his station.
interpretation_gold: One should keep to comrades whose station is similar to one's.
deepseek_translation: The rich eat leisurely; the poor eat hurriedly; the poor who walks with the rich, his eyes are wide open.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights the disparity in lifestyles between the rich and the poor, and how the poor may become more aware of their struggles when associating with the wealthy.
claude_translation: The rich person eats food gently; the poor person eats food hurriedly and roughly; the poor person who walks with the wealthy is only putting on appearances.
claude_interpretation: People often pretend to have wealth or status they don't possess when associating with those of higher social standing.
gemini_translation: The rich eats gently; the poor eats with struggle and fight; the poor who walks with the rich, it is a borrowed face he uses.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb highlights the disparity in ease and dignity between the rich and the poor, suggesting that the poor often have to compromise their self-respect or appear to be something they are not when associating with the wealthy.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The rich eats gently; the poor eats with struggle and fight; the poor who walks with the rich, it is a borrowed face he uses.", "interpretation": "The proverb highlights the disparity in ease and dignity between the rich and the poor, suggesting that the poor often have to compromise their self-respect or appear to be something they are not when associating with the wealthy."}
mistral_translation: The rich person eats gently; the poor person eats hurriedly; the poor person who walks with a rich person, it is the corner of the eye that is tearing up.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb illustrates how the poor often feel pressured or ashamed when associating with the wealthy, leading to discomfort or envy.
llama_translation: The rich man eats well; the poor man eats hastily; the poor man who runs after the rich man, it is the rich man's dog that chases him.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on their own struggles rather than trying to keep up with someone more privileged.

yoruba: Pẹ̀lẹ́ larẹwà ńrìn; jẹ́jẹ́ lọmọ ọlọ́jà ńyan.
interpretation_gold: Gently and carefully is the best manner to take life.
deepseek_translation: The snail moves slowly; the child of the market walks hastily.
deepseek_interpretation: Different people have different paces and approaches to life based on their circumstances.
claude_translation: Gently is how a beautiful woman walks; quietly is how a merchant's child behaves.
claude_interpretation: Grace, composure, and proper conduct are the hallmarks of those from good upbringing and social standing.
gemini_translation: Gently the beautiful one walks; softly the child of the market owner strolls.
gemini_interpretation: Those who are privileged or possess inherent value often move with a calm and unhurried demeanor, reflecting their secure position.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Gently the beautiful one walks; softly the child of the market owner strolls.", "interpretation": "Those who are privileged or possess inherent value often move with a calm and unhurried demeanor, reflecting their secure position."}
mistral_translation: Gentleness is the beauty of walking; calmness is how the child of the market owner eats
mistral_interpretation: Patience and composure are virtues that bring success and respect in life.
llama_translation: The one who is gentle walks alone; the one who is stubborn is the child of the market woman.
llama_interpretation: Stubbornness can lead to isolation and loneliness.

yoruba: Pátápátá alágbẹ̀dẹ ò ju ilé àrọ lọ.
english_literal: The most one can expect of the blacksmith is confined to the smithy.
interpretation_gold: There is a limit to a person's bragging.
deepseek_translation: The blacksmith's hammer is not heavier than the anvil.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that no matter how strong or powerful someone may seem, there is always a greater force or authority.
claude_translation: The blacksmith's workshop is not bigger than the dye pit house.
claude_interpretation: No matter how skilled or important someone becomes, they should not consider themselves superior to their origins or community.
gemini_translation: The blacksmith's utmost is not beyond the forge.
gemini_interpretation: A person's capabilities and influence are often limited to their area of expertise or immediate environment.
mistral_translation: The blacksmith's anvil is never better than the forge house.
mistral_interpretation: One's tools or resources are only as effective as the environment or foundation that supports them.
llama_translation: A small axe is not superior to a house of hoes
llama_interpretation: A small but effective tool can be more valuable than a large collection of useless ones.

yoruba: Pamí-nkú obìnrín ṣorí bẹmbẹ sọ́kọ.
english_literal: A masochistic woman hardens her head against her husband.
interpretation_gold: Obstinacy only invites harsh punishment.
deepseek_translation: The death of a woman is like the breaking of a calabash.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the fragility and irreplaceable value of a woman's life in the community.
claude_translation: A woman who kills and eats speaks sweetly to her husband
claude_interpretation: People who are capable of harmful acts can still present themselves as gentle and loving to those closest to them.
gemini_translation: The woman who dies and has a flat head marries a husband.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb is a playful and somewhat nonsensical saying, often used to express that some things are inherently contradictory or impossible, or to highlight the absurdity of certain situations.
mistral_translation: The woman who is always crying 'I am dying' climbs the palm tree to tap wine for her husband
mistral_interpretation: People who constantly complain or exaggerate their struggles may still perform their duties despite their grievances
llama_translation: A woman's death is on a mortar
llama_interpretation: A woman's greatest sorrow is the loss of her child.

yoruba: Pẹ̀lẹ́-pẹ̀lẹ́ nijó àgbà; ara gbogbo ló di àkísà tán.
english_literal: An elderly person's manner of dancing must be very gentle, because the whole body has become worn to a rag.
interpretation_gold: Elderly people should not over-exert themselves.
deepseek_translation: Slowly-slowly in the elder's day; the whole body has become completely lean.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that patience and moderation lead to better outcomes, as rushing can result in exhaustion or loss.
claude_translation: Gently-gently is the dance of the elder; the whole body has become stiff.
claude_interpretation: Elders move carefully and deliberately because age has made their bodies less flexible, teaching us to respect the natural limitations that come with aging.
gemini_translation: Slowly, slowly is the dance of the elder; the whole body becomes rags.
gemini_interpretation: Elders, due to their age and wisdom, approach tasks with caution and deliberation, which may appear slow but is a result of their accumulated experience and the physical toll of life.
mistral_translation: Slowly-slowly is the way of the elder; the whole body has become rags completely.
mistral_interpretation: Patience and carefulness are virtues of wisdom, as rushing leads to ruin or loss of dignity.
llama_translation: Slowly-slowly is the dance of the elderly; the whole body becomes a walking stick.
llama_interpretation: With age, one's pace and strength naturally decline.

yoruba: San là ńrìn; ajé ní ḿmúni pá kọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: Straight and upright is the way one would walk; it is money that forces one to sneak about.
interpretation_gold: When one is in debt, one's freedom of movement is compromised.
deepseek_translation: Wealth walks; poverty holds it by the leg.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb highlights how poverty hinders progress and keeps one from achieving wealth.
claude_translation: Slowly one walks; it is wealth that makes one kill a leopard.
claude_interpretation: Success and achievement come through patience and gradual accumulation of resources rather than hasty actions.
gemini_translation: It is with health that we walk; wealth makes one walk with a stoop.
gemini_interpretation: Good health is more valuable than wealth, as wealth can bring burdens or ailments that diminish one's well-being.
mistral_translation: We walk gently; it is witchcraft that makes one walk arrogantly
mistral_interpretation: Modesty and humility are virtues, while arrogance is often seen as a sign of negative spiritual influence
llama_translation: The road is long; the hawk is crying, let us not be slow.
llama_interpretation: One should not delay in taking action or making decisions.

yoruba: Sesere ńdá gọ́ọ́bú; oníkamẹ́sàn-án ńgbé ṣíbí.
english_literal: The insignificant thing is attempting an earth-shaking feat; the person with only nine fingers is lifting a spoon.
interpretation_gold: Said of a person overreaching.
deepseek_translation: The grasshopper is cutting the sugarcane; the one with sore legs is carrying it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony of life where those who work hard often do not enjoy the fruits of their labor, while others benefit without effort.
claude_translation: The grasshopper is making a hunchback; the one with twenty-nine is living in a corner.
claude_interpretation: Everyone has their own burdens and limitations to bear, regardless of their circumstances.
gemini_translation: The Sesere bird is making a nest; the one with nine fingers is carrying a spoon.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony or absurdity of a situation where someone is engaged in an activity that seems contradictory or ill-suited to their nature or circumstances.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The Sesere bird is making a nest; the one with nine fingers is carrying a spoon.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the irony or absurdity of a situation where someone is engaged in an activity that seems contradictory or ill-suited to their nature or circumstances."}
mistral_translation: The crab is making a hole in the sand; the one who has nine mouths is carrying a load of trouble.
mistral_interpretation: Those who are overly meddlesome or greedy often bring unnecessary trouble upon themselves.
llama_translation: The sesame seed is not too big to be ground; the one who has a grinding stone will grind it.
llama_interpretation: No matter how small or insignificant something may seem, it can still be dealt with or overcome with the right tools or resources.

yoruba: Sún mọ ọ̀hún, sún mọ́ ìhín! Bí a bá kan ògiri ilé-e baba ẹni, ṣe là ńdúró gbọin-gbọin.
english_literal: Move away, move over here! When one moves until one is against the walls of one's father's house, one stands steadfast.
interpretation_gold: There must be a limit to how much one will back down before enemies.
deepseek_translation: Lie with the scorpion, lie with the worm! If we lean against the wall of our father's house, we stand comfortably.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that associating with dangerous or troublesome people will lead to harm, while staying close to one's family brings security and comfort.
claude_translation: Move close to that, move close to this! When one touches the wall of one's father's house, one stands firmly and confidently.
claude_interpretation: Being in familiar territory or among one's own people gives confidence and security.
gemini_translation: Move closer to that, move closer to this! If one reaches the wall of one's father's house, one stands firmly.
gemini_interpretation: One should explore and be open to different options, but ultimately find stability and security in one's roots or foundational principles.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Move closer to that, move closer to this! If one reaches the wall of one's father's house, one stands firmly.", "interpretation": "One should explore and be open to different options, but ultimately find stability and security in one's roots or foundational principles."}
mistral_translation: Sleep towards this side, sleep towards that side! If we reach the wall of our father's house, why are we standing stiffly?
mistral_interpretation: One should adapt and find solutions when faced with obstacles, rather than remaining rigid or helpless.
llama_translation: Sleeping and dreaming, sleeping and waking! If we are to count the pillars of one's father's house, it is a task that requires thoroughness.
llama_interpretation: One must be thorough and meticulous in their endeavors, just as counting the pillars of a house requires attention to detail.

yoruba: Ta ní ńjẹun tájá ńjùrù?
english_literal: At whose dinner table is the dog wagging its tail?
interpretation_gold: Said to tell off people who make their presence felt when they should rather make themselves scarce.
deepseek_translation: Who is eating the dog's food that the dog is barking at?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb questions the unnecessary hostility or aggression from someone who is not directly affected by a situation.
claude_translation: Who is eating while the dog is drooling?
claude_interpretation: This questions someone who enjoys privileges or benefits while others who deserve them are left wanting or suffering.
gemini_translation: Who is eating that the dog is wagging its tail?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the source of a dog's excitement, implying that someone must be providing it with food or a reason to be happy.
mistral_translation: Who is eating quietly while the dog is eating noisily?
mistral_interpretation: It warns against being complacent or careless while others are actively and visibly pursuing their goals.
llama_translation: Who eats the food of the tiger and then sleeps?
llama_interpretation: One must be prepared to face the consequences of their actions.

yoruba: Ta ní ńjájá ní mọ́ṣáláṣí?
english_literal: What would a dog be doing in a mosque?
interpretation_gold: Said to tell off people who are not wanted in a company.
deepseek_translation: Who is the one dancing at the gathering of the crippled?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb questions the appropriateness or wisdom of showing off in a situation where others are disadvantaged.
claude_translation: Who is teaching the dog to pray?
claude_interpretation: It is foolish to try to teach someone something that is completely against their nature or to expect behavior that goes against their fundamental character.
gemini_translation: Who is calling a dog 'Moshalasi'?
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to give a name to something that already has a well-established and common name, implying a lack of understanding or respect for existing norms.
mistral_translation: Who is fighting in the mosque?
mistral_interpretation: It warns against causing unnecessary conflict or disturbance in a peaceful or sacred setting.
llama_translation: Who is the owner of the market in the forest?
llama_interpretation: This proverb cautions against meddling in affairs that are not one's concern or expertise.

yoruba: Tòlótòló mọ ẹni tó ńyìnbọn ìdí sí.
english_literal: The turkey knows towards whom it farts.
interpretation_gold: People must be careful how to choose the people they presume to approach with familiarity.
deepseek_translation: The tòlótòló bird knows the person who is pointing at its buttocks.
deepseek_interpretation: One is aware of those who mock or criticize them behind their back.
claude_translation: The turkey knows the one who is pointing a gun at its buttocks.
claude_interpretation: A person is always aware of who poses a direct threat or danger to them.
gemini_translation: The turkey knows who is shooting at its behind.
gemini_interpretation: People are aware of those who are causing them trouble or harm, even if they pretend not to be.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The turkey knows who is shooting at its behind.", "interpretation": "People are aware of those who are causing them trouble or harm, even if they pretend not to be."}
mistral_translation: The turkey knows who is pulling its tail feathers.
mistral_interpretation: One is aware of those causing their troubles or discomfort.
llama_translation: The deaf knows the one who is whispering into the ear.
llama_interpretation: One who is being secretly informed or influenced is often aware of the source.

yoruba: Tẹ̀tẹ̀ kì í tẹ́.
english_literal: Spinach is never disgraced.
interpretation_gold: May one never know disgrace.
deepseek_translation: Slowly does not mean weak.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that taking one's time does not imply lack of strength or capability.
claude_translation: Mud does not step on itself
claude_interpretation: One cannot harm or destroy oneself through one's own actions.
gemini_translation: The early bird does not get disgraced.
gemini_interpretation: Diligence and promptness in one's actions prevent failure or embarrassment.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The early bird does not get disgraced.", "interpretation": "Diligence and promptness in one's actions prevent failure or embarrassment."}
mistral_translation: The mushroom does not flatten itself.
mistral_interpretation: One should not diminish their own worth or capabilities out of false humility or fear.
llama_translation: The one who is slow will not get lost.
llama_interpretation: Patience and carefulness are essential for avoiding mistakes and achieving success.

yoruba: “Ta ní ḿbẹ níbẹ̀?” làgbẹ́ fi ńsán ìbàǹtẹ́ wọ̀lú.
english_literal: “Who is there whose opinion matters?” is the attitude that makes the farmer come into town dressed only in a loin cloth.
interpretation_gold: People who make a spectacle of themselves show no regard for others.
deepseek_translation: Who is there in the boat? is the question the paddler asks while entering the town.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of awareness and inquiry before taking action in unfamiliar situations.
claude_translation: Who is there? is what the blacksmith uses to drive away strangers from town.
claude_interpretation: A skilled craftsman's reputation and presence alone is enough to deter unwanted visitors or competitors from encroaching on their territory.
gemini_translation: “Who is there?” is how a farmer wears his trousers into town.
gemini_interpretation: People often act differently in public than they do in private, adjusting their behavior based on perceived scrutiny.
mistral_translation: “Who is there?” is why the toad looks sideways into the town.
mistral_interpretation: Caution and suspicion often arise from uncertainty about others' presence or intentions.

yoruba: Wọ́n ńpe gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nà ẹyẹ àkókó ńyọjú.
english_literal: The call goes out for a carpenter and the woodpecker presents itself.
interpretation_gold: One should not think too much of one's capabilities.
deepseek_translation: They are calling the road builder, the first bird is pecking.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against taking credit for others' work or efforts.
claude_translation: They call it gbẹ́nàgbẹ́nà while the woodpecker is watching.
claude_interpretation: People may give things different names or interpretations, but the truth or the one who knows best is always observing.
gemini_translation: They are calling the sculptor, the woodpecker is showing its face.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the folly of someone presenting themselves for a task for which they are clearly unqualified or unsuitable.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "They are calling the sculptor, the woodpecker is showing its face.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the folly of someone presenting themselves for a task for which they are clearly unqualified or unsuitable."}
mistral_translation: They are calling a woodcarver a woodcarver while the early bird watches.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights how people may ignore obvious truths or expertise while focusing on trivial or irrelevant matters.
llama_translation: They are calling the name of the parrot in front of the parrot.
llama_interpretation: It is unnecessary to explain something to someone who is already aware of it.

yoruba: Wèrè èèyàn ní ńwípé irú òun ò sí; irú ẹ̀ẹ́ pọ̀ ó ju ẹgbàágbèje lọ.
english_literal: Only an imbecile asserts that there is none like him or her; his or her likes are numerous, numbering more than millions.
interpretation_gold: No one is incomparable.
deepseek_translation: A foolish person is the one who says his kind does not exist; his kind are more than two thousand.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against arrogance and the false belief that one is unique or superior to others.
claude_translation: A mad person says there is no one like him; your type is more than nine hundred.
claude_interpretation: People who boast about their uniqueness are deluded, as there are countless others just like them.
gemini_translation: A foolish person says that their kind does not exist; their kind is numerous, more than twenty thousand.
gemini_interpretation: One should not think they are unique in their foolishness or problems, as many others share similar experiences.
mistral_translation: A mad person says his own kind does not exist; his own kind is more than fourteen thousand in number.
mistral_interpretation: This proverb teaches that those who deny their own flaws or shortcomings are often surrounded by many others who share the same faults.
llama_translation: A mad person says his type is not around; his type is more than the multitude.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the tendency for people to deny their own flaws or weaknesses while acknowledging them in others.

yoruba: “Yan àkàrà fún mi wá ká jìjọ jẹ ẹ́”: àìtó èèyàn-án rán níṣẹ́ ní ńjẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀.
english_literal: “Go buy bean fritters for me so we can eat them together”: that spells uncertainly about one's right to send the person concerned on an errand.
interpretation_gold: People in authority should not be tentative in asserting their authority.
deepseek_translation: "Pick bean cakes for me to eat together": a person's inability to send an errand is what causes it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes laziness or unwillingness to delegate tasks, leading to unmet needs.
claude_translation: Select bean cakes for me so we can eat together: that's how dishonest people behave when sent on errands
claude_interpretation: Untrustworthy people will take advantage of being sent to buy things by choosing the best items for themselves while pretending to share.
gemini_translation: 'Fry akara for me so we can eat it together': it is the inadequacy of the person sent on an errand that makes it so.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that when a messenger fails to deliver a message accurately or completely, it is due to their own shortcomings, not the message itself.
mistral_translation: “Make bean cakes for me so we can eat together”: a person’s refusal is what causes it to be said like this.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights how people often make insincere offers only after being turned down, revealing their true reluctance.
llama_translation: Give me a corn and I will use it to eat and be full
llama_interpretation: A small opportunity can lead to greater satisfaction and fulfillment.

yoruba: Ẹni tí kò lè gbé eèrà, tí ńkùsà sí erin, títẹ́ ní ńtẹ́.
english_literal: A person who lacks the strength to lift an ant but rushes forward to lift an elephant ends in disgrace.
interpretation_gold: One should know one's capabilities and limit oneself to what one can accomplish.
deepseek_translation: One who cannot carry an ant, yet claims to carry an elephant, is merely lying.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against boasting about abilities one clearly lacks, emphasizing humility and honesty.
claude_translation: The person who cannot carry an ant but keeps provoking an elephant is only stepping on themselves
claude_interpretation: Those who pick fights with opponents far stronger than themselves will only bring harm upon themselves.
gemini_translation: He who cannot carry an ant, but complains about an elephant, will be disgraced.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to complain about a large task when one cannot even handle a small one.
mistral_translation: The one who cannot carry an ant, yet throws dirt at an elephant, is only deceiving himself.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against overestimating one's abilities while belittling those stronger or more capable.
llama_translation: The person who cannot carry a load, is crying out to carry an elephant, will eventually carry it.
llama_interpretation: One who is determined and persistent will eventually accomplish what seems impossible.

yoruba: Ẹní dádé ti kúrò lọ́mọdé.
english_literal: The person who wears a crown has outgrown childhood.
interpretation_gold: A high office carries high responsibilities with it.
deepseek_translation: The person who wears a crown is not a child.
deepseek_interpretation: Leadership and responsibility require maturity and experience.
claude_translation: The one who wears a crown has departed from childhood
claude_interpretation: Leadership and responsibility require maturity and the abandonment of childish ways.
gemini_translation: He who wears the crown has ceased to be a child.
gemini_interpretation: Assuming a position of leadership or responsibility signifies the end of childhood and the beginning of maturity.
mistral_translation: The one who wore the crown has left, leaving it for the youth
mistral_interpretation: When leaders or elders pass away or step aside, the younger generation must take up responsibility
llama_translation: The person who wears a crown is the one who goes to the market
llama_interpretation: Leadership comes with responsibilities and challenges.

yoruba: Ṣàgbà-ṣàgbà ò níí sé àgbà títí láí.
english_literal: The elderly person who acts his proper part will always be respected as an elder.
interpretation_gold: If responsible people wish to be retain people's respect they must always act like elders.
deepseek_translation: Growing old does not necessarily mean growing wise.
deepseek_interpretation: Age does not always bring wisdom; experience and learning are required.
claude_translation: Pretending to be an elder does not make one a true elder forever
claude_interpretation: Fake maturity or wisdom will eventually be exposed as authentic leadership requires genuine experience and character.
gemini_translation: An elder will not be an elder forever.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the transient nature of power, authority, or any position, suggesting that one's time in a particular role is limited.
mistral_translation: No matter how old an elder is, they will not become an elder forever without end
mistral_interpretation: Even the most respected elders must eventually pass away, reminding us of the inevitability of death and the importance of humility
llama_translation: Elder-elder does not make one an elder forever.
llama_interpretation: Respect and authority are not solely based on age, but on continued demonstration of wisdom and character.

yoruba: Ẹni tí ìbá hùwà ipá ò hùwà ipá; ẹni tí ìbá hùwà ẹ̀lẹ̀ ò hu ẹ̀lẹ̀; ọ̀kùn tó nígba ọwọ́, tó nígba ẹsẹ̀ ńhùwà pẹ̀lẹ́.
english_literal: The person one would expect to be reckless is not reckless; the person one would expect to be cautious is not cautious; the millipede with two hundred arms and two hundred legs behaves very gently.
interpretation_gold: Even though one has a great deal of weight, one should still tread lightly.
deepseek_translation: The one who would act strong does not act strong; the one who would act lazy does not act lazy; the rope that has both hands and feet behaves gently.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that true strength and character are revealed in humility and adaptability, not in overt displays.
claude_translation: One who would behave violently does not behave violently; one who would behave gently does not behave gently; the rope that has a hundred hands and a hundred feet behaves gently.
claude_interpretation: True strength and power are demonstrated through gentleness and restraint, not through force or aggression.
gemini_translation: He who would have acted violently did not act violently; he who would have acted deceitfully did not act deceitfully; the rope that has two hundred hands and two hundred feet acts gently.
gemini_interpretation: Even those with great power or capability should choose to act with gentleness and restraint.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "He who would have acted violently did not act violently; he who would have acted deceitfully did not act deceitfully; the rope that has two hundred hands and two hundred feet acts gently.", "interpretation": "Even those with great power or capability should choose to act with gentleness and restraint."}
mistral_translation: The one who would act with force does not act with force; the one who would act with gentleness does not act with gentleness; the rope that is used for the hand is the same one used for the foot, acting gently.
mistral_interpretation: A person should adapt their behavior to the situation, using strength or gentleness as needed, rather than being rigid in their approach.
llama_translation: The person who is called to the forest does not hear the forest; the person who is called to the farm does not hear the farm; the river that has a source has a place where it flows.
llama_interpretation: One must follow their calling or destiny, as it is the source of their purpose and direction in life.

yoruba: Ẹ̀yá ló bí mi, ẹkùn ló wò mí dàgbà, ológìnní gbà mí tọ́; bí kò sẹ́ran lọ́bẹ̀ nkò jẹ.
english_literal: I was born of a monkey; I was raised by a leopard, I was adopted by a cat; if there is no meat in the stew I will not eat it.
interpretation_gold: I will not act in a way inconsistent with my upbringing.
deepseek_translation: My mother gave birth to me, the leopard raised me, the wealthy took me in; if not for the animal in the bush, I would not eat.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes gratitude and acknowledges the various sources of support and sustenance in one's life.
claude_translation: A fish gave birth to me, a leopard raised me to adulthood, a crocodile rescued me; if there is no meat in the soup I will not eat.
claude_interpretation: Someone who has experienced extraordinary care and protection throughout life develops refined tastes and high expectations.
gemini_translation: A leopard gave birth to me, a tiger raised me, a cat adopted me; if there is no meat in the soup, I will not eat.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes a person's strong and unyielding nature, suggesting they are accustomed to the best and will not settle for less.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A leopard gave birth to me, a tiger raised me, a cat adopted me; if there is no meat in the soup, I will not eat.", "interpretation": "This proverb emphasizes a person's strong and unyielding nature, suggesting they are accustomed to the best and will not settle for less."}
mistral_translation: It was a leopard that gave birth to me, a tiger that raised me to adulthood, a hunter took me; if it doesn't taste like meat, what else should I eat?
mistral_interpretation: One's upbringing and environment shape their behavior, so they should not be blamed for acting according to their nature.
llama_translation: My mother gave birth to me, a tiger raised me to adulthood, an elephant took me to its bosom; if I don't behave like a beast, what will I do?
llama_interpretation: One's upbringing and environment shape their behavior and character.

yoruba: “Ẹ fà á wọlé” ló yẹ ẹlẹ́ṣin.
english_literal: “Lead it into the stable” is what becomes a horseman.
interpretation_gold: To be able to afford a horse but not a groom is something of a disgrace.
deepseek_translation: “It pulled it inside” is proper for the horse.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that actions should be appropriate to the context or the subject involved.
claude_translation: It is 'pull it inside' that befits the horse owner
claude_interpretation: A responsible owner should protect and secure their valuable possessions rather than leaving them exposed to harm or theft.
gemini_translation: “Pull it inside” is what suits the horse owner.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb advises that one should take responsibility for their own belongings or problems, rather than expecting others to do so.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "“Pull it inside” is what suits the horse owner.", "interpretation": "This proverb advises that one should take responsibility for their own belongings or problems, rather than expecting others to do so."}
mistral_translation: It is 'drag it inside' that suits the horse owner
mistral_interpretation: One should act in ways that directly benefit or suit their own position or responsibilities.
llama_translation: It is the one who has not entered that says the house is not big
llama_interpretation: One should not judge or criticize something without experiencing it firsthand.

yoruba: Ọ̀gẹ̀gẹ́ ò lẹ́wà; lásán ló fara wéṣu.
english_literal: The poisonous cassava has no attraction; it resembles a yam only in vain.
interpretation_gold: No imitation can be as good as the real thing.
deepseek_translation: The hoe is not beautiful; it is merely covered with earth.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that true value lies in usefulness, not outward appearance.
claude_translation: The plantain has no beauty; it only resembles the yam.
claude_interpretation: People should not judge others based on superficial appearances, as true worth lies beyond outward looks.
gemini_translation: The razor does not have beauty; it only resembles the yam beetle in vain.
gemini_interpretation: Outward appearances can be deceiving, and something that looks similar to something valuable may in fact be worthless.
mistral_translation: The hoe does not beautify; it is merely what covers the buttocks
mistral_interpretation: Outward appearances or possessions do not define true worth or dignity
llama_translation: The forest is not a cloth; it is the leaves that make it thick.
llama_interpretation: Many small contributions can collectively make a significant impact.

yoruba: Ṣágo ḿbúgò, ó ló ṣẹnu gbáṣọ́rọ́.
english_literal: The demijohn insults the bottle, saying the latter has a long snout.
interpretation_gold: It is silly to pick a blemish one shares as the basis for insulting others; the pot should not call the kettle black.
deepseek_translation: The squirrel climbs the tree, it is there it cracks the palm kernel.
deepseek_interpretation: One must face challenges directly to achieve success.
claude_translation: The cassava flour is swelling, it has gone to make the mouth argue.
claude_interpretation: When someone becomes prosperous or gains status, they often become arrogant and argumentative.
gemini_translation: The chameleon is scolding the snail, saying it has a mouth that makes a loud noise.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights hypocrisy, where someone criticizes another for a fault they themselves possess or for a characteristic that is natural to the other.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The chameleon is scolding the snail, saying it has a mouth that makes a loud noise.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights hypocrisy, where someone criticizes another for a fault they themselves possess or for a characteristic that is natural to the other."}
mistral_translation: The frog that puffs itself up has a mouth that is too wide for its body.
mistral_interpretation: Overconfidence or boasting often leads to one's downfall or embarrassment.
llama_translation: The cloth that is not sold, it is the one that is used to tie the load.
llama_interpretation: One should make use of what is readily available rather than waiting for something better.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a fẹ́ yàtọ̀ sí ẹni tó ní kò sí irú òun.
english_literal: A person one loves is different from a person who says there is no one like him/herself.
interpretation_gold: One's worth is more a matter of what other people think of one than what one thinks of oneself.
deepseek_translation: The person we love is different from the one who says there is none like him.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that genuine love and appreciation come from others, not from self-praise or arrogance.
claude_translation: The person we want to be different from is the one who says there is no one like them
claude_interpretation: We often seek to distinguish ourselves from those who are arrogant or boastful about their uniqueness.
gemini_translation: The one we love is different from the one who says there is no one like them.
gemini_interpretation: True love is distinct from self-admiration or arrogance.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one we love is different from the one who says there is no one like them.", "interpretation": "True love is distinct from self-admiration or arrogance."}
mistral_translation: The person we want to be different from the one who has what we lack.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against envying others for what they have while ignoring one's own unique qualities or circumstances.
llama_translation: The person we love is the one who has no equal
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the tendency to idealize and uniquely value those we love or admire.

yoruba: Ẹyẹ akòko-ó ní òún le gbẹ́ odó; ta ní jẹ́ fi odó akòko gúnyán jẹ?
english_literal: The woodpecker boasts that it can carve a mortar; who ever used a mortar carved by the woodpecker to make pounded yam?
interpretation_gold: The puny person's best efforts cannot amount to much.
deepseek_translation: The first bird claims it can carry the mortar; who dares use the first bird's mortar to eat pounded yam?
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against overestimating one's abilities or making empty boasts.
claude_translation: The woodpecker says it can dry up the river; who will use a dried river to swallow pounded yam?
claude_interpretation: Empty boasts that harm communal resources ultimately hurt the boaster themselves, as they depend on those same resources.
gemini_translation: The woodpecker says it can carry a mortar; who would use a woodpecker's mortar to pound yam and eat?
gemini_interpretation: Boasting about an ability that is impractical or useless is meaningless.
mistral_translation: The akoko bird says it can carry a pot; who then uses the akoko pot to pound yam?
mistral_interpretation: One should not overestimate their abilities or take on tasks beyond their capacity.
llama_translation: The bird that is learning to fly is the one that will carry the load; who will carry the load for the bird that is still learning to fly?
llama_interpretation: One must take responsibility for their own actions and decisions, rather than relying on others to do so.

yoruba: Ọlọgbọ́n kan ò ta kókó omi sáṣọ; ọ̀mọ̀ràn kan ò mọ oye erùpẹ̀ ilẹ̀.
english_literal: No wise man ever ties water in a knot in his cloth; no knowledgeable person can tell the number of grains of sand on the earth.
interpretation_gold: There are certain feats that are beyond even the most accomplished of men.
deepseek_translation: One hundred rats cannot tie a water pot; one foolish person does not know the value of a grinding stone.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights that numbers without wisdom are useless, and foolishness leads to undervaluing important things.
claude_translation: A wise person does not sell cocoa pods for cloth; an intelligent person does not know the value of earth's dust.
claude_interpretation: True wisdom lies in recognizing that some things of great value cannot be measured by conventional standards or exchanged for material goods.
gemini_translation: A wise person does not sell water in a calabash; a knowledgeable person does not know the quantity of sand on the ground.
gemini_interpretation: Even the wisest and most knowledgeable individuals have limitations to their understanding and capabilities.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A wise person does not sell water in a calabash; a knowledgeable person does not know the quantity of sand on the ground.", "interpretation": "Even the wisest and most knowledgeable individuals have limitations to their understanding and capabilities."}
mistral_translation: One wise cat does not sell water cocoons in a cloth; one knowledgeable person does not know the meaning of the earth's dust.
mistral_interpretation: No matter how wise or knowledgeable someone is, there are always limits to their understanding.
llama_translation: One snail shell cannot contain the entire ocean; one child cannot inherit the entire family's wealth.
llama_interpretation: No single individual can possess or control everything.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a gbé gun ẹlẹ́dẹ̀, ìwọ̀n ni kó yọ̀ mọ; ẹni tó gẹṣin, ilẹ̀ ló ḿbọ̀.
english_literal: The person whom people have seated on a pig should moderate his or her strutting; even a horse rider will eventually come down to earth.
interpretation_gold: One should not let one's good fortune go to one's head; circumstances do change.
deepseek_translation: The person who is lifted onto the elephant's back, it is the rope that he holds onto; the person who rides the horse, the ground is what he fears.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should be mindful of the support and dangers associated with their position or status.
claude_translation: The person who is lifted onto a pig should know when to come down; the person who mounts a horse is heading to the ground.
claude_interpretation: One should know when to step down from power or position gracefully, as all elevated positions are temporary and will eventually end.
gemini_translation: He who is carried on a pig should be careful not to fall; he who rides a horse will eventually come down to the ground.
gemini_interpretation: Even those in positions of power or privilege should remain humble and aware that their elevated status is temporary.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "He who is carried on a pig should be careful not to fall; he who rides a horse will eventually come down to the ground.", "interpretation": "Even those in positions of power or privilege should remain humble and aware that their elevated status is temporary."}
mistral_translation: The one who rides a pig must bend low; the one who rides a horse, the ground is what approaches.
mistral_interpretation: One's status or circumstances dictate the level of humility or caution required in life.
llama_translation: The person who carries a load on his head, his back does not know; the person who carries a load on his back, his house knows.
llama_interpretation: One's burden is not truly known to others, only those closest to them are aware of their struggles.

yoruba: Ọwọ́ àìdilẹ̀ ní ńyọ koríko lójú àna ẹ̀.
english_literal: Idle hands are the ones obliged to remove grass specks from their in-law's eyes.
interpretation_gold: People who are unemployed can expect to be asked to perform all sorts of belittling tasks.
deepseek_translation: The hand that does not rest plucks grass in the face of the elder.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that disrespectful or hasty actions will lead to shame or rebuke from elders.
claude_translation: The hand that does not touch the ground is what removes grass from the face of its in-law
claude_interpretation: Those who avoid getting their hands dirty with work are quick to criticize or interfere in others' affairs.
gemini_translation: A hand that does not weed is what causes grass to grow in its path.
gemini_interpretation: Neglecting one's responsibilities or duties leads to problems and obstacles in one's life.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A hand that does not weed is what causes grass to grow in its path.", "interpretation": "Neglecting one's responsibilities or duties leads to problems and obstacles in one's life."}
mistral_translation: The hand that does not farm celebrates the grass on the neighbor's farm
mistral_interpretation: Those who fail to work hard often envy others' success without acknowledging their own lack of effort.
llama_translation: The hand that does not work does not eat the head of the fish.
llama_interpretation: One must work to enjoy the benefits of life.

yoruba: Ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ ò mẹ̀yẹ.
english_literal: A pig does not know what is becoming.
interpretation_gold: Some people do not know fitting behavior.
deepseek_translation: The pig does not know proverbs.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb implies that some people lack wisdom or understanding despite opportunities to learn.
claude_translation: A pig does not know shame
claude_interpretation: Some people lack self-awareness and continue behaving inappropriately without feeling embarrassed about their actions.
gemini_translation: A pig does not know honor.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that some individuals are incapable of appreciating or understanding what is valuable or honorable.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A pig does not know honor.", "interpretation": "This proverb suggests that some individuals are incapable of appreciating or understanding what is valuable or honorable."}
mistral_translation: The owner of the pig does not defecate.
mistral_interpretation: One should not behave in a way that brings shame or disgrace to their own family or community.
llama_translation: The tongue does not know two
llama_interpretation: One should be truthful and consistent in their words and actions.

yoruba: Ẹ̀gbọ́n ṣíwájú ó so aṣọ kọ́; àbúrò-ó kẹ́hìn ó wẹ̀wù; bí a ò mọ̀lẹ, ọ̀lẹ ò mọ araa rẹ̀?
english_literal: The elder walks in front, a loincloth draped over his shoulder; the younger walks behind, wearing a garment; if people cannot tell which one is shiftless, does he not know himself?
interpretation_gold: The shiftless person cannot hide his shiftlessness either from himself or from others.
deepseek_translation: The elder in front tears the cloth; the younger behind wears the torn cloth; if we do not know the lazy one, does the lazy one not know himself?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the consequences of irresponsibility, where the actions of the elder (or leader) negatively affect the younger (or follower), and questions self-awareness in such situations.
claude_translation: The elder goes ahead and doesn't tie his cloth properly; the younger one follows behind and doesn't dress well; if we don't know the lazy one, doesn't the lazy one know himself?
claude_interpretation: When both leaders and followers fail in their responsibilities, the one who is truly at fault should recognize their own shortcomings.
gemini_translation: The elder brother went ahead and hung clothes to dry; the younger brother came behind and wore clothes; if we don't know the lazy person, the lazy person doesn't know himself?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the contrast between hard work and laziness, suggesting that a lazy person may not recognize their own idleness unless it is pointed out or compared to the diligence of others.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The elder brother went ahead and hung clothes to dry; the younger brother came behind and wore clothes; if we don't know the lazy person, the lazy person doesn't know himself?", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the contrast between hard work and laziness, suggesting that a lazy person may not recognize their own idleness unless it is pointed out or compared to the diligence of others."}
mistral_translation: The elder sibling in front tears the cloth; the younger sibling behind washes it; if we don't know a lazy person, does the lazy person not know themselves?
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights how people often recognize others' faults while ignoring their own, especially in matters of responsibility and effort.
llama_translation: The elder sibling precedes and wears the cloth; the younger sibling follows and tears it; if we don't know the road, does the road know us?
llama_interpretation: Experience and wisdom come from those who have gone before us, and we should learn from their examples to avoid mistakes.

yoruba: Ẹni tí kò tó gèlètè kì í mí fìn-ìn.
english_literal: A person who is not huge in stature does not breathe heavily.
interpretation_gold: One should match one's strutting to one's accomplishment.
deepseek_translation: A person who cannot afford a small bell does not wear one.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not pretend to have what they cannot afford or do not possess.
claude_translation: One who cannot reach the gelede mask does not blow the flute
claude_interpretation: A person should not attempt tasks or roles that are beyond their capabilities or status.
gemini_translation: One who is not strong enough to lift a heavy load does not breathe heavily.
gemini_interpretation: People do not attempt tasks for which they are clearly unqualified or incapable.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who is not strong enough to lift a heavy load does not breathe heavily.", "interpretation": "People do not attempt tasks for which they are clearly unqualified or incapable."}
mistral_translation: The one who is not light-footed does not step on excrement stealthily
mistral_interpretation: A person who lacks caution or skill will inevitably encounter trouble or embarrassment
llama_translation: A person who does not reach the ceiling does not know the depth of the room.
llama_interpretation: One must experience challenges to appreciate the value of overcoming them.

yoruba: Ọbẹ̀ kì í gbé inú àgbà mì.
english_literal: A stew does not slush around once inside an elder.
interpretation_gold: An elder should know how to keep confidences.
deepseek_translation: The soup does not carry the elder's belly.
deepseek_interpretation: One must take action to benefit from opportunities, as nothing will be handed to you without effort.
claude_translation: Soup does not shake an elder's stomach.
claude_interpretation: An experienced person is not easily disturbed or unsettled by minor issues that might affect others.
gemini_translation: Soup does not stay in the elder's stomach and spoil.
gemini_interpretation: Elders are expected to share their wisdom and knowledge, not hoard it.
mistral_translation: Soup does not fill the belly of an elder.
mistral_interpretation: Elders require more than just basic sustenance; they need respect, wisdom, and meaningful engagement.
llama_translation: A knife does not reside in the belly of an elder
llama_interpretation: One should not harbor malice or ill intentions towards a respected elder or authority figure.

yoruba: Ẹni à bá tà ká fowó-o rẹ̀ ra àtùpà: ó ní òun à-jí-tanná-wò-lóru.
english_literal: A person who should be sold for money to purchase a lamp boasts that he is one-people-light-lamps-to-admire-at-night.
interpretation_gold: A person most unwanted in a company regards himself/herself as the soul of the party.
deepseek_translation: The person we sold to buys a lamp with his own money: he says he does not wake up to look around in the dark.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches self-reliance and the importance of using one's own resources to solve problems.
claude_translation: The person we sell to and they use their money to buy a lamp says they will wake up to look at light at night
claude_interpretation: People often make foolish purchases or decisions and then try to justify them with elaborate explanations.
gemini_translation: The one we sold to buy a lamp: he says he is one to be lit at night to be seen.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony of someone claiming importance or usefulness only after being discarded or repurposed for a different, often lesser, function.
mistral_translation: Whoever sells us a lamp and we use our money to buy a wick: they say they are the one who lights up the night.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against taking undue credit for another person's effort or investment.
llama_translation: Whoever is going to fight should look at the size of his buttocks: he says he who has a big buttock should not be afraid of a fall
llama_interpretation: One should consider their own limitations and capabilities before taking on a challenge.

yoruba: Ọ̀wọ́n là ńra ògo, ọ̀pọ̀ là ńra ọ̀bùn, iyekíye là ńra ìmẹ́lẹ́.
english_literal: Honor is always bought dear, filthiness cheap, and idleness at an indifferent price.
interpretation_gold: Nothing is more difficult to come by than honor.
deepseek_translation: Honor is bought with money, a spoon is bought with plenty, carefulness is bought with patience.
deepseek_interpretation: Different things require different approaches or resources to achieve them.
claude_translation: It is with money that one buys honor, it is with abundance that one buys respect, it is with whatever one has that one buys knowledge.
claude_interpretation: Different valuable things in life require different types of resources to acquire, but knowledge can be obtained regardless of one's financial status.
gemini_translation: Honor is bought at a high price, a lazy person is bought cheaply, a worthless person is bought at any price.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that valuable things like honor require significant effort and sacrifice, while undesirable traits like laziness and worthlessness are easily acquired or come with little cost.
mistral_translation: It is with a thin hand we buy prestige, with a thick hand we buy a hoe, and with a beautiful hand we buy laziness
mistral_interpretation: One's spending habits reflect their priorities—whether on status, hard work, or idleness
llama_translation: The hands are washing the legs, the legs are washing the buttocks, the buttocks are washing the thighs.
llama_interpretation: Everyone has a role to play in helping one another, and no one is too high or too low to assist another.

yoruba: Ẹni tí à ńwò láwò-sunkún ńwo ara-a rẹ̀ láwò-rẹ́rìnín.
english_literal: A person whose appearance moves one to tears is moved to laughter by his own appearance.
interpretation_gold: The miserable person has no notion of his own miserableness.
deepseek_translation: The person who is crying is also laughing at himself.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the duality of human emotions, suggesting that joy and sorrow often coexist in life.
claude_translation: The person we are looking at with tears in our eyes is looking at themselves with laughter in their eyes
claude_interpretation: People often pity others who are actually content with their situation, while those being pitied may find joy or satisfaction in circumstances that appear unfortunate to outsiders.
gemini_translation: The one we are looking at with tearful eyes is looking at himself with laughing eyes.
gemini_interpretation: People often perceive their own situations differently, and sometimes more positively, than how others perceive them.
mistral_translation: The person who is looking at you with a sad face is looking at themselves with a smiling face.
mistral_interpretation: People often criticize or pity others for faults they themselves possess.
llama_translation: The person who is searching for a needle in the darkness is searching for his own body in the darkness.
llama_interpretation: One should focus on solving their own problems rather than trying to solve others'.

yoruba: Ẹni tí a ò fẹ́, àlọ́ ò kàn án.
english_literal: A person whose company is not desired gets no turn at riddling.
interpretation_gold: A person not wanted in a group should not press his or her rights.
deepseek_translation: The person we do not love, the story does not concern them.
deepseek_interpretation: This means that people who are not favored or loved are often excluded or ignored in matters that do not concern them.
claude_translation: The person who is not loved, soap does not touch them.
claude_interpretation: Someone who is disliked or rejected by others will not receive care or attention from anyone.
gemini_translation: The one we do not like, going away does not concern them.
gemini_interpretation: People who are disliked or unwanted are not affected by the departure of those who dislike them.
mistral_translation: The person we do not like, their story does not concern us.
mistral_interpretation: One should not waste time or energy on people or matters that do not deserve attention.
llama_translation: The person we do not trust, we do not tell our secret.
llama_interpretation: One should be cautious about sharing confidential information with someone they do not trust.

yoruba: Ẹni tó tijú tì í fún ara-a rẹ̀.
english_literal: The person who is self-aware protects his or her own reputation thereby.
interpretation_gold: Good character benefits the owner more than others.
deepseek_translation: The person who has shame takes care of themselves.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that self-respect leads to self-discipline and proper conduct.
claude_translation: The person who feels shame feels it for themselves.
claude_interpretation: Shame is a personal emotion that one experiences individually, and each person is responsible for their own feelings of embarrassment or disgrace.
gemini_translation: He who is ashamed is ashamed for himself.
gemini_interpretation: Shame is a personal experience and its burden is borne by the individual who feels it.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "He who is ashamed is ashamed for himself.", "interpretation": "Shame is a personal experience and its burden is borne by the individual who feels it."}
mistral_translation: The person who is too shy will provide for themselves.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive shyness or hesitation can prevent one from receiving help, forcing them to rely on their own efforts.
llama_translation: The person who wakes up early will have it at his own body's disposal
llama_interpretation: Rising early gives one control over their day and destiny.

yoruba: Ọ̀nà ọ̀fun ò gba egungun ẹja.
english_literal: The throat cannot accommodate fish-bone.
interpretation_gold: Everybody and everything has some limitation.
deepseek_translation: The throat's path does not accommodate fish bones.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against engaging in actions or behaviors that are inherently risky or unsuitable.
claude_translation: The path of the crab does not carry fish bones
claude_interpretation: Each person must follow their own natural way and cannot take on burdens or responsibilities that don't belong to their nature or path in life.
gemini_translation: The throat does not accept fish bones.
gemini_interpretation: Some things are inherently incompatible or unsuitable for certain situations.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The throat does not accept fish bones.", "interpretation": "Some things are inherently incompatible or unsuitable for certain situations."}
mistral_translation: The smooth path does not accommodate the fish bone.
mistral_interpretation: Easy or comfortable situations do not prepare one for life's challenges or difficulties.
llama_translation: The path of the river does not block the movement of fish.
llama_interpretation: One should not obstruct others from pursuing their goals or destiny.

yoruba: Ọjọ́ àgbà-á kú sàn ju ọjọ́ àgbà-á tẹ́.
english_literal: The day an elder dies is far better than the day an elder is disgraced.
interpretation_gold: Death is preferable to disgrace.
deepseek_translation: The day the elder dies is better than the elder's day.
deepseek_interpretation: It is better to honor elders while they are alive than to celebrate them only after death.
claude_translation: The day an elder dies is better than the day an elder is disgraced
claude_interpretation: It is better to die with honor than to live in shame and disgrace.
gemini_translation: The day an elder dies is better than the day an elder is disgraced.
gemini_interpretation: It is preferable for an elder to die with their dignity intact than to live and face public shame.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The day an elder dies is better than the day an elder is disgraced.", "interpretation": "It is preferable for an elder to die with their dignity intact than to live and face public shame."}
mistral_translation: The day an elder dies is better than the day an elder becomes senile
mistral_interpretation: It is preferable for an elder to die with dignity than to live in a state of helplessness or loss of respect
llama_translation: The rain that falls on the elderly is more than the rain that falls on the elderly's roof
llama_interpretation: The elderly bear more burdens and responsibilities than others.

yoruba: Ọ̀rọ̀ bọ̀tí-bọ̀tí ò yẹ àgbàlagbà.
english_literal: Speech like drunken babble does not befit a venerable person.
interpretation_gold: Responsible adults should be very careful about what they say.
deepseek_translation: Too much talk does not befit an elder.
deepseek_interpretation: Elders should speak wisely and sparingly to maintain respect.
claude_translation: Careless or reckless speech does not befit an elder
claude_interpretation: Mature people should speak thoughtfully and responsibly, as wisdom comes with age and experience.
gemini_translation: Whispered words do not befit an elder.
gemini_interpretation: Elders are expected to be transparent and straightforward in their communication, avoiding secrecy or gossip.
mistral_translation: Words spoken bit by bit do not suit an elder.
mistral_interpretation: An elder should speak directly and clearly, not in a roundabout or hesitant manner.
llama_translation: A matter that is not clear is not a big matter.
llama_interpretation: Clarity is essential for resolving conflicts or making progress in any situation.

yoruba: Ọ̀yájú-u baálé ní ńpàdé ìbòsí lọ́nà.
english_literal: It is a reckless home owner who is met with alarms when he ventures outside.
interpretation_gold: A patriarch who misbehaves earns disgrace.
deepseek_translation: The eyes of the household head meet the buttocks on the way.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that disrespect or misbehavior will eventually be noticed and confronted by those in authority.
claude_translation: It is the shameless head of household that meets disgrace on the road
claude_interpretation: A leader who acts without dignity or proper conduct will inevitably face public humiliation.
gemini_translation: The impudence of the household head is what meets disgrace on the road.
gemini_interpretation: A leader's arrogance or disrespect can lead to public humiliation for themselves and their community.
mistral_translation: It is the owner of the house who meets the thief on the way
