gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that one should not be overly confident or boastful when they have a powerful protector, as it can lead to recklessness or a false sense of security.
mistral_translation: The chicken that sees a loincloth kills its own mother.
mistral_interpretation: A person who fails to recognize the value of what they have may destroy their own source of support or blessing.
llama_translation: A chicken sees a kite, it kills its mother
llama_interpretation: This proverb warns against false alarms or unnecessary panic that can lead to harm or destruction.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpà èèyàn ò mọ̀ pé ohun tó pọ̀-ọ́ lè tán.
english_literal: A wastrel does not know that what is plentiful can be used up.
interpretation_gold: A wastrel knows no thrift.
deepseek_translation: The arm does not know that what is plenty can finish.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against overconfidence in abundance, reminding us that resources can deplete unexpectedly.
claude_translation: The arm of a person does not know that what is abundant can finish.
claude_interpretation: People often waste resources when they are plentiful, not realizing that abundance can eventually come to an end.
gemini_translation: A foolish person does not know that what is abundant can finish.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb warns against complacency and encourages prudence, reminding us that even seemingly inexhaustible resources can deplete over time.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A foolish person does not know that what is abundant can finish.", "interpretation": "This proverb warns against complacency and encourages prudence, reminding us that even seemingly inexhaustible resources can deplete over time."}
mistral_translation: A person's arm does not know that what is gathered can finish.
mistral_interpretation: People often overlook the reality that resources or opportunities are limited and can be exhausted.
llama_translation: A person's back does not know what is on its head
llama_interpretation: One's past experiences or accomplishments do not guarantee future success or recognition.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ogun dán ẹ̀ṣọ́ wò.
english_literal: One does not tease a warrior by saying there is a war (or an invasion.)
interpretation_gold: Do not play with a loaded and primed gun.
deepseek_translation: We do not use war to test the strength of a squirrel.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not use excessive force to deal with minor issues.
claude_translation: One does not use medicine to test a curse.
claude_interpretation: It is unwise to experiment with dangerous or harmful things just to see what will happen.
gemini_translation: One does not use war to test a guard.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to test the loyalty or capability of a protector by creating a dangerous situation.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not use war to test a guard.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to test the loyalty or capability of a protector by creating a dangerous situation."}
mistral_translation: We do not use twenty thousand cowries to buy a mere wrapper.
mistral_interpretation: It is unwise to expend excessive resources or effort on something of little value or importance.
llama_translation: We do not use medicine to treat a boil that is not yet ripe.
llama_interpretation: One should not intervene in a situation prematurely, before it has fully developed or matured.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláṣedànù tí ńfajá ṣọdẹ ẹja.
english_literal: A wastrel “who” uses a dog to stalk fish.
interpretation_gold: It is folly to employ an impossible tool for a given task.
deepseek_translation: The fisherman who forgets to fish will blame the fish.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against blaming others for one's own negligence or failures.
claude_translation: The wasteful person who uses a dog to hunt for fish
claude_interpretation: Using the wrong method or tool for a task leads to failure and waste of resources.
gemini_translation: The wasteful person who uses a dog to hunt fish.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb criticizes someone who uses inappropriate or ineffective methods to achieve a goal, leading to wasted effort and resources.
mistral_translation: The careless person who fries fish at the riverside.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against reckless actions that expose one to unnecessary risks or losses.
llama_translation: The one who is selling fish is the one who is eating the fish.
llama_interpretation: Those who are in charge of something are often the ones who benefit the most from it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbọn kì í ṣe oúnjẹ ẹyẹ.
english_literal: Coconut is no food for birds.
interpretation_gold: Some things and some people are immune to some types of danger; one should not attempt the impossible.
deepseek_translation: The snail is not food for the bird.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not underestimate or mistreat those who appear vulnerable, as they may have hidden strengths or protections.
claude_translation: The coconut is not food for birds.
claude_interpretation: Some things are naturally beyond one's capacity or reach, and it's futile to attempt what you're not equipped to handle.
gemini_translation: The coconut is not food for the bird.
gemini_interpretation: Some things are beyond the capacity or reach of certain individuals or entities.
mistral_translation: The hornbill does not serve as food for birds
mistral_interpretation: A person of high status or unique ability is not easily replaced or taken advantage of by others
llama_translation: The snail does not cook the bird's food
llama_interpretation: One should not interfere with or try to control the affairs of someone more powerful or superior.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í duni lóyè ká fọ̀nà ilé-e Baálẹ̀ hanni.
english_literal: One does not compete with another for a chieftaincy title and also show the way to the king's house to the competitor.
interpretation_gold: A person should be treated either as an adversary or as an ally, not as both.
deepseek_translation: One does not become a king and then destroy the house of the Baale who helped them.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the importance of gratitude and not harming those who have helped you in your rise to success.
claude_translation: One does not honor someone with a title and then show them the way to the chief's house.
claude_interpretation: You cannot claim to respect someone's authority while simultaneously treating them as if they don't know their proper place or responsibilities.
gemini_translation: One does not contend with someone for a chieftaincy title and then show them the way to the Baale's house.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to help a rival or competitor, as it may lead to your own downfall.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not contend with someone for a chieftaincy title and then show them the way to the Baale's house.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to help a rival or competitor, as it may lead to your own downfall."}
mistral_translation: One does not jump over the path to the Baale's house in broad daylight
mistral_interpretation: It is unwise to openly disrespect or bypass authority figures in a way that is obvious to everyone.
llama_translation: We do not sleep and wake up to find the palace of the king in our house
llama_interpretation: One should not expect to achieve greatness or power overnight.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbá kì í di òtítọ́; ojo ni kì í jẹ́ ká dá a.
english_literal: Plans do not automatically bear fruit; only the faint-hearted do not make plans.
interpretation_gold: While plans may never bear fruit, people should still make them.
deepseek_translation: A lie does not become truth; it is time that prevents us from revealing it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that falsehood will eventually be exposed by time, emphasizing the importance of truth.
claude_translation: A shelter does not become truth; it is rain that prevents us from abandoning it
claude_interpretation: Temporary solutions or conveniences should not be mistaken for permanent truths or principles.
gemini_translation: A wish does not become truth; it is fear that prevents us from achieving it.
gemini_interpretation: Unrealized aspirations are often due to a lack of courage rather than the impossibility of the wish itself.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A wish does not become truth; it is fear that prevents us from achieving it.", "interpretation": "Unrealized aspirations are often due to a lack of courage rather than the impossibility of the wish itself."}
mistral_translation: A lie does not become truth; time will not allow us to make it so.
mistral_interpretation: No matter how long a lie persists, it will eventually be exposed by the truth over time.
llama_translation: The palm tree does not become a palm kernel; it is the rain that does not allow it to grow.
llama_interpretation: External factors can hinder one's growth or progress.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àìpé, “Tìrẹ nìyí” ní ḿbí ayé nínú.
english_literal: Neglect to say, “Here is your's” is what incites the earth's anger.
interpretation_gold: Failure to take account of people's possible influence on one's affairs incites their anger. As long as one assumes humility, people will let one be.
deepseek_translation: Patience, "It is yours" gives birth to life in it.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that patience and contentment lead to a fulfilling life.
claude_translation: Not long ago, 'This is yours' is what angers the world.
claude_interpretation: Claims of ownership and possessiveness are what cause conflict and discord among people.
gemini_translation: Not saying, 'This is yours' makes the world angry.
gemini_interpretation: Failing to acknowledge and give someone their due or rightful share causes resentment and conflict.
mistral_translation: Not calling it 'yours' is what makes the world swallow one inside
mistral_interpretation: Failing to assert ownership or claim what is rightfully yours can lead to loss or disadvantage
llama_translation: Wealth, “It is yours” is what the world says.
llama_interpretation: The world acknowledges and respects one's wealth and possessions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àbàtì àlàpà; a bà á tì, a bá a rẹ́.
english_literal: Unfinished abandoned wall: unable to master it, one befriends it.
interpretation_gold: One reconciles oneself to matters one cannot control.
deepseek_translation: The mat of the alaapaa; we spread it, we roll it up.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb signifies the transient nature of life and relationships, emphasizing that things come together and eventually part ways.
claude_translation: The palm frond shelter; we help build it, we help it fall down.
claude_interpretation: What we help to create, we also have the power to destroy.
gemini_translation: A wall that is collapsing; if we lean on it, we collapse with it.
gemini_interpretation: Relying on something unstable or unreliable will lead to one's own downfall.
mistral_translation: Like the one with a broken arm; we met it on the way, we left it on the way
mistral_interpretation: Some problems or misfortunes are inherent to a person and cannot be easily fixed by others.
llama_translation: The snail shell is beautiful; if it is not for the snail, it would not be beautiful.
llama_interpretation: One's worth is often tied to the value others place on them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣòroójà bí ìjà ọjà; onítìjú ò níí sá; ẹni tí ńnà án ò níí dáwọ́ dúró.
english_literal: Difficult-to-fight as the fight of the market place; the self-conscious person will not run, and the person beating him up will not stop.
interpretation_gold: Too much concern with appearances exposes one to occasional inconveniences.
deepseek_translation: Market noise is like market fight; the bystander will not run; the one fighting will not stop to look around.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that people involved in a conflict are too engrossed to notice its effects, while outsiders remain unaffected.
claude_translation: Market quarrel is like market fight; the shameful one will not run away; the one being beaten will not stop fighting.
claude_interpretation: In public disputes, pride and shame often prevent people from backing down even when it would be wise to do so.
gemini_translation: A difficult fight like a market fight; the shy one will not run away; the one beating him will not stop his hand.
gemini_interpretation: When a conflict is public and intense, those involved are often compelled to continue, regardless of personal discomfort or the desire to stop, due to the pressure of the situation.
mistral_translation: Like the noise of a market fight; the shameless one will not run away; the one who is involved will not stand aside.
mistral_interpretation: Those directly involved in a conflict or scandal cannot easily distance themselves, while the shameless remain undeterred.
llama_translation: The market dispute is like a market fight; the owner of the goods does not intervene; the one who is being beaten does not stop to think.
llama_interpretation: In times of conflict, those who can resolve the issue often stay neutral, leaving the parties involved to suffer the consequences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-sìnkú-àì-jogún, òṣì ní ńtani.
english_literal: Burying-the-dead-without-sharing-in-the-inheritance leads one to poverty.
interpretation_gold: One should have something to show for one's efforts.
deepseek_translation: He who buries but does not inherit, poverty is what he is calling.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against engaging in unprofitable or thankless tasks that bring no benefit to oneself.
claude_translation: Not dying without inheriting, poverty is what follows one
claude_interpretation: Those who fail to leave behind any inheritance or legacy for their descendants will only pass on poverty to their lineage.
gemini_translation: Not burying (the dead) and not inheriting, it is poverty that is afflicting one.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that the inability to perform funeral rites and inherit property are both indicators of extreme poverty.
mistral_translation: The one who does not attend funerals will not inherit, it is the poor who are being asked
mistral_interpretation: Those who avoid communal responsibilities or difficult tasks will miss out on benefits, while the disadvantaged are often burdened with expectations.
llama_translation: We do not mourn, we do not worship, the god of the forest is the one we worship.
llama_interpretation: One should prioritize the worship of a powerful and relevant deity over a lesser one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlejò tó bèèrè ọ̀nà kò níí sọnù.
english_literal: A stranger who asks the way will not get lost.
interpretation_gold: One should be willing to admit one's ignorance and seek direction.
deepseek_translation: A stranger who asks for directions will not get lost.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches the importance of seeking guidance to avoid mistakes or failure.
claude_translation: A visitor who asks for directions will not get lost.
claude_interpretation: Those who seek guidance and ask questions when uncertain will avoid making mistakes or failing in their endeavors.
gemini_translation: A visitor who asks for directions will not get lost.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to seek guidance when in unfamiliar situations to avoid making mistakes.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A visitor who asks for directions will not get lost.", "interpretation": "It is wise to seek guidance when in unfamiliar situations to avoid making mistakes."}
mistral_translation: A visitor who asks for directions will not get lost.
mistral_interpretation: Seeking guidance or advice prevents mistakes and ensures success.
llama_translation: A traveler who is in a hurry does not know the road
llama_interpretation: Haste can lead to confusion and mistakes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbẹ́ àwòrán gàgàrà ká má fi ọwọ́ ẹ ti nǹkan.
english_literal: One does not carve a tall statue without resting its hand on something.
interpretation_gold: Everybody needs some support.
deepseek_translation: One does not carry a heavy load and still have hands free for other things.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one cannot take on major responsibilities and still expect to handle minor tasks effortlessly.
claude_translation: We do not carry a tall portrait without using our hands to support something
claude_interpretation: Important or valuable things require careful handling and proper support to prevent damage or loss.
gemini_translation: One does not carve a giant image without supporting it with something.
gemini_interpretation: Significant achievements or large undertakings require substantial support and effort to be successful.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not carve a giant image without supporting it with something.", "interpretation": "Significant achievements or large undertakings require substantial support and effort to be successful."}
mistral_translation: We do not carry a picture far away only to use someone else's hand for the thing.
mistral_interpretation: One should not undertake a task and then rely on others to complete it, especially when it concerns personal responsibility.
llama_translation: We don't use a calabash to fetch water from a deep well
llama_interpretation: One should use the right tool or approach for a task to achieve success.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjímú kì í tí.
english_literal: The task one takes on waking in the morning does not flounder.
interpretation_gold: The task to which one gives the highest priority does not suffer.
deepseek_translation: The one who eats first does not get satisfied.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that greed or rushing to take everything for oneself does not lead to true fulfillment or success.
claude_translation: A newborn baby does not push
claude_interpretation: New or inexperienced people should not be expected to take on responsibilities or make decisions beyond their capabilities.
gemini_translation: The one who wakes up early does not get tired.
gemini_interpretation: Diligence and early effort lead to sustained productivity and success.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who wakes up early does not get tired.", "interpretation": "Diligence and early effort lead to sustained productivity and success."}
mistral_translation: A debt does not disappear.
mistral_interpretation: An obligation or responsibility must eventually be fulfilled, no matter how long it takes.
llama_translation: The one who is not present does not know
llama_interpretation: Absence can lead to ignorance or lack of understanding.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹran ikún gbọn ti àgbọ̀nrín nù.
english_literal: One does not brush off antelope meat with squirrel meat.
interpretation_gold: Never prefer something of little value to something of great value.
deepseek_translation: One does not throw away the meat of the antelope because of the deer's wisdom.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not discard something valuable due to another's perceived superiority.
claude_translation: One does not use squirrel meat to prepare soup when antelope is missing.
claude_interpretation: You should not settle for inferior substitutes when something of higher quality or value is unavailable.
gemini_translation: One does not use the meat of a squirrel to wipe off that of an antelope.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to use something of lesser value or significance to address or replace something of greater value or importance.
mistral_translation: One does not use the meat of a squirrel to replace what a leopard has lost.
mistral_interpretation: You cannot substitute something of little value for something far more valuable or irreplaceable.
llama_translation: We do not use the meat of a crocodile to feed a monitor lizard
llama_interpretation: One should not use something precious or valuable to satisfy someone who does not appreciate its worth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi owó du oyè-e alágbára.
english_literal: One does not rely on money to contest a chieftaincy reserved for the strong.
interpretation_gold: Money won't buy everything.
deepseek_translation: One does not use money to buy a powerful position.
deepseek_interpretation: Leadership or authority cannot be legitimately obtained through wealth alone.
claude_translation: One does not buy the title of a powerful person with money
claude_interpretation: True authority and respect cannot be purchased but must be earned through character and actions.
gemini_translation: One does not use money to contest for the chieftaincy of a powerful person.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to challenge a powerful individual in their area of strength, especially when they have an inherent advantage.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not use money to contest for the chieftaincy of a powerful person.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to challenge a powerful individual in their area of strength, especially when they have an inherent advantage."}
mistral_translation: We do not use money to measure the chieftaincy of a powerful person.
mistral_interpretation: True leadership and respect are earned through character and influence, not wealth or material possessions.
llama_translation: We don't use money to buy a title of a brave person
llama_interpretation: True bravery and honor cannot be bought with wealth or material possessions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-wí-fúnni-kó-tó-dáni, àgbà òmùjà ni.
english_literal: He-who-alerts-one-before-he-throws-one is a past master of wrestling.
interpretation_gold: One would be wise to avoid adversaries confident enough to show their hands beforehand.
deepseek_translation: One who warns before striking is an elder who avoids conflict.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of giving fair warning or advice before taking action, as a wise and peaceful approach to resolving disputes.
claude_translation: One who speaks to us before betraying us is an elder who respects boundaries
claude_interpretation: It is better to be warned or informed before being harmed, as this shows respect and maturity from the person causing the harm.
gemini_translation: One who warns before fighting is a wise warrior.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to give a warning or make one's intentions clear before engaging in conflict or taking action.
mistral_translation: If one speaks to you without respect, it is an elder of the market
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns that disrespectful speech often comes from those who hold influence or authority in public spaces.
llama_translation: We are not yet done with the funeral rites, the elder is still in the mortuary
llama_interpretation: One should not rush to take over a position or responsibility before the previous holder has fully relinquished it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ńyan lóko, aláìlóye-é ní ó jọ pẹ́pẹ́yẹ.
english_literal: The tortoise struts on the farm, the senseless person says it resembles a duck.
interpretation_gold: It is indeed a fool that cannot discern the obvious.
deepseek_translation: The tortoise dances in the farm, the ignorant says it is limping.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against misjudging someone's actions due to lack of understanding or knowledge.
claude_translation: The tortoise is defecating in the farm, the ignorant one says it looks like a duck
claude_interpretation: Ignorance leads people to misinterpret obvious situations or call things by wrong names.
gemini_translation: The tortoise is strutting in the farm, the ignorant one says it resembles a duck.
gemini_interpretation: Those who lack understanding often misinterpret or misjudge situations and individuals.
mistral_translation: The tortoise is boasting on the farm, the one who does not understand the situation thinks it is a duck
mistral_interpretation: A show-off may deceive those who are ignorant, but their true nature will eventually be revealed to the wise.
llama_translation: The tortoise is eating in the farm, it is not the owner of the farm that is eating quietly.
llama_interpretation: One who benefits from a situation is not necessarily the one who owns or controls it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú oko mú ẹjọ́ kí ọ̀kan má yẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not opt to work on the farm and also opt to go argue one's case and avoid neglecting one or the other.
interpretation_gold: One cannot do two mind-absorbing tasks at once.
deepseek_translation: One does not hold a hoe and a court case without one being neglected.
deepseek_interpretation: You cannot effectively handle two important tasks at the same time without one suffering.
claude_translation: One does not take a hoe and take a case to court so that one may not be right
claude_interpretation: You cannot pursue two different approaches to the same problem simultaneously and expect both to succeed.
gemini_translation: One does not take a farm and a lawsuit without one of them failing.
gemini_interpretation: It is difficult to manage two demanding tasks simultaneously without one suffering neglect or failure.
mistral_translation: One does not hold a hoe and a snake at the same time so that one does not get confused
mistral_interpretation: Avoid juggling too many tasks or responsibilities simultaneously to prevent mistakes or failure
llama_translation: We don't take a hoe to the farm to catch a rat so that one can be famous
llama_interpretation: One should not use excessive or inappropriate means to achieve a goal.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláǹtakùn, bí yóò bá ọ jà, a ta ká ọ lára.
english_literal: When the spider wants to engage an enemy, it spins its web around it.
interpretation_gold: The attentive person can detect signs of hostility before it occurs. Also, one makes good preparations before embarking on a venture.
deepseek_translation: Spider, if it fights you, we will squash it on your body.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that even if someone powerful (like a spider) tries to harm you, others will intervene to protect you by crushing the threat directly on you.
claude_translation: Spider, if it wants to fight you, it spins its web around you.
claude_interpretation: When someone intends to harm or oppose you, they will use their particular skills or resources as weapons against you.
gemini_translation: The spider, if it wants to fight you, it spins its web around you.
gemini_interpretation: One should be wary of those who subtly entrap or manipulate others before directly confronting them.
mistral_translation: The spider, if it will fight you, we sell it on its body
mistral_interpretation: One should be cautious of the consequences of provoking or underestimating a seemingly weak opponent, as they may have hidden strengths or resources.
llama_translation: The one who is not strong, if he wants to fight, he will be thrown to the ground.
llama_interpretation: One should not take on challenges that are beyond one's capabilities.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ, kàgbo wàrà; ọjọ́ ńlọ.
english_literal: Nursing mother, make the herbal decoction in good time; the day is waning.
interpretation_gold: Attend to duties in time.
deepseek_translation: The child of the soil, the milk is there; the day is coming.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb reminds us that patience and persistence will eventually be rewarded, as opportunities or blessings will come in due time.
claude_translation: Mother, do not listen to gossip; the day is passing.
claude_interpretation: Time is too precious to waste on idle talk or rumors, so focus on what truly matters.
gemini_translation: A nursing mother, prepare the herbal concoction quickly; the day is going.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the urgency of attending to responsibilities, especially those related to caregiving, as time is fleeting.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A nursing mother, prepare the herbal concoction quickly; the day is going.", "interpretation": "This proverb emphasizes the urgency of attending to responsibilities, especially those related to caregiving, as time is fleeting."}
mistral_translation: While breastfeeding, count the milk in the calabash; the day is passing.
mistral_interpretation: Make the most of available resources now, as time is running out.
llama_translation: The newborn, the rope is long; the rain is going.
llama_interpretation: New challenges or problems will arise as one navigates through life.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í tijú bá baálé ilé jẹ akátá; bó bá mú, ìwọ náà a mú tìẹ.
english_literal: One should not be too embarrassed to eat a jackal with one's host; as he helps himself, one also helps oneself.
interpretation_gold: Never be too bashful to adopt the ways of the people among whom you find yourself.
deepseek_translation: One does not feel ashamed to eat leftovers with the head of the house; if he grabs, you too will grab some.
deepseek_interpretation: It teaches the importance of humility and sharing resources within a family or community.
claude_translation: One does not feel ashamed to eat leftover food with the head of the household; if he takes some, you too should take yours.
claude_interpretation: There is no shame in sharing humble circumstances or simple pleasures with those in authority or respected positions.
gemini_translation: One does not shy away from eating a wild dog with the head of the household; if he catches it, you too will catch yours.
gemini_interpretation: One should not be ashamed to participate in a difficult or unusual task with a leader, as their success can lead to one's own.
mistral_translation: One does not shame the head of the household by eating a cat; if it is caught, you too will be caught in the same way.
mistral_interpretation: Do not mock or disrespect someone in a position of authority, as you may face similar consequences.
llama_translation: We don't wake up to find the owner of the house eating cornmeal; if he eats, you too will eat
llama_interpretation: When the leader or head of a household prospers, the members of the household also benefit.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ayé ńlọ, à ńtọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: The world goes forth, and we follow.
interpretation_gold: One lives according to what life confronts one with.
deepseek_translation: The world is going, we are following it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the inevitability of change and the need to adapt to life's constant transformations.
claude_translation: The world is going, we are following it.
claude_interpretation: We must adapt and move with the changing times rather than resist progress or change.
gemini_translation: The world is going, we are following it.
gemini_interpretation: Life is a continuous journey of progress and change, and we are all participants in its unfolding.
mistral_translation: The world is moving, we are just catching up.
mistral_interpretation: Life progresses continuously, and one must adapt to its changes rather than resist them.
llama_translation: The world is going, we are following
llama_interpretation: One must adapt to the changing circumstances of life.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í jẹ “Mo fẹ́rẹ̀-ẹ́” lọ́bẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not eat “I almost” in a stew.
interpretation_gold: What one missed narrowly, one cannot enjoy at all.
deepseek_translation: One does not eat 'I am hungry' in the soup.
deepseek_interpretation: Merely saying you are hungry does not fill your stomach; action is required to solve a problem.
claude_translation: One does not eat 'I almost had it' in soup
claude_interpretation: Mere intentions or near-successes cannot substitute for actual achievements or results.
gemini_translation: One does not eat 'I almost' in soup.
gemini_interpretation: Wishing or nearly achieving something is not the same as actually accomplishing it, and therefore yields no tangible benefit.
mistral_translation: We do not say 'I want to taste it' with a knife.
mistral_interpretation: One should not use inappropriate or excessive means to achieve a simple or harmless desire.
llama_translation: We don't eat 'I love you' in a time of hunger.
llama_interpretation: Words of affection are insufficient in times of need, action is required.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtàrí ìbá ṣe ìkòkò ká gbé e fún ọ̀tá yẹ̀wò; a ní ó ti fọ́ yányán.
english_literal: If one's head was a pot and one gave it to an enemy to inspect, he would say it was irretrievably broken.
interpretation_gold: An enemy is not one to trust with one's destiny.
deepseek_translation: Because we made a pot for the enemy to inspect; we say it has broken into pieces.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against revealing one's plans or weaknesses to adversaries, as they may exploit them.
claude_translation: If the head could be made into a pot to give to an enemy to examine, they would say it is already cracked beyond repair.
claude_interpretation: People will always find fault with you or criticize you harshly, especially your enemies, no matter how good or perfect you try to be.
gemini_translation: If the head were a pot, we would give it to the enemy to examine; he would say it is completely broken.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to expose one's vulnerabilities or weaknesses to an adversary, as they will exploit them.
mistral_translation: The pepper seller who uses a clay pot to carry it for an enemy to inspect; we say it has already scattered everywhere
mistral_interpretation: Trusting an untrustworthy person with something valuable will likely lead to loss or betrayal.
llama_translation: The seller of pepper makes a bundle and gives it to the buyer to carry; he says it is light.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the tendency for people to downplay the difficulties or challenges of a task or situation when they are not the ones responsible for it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbójú-u fífò lé adìẹ àgàgà; a kì í gbójú-u yíyan lé alágẹmọ.
english_literal: One should not expect flight from the flightless chicken; one should not expect striding from a chameleon.
interpretation_gold: To expect the impossible is to delude oneself.
deepseek_translation: One does not stare intently at a guinea fowl; one does not stare defiantly at a chameleon.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against provoking or challenging those who are inherently dangerous or unpredictable.
claude_translation: One does not rely on blowing to drive away a stubborn chicken; one does not rely on selection when dealing with a chameleon.
claude_interpretation: Different situations require different approaches, and you cannot use the same method to solve all problems.
gemini_translation: One does not rely on a lame hen for flying; one does not rely on a chameleon for dancing.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to expect someone to perform a task for which they are inherently unsuited or incapable.
mistral_translation: One does not stare at the flapping wings of a turkey; one does not stare at the frying of a chameleon
mistral_interpretation: Avoid unnecessary attention to things that may bring misfortune or trouble upon you.
llama_translation: We do not use a hoe to cut a tree; we do not use a machete to cut a yam.
llama_interpretation: One should use the right tool for the right task to achieve efficiency and avoid damage.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ìrànà ní ńṣíwájú òkú.
english_literal: It is the votive herald-chicken that precedes a dead person.
interpretation_gold: Matters must be attended to in their proper sequence.
deepseek_translation: The chicken that leads the way is the first to die.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against recklessness or being overly eager, as those who rush ahead without caution often face the gravest consequences.
claude_translation: The hen that leads the way goes ahead of the dead one
claude_interpretation: Leadership requires being alive to one's responsibilities and actively taking initiative rather than being passive or inactive.
gemini_translation: The chicken that leads the way is the one that goes before the corpse.
gemini_interpretation: The one who takes the lead or volunteers for a task often faces the greatest risks or burdens.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The chicken that leads the way is the one that goes before the corpse.", "interpretation": "The one who takes the lead or volunteers for a task often faces the greatest risks or burdens."}
mistral_translation: The in-law's chicken is leading the corpse ahead.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against allowing outsiders or those with ulterior motives to take charge of important matters.
llama_translation: The chicken's intestine is in front of death
llama_interpretation: One's destiny is already predetermined and inescapable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ́ purọ́ mọ́mọ-ọ rẹ̀ jẹun.
english_literal: The nursing mother lies against her child to secure food.
interpretation_gold: One uses every ruse available to one in the interest of one's well-being.
deepseek_translation: The nursing mother licks her baby's food clean.
deepseek_interpretation: Parents make sacrifices for their children's well-being.
claude_translation: A mother lies to her child to eat food
claude_interpretation: Sometimes deception or gentle lies are necessary when they serve a greater good, especially in caring relationships.
gemini_translation: A mother lies to her child to eat.
gemini_interpretation: A mother may resort to deception for the well-being of her child.
mistral_translation: A mother does not eat her child's food in secret.
mistral_interpretation: A parent should not exploit or take advantage of their child's resources or efforts.
llama_translation: The mother's breast is the child's food.
llama_interpretation: A mother's love and care are the most essential nourishment for her child.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í rí ẹ́ni ranni lẹ́rù ká yọké.
english_literal: One does not find helpers willing to help with one's load and yet sprout a hump on one's back “from carrying too heavy a load”.
interpretation_gold: Always avail yourself of offered help.
deepseek_translation: We do not see someone helping us carry a load and we ascend.
deepseek_interpretation: One should acknowledge and appreciate the help of others.
claude_translation: One does not see someone who helps and then become proud or arrogant
claude_interpretation: Gratitude and humility should be maintained toward those who assist you, rather than developing pride or superiority.
gemini_translation: One does not see someone carrying a heavy load and then add more to it.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to burden someone who is already struggling or overwhelmed.
mistral_translation: We do not see someone carrying a load on their head and then add more to it.
mistral_interpretation: It is unkind to add to the burdens of someone who is already struggling.
llama_translation: We do not see a person's buttocks on the day of marriage
llama_interpretation: One should not judge a person's true nature based on their initial appearance or behavior.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi iná sórí òrùlé sùn.
english_literal: One does not go to bed while there is a fire on one's roof.
interpretation_gold: Better take care of problems before relaxing.
deepseek_translation: One does not set fire to the roof and sleep.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against creating problems and then ignoring the consequences.
claude_translation: One does not sleep with fire on top of the roof.
claude_interpretation: It is unwise to ignore dangerous situations or live carelessly with potential threats around you.
gemini_translation: One does not sleep with fire on the roof.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to ignore or be complacent about a dangerous situation that could lead to serious consequences.
mistral_translation: One does not use fire to burn the roof while sleeping.
mistral_interpretation: Avoid actions that will bring harm or destruction to yourself or your own household.
llama_translation: We do not use fire to roast the earth
llama_interpretation: One should not use excessive or destructive means to achieve a goal.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbàká labiyamọ ńgbàjá mọ́ ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: It is completely and securely that a mother (bearing her child on her back) supports the child with a strip of cloth.
interpretation_gold: One must be thorough in discharging one's responsibility.
deepseek_translation: The old crab teaches its young one how to walk sideways.
deepseek_interpretation: Parents or elders pass down their knowledge and behaviors to the younger generation.
claude_translation: It is with a basket that a mother carries her child on her back
claude_interpretation: A mother uses the proper tools and methods to care for and protect her child.
gemini_translation: It is in a circle that a mother ties the waist-beads on her child.
gemini_interpretation: A mother's love and care for her child are all-encompassing and protective.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It is in a circle that a mother ties the waist-beads on her child.", "interpretation": "A mother's love and care for her child are all-encompassing and protective."}
mistral_translation: The old cat with a litter of kittens fights the young cat for its own offspring.
mistral_interpretation: Elders may act protectively or competitively towards younger individuals to safeguard their own interests or those they consider their responsibility.
llama_translation: The elder who is not present when the child is being beaten will not know the child's cry.
llama_interpretation: One must be present and involved to truly understand a situation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìtìjú kárùn.
english_literal: One does not because of shyness expose oneself to a disease.
interpretation_gold: Never be too shy to speak out on your own behalf.
deepseek_translation: One does not use shame to peel a cassava.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that certain tasks require patience and proper methods, not shortcuts driven by shame or haste.
claude_translation: One does not use shame to cure illness
claude_interpretation: Shame or embarrassment cannot solve real problems that require practical action and proper treatment.
gemini_translation: One does not use shame to prevent a disease.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to let embarrassment prevent one from seeking necessary help or treatment.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not use shame to prevent a disease.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to let embarrassment prevent one from seeking necessary help or treatment."}
mistral_translation: We do not use shame to scratch an itch.
mistral_interpretation: One should not resort to harmful or inappropriate means to solve a problem, even if it seems expedient.
llama_translation: We do not use the head to carry a load.
llama_interpretation: One should not take on more responsibility than they can handle.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Akọ̀pẹ Ìjàyè ò gbọ́ tiẹ̀, ó ní ogún kó Agboroode.
english_literal: The palm-wine tapper of Ijaye: instead of looking to his own affairs says Agboroode has been destroyed by invaders.
interpretation_gold: The wise person learns from others' misfortunes instead of gawking at them.
deepseek_translation: The parrot of Ìjàyè did not hear the sound of the drum, it said twenty beats Agboroode.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against making assumptions or speaking without proper knowledge or understanding.
claude_translation: The Akọ̀pẹ of Ìjàyè did not listen to advice, he said twenty should carry Agboroode
claude_interpretation: Stubbornness and refusal to heed wise counsel leads to unrealistic demands and eventual downfall.
gemini_translation: The palm tree of Ijayè did not heed its own advice, it said twenty should surround Agboroode.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the irony of someone giving advice they themselves fail to follow, often leading to their own detriment.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The palm tree of Ijayè did not heed its own advice, it said twenty should surround Agboroode.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the irony of someone giving advice they themselves fail to follow, often leading to their own detriment."}
mistral_translation: The palm-wine tapper of Ìjàyè did not hear his own, he said twenty should gather the Agboroode tree
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns against hypocrisy—criticizing others for faults one also possesses.
llama_translation: The tortoise of Ijaye does not hear the drum, it says the drum is not loud enough for Agboroode.
llama_interpretation: One should not blame others for not responding when the message or signal is not clear or strong enough.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńsọ̀rọ̀ obìnrin, a ní ká sọ́ bàrà ká lọ gbin bàrà sódò; ta ní máa báni pa á?
english_literal: We speak of women and someone suggests that we hedge our words and go plant water melon by the stream; who will help in harvesting it?
interpretation_gold: This is a variant of the preceding entry.
deepseek_translation: We are discussing women, and someone says let us plant corn by the riverside; who will help us kill it?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against making decisions without considering the practical challenges or consequences that may arise.
claude_translation: We are discussing a woman's matter, and we are told to take cassava stems and go plant cassava by the river; who will help us harvest it?
claude_interpretation: When discussing serious matters, don't divert attention to unrelated tasks that you cannot complete alone.
gemini_translation: We are talking about a woman, and we are told to tie a gourd and go plant it in the river; who will help us kill it?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the absurdity of being asked to perform an irrelevant or impossible task when a pressing issue needs attention.
mistral_translation: When we talk about a woman, we say we should first tie a wrapper and go plant it by the riverside; who will come to kill her?
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the perceived resilience and enduring nature of women, suggesting they cannot be easily destroyed or defeated.
llama_translation: We are searching for a woman, we say let us search for a needle and go to the river to search for a needle; who will we ask to help us?
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the futility of seeking help from someone who is equally clueless or powerless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àwítẹ́lẹ̀ ní ńjẹ́ ọmọ́ gbẹ́nà; ọmọ kì í gbẹ́nà lásán.
english_literal: Previous-instruction enables a child to understand coded speech; a child does not naturally understand codes.
interpretation_gold: A clever child reflects the instruction he/she has received.
deepseek_translation: The child of a watchman is the one who eats the road; a child does not just eat the road for nothing.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that children often inherit or follow the behaviors and professions of their parents.
claude_translation: It is lack of proper guidance that makes a child become wayward; a child does not become wayward for no reason.
claude_interpretation: Children's bad behavior is usually the result of inadequate parental guidance and training, not inherent wickedness.
gemini_translation: Forethought is what makes a child a sculptor; a child does not sculpt in vain.
gemini_interpretation: Careful planning and preparation are essential for achieving a successful outcome, especially in creative endeavors.
mistral_translation: It is the one who clears the path ahead that claims the child is straying; a child does not stray for no reason.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights that those who create obstacles or fail to guide others should not blame them for going astray.
llama_translation: The one who is not a child is the one who is carrying the child on the back; the child does not carry the child on the back.
llama_interpretation: Elderly people are expected to take care of the younger ones, not the other way around.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ohun sọ́wọ́ búra.
english_literal: One does not hide something in one's hand and yet swear [that one knows nothing about it].
interpretation_gold: It is foolish to tempt fate; the dishonest exposes himself/herself to the possibility of discovery.
deepseek_translation: One does not hold something in the hand and swear.
deepseek_interpretation: Actions speak louder than words; tangible evidence is more convincing than mere promises.
claude_translation: One does not swear an oath with something precious in hand
claude_interpretation: You should not make promises or commitments while holding onto something valuable that you're not willing to lose, as it shows insincerity.
gemini_translation: One does not use something to swear an oath.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to use a physical object as a substitute for a solemn oath or promise.
mistral_translation: We do not use something worthless to swear an oath.
mistral_interpretation: One should not make promises or commitments based on unreliable or insignificant things.
llama_translation: We do not use a thing of beauty to cover a smelly thing.
llama_interpretation: One should not use something valuable or beautiful to cover up something unpleasant or shameful.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “À ńjùwọ́n” ò ṣéé wí lẹ́jọ́; ìjà ìlara ò tán bọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: “We are driven by envy of them” is a bad case to make; a quarrel spawned by jealousy is not easy to settle.
interpretation_gold: Quarrels whose causes cannot be openly admitted will not readily end.
deepseek_translation: "We are watching" cannot be said in court; a physical fight does not end quietly.
deepseek_interpretation: Actions speak louder than words, and conflicts often escalate beyond words.
claude_translation: We are fighting cannot be said in court; a personal fight is not finished with words.
claude_interpretation: Legal disputes require proper evidence and procedure rather than emotional claims, and personal conflicts cannot be resolved through mere verbal arguments alone.
gemini_translation: “We are better than them” is not something to say in a dispute; the fight of envy does not end easily.
gemini_interpretation: Boasting about superiority or acting out of envy only prolongs conflict and makes resolution difficult.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "“We are better than them” is not something to say in a dispute; the fight of envy does not end easily.", "interpretation": "Boasting about superiority or acting out of envy only prolongs conflict and makes resolution difficult."}
mistral_translation: “We are looking at each other” cannot be used as evidence in court; a personal quarrel does not end in public.
mistral_interpretation: Private disputes should be resolved privately and not dragged into public or formal settings where they lack proper context or resolution.
llama_translation: The one who is being pitied does not know; the fight of the destitute is not a joke.
llama_interpretation: Those who are struggling may not realize the severity of their situation, but their struggles are not to be taken lightly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkó balẹ̀, ó fi gbogbo ara kígbe.
english_literal: Àko hit the ground and cried out with its whole body.
interpretation_gold: A person who needs help should not be coy in asking.
deepseek_translation: The lizard prostrates, it uses its whole body to shout.
deepseek_interpretation: One must fully commit to a task to achieve success.
claude_translation: The young man fell down, he cried with his whole body
claude_interpretation: When someone experiences failure or misfortune, they may react with excessive emotion or drama beyond what the situation warrants.
gemini_translation: The basket fell, and it cried with its whole body.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb signifies that when a problem or misfortune occurs, its impact is felt by everyone or everything associated with it.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The basket fell, and it cried with its whole body.", "interpretation": "This proverb signifies that when a problem or misfortune occurs, its impact is felt by everyone or everything associated with it."}
mistral_translation: The male hawk lands, it uses its whole body to cry out
mistral_interpretation: When someone in authority arrives, they should make their presence and intentions known clearly and decisively.
llama_translation: The parrot is in the palace, it has taken the whole body to be proud
llama_interpretation: One's status or position can inflate one's sense of self-importance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A lé tẹ̀m̀bẹ̀lẹ̀kun jìnnà bí ẹnipé kó bọ́ jù sígbó.
english_literal: One chases conspiracy away, as though one would have it disappear into the bush.
interpretation_gold: No one should want anything to do with conspiracy.
deepseek_translation: We crossed the big river like someone who is afraid of the forest.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights how fear can drive people to take on seemingly greater challenges while avoiding smaller, more familiar ones.
claude_translation: We chase the snail far as if it should run into the forest
claude_interpretation: It is foolish to pursue something with excessive force when a gentle approach would be more effective.
gemini_translation: We can push a chameleon far away as if it shouldn't fall into the bush.
gemini_interpretation: It is futile to try and prevent the inevitable or to control something that will naturally find its way.
mistral_translation: You can keep a snail at a distance as if it will not reach the forest.
mistral_interpretation: No matter how much you delay or underestimate someone, they will eventually achieve their goal.
llama_translation: We are not as strong as the one who has a helper to lean on
llama_interpretation: Having a supportive community or helper can increase one's strength and resilience.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi oko sin fún ìwọ̀fà.
english_literal: One does not hide the farm from the pawned worker.
interpretation_gold: It does not make sense to prevent a servant one has hired from doing what one hired him to do.
deepseek_translation: One does not give a hoe as a gift to a debtor.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not offer help that burdens the recipient further.
claude_translation: One does not give a hoe as inheritance to a slave.
claude_interpretation: You don't waste valuable resources or opportunities on someone who has no permanent stake in your family or community.
gemini_translation: One does not use a farm to bury a pawn.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to use something valuable or significant for a trivial or unworthy purpose.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not use a farm to bury a pawn.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate to use something valuable or significant for a trivial or unworthy purpose."}
mistral_translation: One does not lend a hoe to a pawnbroker
mistral_interpretation: Do not entrust important tasks or resources to someone who is already burdened or unreliable
llama_translation: We don't use a farm to repay a debt
llama_interpretation: One should not use a valuable resource to settle a trivial obligation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ará ọ̀run ò ṣẹ́tí aṣọ.
english_literal: Natives of heaven do not sew their hems.
interpretation_gold: The uninitiated do not know the customs of a place.
deepseek_translation: The heavenly beings do not wear dirty clothes.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of maintaining purity and integrity in all aspects of life.
claude_translation: Heavenly beings do not choose clothes
claude_interpretation: Spiritual matters and divine beings are not concerned with material possessions or earthly vanities.
gemini_translation: The people of heaven do not sew clothes.
gemini_interpretation: One should not expect the impossible or things that are outside the natural order of things.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The people of heaven do not sew clothes.", "interpretation": "One should not expect the impossible or things that are outside the natural order of things."}
mistral_translation: Heavenly beings do not wear clothes.
mistral_interpretation: Some things are naturally perfect and do not require artificial adornment or correction.
llama_translation: The people of heaven do not sew clothes.
llama_interpretation: One should not worry about things that are beyond their control or realm.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpà-á fi ọwọ́ mẹ́wẹ̀ẹ̀wá bọ ẹnu; àpà, a-bìjẹun-wọ̀mù-wọ̀mù.
english_literal: The wastrel puts all ten fingers into his mouth; wastrel, a-person-who-eats-with-abandon.
interpretation_gold: A wastrel is immoderate in his feeding.
deepseek_translation: The arm has ten fingers to put in the mouth; the arm, the one that eats hurriedly.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches the importance of patience and moderation in actions, especially in matters of sustenance and survival.
claude_translation: The left-handed person uses ten fingers to cover the mouth; left-handed person, one who eats food in a gulping manner
claude_interpretation: This proverb criticizes someone who eats greedily or without proper manners, suggesting they need to use both hands to hide their shameful eating behavior.
gemini_translation: The glutton puts ten fingers in their mouth; the glutton, one who eats messily.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes a gluttonous person as someone who eats excessively and without manners.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The glutton puts ten fingers in their mouth; the glutton, one who eats messily.", "interpretation": "This proverb describes a gluttonous person as someone who eats excessively and without manners."}
mistral_translation: The armpit uses its ten fingers to cover the mouth; the armpit, the one that eats food stealthily and secretly.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against hypocrisy—criticizing others for faults one secretly commits oneself.
llama_translation: The tortoise uses its legs to enter the mouth; the tortoise, we do not see its buttocks.
llama_interpretation: One should be mindful of how they present themselves to the world, as their true nature may not be immediately apparent.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahún dùn;kò tóó jẹ fúnni.
english_literal: Tortoise meat is delicious, but there is not enough of it to make a meal.
interpretation_gold: One should husband one's resources wisely.
deepseek_translation: The crab is sweet; it is not enough to eat alone.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of sharing good things with others rather than keeping them to oneself.
claude_translation: The miser is stingy; it is not worth eating for one.
claude_interpretation: A stingy person's miserliness ultimately harms themselves more than others.
gemini_translation: The tortoise is sweet; it is not enough to eat for one.
gemini_interpretation: Something that is desirable but insufficient for everyone should be shared.
mistral_translation: The tortoise is sweet; it is not enough to eat alone.
mistral_interpretation: Sharing good fortune or resources with others brings greater fulfillment than hoarding them selfishly.
llama_translation: The tortoise is sweet; it is not the one that eats it.
llama_interpretation: One should not judge something by its appearance or reputation, but rather by personal experience.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Apajájẹẹ́ ní ẹ̀rù adìẹ ḿba òun.
english_literal: The-person-who-kills-and-eats-dogs claims to be afraid of chickens.
interpretation_gold: A hardened criminal pretends to have scruples about mere peccadillos.
deepseek_translation: The leftover is the chicken's burden.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one must take responsibility for what remains after others have taken their share.
claude_translation: The hawk says the chicken is afraid of it
claude_interpretation: Those in positions of power often overestimate how much others fear them or may not realize their intimidating effect on the vulnerable.
gemini_translation: The one who eats the chicken says they are afraid of the chicken.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the hypocrisy of someone who benefits from a situation while feigning fear or concern about it.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who eats the chicken says they are afraid of the chicken.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the hypocrisy of someone who benefits from a situation while feigning fear or concern about it."}
mistral_translation: The one who eats with a greedy companion is the one who carries the chicken's load.
mistral_interpretation: Associating with greedy or selfish people will bring you unnecessary burdens or troubles.
llama_translation: The one who is being carried does not know the weight of the load.
llama_interpretation: Those who are being taken care of or supported often do not appreciate the burden borne by their caregivers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi àgbà sílẹ̀ sin àgbà.
english_literal: One does not leave one elder sitting to walk another elder part of his way.
interpretation_gold: One should not slight one person in order to humor another.
deepseek_translation: We do not leave the elderly to bury the elderly.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of younger generations caring for and respecting their elders while they are still alive.
claude_translation: One does not abandon an elder to follow another elder
claude_interpretation: Loyalty and consistency in relationships are valued over constantly switching allegiances between people of similar status or authority.
gemini_translation: One does not leave an elder to bury an elder.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate and disrespectful to neglect a living elder while attending to the burial of another elder.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not leave an elder to bury an elder.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate and disrespectful to neglect a living elder while attending to the burial of another elder."}
mistral_translation: One does not leave an elder to serve another elder.
mistral_interpretation: It is unwise to abandon a respected or experienced person for another of equal status or value.
llama_translation: We do not use an elder to test the ground for another elder.
llama_interpretation: One should not use someone of equal or greater status to test or prove a point to another person of similar status.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-gbọ́n-léwe ni à-dàgbà-di-wèrè.
english_literal: Lack-of-wisdom-in-youth is imbecility in adulthood.
interpretation_gold: The man turns out just as the child was; the grown person acquires his traits in childhood.
deepseek_translation: Not learning wisdom in youth is growing up to become a fool.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of acquiring wisdom early in life to avoid foolishness in adulthood.
claude_translation: Not being wise in youth is what makes one become foolish in old age
claude_interpretation: Failing to develop wisdom and good judgment when young leads to foolishness and poor decision-making in later life.
gemini_translation: Not being wise as a youth is growing old to become foolish.
gemini_interpretation: Failing to acquire wisdom and good character in one's youth leads to foolishness in old age.
mistral_translation: Not listening to advice as a child is what makes one become foolish as an adult
mistral_interpretation: The proverb warns that failing to heed wisdom in youth leads to poor judgment in adulthood.
llama_translation: The one who does not listen to advice is the one who will be called a mad person.
llama_interpretation: Disregarding wise counsel can lead to ruin and loss of dignity.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ní ọjọ́ tí òún ti jágbọ́n-ọn òo lọrùn ò ti wọ òun mọ́.
english_literal: Tortoise says that since the day it learned the trick of saying yes its neck has ceased to shrink.
interpretation_gold: One who says yes to every request avoids a great many arguments.
deepseek_translation: The tortoise on the day it got wisdom did not carry a load nor did it wear any.
deepseek_interpretation: Wisdom does not always come with immediate practical benefits or visible changes.
claude_translation: The tortoise says that since the day it became wise, trouble has not befallen it again.
claude_interpretation: Wisdom and careful thinking help one avoid problems and difficulties in life.
gemini_translation: Tortoise says the day he became wise, his neck stopped entering his shell.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb suggests that wisdom or experience can lead to a state where one is no longer easily deceived or trapped.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Tortoise says the day he became wise, his neck stopped entering his shell.", "interpretation": "The proverb suggests that wisdom or experience can lead to a state where one is no longer easily deceived or trapped."}
mistral_translation: It is the tortoise who says that on the day he tied his load on his neck, it did not enter his body anymore
mistral_interpretation: This proverb highlights the tendency of people to make excuses or blame circumstances for their own mistakes or misfortunes
llama_translation: The leopard is crying on the day its child has been taken to heaven and it is not there to see it.
llama_interpretation: A person cannot mourn or show concern for a problem they have caused or contributed to.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í wà nínú ìṣẹ́ ká perin tọrẹ.
english_literal: One does not wallow in poverty and yet kill an elephant for public distribution.
interpretation_gold: Always live according to your circumstances.
deepseek_translation: One cannot be in the midst of work and stretch out legs.
deepseek_interpretation: You cannot relax or be lazy when there is work to be done.
claude_translation: One does not stay in work/business and send an elephant to a friend
claude_interpretation: You cannot afford to be overly generous with valuable resources when you are still building your own livelihood or business.
gemini_translation: One does not give a hippopotamus as a gift when in poverty.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate and impractical to offer lavish gifts or make grand gestures when one is in a state of poverty or hardship.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not give a hippopotamus as a gift when in poverty.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate and impractical to offer lavish gifts or make grand gestures when one is in a state of poverty or hardship."}
mistral_translation: We do not stay inside work to roll it around like a ball
mistral_interpretation: One should not avoid or delay work but rather tackle it promptly and efficiently
llama_translation: One does not stay inside a job and be counting the days
llama_interpretation: One should be patient and not rush to finish a task or project.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fá orí lẹ́hìn olórí.
english_literal: One does not shave a head in the absence of the owner.
interpretation_gold: One does not settle a matter in the absence of the person most concerned.
deepseek_translation: One does not shave the head behind the head.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises against unnecessary actions or going against natural order.
claude_translation: One does not drag the head behind the owner of the head
claude_interpretation: You cannot force someone to go where they don't want to go or make decisions they don't agree with.
gemini_translation: One does not shave a head behind the owner of the head.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to make decisions or take actions concerning someone without their knowledge or involvement.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not shave a head behind the owner of the head.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate to make decisions or take actions concerning someone without their knowledge or involvement."}
mistral_translation: We do not shave the head in the absence of the owner of the head.
mistral_interpretation: One should not make important decisions or take actions on behalf of someone without their knowledge or consent.
llama_translation: We do not shave the head behind the king.
llama_interpretation: One should not undermine or disrespect those in authority.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àgbò dúdú kọjá odò ó di funfun.
english_literal: The black ram crosses the river and becomes white.
interpretation_gold: Propitious events can drastically change a person's fortunes for the better.
deepseek_translation: The black goat crosses the river and becomes white.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that difficult experiences can lead to transformation or purification.
claude_translation: The black ram crosses the river and becomes white
claude_interpretation: Circumstances and experiences can fundamentally transform a person's character or appearance.
gemini_translation: A black ram crosses the river and becomes white.
gemini_interpretation: Circumstances or environment can drastically change one's appearance or nature.
mistral_translation: A black ram passes through the river and becomes white.
mistral_interpretation: Outward appearances can change, but the true nature of a person or thing remains unchanged.
llama_translation: Black goat crosses the river and becomes white
llama_interpretation: A person's circumstances can change their reputation or appearance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ejò sórí òrùlé sùn.
english_literal: One does not go to bed while a snake is on the roof.
interpretation_gold: Never let down your guard while danger still lurks.
deepseek_translation: One does not lay a snake on the roof to sleep.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not trust or accommodate those who are inherently dangerous or untrustworthy.
claude_translation: One does not sleep with a snake on the pillow
claude_interpretation: You should not ignore or live comfortably with obvious dangers or threats around you.
gemini_translation: One does not sleep with a snake on the roof.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to ignore a known danger or threat, as it will eventually cause harm.
mistral_translation: One does not use a snake as a pillow to sleep on the roof.
mistral_interpretation: Avoid taking unnecessary risks or trusting dangerous things that could harm you.
llama_translation: We do not use a broom to sweep the ceiling
llama_interpretation: One should not use excessive or inappropriate means to solve a problem.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adìẹ ò lórúnkún ẹjọ́.
english_literal: A chicken has no knees for cases.
interpretation_gold: One should steer clear of actionable behavior.
deepseek_translation: The guinea fowl does not mourn the hawk.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not grieve for those who cause harm or are natural adversaries.
claude_translation: A chicken does not have the neck of a snake
claude_interpretation: Everyone has their own natural limitations and should not attempt what is beyond their inherent capabilities.
gemini_translation: A chicken does not have a knee for a lawsuit.
gemini_interpretation: One should not expect a weak or incapable person to perform tasks beyond their ability.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A chicken does not have a knee for a lawsuit.", "interpretation": "One should not expect a weak or incapable person to perform tasks beyond their ability."}
mistral_translation: A chicken does not have the neck of a snake
mistral_interpretation: Each creature has its own unique abilities and limitations; do not expect someone to do what they are not naturally equipped for
llama_translation: The chicken does not enter the sky
llama_interpretation: Some goals or aspirations are unattainable or unrealistic.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ahún ńre àjò, ó gbé ilé-e rẹ̀ dání.
english_literal: Tortoise embarks on a journey and takes his house with it.
interpretation_gold: One's dearest possessions deserve one's closest attention.
deepseek_translation: The crab went on a journey, it carried its house along.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches self-reliance and preparedness, as the crab carries its home wherever it goes.
claude_translation: The tortoise is going on a journey, it carries its house on its back.
claude_interpretation: Self-reliance and preparedness are essential virtues, as one should always be ready to provide for oneself wherever life takes them.
gemini_translation: The tortoise is traveling, it carries its house with it.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the self-sufficiency and preparedness of an individual who is always ready for any situation.
mistral_translation: The tortoise is on a journey, it has carried its home on its back.
mistral_interpretation: One should always be prepared and self-sufficient, relying on oneself rather than external support.
llama_translation: The tortoise is traveling, it carries its home on its back.
llama_interpretation: One should be prepared to face challenges and have a sense of self-sufficiency when venturing into new or unfamiliar territories.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àlejò bí òkété là ńfi èkùrọ́ lọ̀.
english_literal: It is a visitor like a giant rat to whom one offers palm-nuts.
interpretation_gold: One should approach other people as their stations dictate.
deepseek_translation: A guest like a bush rat is treated with palm kernels.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that hospitality should be extended generously, even to unexpected or humble guests.
claude_translation: It is a guest like a grass-cutter that we send away with palm kernels.
claude_interpretation: We should send guests away with gifts or provisions to show hospitality and ensure they remember us fondly.
gemini_translation: A guest like a giant rat is treated with palm kernel.
gemini_interpretation: One should treat a difficult or troublesome guest with a small, insignificant offering, rather than a valuable one.
mistral_translation: A visitor like a giant rat is the one we use a trap to drive away
mistral_interpretation: Some guests overstay their welcome and must be subtly encouraged to leave.
llama_translation: A stranger is like a monkey, it is the tail that is used to identify it.
llama_interpretation: One's true nature or identity can be revealed through their actions or behavior.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjàpá ní kò sí oun tó dà bí oun tí a mọ̀ ọ́ṣe; ó ní bí òún bá ńrìn lóko ẹ̀pà, ọ̀kọ̀ọ̀kan a máa bọ́ sóun lẹ́nu.
english_literal: Tortoise says there is nothing quite like what one knows how to do; it says when it walks through a peanut farm, peanuts keep popping one by one into its mouth.
interpretation_gold: When one does what one is a true expert at doing, it seems like performing magic.
deepseek_translation: The tortoise says there is nothing like what we know how to do; it says when it walks on the farm, each footstep will follow its mouth.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of confidence and self-assurance in one's abilities.
claude_translation: The tortoise says there is nothing as good as being known for something; he says when he walks in the groundnut farm, each one will fall into his mouth.
claude_interpretation: Having a good reputation or being known for positive qualities brings automatic benefits and opportunities.
gemini_translation: Àjàpá (the tortoise) said there is nothing like what one knows how to do; he said if he is walking in the groundnut farm, one by one they will fall into his mouth.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the ease and natural proficiency that comes with expertise and familiarity in a particular skill or situation.
