gemini_raw: {"translation": "Àjàpá (the tortoise) said there is nothing like what one knows how to do; he said if he is walking in the groundnut farm, one by one they will fall into his mouth.", "interpretation": "The proverb emphasizes the ease and natural proficiency that comes with expertise and familiarity in a particular skill or situation."}
mistral_translation: The tortoise says there is nothing like what it knows how to do; it says that as it walks through the peanut farm, every peanut pod will bow into its mouth.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights overconfidence in one's abilities, suggesting that arrogance can blind one to potential failures or limitations.
llama_translation: The tortoise does not have a house as big as the one we know; if it walks to the farm, each of its legs will enter its house.
llama_interpretation: One should be content with what one has, rather than comparing oneself to others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À ńkì í, à ńsà á, ó ní òun ò mọ ẹni tó kú; a ní, “Alákàá ẹgbàá, a-biṣu-wọ̀rọ̀-wọ̀rọ̀-lóko, a-bàgbàdo-tàkì-tàkì-lẹ́gàn”; ó ní, “Ọlọ́dẹ ló kú, tàbí ìnájà?”
english_literal: We recite someone's praise names, we intone his attributes, and a person says he does not know who died; we say, “He of the two hundred granaries, he whose yams are plentiful on the farm, he whose corn is abundant in the fields,” and the person asks, “Is the dead person a hunter, or a trader?”
interpretation_gold: A person for whom everything must be spelled out, a person who cannot make deductions from the most obvious hints, is daft indeed.
deepseek_translation: He was asked, he was questioned, he said he does not know the deceased; they said, "Alaka of the farm, the one who plants corn in rows, the one who plants maize in clusters"; he said, "Is it the hunter who died, or the market?"
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes evasive or dishonest answers by highlighting the absurdity of pretending not to recognize someone whose identity is obvious.
claude_translation: We greet him, we run to him, he says he doesn't know who died; we say, 'The owner of the farm with yams planted sparsely in the field, the one who plants corn abundantly in the garden'; he says, 'Is it the hunter who died, or the lazy one?'
claude_interpretation: People often pretend not to know about matters that directly concern them, even when given clear descriptions.
gemini_translation: We are calling him, we are searching for him, he says he doesn't know who died; we said, 'The one with two thousand cowries, the one with abundant yams in the farm, the one with abundant corn in the bush'; he said, 'Is it the hunter who died, or the market trader?'
gemini_interpretation: This proverb illustrates that people often only pay attention or respond when a situation directly affects their personal interests or benefits.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We are calling him, we are searching for him, he says he doesn't know who died; we said, 'The one with two thousand cowries, the one with abundant yams in the farm, the one with abundant corn in the bush'; he said, 'Is it the hunter who died, or the market trader?'", "interpretation": "This proverb illustrates that people often only pay attention or respond when a situation directly affects their personal interests or benefits."}
mistral_translation: We greet him, we ask him, he says he does not know who died; we say, 'The one with a hundred baskets, who plants yams one by one in the farm, who sells corn in small heaps at the market'; he says, 'Was it the hunter who died, or the trader?'
mistral_interpretation: The proverb illustrates how someone feigns ignorance to avoid acknowledging a well-known truth or situation.
llama_translation: We are crying, we are mourning, he says he doesn't know who died; we say, “The hunter's dog has died, the one that used to follow him to the forest, the one that used to follow him to the farm”; he says, “Is it the hunter who died, or the dog?”
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of clarity and specificity in communication to avoid confusion.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣe fáàárí itọ́ dídà sọ́mọ a-kú-wárápá.
english_literal: One does not drool in jest in the presence of the child of an epileptic.
interpretation_gold: Never make fun of afflicted people by mimicking their affliction.
deepseek_translation: We do not use the rope for drawing water to tie a corpse.
deepseek_interpretation: Different situations require different tools or approaches.
claude_translation: One does not boast about the straightness of a path to someone who died on the way
claude_interpretation: It is insensitive and inappropriate to praise something to someone who has suffered because of it.
gemini_translation: One does not boast about spitting on the child of an epileptic.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate and insensitive to mock or exploit the misfortune of others.
mistral_translation: We do not use a sieve to fetch water to wash the arm of a child who has just died
mistral_interpretation: It is inappropriate to waste resources or effort on a lost cause or something that no longer matters.
llama_translation: We don't make a fire in the forest to roast a dead child
llama_interpretation: One should not go to great lengths to solve a problem that is already hopeless.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àkísà aṣọ la fi ńṣe òṣùká.
english_literal: A rag is what one uses as a carrying pad.
interpretation_gold: One's most valuable possessions are not for careless use.
deepseek_translation: A torn cloth is used to make a rag.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that even damaged or seemingly worthless things can still be useful.
claude_translation: It is with torn cloth that we make rags.
claude_interpretation: We make the best use of what we have, even when it's damaged or imperfect.
gemini_translation: It is with tattered clothes that one makes a head-pad.
gemini_interpretation: One should make the best of available resources, even if they are imperfect or humble.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It is with tattered clothes that one makes a head-pad.", "interpretation": "One should make the best of available resources, even if they are imperfect or humble."}
mistral_translation: It is with a rag that we make a wrapper (cloth).
mistral_interpretation: Small or seemingly insignificant efforts can combine to create something valuable or useful.
llama_translation: It is the torn cloth that is used to sew the torn cloth.
llama_interpretation: One can only use what is available, even if it is imperfect, to solve a problem or meet a need.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alákìísà ní ńtọ́jú abẹ́rẹ́ tòun tòwú.
english_literal: It is the owner of rags who makes sure that needle and thread are available.
interpretation_gold: Each person looks after his/her own interests.
deepseek_translation: The poor person is the one who takes care of his needle and thread.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of valuing and maintaining even the smallest possessions, especially when resources are scarce.
claude_translation: The one without scissors is the one taking care of the needle and thread
claude_interpretation: Those who lack the proper tools or resources often end up doing the preparatory or supporting work for others.
gemini_translation: The ragged person is the one who takes care of the needle and thread.
gemini_interpretation: Those who lack resources are often more careful with what little they have.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The ragged person is the one who takes care of the needle and thread.", "interpretation": "Those who lack resources are often more careful with what little they have."}
mistral_translation: It is the ragged person who patches the hole in their own needle
mistral_interpretation: Those who are in need or lack resources are often the most resourceful and take care of their own problems.
llama_translation: The one who is not a farmer is watching the farm with a keen eye
llama_interpretation: A non-expert can easily criticize or offer unsolicited advice on a task they have no experience with.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara kì í rọni ká ṣẹ́gi ta.
english_literal: If one has the wherewithal to live a life of ease, one does not gather firewood for sale.
interpretation_gold: When one has found success, one does not persist in grubbing.
deepseek_translation: The body does not bend like a tree.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that humans have limitations and cannot endure everything like inanimate objects.
claude_translation: The body does not deceive one to sell shame.
claude_interpretation: One's physical condition or circumstances will not mislead them into acting shamefully or dishonorably.
gemini_translation: The body does not feel well and one sells a wooden leg.
gemini_interpretation: One should not engage in activities that are detrimental to their own well-being or future.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The body does not feel well and one sells a wooden leg.", "interpretation": "One should not engage in activities that are detrimental to their own well-being or future."}
mistral_translation: One's body does not lie down for another to use as a ladder to climb
mistral_interpretation: People should not exploit or take advantage of others for their own benefit.
llama_translation: The body does not know how to do the work of the head
llama_interpretation: One should not overstep their boundaries or try to do a task that is beyond their capabilities.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A ta bàbà a fowó-o bàbà ra bàbà.
english_literal: We sell guinea-corn, and with the guinea-corn money we buy guinea corn.
interpretation_gold: This variant of the previous entry suggests that for all one's efforts and exertions one has not significantly altered one's circumstances.
deepseek_translation: If you sell the bàbà, use the money to buy another bàbà.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises reinvesting resources wisely to maintain or grow one's wealth or status.
claude_translation: We sell father and use father's money to buy father
claude_interpretation: This highlights the futility and contradiction of actions that ultimately cancel each other out or return to the original state.
gemini_translation: We sold corn, and with the money from corn, we bought corn.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes a futile or unproductive endeavor where effort is expended without any real gain or progress.
mistral_translation: If we sell the father, we use the father's money to buy the father
mistral_interpretation: It warns against self-defeating actions that harm the very source of one's benefit.
llama_translation: We search for father and find father's father
llama_interpretation: One's search for guidance or wisdom may lead to discovering a deeper, more profound source of knowledge.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-sọ̀kò-sádìẹ-igba, òkò ní ńsọ tí ilẹ̀-ẹ́ fi ńṣú.
english_literal: One-who-throws-stones-at-two-hundred-chickens will be engaged in stone throwing until nightfall.
interpretation_gold: Tackling a job with inadequate tools makes the job interminable.
deepseek_translation: The hoe that digs the grave, the hoe is the one that digs the ground.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns that the same tools or actions used for good can also bring harm if misused.
claude_translation: The one who speaks carelessly about the hoe, it is the hoe that speaks while the ground becomes dark
claude_interpretation: Those who criticize tools or methods they don't understand will face consequences when those very tools prove their worth through results.
gemini_translation: He who throws stones at two hundred chickens, it is the stone he throws that makes the ground dark.
gemini_interpretation: One who attempts to harm many people simultaneously will ultimately bring trouble upon themselves.
mistral_translation: The one who wears a hundred-layered cloth, it is the arrow that boasts while the ground it lands on is crying
mistral_interpretation: Those who appear strong or boastful often overlook the suffering or effort of others who bear the consequences of their actions.
llama_translation: The farmer who farms for a day, the farm is what teaches him the lesson of his house
llama_interpretation: One's actions or work can teach them a lesson about their own life or situation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-jí-má-bọ̀ọ́jú, tí ńfi ojú àná wòran.
english_literal: A-person-who-rises-in-the-morning-without-washing-his-face, one who sees things with yesterday's eyes.
interpretation_gold: A person who does not keep his eyes peeled for developments is ever behind times.
deepseek_translation: One who wakes up but does not wash the face, yet uses yesterday's eyes to see.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against approaching new situations with old, unchanged perspectives or habits.
claude_translation: One who wakes up but doesn't wash their face, who uses yesterday's eyes to look at things
claude_interpretation: A person who refuses to gain new perspective or insight continues to see the world through outdated understanding.
gemini_translation: One who wakes up without washing their face, and watches a play with yesterday's eyes.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb describes someone who is unprepared or unready for new experiences, relying on outdated perspectives.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who wakes up without washing their face, and watches a play with yesterday's eyes.", "interpretation": "This proverb describes someone who is unprepared or unready for new experiences, relying on outdated perspectives."}
mistral_translation: The one who wakes up early to sweep, using yesterday's eyes to watch the spectacle
mistral_interpretation: It warns against relying on outdated knowledge or past experiences to judge current situations.
llama_translation: One who wakes up early, sees the road before the one who is sleeping.
llama_interpretation: Early preparation and diligence give one an advantage over others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú ọmọ oǹdọ́pọ̀ dè.
english_literal: One does not chain the child of a person who offers too low a price for one's wares.
interpretation_gold: It is not a crime to make an offer that might be unacceptable.
deepseek_translation: We do not carry the child of a hunchback.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not take on responsibilities that belong to others, especially when they are capable of handling them themselves.
claude_translation: One does not catch a chameleon by hunting it.
claude_interpretation: Some goals require patience and indirect approaches rather than aggressive pursuit.
gemini_translation: One does not use a child of a person with a hunchback to wait.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate and disrespectful to use someone's physical disability as a means of identification or to make them wait for a task.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not use a child of a person with a hunchback to wait.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate and disrespectful to use someone's physical disability as a means of identification or to make them wait for a task."}
mistral_translation: We do not carry a child who is standing on a mortar.
mistral_interpretation: One should not interfere in a matter where someone is already capable of handling it themselves.
llama_translation: We do not wake a sleeping child
llama_interpretation: One should not provoke or disturb a peaceful situation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ṣòwò méjì kẹ́ran má jẹ ọ̀kan.
english_literal: One does not engage in two trades without having one consumed by goats.
interpretation_gold: One cannot effectively manage two enterprises at once.
deepseek_translation: One does not trade two things and not eat one.
deepseek_interpretation: It is unwise to engage in multiple ventures without benefiting from at least one.
claude_translation: One does not do two trades without one suffering
claude_interpretation: Dividing your attention between multiple endeavors often leads to failure in at least one of them.
gemini_translation: One does not trade two things without an animal eating one.
gemini_interpretation: It is impossible to engage in multiple ventures without experiencing some form of loss or setback.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not trade two things without an animal eating one.", "interpretation": "It is impossible to engage in multiple ventures without experiencing some form of loss or setback."}
mistral_translation: One does not engage in two trades and refuse to eat one of them.
mistral_interpretation: It is unwise to juggle multiple responsibilities or opportunities and then fail to benefit from any of them.
llama_translation: One cannot engage in two businesses and eat one
llama_interpretation: One cannot pursue multiple interests and expect to achieve success in one.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àtẹ́lẹwọ́ ò ṣéé fi rúná.
english_literal: The palm of the hand is not good for stoking fires.
interpretation_gold: One should not attempt difficult tasks without the proper resources.
deepseek_translation: The one who looks at the ground does not deserve to be burned with fire.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that humility and downcast eyes (signifying respect or submission) should protect one from harm or punishment.
claude_translation: Palm kernel cannot be used to make fire
claude_interpretation: Some things are simply not suitable for certain purposes, no matter how much you try to force them.
gemini_translation: The palm of the hand cannot be used to cover fire.
gemini_interpretation: Some problems or truths are too significant to be concealed or ignored.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The palm of the hand cannot be used to cover fire.", "interpretation": "Some problems or truths are too significant to be concealed or ignored."}
mistral_translation: The palm of the hand cannot be used to cover a fire.
mistral_interpretation: Some problems are too big or complex to be solved by simple or inadequate means.
llama_translation: The one who is not at home does not know the one who is sleeping.
llama_interpretation: One who is not present or involved cannot truly understand the situation.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Atẹ́gùn ò ṣéé gbé.
english_literal: The wind is impossible to carry.
interpretation_gold: Certain propositions are unrealizable.
deepseek_translation: The roof cannot be carried.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that some burdens or responsibilities are too heavy for one person to bear alone.
claude_translation: A leper cannot be carried
claude_interpretation: Some burdens or problems are too difficult or dangerous for others to help you bear, so you must handle them yourself.
gemini_translation: The wind cannot be carried.
gemini_interpretation: Some things are inherently impossible to achieve or control.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The wind cannot be carried.", "interpretation": "Some things are inherently impossible to achieve or control."}
mistral_translation: The ladder cannot carry itself.
mistral_interpretation: No one can achieve success or progress entirely on their own without the help of others.
llama_translation: The roof does not make the house.
llama_interpretation: A person's external appearance or material possessions do not define their true character or worth.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í múlé móko kọ́kan má yẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not devote oneself to the home and devote oneself to the farm and not wind up neglecting one of them.
interpretation_gold: One cannot go in two opposite directions at once.
deepseek_translation: One cannot enter every farm and know everything.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches humility by acknowledging that no one can know or master everything in life.
claude_translation: One does not build a house and a hut so that one will not be suitable
claude_interpretation: You cannot pursue two different standards or approaches simultaneously and expect both to succeed properly.
gemini_translation: One does not build a house in the farm without one part being crooked.
gemini_interpretation: It is impossible to achieve perfection in any endeavor, as there will always be some minor flaw or imperfection.
mistral_translation: One does not return home from the farm and then start counting the yams one by one.
mistral_interpretation: It is unwise to waste time re-examining or overanalyzing a task that has already been completed.
llama_translation: We do not sell the market and still have the market
llama_interpretation: One cannot have two mutually exclusive things at the same time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajàkàṣù ò mọ̀ bí ìyàn-án mú.
english_literal: The person who eats large helpings does not care that there is a famine.
interpretation_gold: Greed knows no thrift.
deepseek_translation: The dog does not know how to chew the bone.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes someone who fails to appreciate or properly utilize what they have been given.
claude_translation: The glutton does not know how hunger feels
claude_interpretation: Those who have abundance cannot truly understand the suffering of those who lack basic necessities.
gemini_translation: The one who eats leftovers does not know if there is famine.
gemini_interpretation: Those who benefit from the struggles of others often remain unaware of the hardships faced by the less fortunate.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who eats leftovers does not know if there is famine.", "interpretation": "Those who benefit from the struggles of others often remain unaware of the hardships faced by the less fortunate."}
mistral_translation: The gluttonous dog does not know how hunger pinches.
mistral_interpretation: Excessive indulgence blinds one to the struggles of those who lack.
llama_translation: The dog does not know how the elephant's buttocks smell.
llama_interpretation: One should not judge or criticize something one has no experience with.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aṣọ funfun òun àbàwọ́n kì í rẹ́.
english_literal: White cloth and stains are not friends.
interpretation_gold: A person of good breeding does not associate with an ill-bred person.
deepseek_translation: A white cloth and indigo dye do not mix.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against associating with those who may tarnish one's reputation.
claude_translation: White cloth and indigo dye do not get along.
claude_interpretation: Some things are naturally incompatible and cannot coexist harmoniously.
gemini_translation: White cloth and stain do not agree.
gemini_interpretation: Some things are inherently incompatible and cannot coexist peacefully.
mistral_translation: White cloth and a leper do not compete.
mistral_interpretation: One should not compare things or people that are fundamentally different in nature or status.
llama_translation: White cloth does not make one a priest.
llama_interpretation: One's appearance or attire does not necessarily reflect their true character or status.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ìgbín sọ̀kò sórìṣà.
english_literal: One does not throw a snail at a god.
interpretation_gold: Service to the worthy should be performed with decorum, not with insult.
deepseek_translation: We do not use a snail to worship the deity.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not use inappropriate or inadequate means to achieve a sacred or important goal.
claude_translation: One does not use a snail to worship the gods
claude_interpretation: Certain things are considered inappropriate or inadequate for sacred purposes, emphasizing the importance of using proper offerings in spiritual matters.
gemini_translation: One does not use a snail to stone an orisha.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate and ineffective to use a weak or unsuitable means to address a powerful or sacred entity.
mistral_translation: We do not use a snail to peg a shrine to the ground.
mistral_interpretation: One should not use weak or unsuitable tools for important tasks.
llama_translation: We don't use snail shell to call the gods
llama_interpretation: One should use the appropriate means or tools to achieve a goal or communicate effectively.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í yin ọmọdé lójú ara ẹ̀; ìfàsẹ́hìn ní ńkángun ẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not praise a child in his presence; only backsliding results.
interpretation_gold: Children should not be praised too highly; they should always be made aware that they can be even better.
deepseek_translation: We do not praise a child in the presence of his mother; it is the eavesdropper that gets the reward.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against praising someone excessively in front of their close ones, as it may lead to envy or unintended consequences.
claude_translation: We do not praise a child in their own presence; it is praise behind their back that builds them up
claude_interpretation: Children should be praised when they are not present to prevent them from becoming arrogant or overly proud.
gemini_translation: One does not praise a child in their own presence; it leads to backwardness.
gemini_interpretation: Praising a child excessively or directly in their presence can lead to arrogance or a lack of further effort.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not praise a child in their own presence; it leads to backwardness.", "interpretation": "Praising a child excessively or directly in their presence can lead to arrogance or a lack of further effort."}
mistral_translation: We do not praise a child in their presence; it is the aftermath that causes them to become haughty
mistral_interpretation: Praising someone excessively to their face can lead to arrogance or overconfidence.
llama_translation: We do not call a child a child in front of its mother; it is the one who is not a child that is called a child.
llama_interpretation: One should not insult or belittle someone in front of their loved ones or those who care about them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Arìngbẹ̀rẹ̀ ni yó mùú oyè délé; asárétete ò róyè jẹ.
english_literal: The person who walks casually is the one who will bear a title home; the person who runs fast has no title to show for his efforts.
interpretation_gold: The spoils do not necessarily go to those who exert themselves most.
deepseek_translation: The slow and steady one will bring the chieftaincy title home; the hasty one will not eat the title.
deepseek_interpretation: Patience and perseverance lead to success, while haste leads to failure.
claude_translation: The patient one will bring honor home; the impatient one does not find honor to eat.
claude_interpretation: Patience leads to success and recognition, while impatience results in failure and missed opportunities.
gemini_translation: The slow and steady one will take the chieftaincy title home; the one who runs fast will not enjoy the chieftaincy title.
gemini_interpretation: Patience and perseverance are more effective in achieving lasting success than haste and impulsiveness.
mistral_translation: It is the one who prepares thoroughly that will take the title home; the one who acts carelessly will not enjoy the title.
mistral_interpretation: Diligence and preparation lead to success, while carelessness results in failure or loss of opportunity.
llama_translation: The one who is not a troublemaker does not enter the palace; the one who is not a troublemaker does not eat the king's food.
llama_interpretation: One must be prepared to face challenges and difficulties in order to achieve greatness or high status.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ayé ò ṣé-é finú hàn; bí o lọ́gbọ́n, fi síkùn ara-à rẹ.
english_literal: The world does not deserve to be trusted; if you have a store of wisdom, keep it in you.
interpretation_gold: People of the world are not reliable; whatever wisdom one wishes to pass on one should reserve for one's own use.
deepseek_translation: The world is not to be swallowed whole; if you are wise, keep your own spoon.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises caution and self-preservation in navigating life's challenges.
claude_translation: The world is not to be trusted with one's inner thoughts; if you are wise, keep it in your own stomach.
claude_interpretation: Wisdom lies in keeping your private thoughts and plans to yourself rather than sharing them with others who may not have your best interests at heart.
gemini_translation: The world is not to be trusted with one's inner thoughts; if you are wise, keep it to yourself.
gemini_interpretation: It is prudent to be discreet and not reveal all your plans or thoughts to others, as the world can be unpredictable and people may not always have your best interests at heart.
mistral_translation: The world does not reveal its secrets easily; if you are wise, apply yourself to understanding it
mistral_interpretation: Wisdom requires effort and personal reflection to navigate life's complexities
llama_translation: The world does not spoil the nose; if it spoils, it spoils the body.
llama_interpretation: One's actions have consequences that ultimately affect oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbọ́ ẹjọ́ẹnìkan dájọ́.
english_literal: One does not deliver a verdict after hearing only one side.
interpretation_gold: Justice requires impartiality and a full hearing.
deepseek_translation: One does not hear a case and judge it immediately.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises against rushing to judgment without fully understanding all sides of a situation.
claude_translation: One does not hear one person's case and give judgment
claude_interpretation: Fair judgment requires hearing all sides of a dispute before making a decision.
gemini_translation: One does not hear one person's case and give judgment.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to hear both sides of a story before making a decision or judgment.
mistral_translation: We do not hear one person's lawsuit judged alone
mistral_interpretation: Justice requires hearing all sides before making a fair decision
llama_translation: We don't hear the cry of one who is being beaten
llama_interpretation: One should not wait for others to intervene in a problem, but rather take action to address it personally.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A dẹ́bọ fún igúnnugún, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún àkàlà, ó ní òun kò rú; a dẹ́bọ fún ẹyẹlé, ẹyẹlé gbẹ́bọ, ó rúbọ.
english_literal: A sacrifice was prescribed for the vulture, but it refused to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the ground-hornbill, but it declined to sacrifice; a sacrifice was prescribed for the pigeon, and it gathered the prescribed materials and made the sacrifice.
interpretation_gold: The vulture and the ground-hornbill are unfortunate in comparison with the pigeon, because they did not carry out the prescribed sacrifice.
deepseek_translation: They prepared sacrifice for the vulture, it said it would not sacrifice; they prepared sacrifice for the hawk, it said it would not sacrifice; they prepared sacrifice for the pigeon, the pigeon carried the sacrifice, it sacrificed.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that responsibility and duty should be accepted when called upon, as the pigeon did, rather than shirking like the vulture and hawk.
claude_translation: We made sacrifice for the vulture, it said it would not offer it; we made sacrifice for the crow, it said it would not offer it; we made sacrifice for the dove, the dove accepted the sacrifice and offered it.
claude_interpretation: Good fortune comes to those who are humble and accept guidance, while the proud who reject help miss out on blessings.
gemini_translation: We offered sacrifice to the vulture, it said it would not sacrifice; we offered sacrifice to the hornbill, it said it would not sacrifice; we offered sacrifice to the pigeon, the pigeon accepted the sacrifice, it sacrificed.
gemini_interpretation: Some individuals are receptive to opportunities and guidance, while others are not, and those who are receptive often benefit.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "We offered sacrifice to the vulture, it said it would not sacrifice; we offered sacrifice to the hornbill, it said it would not sacrifice; we offered sacrifice to the pigeon, the pigeon accepted the sacrifice, it sacrificed.", "interpretation": "Some individuals are receptive to opportunities and guidance, while others are not, and those who are receptive often benefit."}
mistral_translation: We offered sacrifice to the vulture, it said it did not perform it; we offered sacrifice to the hawk, it said it did not perform it; we offered sacrifice to the pigeon, the pigeon accepted the sacrifice and performed it.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that while some may refuse help or responsibility, others will step up to fulfill it without hesitation.
llama_translation: We asked the vulture, it said it didn't eat; we asked the hawk, it said it didn't eat; we asked the vulture's child, the vulture's child accepted, it ate.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the tendency for children to follow in their parents' footsteps, often inheriting their habits and behaviors.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alágbàfọ̀ kì í bá odò ṣọ̀tá.
english_literal: A washerman does enter harbor a grudge with the river.
interpretation_gold: One does not turn one's back on one's means of livelihood.
deepseek_translation: The fisherman does not make enemies with the river.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not antagonize the source of their livelihood or sustenance.
claude_translation: The one who carries a calabash does not become enemies with the river
claude_interpretation: Those who depend on something for their livelihood should not quarrel with their source of sustenance.
gemini_translation: A washerman does not quarrel with the river.
gemini_interpretation: One should not antagonize the source of their livelihood or support.
mistral_translation: A mediator does not take sides with the river against the enemy.
mistral_interpretation: A fair mediator must remain neutral and not favor one party over another in a dispute.
llama_translation: The elder does not join the children to play in the mud.
llama_interpretation: Respect and dignity are expected of elders and leaders.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mú ìbọn tetere.
english_literal: One does not hold a gun carelessly.
interpretation_gold: Always be careful in handling dangerous matters.
deepseek_translation: We do not carry the basket hurriedly.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises against rushing tasks that require care and attention, as haste may lead to mistakes or loss.
claude_translation: One does not carry a gun carelessly.
claude_interpretation: Dangerous or powerful things must be handled with proper care and responsibility.
gemini_translation: One does not carry a gun to a wrestling match.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate to bring an overwhelming or unsuitable tool to a situation that requires a different approach.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not carry a gun to a wrestling match.", "interpretation": "It is inappropriate to bring an overwhelming or unsuitable tool to a situation that requires a different approach."}
mistral_translation: We do not carry a tiny gun.
mistral_interpretation: One should not underestimate or overlook small or seemingly insignificant things, as they can have significant impact.
llama_translation: We do not use a basket to carry a calabash
llama_interpretation: One should use the right tool or approach for a task to avoid failure or inefficiency.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹ́kù là ńmayo.
english_literal: Leaving-remnants is the indicator of satiation.
interpretation_gold: How one lives will show how well off one is.
deepseek_translation: It is the leftover that we lick.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches contentment and gratitude for what remains after sharing or giving.
claude_translation: It is the leftover that we are licking.
claude_interpretation: We should be grateful for whatever we have, even if it seems like remnants or less than what others possess.
gemini_translation: It is the leftover that one rejoices over.
gemini_interpretation: One appreciates what remains after a difficult or challenging situation, as it signifies survival or a positive outcome.
mistral_translation: What is left over is what we enjoy.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that patience and perseverance often lead to enjoying the remaining benefits after others have taken their share.
llama_translation: The tortoise is eating the frog
llama_interpretation: This proverb warns against taking advantage of someone weaker or more vulnerable.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í mọ ọkọ ọmọ ká tún mọàlè-e rẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not acknowledge the husband for one's child and also acknowledge her illicit lover.
interpretation_gold: Never betray trust or connive at betraying it.
deepseek_translation: We do not know the husband of a child and still know the one who will inherit her.
deepseek_interpretation: One cannot predict or control future events or outcomes.
claude_translation: One does not know a child's husband and then also know his concubine
claude_interpretation: It is impossible to know everything about someone's private affairs or personal relationships.
gemini_translation: One does not know the husband of a child and also know her lover.
gemini_interpretation: It is inappropriate and disrespectful to be involved in both a legitimate and an illicit relationship concerning the same person.
mistral_translation: We do not know a child's husband only to then get to know his family again.
mistral_interpretation: One should not repeat or revisit a matter that has already been settled or thoroughly discussed.
llama_translation: We do not know the husband of a child before we know the husband of the mother
llama_interpretation: One's character is often shaped by the influence of those who raised them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: À-ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀-tọ́-ọtí-wò okùn-un bàǹtẹ́ já; bí a bá mu àmuyó ńkọ́?
english_literal: One taste of wine and the belt snaps; what would happen in the event of drunkenness?
interpretation_gold: One should match the response to the stimulus.
deepseek_translation: The rope that ties the drunkard is loose; how can we hold the one who feigns drunkenness?
deepseek_interpretation: It is harder to control someone pretending to be irresponsible than someone who actually is.
claude_translation: The one who just started drinking palm wine has broken the rope of his trousers; what if he drinks to his heart's content?
claude_interpretation: If someone shows poor judgment or loses control with just a little indulgence, imagine how much worse things will be if they fully indulge.
gemini_translation: The one who just tasted wine had his belt string cut; what if he had drunk to his fill?
gemini_interpretation: Even a small indulgence can lead to significant consequences, implying that greater excess would be far more destructive.
mistral_translation: The careful one who inspects palm-wine with a rope suddenly tears his wrapper; if we drink and enjoy, what then?
mistral_interpretation: Over-caution can lead to unnecessary loss, so sometimes it is better to embrace life's pleasures without excessive hesitation.
llama_translation: The one who has not seen the bottom of the river does not know the depth of the river; what will he do if he is asked to fetch water?
llama_interpretation: One must have experience or knowledge of a situation before attempting to tackle it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abẹ́rẹ́ tó wọnú òkun ò ṣéé wá.
english_literal: A needle that drops into the ocean defies finding.
interpretation_gold: Some tasks are hopelessly impossible to accomplish.
deepseek_translation: A needle that falls into the ocean cannot be retrieved.
deepseek_interpretation: Some things, once lost, are impossible to recover.
claude_translation: A needle that falls into the ocean cannot be found
claude_interpretation: Some things once lost are impossible to recover, especially when they fall into situations far beyond our reach or control.
gemini_translation: A needle that falls into the ocean is not searchable.
gemini_interpretation: Some losses or problems are so significant or overwhelming that they are impossible to recover from or resolve.
mistral_translation: A needle that fell into the ocean cannot be retrieved
mistral_interpretation: Some losses or mistakes are irreversible and cannot be undone
llama_translation: The bead that is lost in the sea does not come back.
llama_interpretation: Some losses are irretrievable and irreversible.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-sọ̀rọ̀ ní ńmú ẹnu rùn.
english_literal: It is abstention from speaking that makes the mouth smell.
interpretation_gold: One should always say one's piece in a discussion.
deepseek_translation: Not speaking carefully makes the mouth stink.
deepseek_interpretation: Careless speech can lead to trouble or offense.
claude_translation: Not speaking is what makes the mouth smell bad
claude_interpretation: Remaining silent when you should speak up leads to negative consequences or problems.
gemini_translation: Not speaking is what makes the mouth smell.
gemini_interpretation: Silence or lack of communication can lead to misunderstandings or problems.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Not speaking is what makes the mouth smell.", "interpretation": "Silence or lack of communication can lead to misunderstandings or problems."}
mistral_translation: Not speaking is what makes the mouth heavy
mistral_interpretation: Silence or reluctance to speak can cause unnecessary discomfort or burden
llama_translation: It is the tongue that is used to lick the lips.
llama_interpretation: One's words can be used to either harm or help oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Afẹ́fẹ́ ńda ológìì láàmú; oníyẹ̀fun rọra.
english_literal: The wind is making life difficult for the seller of liquid corn starch; corn flour seller, you had better watch out!
interpretation_gold: When those better situated than one are defeated, one must be prepared for tough times.
deepseek_translation: The wind is blowing the bald head; the owner of hair is gentle.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against mocking others' misfortunes, as one's own situation could change.
claude_translation: The wind tests the palm wine tapper; the chalk seller takes care.
claude_interpretation: Those in precarious or high-risk positions must be especially cautious and careful in their actions.
gemini_translation: The wind is troubling the weaver; the flour seller should be careful.
gemini_interpretation: One person's misfortune or challenge can serve as a warning for others to be cautious, as similar difficulties might befall them.
mistral_translation: The wind blows against the naked person; the one with clothes shivers.
mistral_interpretation: Adversity affects everyone differently, but no one is entirely immune to its impact.
llama_translation: The wind blows and the palm tree bends; the stubborn one breaks.
llama_interpretation: Flexibility is key to survival and success in life.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbé ẹran erin lérí ká máa fẹsẹ̀ wa ihò ìrẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not carry elephant meat on one's head and dig cricket holes with one's big toe.
interpretation_gold: If one is blessed with plenty, one should not keep chasing after trifles.
deepseek_translation: One does not carry an elephant's meat on the head and still look for rabbit holes.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not take on heavy responsibilities and still engage in trivial pursuits.
claude_translation: One does not carry elephant meat on the head and still be searching for ant holes with the feet
claude_interpretation: When you already have something valuable or substantial, don't waste time pursuing trivial things.
gemini_translation: One does not carry an elephant on their head and at the same time use their feet to dig for crickets.
gemini_interpretation: It is impossible to focus on a significant task while simultaneously being distracted by trivial matters.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not carry an elephant on their head and at the same time use their feet to dig for crickets.", "interpretation": "It is impossible to focus on a significant task while simultaneously being distracted by trivial matters."}
mistral_translation: One does not carry elephant meat on one's head and then go searching for a rat hole.
mistral_interpretation: Do not abandon a great opportunity in pursuit of something trivial or insignificant.
llama_translation: We do not take elephant meat to the forest to share with the elephant
llama_interpretation: One should not take something that belongs to someone to their doorstep to share with them.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjò kì í dùn kónílé má relé.
english_literal: The journey is never so pleasant that the traveler does not return home.
interpretation_gold: The traveler should never forget his or her home.
deepseek_translation: A journey is never so sweet that the traveler does not return home.
deepseek_interpretation: No matter how enjoyable an experience is, one must eventually return to their roots or responsibilities.
claude_translation: A journey is never so sweet that one does not think of home.
claude_interpretation: No matter how enjoyable an experience away from home may be, one always longs to return home.
gemini_translation: A journey is not sweet until the owner of the house returns home.
gemini_interpretation: True enjoyment or completion of an endeavor is only fully realized upon returning to one's familiar and secure environment.
mistral_translation: A journey is not sweet if one does not return home
mistral_interpretation: No matter how enjoyable an experience is away from home, true fulfillment comes from returning to one's roots
llama_translation: A traveler does not sleep on the way and reach home
llama_interpretation: One should not be complacent or distracted while pursuing a goal.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Alákatam̀pòó ṣe bí ọ̀bọ ò gbọ́n; ọ̀bọ́ gbọ́n; tinú ọ̀bọ lọ̀bọ́ ńṣe.
english_literal: The person with the cross-bow thinks that the monkey is not clever; the monkey is clever, but it is following its own strategy.
interpretation_gold: It matters nothing if one is derided, as long as one knows what one is doing and why.
deepseek_translation: The bat behaves as if the monkey is not wise; the monkey is wise; it is inside the monkey that the bat operates.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against underestimating others, as even those who seem foolish may have hidden wisdom or influence.
claude_translation: The monkey acts as if the monkey is not wise; the monkey is wise; it is from the monkey's mind that the monkey acts.
claude_interpretation: People often act foolishly not from lack of intelligence, but from their own deliberate choices and inner motivations.
gemini_translation: The one who carries a lamp acts like a monkey, but the monkey is wise; the monkey acts according to its inner self.
gemini_interpretation: Appearances can be deceiving, and true wisdom or character is often revealed by one's inherent nature, not by outward actions or possessions.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who carries a lamp acts like a monkey, but the monkey is wise; the monkey acts according to its inner self.", "interpretation": "Appearances can be deceiving, and true wisdom or character is often revealed by one's inherent nature, not by outward actions or possessions."}
mistral_translation: The squirrel acts as if the monkey is not wise; the monkey is wise; it is the monkey's mind that the squirrel is trying to outsmart.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against underestimating others' intelligence while overestimating one's own cunning.
llama_translation: The drummer's drumming is like the deaf person's hearing; the deaf person hears; it is with the deaf person's ear that the drummer drums.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of understanding and relating to one's audience, as effective communication requires considering the listener's perspective.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-pẹ́-ẹ́-jẹ kì í jẹ ìbàjẹ́.
english_literal: A person who waits patiently for a long time before eating will not eat unwholesome food.
interpretation_gold: Those who are patient will have the best of things.
deepseek_translation: He who is called 'do not eat' does not eat spoiled food.
deepseek_interpretation: A person known for their discipline will not engage in corrupt behavior.
claude_translation: What is eaten slowly does not spoil
claude_interpretation: Patience and moderation in consumption or approach leads to better outcomes and prevents waste or ruin.
gemini_translation: One who eats slowly does not eat rotten food.
gemini_interpretation: Taking one's time and being patient prevents one from making mistakes or encountering undesirable outcomes.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who eats slowly does not eat rotten food.", "interpretation": "Taking one's time and being patient prevents one from making mistakes or encountering undesirable outcomes."}
mistral_translation: The one who is invited to eat does not eat spoilage
mistral_interpretation: A person of integrity does not take advantage of an opportunity to act dishonorably or exploit a situation.
llama_translation: We do not eat the leftover of a fight
llama_interpretation: One should not benefit from the conflict or problems of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Aláàárù kì í ru ẹṣin.
english_literal: The porter cannot carry a horse.
interpretation_gold: Certain tasks are impossible of accomplishment.
deepseek_translation: The owner of a load does not carry a horse.
deepseek_interpretation: One should prioritize their own responsibilities over others' burdens.
claude_translation: A person with a hernia does not carry a horse
claude_interpretation: People should not attempt tasks that exceed their physical capabilities or limitations.
gemini_translation: A porter does not carry a horse.
gemini_interpretation: One should not attempt tasks that are clearly beyond their capacity or role.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A porter does not carry a horse.", "interpretation": "One should not attempt tasks that are clearly beyond their capacity or role."}
mistral_translation: A lazy person does not carry a horse.
mistral_interpretation: Laziness prevents one from achieving significant or demanding tasks.
llama_translation: The one who is not a horseman does not ride a horse.
llama_interpretation: One should not take on a task or responsibility that is beyond their capability or expertise.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-rìn-fàà-lójú-akẹ́gàn, a-yan-kàṣà-lojú-abúni, abúni ò lówó nílé ju ẹnu-u rẹ̀ lọ.
english_literal: One-who-saunters-in-front-of-detractors, one-who-struts-before-abusers, those who abuse one have no money at home, only their mouths.
interpretation_gold: One's best course is to ignore detractors and insulters; all they have is their mouths.
deepseek_translation: The one who walks proudly before the poor, the one who shows off before the needy, the needy does not have more at home than in their mouth.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against arrogance and showing off wealth in front of those less fortunate, as it is disrespectful and unnecessary.
claude_translation: One who walks proudly before the lame, one who selects fine cloth before the naked, the naked person has no money at home more than their mouth.
claude_interpretation: It is insensitive and boastful to display your advantages in front of those who lack what you have.
gemini_translation: One who walks slowly in the presence of a critic, one who walks proudly in the presence of a mocker, the mocker has no more wealth at home than their mouth.
gemini_interpretation: Do not be intimidated by critics or mockers, as their words often lack substance and their own lives may not be as grand as they portray.
mistral_translation: One who walks with a swagger in the presence of the wood-carver, and boasts in the presence of the cloth-weaver, the weaver has no more money at home than the size of his mouth.
mistral_interpretation: Boasting about one's skills or wealth in front of those who are truly superior is foolish and exposes one's ignorance.
llama_translation: One who does not look at the face of the one who is angry, one who does not look at the face of the one who is happy, the one who is happy is not richer than the one who is angry at home.
llama_interpretation: True wealth is not measured by external appearances, but by one's inner state and relationships at home.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àì-roko, àì-rodò tí ńṣápẹ́ fún eégún jó.
english_literal: Not-going-to-the-farm, not-going-to-the-river that claps for masqueraders to dance.
interpretation_gold: It is an idler who makes music for masqueraders to dance.
deepseek_translation: Not farming, not fetching water, yet dancing for the masquerade.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes those who enjoy benefits without contributing to the work.
claude_translation: The one who doesn't go to farm, doesn't go to stream, yet claps for masquerade dance.
claude_interpretation: It criticizes people who avoid productive work but eagerly participate in entertainment and festivities.
gemini_translation: Not farming, not fishing, yet clapping for the masquerade to dance.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb criticizes those who enjoy the benefits of others' labor without contributing themselves.
mistral_translation: Without farm, without river, yet calling on the masquerade to dance
mistral_interpretation: It warns against making demands or expecting results without providing the necessary resources or effort.
llama_translation: No thinking, no planning that is done for the masquerade's dance
llama_interpretation: One must plan and think carefully before embarking on a significant endeavor.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ní ẹgbàá nílé wá ẹgbàá ròde.
english_literal: One does not have a thousand cowries (or six pence) at home and go chasing abroad for a thousand cowries.
interpretation_gold: Only the promise of a greater fortune should tempt one to neglect what one already has.
deepseek_translation: We do not have a calabash at home and go looking for a calabash outside.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises against neglecting available resources while seeking the same elsewhere.
claude_translation: One does not have a thousand at home and go out to seek a thousand
claude_interpretation: You should appreciate and utilize what you already have instead of seeking the same thing elsewhere.
gemini_translation: One does not have two thousand cowries at home and go out to look for two thousand cowries.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to seek what you already possess or have readily available.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not have two thousand cowries at home and go out to look for two thousand cowries.", "interpretation": "It is foolish to seek what you already possess or have readily available."}
mistral_translation: We do not have one hundred at home and go outside to look for one hundred.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against neglecting what you already possess while seeking the same thing elsewhere.
llama_translation: We do not have a hundred in our house, a hundred is on the road.
llama_interpretation: One should not be too confident in their current situation, as circumstances can change suddenly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í ka oyún inú kún ọmọ ilẹ̀.
english_literal: One does not count a fetus among living children.
interpretation_gold: Never count your chickens before they are hatched.
deepseek_translation: One does not count a pregnancy to fill the land with children.
deepseek_interpretation: Do not rely on potential or unfulfilled promises as if they are certain outcomes.
claude_translation: One does not count pregnancy to be full of children of the land
claude_interpretation: Don't count on uncertain future outcomes or make plans based on things that haven't happened yet.
gemini_translation: One does not count the pregnancy in the womb among the children on the ground.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to count on things that are not yet certain or materialized.
mistral_translation: We do not count the pregnancy in the womb to fill the house with children.
mistral_interpretation: Do not count on uncertain outcomes or make plans based on what has not yet happened.
llama_translation: We do not count the number of children in the womb
llama_interpretation: One should not assume or predict the outcome of a situation before it has come to pass.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àwòdì òkè tí ńwo ìkaraun kọ̀rọ̀, kí ni yó fìgbín ṣe?
english_literal: The hawk in the sky eyes the snail-shell slyly; what will it do with a snail.
interpretation_gold: One should not waste one's time on a task one cannot master.
deepseek_translation: The hawk hovering above the chicken coop, what will the chick do?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the vulnerability of the weak when faced with the predatory actions of the powerful.
claude_translation: The hawk on the hill that is watching the snail crawling, what will it do to the snail?
claude_interpretation: Someone in a position of power who merely observes a vulnerable person's struggles without taking action accomplishes nothing meaningful.
gemini_translation: The hawk in the sky that looks at the snail's shell, what will it do with the snail?
gemini_interpretation: One should not desire or pursue things that are useless or impractical to them.
mistral_translation: The high-flying hawk that gazes at the groundnut farm, what will it use to crack the nuts?
mistral_interpretation: One should not desire what they lack the means or ability to obtain.
llama_translation: The one who lives on the hill and watches the farm, what can he do with the farm?
llama_interpretation: One who is not directly involved in a situation cannot truly understand or contribute to its challenges.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Amùṣùà àgbẹ̀ tí ńgbin kókò.
english_literal: A wastrel farmer that plants cocoyams.
interpretation_gold: It is a wastrel farmer that plants cocoyams.
deepseek_translation: The farmer's hoe that cultivates cocoa.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes the importance of tools and resources in achieving success.
claude_translation: The farmer who plants cocoa is a wasteful person
claude_interpretation: Someone who invests in long-term ventures that require patience and delayed gratification may appear wasteful to those who don't understand the future benefits.
gemini_translation: The farmer's hoe that plants cocoa.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of a tool or person that is essential for a specific and valuable task, implying that without it, the task cannot be accomplished.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The farmer's hoe that plants cocoa.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the importance of a tool or person that is essential for a specific and valuable task, implying that without it, the task cannot be accomplished."}
mistral_translation: The farmer's hoe that plants cocoa.
mistral_interpretation: The tool or effort one invests in a task ultimately determines the quality and success of the outcome.
llama_translation: The farmer's apprentice who is eating koko
llama_interpretation: One who benefits from a situation should not pretend to be unaware of its source.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjẹsílẹ̀-ẹ gbèsè tí ò jẹ́ kí ẹgbẹ̀fà tóó ná.
english_literal: Long-standing debt, that makes twelve hundred cowries insufficient to spend.
interpretation_gold: Existing debts eat new fortunes away.
deepseek_translation: The leftover of the feast that does not allow the leftover to be enough.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against greed and selfishness, emphasizing that taking more than one's share leaves others with nothing.
claude_translation: The glutton owes a debt that prevents the six hundred from being spent
claude_interpretation: Excessive indulgence or greed creates obligations that prevent one from enjoying their resources freely.
gemini_translation: Eating on credit is a debt that prevents one from spending six hundred cowries freely.
gemini_interpretation: Accumulated debt restricts one's financial freedom and ability to spend.
mistral_translation: The witch of the house carries a debt that does not allow the six-man team to collect it
mistral_interpretation: A hidden problem or burden within a family or group can prevent collective progress or resolution
llama_translation: The one who is not at home is the one who is being sought with a lantern at night.
llama_interpretation: One's absence is often felt more than their presence.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjànàkú kúrò lẹ́ran à ńgọ dé.
english_literal: The elephant is not among the ranks of animals one lies in ambush for.
interpretation_gold: The wise person puts some distance between himself and an elephant, or a formidable adversary.
deepseek_translation: The elephant dies and leaves its tusks behind.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that a person's legacy or impact remains after their death.
claude_translation: The elephant has left the meat, we are heading there.
claude_interpretation: When a powerful person abandons something, it creates an opportunity for others to benefit from what was left behind.
gemini_translation: The elephant has left the meat, we are now eating the bone.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb signifies that the best part or opportunity has passed, and one is left with the less desirable remnants.
mistral_translation: The elephant has left the meat, and the bush cow is arriving.
mistral_interpretation: It warns against rushing into a situation that others have abandoned due to hidden dangers or difficulties.
llama_translation: The elephant leaves its tusk at home and goes out
llama_interpretation: One should not take their strength or advantage to a place where it will be a disadvantage or unnecessary.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ajá tí ò létí ò ṣé-é dẹ̀gbẹ́.
english_literal: A dog without ears is no good for stalking prey.
interpretation_gold: A person who cannot be instructed is useless.
deepseek_translation: A dog that has no ears cannot be tied.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that one cannot be held accountable for what they do not have the capacity to control or understand.
claude_translation: A dog that has no ears cannot be hunted with
claude_interpretation: Someone who cannot listen or follow instructions is useless as a partner or helper.
gemini_translation: A dog that has no ears cannot be tied with a rope.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot control or guide someone who is unwilling to listen or lacks the capacity to understand instructions.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A dog that has no ears cannot be tied with a rope.", "interpretation": "One cannot control or guide someone who is unwilling to listen or lacks the capacity to understand instructions."}
mistral_translation: A dog that does not listen cannot be restrained by a leash.
mistral_interpretation: A person who refuses to heed advice or warnings cannot be controlled or helped.
llama_translation: A dog that does not listen does not hear well.
llama_interpretation: Disobedience can lead to missed opportunities or failure to learn.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-ká-ìgbá-tà-á náwó ikú.
english_literal: He-who-plucks-the-African-locustbean-tree-seeds-to-sell spends death's money.
interpretation_gold: Whoever engages in a dangerous venture more than earns his/her pay.
deepseek_translation: The one who sells calabashes does not fear death.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb means that one must face challenges boldly in their line of duty.
claude_translation: One who counts four hundred and sells death's money
claude_interpretation: A person who deals in dangerous or forbidden matters will eventually face serious consequences.
gemini_translation: One who gathers locust beans and sells them is spending the money of death.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb warns against the dangers of engaging in risky or illicit activities for profit, as the gains are often short-lived and lead to negative consequences.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One who gathers locust beans and sells them is spending the money of death.", "interpretation": "This proverb warns against the dangers of engaging in risky or illicit activities for profit, as the gains are often short-lived and lead to negative consequences."}
mistral_translation: The one who does not prepare for the market will spend money on death
mistral_interpretation: Neglecting proper planning or preparation can lead to costly and avoidable consequences.
llama_translation: The one who does not take a load does not know the weight of death.
llama_interpretation: One cannot truly understand the value of life until they have experienced hardship or struggle.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í sùn jẹ́rìí ìdí.
english_literal: One cannot be asleep and also be able to vouch for one's anus.
interpretation_gold: Assert only those things you know for certain.
deepseek_translation: One does not sleep and eat the buttocks.
deepseek_interpretation: Success requires effort; one cannot achieve anything by being idle.
claude_translation: One does not sleep and witness the buttocks.
claude_interpretation: You cannot be aware of what happens when you are not present or paying attention.
gemini_translation: One does not sleep to testify to the anus.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot be a witness to something they did not directly observe.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not sleep to testify to the anus.", "interpretation": "One cannot be a witness to something they did not directly observe."}
mistral_translation: We do not sleep to investigate the reason.
mistral_interpretation: One should not delay action or decision-making by overanalyzing the cause of a problem.
llama_translation: We do not sleep on a bed of thorns
llama_interpretation: One should avoid situations that can cause harm or discomfort.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ara ẹ̀ lara ẹ̀: ṣòkòtò ọlọ́pàá.
english_literal: A little bit of it is a little bit of it: the policeman's short pants.
interpretation_gold: Leave nothing to waste, for one can always find some use for the smallest remnant.
deepseek_translation: The body is the body: the trousers are the owner's.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes personal responsibility and ownership, meaning each person is accountable for their own actions and belongings.
claude_translation: Your body is your body: police trousers.
claude_interpretation: You are responsible for your own actions and their consequences, just as police officers are accountable for their conduct while in uniform.
gemini_translation: Your body is your body: the policeman's trousers.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the idea that one's personal belongings or responsibilities are uniquely their own, just as a policeman's trousers are specifically his and not to be shared or borrowed.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Your body is your body: the policeman's trousers.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the idea that one's personal belongings or responsibilities are uniquely their own, just as a policeman's trousers are specifically his and not to be shared or borrowed."}
mistral_translation: One's body is one's own: trousers belong to the one with wide hips
mistral_interpretation: Each person should mind their own affairs and not interfere in what does not concern them
llama_translation: The body is tired, the trousers are not tired
llama_interpretation: One's circumstances may be challenging, but one's responsibilities or obligations remain unchanged.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í gbá ẹni tó yọ̀bẹ mú.
english_literal: One does not grab hold of a person who has pulled a knife.
interpretation_gold: Prudence and caution are imperative in dealing with dangerous people.
deepseek_translation: We do not wrestle with someone who has a knife.
deepseek_interpretation: Avoid engaging in conflicts with those who have an advantage or can cause harm.
claude_translation: One does not arrest someone who removes their cap/hat
claude_interpretation: A person who shows respect and humility should not be punished or treated harshly.
gemini_translation: One does not arrest someone who has drawn a knife.
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to confront a dangerous person who is prepared for conflict.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not arrest someone who has drawn a knife.", "interpretation": "It is unwise to confront a dangerous person who is prepared for conflict."}
mistral_translation: We do not slap someone who is holding a razor blade.
mistral_interpretation: Avoid provoking or attacking someone who is in a position of power or danger.
llama_translation: We do not despise someone who is in a state of madness
llama_interpretation: One should not look down on or mistreat someone who is going through a difficult or chaotic time.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi aṣọ ṣèdìdí yọwó.
english_literal: One does not leave cloth in a bundle while bargaining over it.
interpretation_gold: It is wise to know what one is negotiating to buy.
deepseek_translation: We do not use clothes to wipe the buttocks.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not misuse valuable resources for trivial purposes.
claude_translation: One does not use cloth to make a slingshot and expect to catch a bird
claude_interpretation: You cannot achieve success by using inappropriate or inadequate tools for the task at hand.
gemini_translation: One does not use cloth to block a hole and then remove money.
gemini_interpretation: It is foolish to use a valuable item to solve a trivial problem, only to then remove something even more valuable.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "One does not use cloth to block a hole and then remove money.", "interpretation": "It is foolish to use a valuable item to solve a trivial problem, only to then remove something even more valuable."}
mistral_translation: We do not use thick cloth to wipe the hands.
mistral_interpretation: One should not use valuable or inappropriate resources for trivial or wasteful purposes.
llama_translation: We don't use a cloth to cover a calabash
llama_interpretation: One should not try to hide or cover up something that is already obvious or exposed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ẹ̀jẹ̀ ìbálé pa tírà; alákoto ò bí abo ọmọ.
english_literal: One does not smear blood (from a woman's deflowering) on a Muslim charm; a de-virgined woman does not give birth to a “female” child.
interpretation_gold: One must not do the forbidden if one does not expect trouble.
deepseek_translation: We do not use the blood of the house floor to kill the cockroach; the cockroach does not give birth to a female child.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against using excessive or inappropriate means to solve minor problems, as it can lead to unnecessary harm or consequences.
claude_translation: One does not use the blood of a co-wife to draw tribal marks; a barren woman does not give birth to a female child
claude_interpretation: You cannot use what belongs to your rival or enemy to benefit yourself, and those who lack something cannot provide it to others.
gemini_translation: One does not use the blood of defloration to make a charm; the one who has a large penis does not give birth to a female child.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights that certain things are inherently impossible or contradictory, emphasizing that some outcomes cannot be forced or expected despite appearances or desires.
mistral_translation: We do not use the blood of a concubine to seal a deal; a barren woman does not give birth to a female child.
mistral_interpretation: One should not rely on unreliable or inappropriate means to achieve a goal, as it will not yield the desired outcome.
llama_translation: We don't use a broom to sweep a mat; a farmer does not give birth to a child
llama_interpretation: One should use the right tool or approach for a task, and not confuse roles or responsibilities.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A kì í fi ọ̀rọ̀ sílẹ̀ gbọ́ ọ̀rọ̀.
english_literal: One does not ignore one matter to attend to another matter.
interpretation_gold: Every obligation deserves attention.
deepseek_translation: We do not abandon a matter to hear a matter.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not neglect an important task to attend to something less significant.
claude_translation: One does not put down a matter to listen to another matter
claude_interpretation: You should focus on and complete one important issue before attending to another.
gemini_translation: One does not leave a matter to hear a matter.
gemini_interpretation: It is important to address current issues before moving on to new ones.
mistral_translation: We do not leave a matter unresolved to hear another matter.
mistral_interpretation: One should address and resolve an issue before moving on to the next.
llama_translation: We don't use a word to respond to a word on the floor
llama_interpretation: One should not respond to a matter that has already been settled or laid to rest.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àfẹ́ẹ̀rí kan ò ju ká rí igbó ńlá bọ́ sí lọ; ẹbọ kan ò ju ọ̀pọ̀ èèyàn lọ; “Òrìṣá gbé mi lé àtète” kan ò ju orí ẹṣin lọ.
english_literal: There is no disappearing trick better than the availability of a dense forest to disappear into; there is no sacrifice more efficacious than having many people on one's side; there is no “The gods have elevated me” that is higher than the back of a horse.
interpretation_gold: Practical and realistic moves are more reliable than mysterious expectations.
deepseek_translation: One squirrel is not enough to cover a large forest; one sacrifice is not enough for many people; one "Òrìṣá save me quickly" is not enough for a horse's head.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that a single effort or solution is often insufficient to address large or complex problems.
claude_translation: One glimpse is not better than seeing a large forest fall; one sacrifice is not better than many people; one 'God help me quickly' is not better than a horse's head.
claude_interpretation: Individual efforts or single actions cannot surpass collective strength, community support, or substantial resources.
gemini_translation: A great disappearance is not more than seeing a large forest and entering it; a great sacrifice is not more than many people; 'Orisha, lift me onto the platform' is not more than a horse's head.
gemini_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that the most effective or ultimate solution to a problem is often the most direct, practical, or readily available one, rather than something complex or supernatural.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A great disappearance is not more than seeing a large forest and entering it; a great sacrifice is not more than many people; 'Orisha, lift me onto the platform' is not more than a horse's head.", "interpretation": "The proverb emphasizes that the most effective or ultimate solution to a problem is often the most direct, practical, or readily available one, rather than something complex or supernatural."}
mistral_translation: One wildfire does not surpass seeing a great forest being consumed; one sacrifice does not surpass a multitude of people; 'The deity has lifted me to the forefront' does not surpass the horse's head.
mistral_interpretation: No single advantage or personal boast outweighs the collective strength, wisdom, or established order of the community.
llama_translation: One leaf does not cover a large forest; one sacrifice does not surpass the multitude of people; 'The god has lifted me up' does not surpass the horse's back.
