mistral_interpretation: Those who expose others' faults often bring ruin upon themselves.
llama_error: 'choices'

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Asínwín ní òun ó ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní kó má ti iná bọlé; ó ní òun ó sáà ti iná bọlé; wọ́n ní bó bá tiná bọlé àwọn ó sọ ọ́ si; ó ní ìyẹn kẹ̀ ìkan.
english_literal: The imbecile said he would torch the house; he was asked not to torch the house; he said he certainly would torch the house; he was told that if he torched the house he would be thrown in it; he said, “That casts the matter in a different light.”
interpretation_gold: Even an imbecile becomes sane when his life is at stake.
deepseek_translation: The blind man says he will carry fire home; they tell him not to carry fire home; he says he will quickly carry fire home; they say if he carries fire home they will chase him away; he says that is nothing.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against stubbornness and ignoring wise advice, as it can lead to rejection or consequences.
claude_translation: The foolish person says he will bring fire home; they tell him not to bring fire home; he says he will still bring fire home; they say if he brings fire home they will report him; he says that is the least of his concerns.
claude_interpretation: A stubborn fool will persist in dangerous behavior despite warnings and threats of consequences, dismissing all concerns as trivial.
gemini_translation: The madman said he would set the house on fire; they told him not to set the house on fire; he said he would still set the house on fire; they said if he sets the house on fire, they would throw him into it; he said, 'That's another matter.'
gemini_interpretation: This proverb illustrates the foolishness of someone who persists in a destructive path despite warnings, only to be surprised by the inevitable consequences of their actions.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The madman said he would set the house on fire; they told him not to set the house on fire; he said he would still set the house on fire; they said if he sets the house on fire, they would throw him into it; he said, 'That's another matter.'", "interpretation": "This proverb illustrates the foolishness of someone who persists in a destructive path despite warnings, only to be surprised by the inevitable consequences of their actions."}

mistral_interpretation: The proverb illustrates how someone persistently seeks ways to cause trouble despite warnings, showing defiance and disregard for consequences.
llama_translation: The gourd said it was the one that was burning in the fire; they said no, it was not the one burning in the fire; it said it was the one burning in the fire; they said if it was the one burning in the fire, they would have heard its sound; it said that was its own voice.
llama_interpretation: One should not claim to have experienced something one has not gone through.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adẹ́tẹ̀-ẹ́ ní òún sẹ́ ọ̀ràn kan de àwọn ará ilé òun; ó ní bí òún bá lọ sídàálẹ̀, wọn ò jẹ́ fi kàn-ìn-kàn-ìn òun wẹ̀.
english_literal: The leper says that he trusts his relatives on a certain matter; he says when he goes on a journey, they would not dare use his sponge to wash themselves.
interpretation_gold: People have a knack for skirting dangerous or distasteful situations.
deepseek_translation: Adete is the one who said he has no problem with his household members; he said if he goes to the grave, they will not allow him to rest in peace.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that unresolved conflicts within a family can lead to lasting discord, even after death.
claude_translation: Adẹ́tẹ̀ says he has committed an offense against his family members; he says if he goes to prostrate before them, they will not allow him to wash away his shame bit by bit.
claude_interpretation: Some offenses are so serious that even sincere apologies and gradual efforts at reconciliation may not be accepted by those who were wronged.
gemini_translation: The leper said he has caused a problem for his family; he said that if he goes to the toilet, they will not wash his anus with a sponge.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the social stigma and isolation faced by individuals with certain conditions, as their affliction can lead to their ostracization even by their own family.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The leper said he has caused a problem for his family; he said that if he goes to the toilet, they will not wash his anus with a sponge.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the social stigma and isolation faced by individuals with certain conditions, as their affliction can lead to their ostracization even by their own family."}

mistral_interpretation: A leader expects full attention and support from their people, not just superficial or dismissive gestures.
llama_translation: The crown is what makes one's town people know one's house; if the crown goes to a distant town, they will not know one's house.
llama_interpretation: A person's status or achievement is what brings recognition and respect to their family or community.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Adánilóró fagbára kọ́ni.
english_literal: He who disappoints one teaches one to be more resourceful.
interpretation_gold: Once disappointed or injured, one learns to be self-reliant.
deepseek_translation: The wealthy person who lacks patience has no one.
deepseek_interpretation: Wealth without patience leads to loneliness and loss of respect.
claude_translation: The one who asks for advice uses strength to teach oneself.
claude_interpretation: Seeking advice and guidance from others is a form of self-empowerment and wisdom.
gemini_translation: The one who causes pain teaches with force.
gemini_interpretation: Experiences of suffering or hardship often impart valuable and lasting lessons.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The one who causes pain teaches with force.", "interpretation": "Experiences of suffering or hardship often impart valuable and lasting lessons."}
mistral_translation: The one who eats alone does not grow strong.
mistral_interpretation: Strength and success come from communal effort and sharing, not isolation.
llama_translation: The one who has a lot to say does not have a basket
llama_interpretation: One who talks excessively often lacks substance or resources.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: A-bayé-jẹ́ kò ṣéé fìdí ọ̀ràn hàn.
english_literal: A treacherous person is not someone to tell profound matters to.
interpretation_gold: One should keep one's secrets from treacherous people.
deepseek_translation: One who has not experienced suffering cannot explain trouble.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that only those who have endured hardship can truly understand and articulate its nature.
claude_translation: One who spoils life cannot be trusted to reveal the truth of a matter
claude_interpretation: A person with a destructive character lacks the credibility to serve as a reliable witness or judge of situations.
gemini_translation: One who spoils the world cannot be shown the root of a matter.
gemini_interpretation: It is futile to explain the truth or details of a situation to someone who is inherently destructive or malicious, as they will only twist or misuse the information.
mistral_translation: The one who spoils the world cannot use a mere pretext to reveal a matter
mistral_interpretation: A person who causes trouble should not try to justify their actions or shift blame onto others.
llama_translation: The one who eats at home does not know the bitterness of the road.
llama_interpretation: Those who have not experienced hardship or struggle cannot truly understand its difficulties.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àpèmọ́ra là ńpe Tèmídire.
english_literal: It is in furtherance of one's own fortune that one calls the name Temidire.
interpretation_gold: Each person must advance his or her own interests.
deepseek_translation: It is gradually that we call Tèmídire.
deepseek_interpretation: Patience and persistence are necessary to achieve meaningful results.
claude_translation: We call Temidire 'the one who knows how to pamper oneself'
claude_interpretation: Self-care and knowing how to treat oneself well is a virtue worthy of recognition and praise.
gemini_translation: It is by calling 'Àpèmọ́ra' that Tèmídire is called.
gemini_interpretation: One's true identity or nature is revealed through their actions or the circumstances surrounding them.
mistral_translation: It is the one who is about to fall that we call 'Hold-on-tight.'
mistral_interpretation: People often seek help or support only when they are already in trouble or facing failure.
llama_translation: The one who is not present is being called by Temidire
llama_interpretation: One's absence can lead to being summoned or sought after, implying that being present and available is important.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Àjòjí lójú, ṣùgbọ́n kò fi ríran.
english_literal: A stranger has eyes, but they do not see.
interpretation_gold: A stranger's eyes are blind to the intricacies of his new surroundings.
deepseek_translation: A stranger is in sight, but does not have eyesight.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against trusting outsiders who may not understand or respect local customs and values.
claude_translation: The stranger has eyes, but cannot see clearly
claude_interpretation: A newcomer or outsider may observe situations but lacks the deep understanding that comes from familiarity and experience within that environment.
gemini_translation: A stranger has eyes, but cannot see with them.
gemini_interpretation: A newcomer may observe a situation but lacks the understanding or insight to truly comprehend it.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A stranger has eyes, but cannot see with them.", "interpretation": "A newcomer may observe a situation but lacks the understanding or insight to truly comprehend it."}
mistral_translation: A stranger in the eyes, but he does not blink
mistral_interpretation: Someone may appear unfamiliar or distant, but they are not necessarily untrustworthy or deceitful.
llama_translation: The dawn has broken, but it has not brought light.
llama_interpretation: Good intentions or beginnings do not necessarily guarantee success or positive outcomes.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Abiyamọ́ ṣọwọ́ kòtò lu ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀.
english_literal: A nursing mother cups her palm to strike her child.
interpretation_gold: Discretion is the better part of discipline.
deepseek_translation: The mother who washes her hands in muddy water harms her child.
deepseek_interpretation: A parent's irresponsible actions negatively affect their children.
claude_translation: A mother washes her hands clean before beating her child.
claude_interpretation: A parent must ensure they are morally clean and justified before disciplining their child.
gemini_translation: A mother does not use a hoe to hit her child.
gemini_interpretation: A mother's love and care for her child are inherent, and she would never intentionally harm them.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A mother does not use a hoe to hit her child.", "interpretation": "A mother's love and care for her child are inherent, and she would never intentionally harm them."}
mistral_translation: A mother hen pecks the ground to hit her own chick
mistral_interpretation: Sometimes those who care for us may unintentionally cause us harm while trying to protect or correct us
llama_translation: The mother's wealth is not hidden from her child.
llama_interpretation: A mother knows her child's true nature and character.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Atipo ò mọ erèé; ó ní, “Bàbá, mo réwé funfun lóko.”
english_literal: Atipo does not recognize beans, he says, “Father, I saw white leaves on the farm.”
interpretation_gold: Ignorance is a curse.
deepseek_translation: The cripple does not know how to crawl; he says, "Father, I harvested white leaves in the farm."
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes someone who makes excuses or boasts about impossible achievements.
claude_translation: The dwarf does not know the taboo; he says, 'Father, I have plucked white leaves in the farm.'
claude_interpretation: Ignorance of cultural rules and taboos can lead one to unknowingly commit serious offenses.
gemini_translation: A stranger does not know okra; he says, “Father, I saw white leaves in the farm.”
gemini_interpretation: Ignorance or unfamiliarity can lead to misidentification or misunderstanding of common things.
mistral_translation: The partridge does not know the game; it says, 'Father, I am bringing white leaves from the farm.'
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights ignorance or arrogance in claiming credit for something one does not truly understand or contribute to meaningfully.
llama_translation: The tortoise does not know play; he says, “Father, I am farming white cloth.”
llama_interpretation: One should not pretend to be what they are not or claim expertise in something they know nothing about.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọkùnrín réjò, tóbìrín pa á, à ní kéjò má ṣáà lọ.
english_literal: If a man sees a snake, and a woman kills it, what matters is that the snake does not escape.
interpretation_gold: One should not be a stickler about roles.
deepseek_translation: If a man escapes a snake, and a woman kills it, they say the snake should not have gone away.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb criticizes the tendency to undermine or dismiss someone's efforts, especially when they succeed where others have failed.
claude_translation: If a man sees a snake and a woman kills it, we tell the snake not to run away.

deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that limited perspective can lead to overestimating one's own possessions or achievements.
claude_translation: If a child does not see another person's father's farm, they will say there is no father's farm as good as their own father's.

mistral_translation: If a child has not seen another person's father's farm, they say their own father's farm is the largest that ever existed.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

interpretation_gold: The youth is mindful of what his superiors think of him, while the elder is mindful of what the young think of him.
deepseek_translation: If a child falls, he looks forward; if an elder falls, he looks backward.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that the young focus on the future after setbacks, while the elderly reflect on the past.
claude_translation: When a child falls, they look forward; when an elder falls, they look backward.
claude_interpretation: Children focus on moving ahead after setbacks while elders tend to reflect on what caused their downfall.
gemini_translation: If a child falls, he looks forward; if an elder falls, he looks backward.
gemini_interpretation: Children focus on the future and moving on from mistakes, while elders reflect on past experiences to understand their present circumstances.
mistral_translation: If a child falls, you look ahead; if an elder falls, you look behind.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb teaches that the consequences of a child's mistake are less severe, while an elder's failure affects the community's past and future.
llama_translation: When a child stumbles, we look to the front; when an elder stumbles, we look to the back.
llama_interpretation: The community is more concerned with the future of the young than with the past mistakes of the elderly.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí eré bí eré, àlàbọrùn-ún dẹ̀wù.
english_literal: Like play, like play, the makeshift cape became a dress.
interpretation_gold: Imperceptibly, a stop-gap arrangement has become the status quo.
deepseek_translation: If play is like play, the playground is wide.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that when people engage in activities with mutual understanding and respect, there is room for everyone to participate and enjoy.
claude_translation: No matter how playful, the scorpion remains dangerous
claude_interpretation: One should never underestimate or trust someone's true nature, even when they appear harmless or friendly.
gemini_translation: Playfully, playfully, the chameleon puts on a garment.
gemini_interpretation: Even in jest or seemingly insignificant actions, one can achieve significant or transformative results.
mistral_translation: However playfully one plays, the wrapper (cloth) will still be tied around the waist.
mistral_interpretation: No matter how much one tries to avoid responsibilities, one must eventually face and fulfill them.
llama_translation: When play is play, the one who plays with the moon will be exhausted.
llama_interpretation: One should know their limits and not overstep their bounds.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọ̀rán bá pẹ́ nílẹ̀, gbígbọ́n ní ńgbọ́n.
english_literal: If a problem remains long enough, it becomes clever.
interpretation_gold: If one keeps at it long enough, one will find the solution for any problem.
deepseek_translation: If a matter stays long on the ground, wisdom is what grows.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that time and patience lead to wisdom in resolving issues.
claude_translation: If a matter stays long on the ground, it becomes wise.
claude_interpretation: Issues that persist over time naturally develop complexity and require greater wisdom to resolve.
gemini_translation: If a matter stays long on the ground, it becomes rotten.
gemini_interpretation: Delaying a task or problem for too long will only make it worse or more difficult to resolve.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If a matter stays long on the ground, it becomes rotten.", "interpretation": "Delaying a task or problem for too long will only make it worse or more difficult to resolve."}
mistral_translation: If a matter lies on the ground, wisdom is what picks it up
mistral_interpretation: Wisdom is required to resolve issues that are openly known or easily accessible
llama_translation: When a drum is beaten at home, the drumstick is the one that hears it.
llama_interpretation: Those closest to a situation are often the ones most aware of its details.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọmọdé bá dúpẹ́ ore àná, a rí tòní gbà.
english_literal: If a child expresses gratitude for yesterday's favor, he will receive today's.
interpretation_gold: The grateful person encourages others to do him more favors.
deepseek_translation: If a child appreciates yesterday's kindness, they will receive today's.
deepseek_interpretation: Gratitude for past favors ensures continued blessings.
claude_translation: If a child appreciates yesterday's favor, they will receive today's.
claude_interpretation: Gratitude for past kindness ensures continued generosity and support.
gemini_translation: If a child thanks for yesterday's favor, he will receive today's.
gemini_interpretation: Expressing gratitude for past kindness increases the likelihood of receiving future blessings.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If a child thanks for yesterday's favor, he will receive today's.", "interpretation": "Expressing gratitude for past kindness increases the likelihood of receiving future blessings."}
mistral_translation: If a child thanks a friend of yesterday, we will see one for today receive.
mistral_interpretation: Gratitude shown to past helpers encourages present and future support.
llama_translation: If a child greets a friend's mother, we see it as a greeting to the friend.
llama_interpretation: A person's actions can reflect on their associates or family members.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá jẹ̀wọ́ tán ẹ̀rín là ńrín; bí a bá yó tán orun ní ńkunni.
english_literal: After a joke one gives way to laughter; after satiation one gives way to sleep.
interpretation_gold: The action should match the occasion.
deepseek_translation: When we finish eating the snail, we laugh; when we finish drinking the wine, we cry.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that temporary pleasures can lead to long-term sorrows.
claude_translation: When we finish eating, we smile; when we finish rejoicing, sleep overcomes us.
claude_interpretation: Satisfaction and contentment naturally lead to peace and rest.
gemini_translation: If we finish eating, we smile; if we are full, sleep overcomes us.
gemini_interpretation: Satisfaction and contentment often lead to a state of relaxation and ease.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If we finish eating, we smile; if we are full, sleep overcomes us.", "interpretation": "Satisfaction and contentment often lead to a state of relaxation and ease."}
mistral_translation: If we finish urinating we laugh; if we finish defecating we groan.
mistral_interpretation: The outcome of an action determines whether it brings relief or regret.
llama_translation: If we are running with the elephant, we are running; if we are running with the ant, we are crawling.
llama_interpretation: One's progress or pace in life is influenced by the company they keep.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a bá rí òwúrọ̀, alẹ́ ńkọ́?
english_literal: Although one has seen the morning, what about night time?
interpretation_gold: Nobody should be judged until he or she has reached the end of his or her days.
deepseek_translation: If we see the morning, is the evening not coming?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb reminds us that time is fleeting and every moment leads to the next, urging mindfulness of the future.
claude_translation: If we see morning, what about evening?
claude_interpretation: One should not celebrate or make conclusions too early, as challenges may still come later.
gemini_translation: If we see the morning, what about the evening?
gemini_interpretation: One should not be overly confident or celebrate prematurely, as circumstances can change unexpectedly.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If we see the morning, what about the evening?", "interpretation": "One should not be overly confident or celebrate prematurely, as circumstances can change unexpectedly."}
mistral_translation: If we see morning, what about the night?
mistral_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that one should not celebrate prematurely, as challenges or uncertainties may still lie ahead.
llama_translation: If we see the dawn, should we sleep?
llama_interpretation: One should take advantage of opportunities as soon as they arise.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ régérégé bá ro ẹjọ́-ọ tirẹ̀ tán, kó rántí pé ẹlẹ́rẹ̀kẹ́ mẹ́kí á rí rò.
english_literal: After the person with smooth cheeks has stated his or her case, he or she should remember that the person with blemished cheeks will have something to say.
interpretation_gold: The person who looks good owing to the efforts of his or her subordinates should remember that they also deserve some credit.
deepseek_translation: When the little lizard nods its head, it should remember that there are other lizards.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb reminds individuals to remain humble and remember that they are not the only ones capable of achieving success or recognition.
claude_translation: When a grasshopper finishes thinking about its own case, let it remember that there are other grasshoppers to consider.
claude_interpretation: One should not be so consumed with personal problems that they forget others also have their own struggles and perspectives to consider.
gemini_translation: If the one with the full cheeks finishes stating their case, they should remember that the one with the sunken cheeks will also have a case to state.
gemini_interpretation: Those in positions of power or privilege should remember that others, even those less fortunate, also have valid perspectives and concerns that deserve to be heard.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If the one with the full cheeks finishes stating their case, they should remember that the one with the sunken cheeks will also have a case to state.", "interpretation": "Those in positions of power or privilege should remember that others, even those less fortunate, also have valid perspectives and concerns that deserve to be heard."}
mistral_translation: If the frog boasts excessively after winning its own case, it should remember that the frog will also face judgment someday.
mistral_interpretation: No matter how much one gloats over a personal victory, humility is necessary because everyone will eventually face their own reckoning.
llama_translation: If a lizard is running with all its might and falls into a pit, it is not because the lizard is weak.
llama_interpretation: This proverb teaches that failure is not always a result of one's weakness, but sometimes due to unforeseen circumstances.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ojú bá mọ́, olówò a gbówò; ọ̀rànwú a gbé kẹ́kẹ́; ajagun a gbé apata; àgbẹ̀ a jí tòun tòrúkọ́; ọmọ ọdẹ a jí tapó tọrán; ajíwẹṣẹ a bá odò omi lọ.
english_literal: When day breaks, the trader takes up his trade; the cotton spinner picks up the spindle; the warrior grabs his shield; the farmer gets up with his hoe; the son of the hunter arises with his quiver and his bows; he-who-wakes-and-washes-with-soap makes his way to the river.
interpretation_gold: When morning comes, everybody should embark on something useful.
deepseek_translation: If the eye sees, the rich will carry their wealth; the poor will carry their load; the warrior will carry his shield; the farmer will wake with his hoe; the hunter's child will wake with his trap and snare; the fisherman will follow the river.
deepseek_interpretation: Everyone has their own responsibilities and roles to fulfill in life.
claude_translation: If the eye is clear/wise, the wealthy person will take money; the trader will take a bicycle; the warrior will take a stone; the farmer will wake up early in the morning; the hunter's child will wake up to hunt animals; the water fetcher will go with the river.
claude_interpretation: When one has wisdom and clear vision, each person will naturally pursue what is most appropriate and beneficial according to their role and circumstances in life.

gemini_interpretation: This proverb illustrates that with the arrival of a new day, everyone returns to their respective duties and responsibilities.

llama_translation: When the eyes are closed, the rich man carries the load; the farmer carries the basket; the warrior carries the stone; the farmer eats the ripe plantain; the hunter eats the roasted rat; the lazy person goes to fetch water from the river.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí obìnrin ò bá gbé ilé tó méjì, kì í mọ èyí tó sàn.

claude_translation: If a woman does not live in two houses, she will not know which one is better.
claude_interpretation: One cannot make proper comparisons or judgments without experiencing different situations or options.
gemini_translation: If a woman does not live in two houses, she does not know which one is better.
gemini_interpretation: One cannot truly appreciate or compare options without experiencing more than one.
mistral_translation: If a woman does not live in two houses, she will not know which one is better.
mistral_interpretation: Experience from different situations helps one make better judgments or choices.
llama_translation: If a woman does not have two homes, she will not know the better one.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the importance of having options and experiences to make informed decisions.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

interpretation_gold: One makes do with what one can find.
deepseek_translation: If we do not have a lamp, we use the moonlight.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches resourcefulness, using available means when ideal options are absent.

mistral_interpretation: One should adapt and make use of available resources when the ideal tool or method is unavailable

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

llama_translation: When two people are fighting, one is the elder
llama_interpretation: In every conflict, one party is often more mature or responsible.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ọ̀bùn ò mọ èrè, a mọ ojú owó.

deepseek_interpretation: Everyone has their own unique skills or talents, even if they are not obvious at first glance.
claude_translation: If the thumb doesn't know profit, it knows the face of money

llama_translation: If the palm tree does not know its leaf, we know the face of the palm tree
llama_interpretation: One's true nature will eventually be revealed despite attempts to conceal it.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí àrùn búburú bá wọ̀lú, oògùn búburú la fi ńwò ó.

claude_interpretation: Extreme problems require extreme solutions, even if those solutions are unpleasant or harsh.
gemini_translation: If a bad disease enters a town, it is with a bad medicine that it is treated.
gemini_interpretation: Drastic problems often require equally drastic solutions.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If a bad disease enters a town, it is with a bad medicine that it is treated.", "interpretation": "Drastic problems often require equally drastic solutions."}
mistral_translation: If a very bad disease enters the town, it is with a very bad medicine that we treat it.
mistral_interpretation: Extreme problems require equally strong or drastic solutions to resolve them.
llama_translation: When a stubborn illness afflicts the head, a stubborn medicine is used to treat it.
llama_interpretation: A difficult problem requires a strong and determined solution.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí ikún bá jẹ, bí ikún bá mu, ikún a wo oòrùn alẹ́.

llama_interpretation: One should always be mindful of one's actions and their potential consequences.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

gemini_translation: If the deity takes the one with a hunchback, let the hunchback prepare himself.

gemini_translation: If we are crying, we will see.

gemini_raw: {"translation": "If we are crying, we will see.", "interpretation": "Even in moments of distress or sadness, one can still gain clarity or insight."}

llama_translation: If we are patient, we will see the beauty.
llama_interpretation: Patience is necessary to appreciate the good things in life.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom

claude_translation: When things are finished on the ground, the child of sacrifice will return to dance, those who are there will prepare to go.
claude_interpretation: When a situation or event comes to an end, people naturally prepare to move on to the next phase or activity.
gemini_translation: If things finish on the ground, the child of sacrifice will jump into a dance, and those who are there will prepare to leave.
gemini_interpretation: When resources are depleted, those who benefit from the situation will celebrate their gain, while others will recognize the end of the opportunity and depart.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "If things finish on the ground, the child of sacrifice will jump into a dance, and those who are there will prepare to leave.", "interpretation": "When resources are depleted, those who benefit from the situation will celebrate their gain, while others will recognize the end of the opportunity and depart."}
mistral_translation: When something ends on the ground, the offspring of the sacrifice will dance on it, those who are there will prepare and go
mistral_interpretation: When an opportunity or situation arises, those present should seize it without delay, as others may benefit from it later.
llama_translation: When a rat is caught in the house, the child of the sacrifice is thrown away, and those who are there beat and run away.
llama_interpretation: When a problem arises, people often abandon their responsibilities and flee in panic.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí a kò bá rígún a ò gbọdọ̀ ṣebọ; bí a ò bá rí àkàlà a ò gbọdọ̀ ṣorò.
english_literal: If we cannot find a vulture we may not offer a sacrifice; if we cannot find a ground hornbill we may not carry out a ritual.
interpretation_gold: Nothing can be accomplished in the absence of the requisite materials.
deepseek_translation: If we do not see the vulture, we must not perform the sacrifice; if we do not see the squirrel, we must not perform the ritual.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not act or make decisions without clear evidence or proper justification.
claude_translation: If we don't see the vulture we must not perform sacrifice; if we don't see the crow we must not speak.
claude_interpretation: One should not act or speak without proper evidence or confirmation of the circumstances that warrant such actions.
gemini_translation: If we don't see the vulture, we must not offer sacrifice; if we don't see the akala bird, we must not perform rituals.
gemini_interpretation: Important actions or rituals should only be undertaken when the necessary signs or conditions are present.
mistral_translation: If we do not see the vulture, we must not perform the sacrifice; if we do not see the hawk, we must not discuss the matter.
mistral_interpretation: One should not proceed with important actions or decisions without the necessary conditions or key participants in place.
llama_translation: If we don't see a vulture, we don't learn how to make a sacrifice; if we don't see a hawk, we don't learn how to make a charm.
llama_interpretation: One learns by observing and imitating the experiences of others.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Bí kò bá tíì rẹ ìjà, a kì í là á.
english_literal: If a fight is not yet spent, one does not intervene to end it.
interpretation_gold: One cannot end a fight that is not yet willing to end.
deepseek_translation: If the fight has not been fought, we do not lick it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one should not claim victory or benefits from a situation they have not actively participated in or contributed to.
claude_translation: If it is not yet time for war, one does not declare it.
claude_interpretation: There is an appropriate time for every action, and one should not rush into conflict or confrontation prematurely.
gemini_translation: If a fight has not yet tired, one does not separate it.
gemini_interpretation: It is futile to intervene in a conflict before the parties involved are ready to cease fighting.
mistral_translation: If it does not reach the point of fighting, we do not split it.
mistral_interpretation: Disputes should only be resolved or divided when they have escalated to a serious conflict.
llama_translation: If it doesn't reach your body, you won't feel the pain.
llama_interpretation: One can only truly understand and empathize with another's struggles when directly affected.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Baálé àìlọ́wọ̀ ni àlejò àìlọ́wọ̀.
english_literal: An unsolicitous host makes for a visitor with no deference.
interpretation_gold: The visitor responds according to his reception.
deepseek_translation: A host without money is a guest without money.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that financial responsibility is essential for both hosts and guests to maintain dignity and respect in social interactions.
claude_translation: A host without hands is a guest without hands
claude_interpretation: A person who cannot give or help others should not expect to receive help or hospitality from others.
gemini_translation: A disrespectful host is a disrespectful guest.
gemini_interpretation: The way one treats others often reflects how they will be treated in return, emphasizing the importance of reciprocity in social interactions.
mistral_translation: The host who does not give is the guest who does not give.
mistral_interpretation: It teaches that stinginess in one person often leads to similar behavior in others, reflecting a cycle of ungenerosity.
llama_translation: The owner of the house does not know the way, the stranger does not know the way.
llama_interpretation: This proverb highlights the idea that even those who are supposed to be knowledgeable or in charge can be just as lost or uncertain as outsiders.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dà-á-sílẹ̀-ká-tun-pín, ogún ijọ́un, a ò pín in re.
english_literal: The recent throw-it-all-on-the-floor-that-we-may-redistribute-it inheritance was not well distributed the first time around.
interpretation_gold: Whatever needs to be done again must not have been done well the first time.
deepseek_translation: The one who divides and does not share, twenty of his own, we will not share with him.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against selfishness and unfairness, emphasizing that those who refuse to share with others will not receive help when in need.
claude_translation: Let us put it down and share it again, twenty days, we have not shared it yet
claude_interpretation: Procrastination and endless deliberation prevent action from ever being taken.
gemini_translation: To throw it down and then redistribute, that is an old inheritance, we do not share it.
gemini_interpretation: Some things are so inherently established or belong to someone that they cannot be re-divided or taken away.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "To throw it down and then redistribute, that is an old inheritance, we do not share it.", "interpretation": "Some things are so inherently established or belong to someone that they cannot be re-divided or taken away."}
mistral_translation: If we set out to share and then decide to divide again, twenty days of dancing, we do not share its benefit
mistral_interpretation: Repeatedly revisiting settled agreements disrupts progress and negates the gains of previous efforts.
llama_translation: We beat the drum and the dance is not sweet, the drum is not the problem.
llama_interpretation: The fault lies not with the circumstances, but with the individual's attitude or approach.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dùgbẹ̀-dùgbẹ̀ kì í fi ẹyin rẹ̀ sílẹ̀.
english_literal: The egg-bearing spider never leaves its eggs behind.
interpretation_gold: One does not turn one's back on one's treasure.
deepseek_translation: The tortoise does not leave its shell behind.
deepseek_interpretation: One should always protect their essential identity or resources.
claude_translation: A brooding hen does not abandon its eggs
claude_interpretation: A responsible person does not abandon their duties or commitments, especially when others depend on them.
gemini_translation: The 'dugbẹ̀-dugbẹ̀' bird does not abandon its eggs.
gemini_interpretation: One should always take responsibility for their creations or offspring.
mistral_translation: Slowly-slowly does not leave its egg behind
mistral_interpretation: Patience and steady progress ensure that nothing important is left unfinished or lost
llama_translation: A small hill does not prevent a bird from flying.
llama_interpretation: Obstacles, no matter how daunting, should not hinder one's pursuit of goals or aspirations.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Díẹ̀-díẹ̀ nimú ẹlẹ́dẹ̀ẹ́ fi ńwọgbà.
english_literal: It is bit by bit that the nose of the pig enters the fence.
interpretation_gold: A small problem, if not attended to, becomes unmanageable.
deepseek_translation: Little by little is how the pig's nose gets flattened.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that persistence and gradual effort lead to significant results.
claude_translation: Little by little is how the pig's snout enters the barn.
claude_interpretation: Gradual persistence and patience lead to achieving significant goals over time.
gemini_translation: Little by little, the pig's snout enters the garden.
gemini_interpretation: Small, seemingly insignificant intrusions can gradually lead to greater damage or a complete takeover.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Little by little, the pig's snout enters the garden.", "interpretation": "Small, seemingly insignificant intrusions can gradually lead to greater damage or a complete takeover."}
mistral_translation: Little by little, the snout of the pig is used to make a basket.
mistral_interpretation: Consistent small efforts over time lead to significant achievements.
llama_translation: It is the smallness of the palm tree that makes it produce fruit
llama_interpretation: Smallness or humility can be a virtue that leads to productivity and success.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dúró o kíkà; bí o ò dúró kíkà, ìkà a ba tìrẹ jẹ́.
english_literal: Stop and say hello to the wicked; if you do not say hello to the wicked, the wicked will find problems for you.
interpretation_gold: One's best defence against the wicked is ingratiation.
deepseek_translation: Stand and be wicked; if you do not stand to be wicked, wickedness will consume you.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that failing to confront or resist evil may lead to being overcome by it.
claude_translation: Wait, don't be wicked; if you don't wait and avoid wickedness, wickedness will destroy yours too
claude_interpretation: Those who practice wickedness will eventually have their own possessions or loved ones destroyed by the same evil they perpetrate.
gemini_translation: Wait, you wicked one; if you do not wait, wickedness will spoil yours.
gemini_interpretation: One should be patient and avoid acting wickedly, as impatience and wickedness can lead to negative consequences for oneself.
mistral_translation: Stand still and read; if you do not stand still to read, wickedness will befall you
mistral_interpretation: Patience and careful attention are necessary to avoid mistakes or misfortune in life
llama_translation: Stay and be patient; if you don't stay and be patient, patience will come and meet you.
llama_interpretation: Patience is inevitable, so it's better to cultivate it willingly rather than being forced to do so.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Dídì ní ḿmú abẹ mú.
english_literal: It is wrapping that makes a knife sharp.
interpretation_gold: Only by taking great care of them does one keep one's possessions in good shape.
deepseek_translation: The beard is what makes the razor sharp.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that challenges or opposition can bring out one's best qualities or sharpen one's abilities.
claude_translation: Tightness is what makes a razor sharp.
claude_interpretation: Discipline and restraint are what give strength and effectiveness to one's abilities.
gemini_translation: Binding is what makes a razor sharp.
gemini_interpretation: Consistent effort and practice are essential for developing and maintaining skills or abilities.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Binding is what makes a razor sharp.", "interpretation": "Consistent effort and practice are essential for developing and maintaining skills or abilities."}
mistral_translation: It is stubbornness that makes the razor hold on to the armpit
mistral_interpretation: Stubbornness or persistence in a harmful action will only lead to self-inflicted suffering.
llama_translation: The head is what the load carries
llama_interpretation: The leader or person in charge bears the ultimate responsibility for the actions of their group or organization.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
interpretation_gold: One should speak to others in a manner that befits one, and that will facilitate one's business with them.
deepseek_translation: The Egbá masquerader must speak Egbá.
deepseek_interpretation: One must adhere to the customs and traditions of their role or community.
claude_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
claude_interpretation: One must stay true to their origins and cultural identity regardless of the role they play.
gemini_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá.
gemini_interpretation: One should always act in accordance with their true identity or origin.
mistral_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must speak Ẹ̀gbá
mistral_interpretation: One should communicate or behave in a way that reflects their true identity or origin
llama_translation: The Ẹ̀gbá masquerader must needs speak Ẹ̀gbá
llama_interpretation: One must act in accordance with one's role or identity.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ebi ńpa mí ọlọ́ṣẹ ńkiri; ìgbà tí ng ò wẹnú ng ó ṣe wẹ̀de?
english_literal: I am hungry and the soap seller hawks her wares; when I have not washed my inside, how can I wash my outside?
interpretation_gold: One must order one's priorities sensibly.
deepseek_translation: I am hungry and the soap is moving around; when I don't have saliva, how will I foam?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the futility of pursuing trivial matters when basic needs (like hunger) are unmet.
claude_translation: Hunger is killing me, the lazy one is wandering about; when I don't enter inside, how will I do entering?
claude_interpretation: One cannot expect to satisfy their needs or achieve success without taking action and making an effort to pursue opportunities.
gemini_translation: I am hungry, and the soap seller is hawking; when I have not eaten, how will I bathe?
gemini_interpretation: One must address fundamental needs before attending to less urgent matters.
mistral_translation: Hunger is killing me while the soap owner is bathing; when I don't bathe, how will I be clean?
mistral_interpretation: It highlights the frustration of lacking resources while others have them in abundance, emphasizing the need to address one's own needs first.
llama_translation: Hunger is killing me, the hunter is crying; when I have not entered the forest, how can I bring game?
llama_interpretation: One must take action and face challenges to achieve success.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ejò-ó rí ihò tó há ó kó wọ̀ ọ́; ìyá-a rẹ̀-ẹ́ lọ́wọ́ àti fà á yọ?
english_literal: A snake sees a tight hole and crawls into it; has its mother hands to pull it out?
interpretation_gold: One had better be certain that one would be able to extricate oneself before one ventures into tight spots.
deepseek_translation: The snake saw a hole and entered it; did its mother hold its hand and pull it out?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes personal responsibility and the consequences of one's own actions.
claude_translation: A snake finds a hole and enters it; is it its mother who will pull it out?
claude_interpretation: People must take responsibility for the consequences of their own actions and decisions.
gemini_translation: The snake saw a hole that was too narrow and did not enter it; does its mother have hands to pull it out?
gemini_interpretation: One should avoid situations that are difficult to escape from, as there may be no one to help.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The snake saw a hole that was too narrow and did not enter it; does its mother have hands to pull it out?", "interpretation": "One should avoid situations that are difficult to escape from, as there may be no one to help."}
mistral_translation: Will the snake see a hole big enough to enter and not go in; is it its mother that has hands to pull it out?
mistral_interpretation: One should avoid dangerous situations rather than relying on others to rescue them later.
llama_translation: The lizard sees the wall it will climb and asks its mother if the wall is climbable
llama_interpretation: One should seek advice from experienced elders before embarking on a challenging task.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-fẹ́-obìnrin-tẹ́nìkan-ńfẹ́, olúwarẹ̀ ò níí fẹ́ obìnrin ni.
english_literal: I-will-court-no-woman-being-courted-by-another-man will court no woman at all.
interpretation_gold: A person who wants exclusive rights to a woman (or anything) will look for a long time and in vain.
deepseek_translation: I do not want the woman that someone else wants, the owner of the house does not want a woman.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against desiring what others value, as it may lead to unnecessary conflict or trouble.
claude_translation: I-will-not-love-the-woman-that-someone-else-loves, her owner will not love the woman.
claude_interpretation: When you pursue someone else's romantic partner, even the original partner may lose interest, showing that interference in relationships often destroys them entirely.
gemini_translation: I will not love a woman that someone else is loving, that person will not love a woman.
gemini_interpretation: One should not be possessive or dictate another's choices, as such an attitude can lead to isolation.
mistral_translation: I will not love a woman who loves only one person, the owner of the town will not love a woman either
mistral_interpretation: This proverb warns against selfish or one-sided relationships, emphasizing that no one, not even a leader, tolerates a partner who is disloyal or self-serving.
llama_translation: I don't love a woman who is always at home, the one I love is the one who is not at home
llama_interpretation: A partner who is industrious and independent is more desirable than one who is idle and dependent.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Eégún tí yó gbeni là ńdáṣọ fún; òrìṣà tí yó gbeni là ńsìn; bi igí bá gbè mí mà kó obì mà bọ igi.
english_literal: It is the masquerader that succors one that one makes shrouds for; it is the god that succors one that one worships; if a tree succors me, I will take kolanuts and worship the tree.
interpretation_gold: One should confine one's efforts to profitable ventures, and one's service to appreciative people.
deepseek_translation: It is the masquerade that will carry one that we sew clothes for; it is the deity that will carry one that we serve; if a tree should carry me, let it carry kola nuts to the tree.
deepseek_interpretation: One should invest time and resources only in those who will reciprocate or bring benefit.
claude_translation: It is the masquerade that will save us that we dress for; it is the deity that will save us that we worship; if a tree supports me, let me not take kola nut to worship the tree.
claude_interpretation: We should be grateful and show respect to those who help and support us in our time of need.
gemini_translation: It is the masquerade that will support one that we sew clothes for; it is the deity that will support one that we worship; if a tree supports me, I will gather kola nuts and offer them to the tree.
gemini_interpretation: One should show gratitude and devotion to those who provide support and assistance.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "It is the masquerade that will support one that we sew clothes for; it is the deity that will support one that we worship; if a tree supports me, I will gather kola nuts and offer them to the tree.", "interpretation": "One should show gratitude and devotion to those who provide support and assistance."}
mistral_translation: We sew clothes for the masquerade that will carry us; we worship the deity that will carry us; if a tree is going to fell me, let it at least bear kola nuts so I can offer it.
mistral_interpretation: One should engage with things or people that will ultimately support or benefit them in the future.
llama_translation: The masquerade that is revered is the one that dances well; the deity that is revered is the one that is worshipped; if a tree falls on me and I use it to make a canoe to sail on the tree.
llama_interpretation: One's abilities and actions determine the respect and recognition they receive.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ebi ò pàmọ̀le ó ní òun ò jẹ àáyá; ebí pa Súlè ó jọ̀bọ.
english_literal: The muslim is not hungry and he vows he will not eat a red Colobus monkey; hunger gripped Suleiman and he ate a monkey.
interpretation_gold: A desperate person is seldom finicky.
deepseek_translation: Hunger did not kill the lizard, yet it claims it does not eat termites; hunger killed Sule, he bowed down.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against pride and false claims, emphasizing that humility and truthfulness are essential for survival.
claude_translation: Hunger does not spare the learned one claiming it does not eat scholars; hunger killed Sule and he fell down.
claude_interpretation: No one is exempt from life's basic needs and hardships, regardless of their education or social status.
gemini_translation: Hunger did not kill the rich man, he said he would not eat bat; hunger killed Sule, he ate a bat.
gemini_interpretation: When faced with extreme hardship, one may be forced to abandon their principles or preferences.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Hunger did not kill the rich man, he said he would not eat bat; hunger killed Sule, he ate a bat.", "interpretation": "When faced with extreme hardship, one may be forced to abandon their principles or preferences."}
mistral_translation: Hunger does not hide behind the door and say it won't eat beans; hunger killed Sule and he was buried
mistral_interpretation: Hardship or necessity will force people to do what they initially resist or deny, no matter their objections.
llama_translation: Hunger does not kill the child of a noble; hunger kills the child of a poor man.
llama_interpretation: Poverty and lack of resources can exacerbate the effects of hardship.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èrò kì í mọ ibùsọ̀ kọ́rùn ó wọ̀ ọ́.
english_literal: A wayfarer does not know the location of the rest stop and yet have his neck crushed from the weight of a heavy load.
interpretation_gold: One measures one's exertions to suit one's capacity.
deepseek_translation: The ant does not know the palm oil will drown it.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against underestimating dangers due to ignorance or overconfidence.
claude_translation: A passenger does not know where to sleep until evening comes upon them
claude_interpretation: One cannot fully prepare for or understand a situation until they are actually experiencing it.
gemini_translation: A thought does not know a resting place and enter it.
gemini_interpretation: One must act on an idea or plan for it to materialize and be effective.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A thought does not know a resting place and enter it.", "interpretation": "One must act on an idea or plan for it to materialize and be effective."}
mistral_translation: A thought does not know the depth of the river before it dives in with its neck.
mistral_interpretation: One should not act hastily without first assessing the risks or challenges involved.
llama_translation: A traveler does not know the depth of a river until he wades into it
llama_interpretation: One must experience a situation firsthand to truly understand its challenges.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èyí tó yẹ ará iwájú, èrò ẹ̀hìn fiyè sílẹ̀.
english_literal: (To) what turned out favorably for those going ahead, you coming behind, pay close attention.
interpretation_gold: Learn from the examples of others.
deepseek_translation: What is proper for those in front, the followers neglect.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against disregarding the wisdom or examples set by predecessors.
claude_translation: What is suitable for those in front, those behind should let it pass by
claude_interpretation: People should recognize their position and not interfere with matters that are meant for those who are ahead of them in rank, age, or status.
gemini_translation: That which befits those in front, those behind should pay attention to it.
gemini_interpretation: One should learn from the experiences and actions of those who have gone before them.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "That which befits those in front, those behind should pay attention to it.", "interpretation": "One should learn from the experiences and actions of those who have gone before them."}
mistral_translation: What is good for those ahead, the ones behind leave it behind.
mistral_interpretation: People often abandon what has already benefited others, assuming it no longer holds value for them.
llama_translation: What is put in front is the face, the back is what is put behind
llama_interpretation: One's true nature is often revealed by their actions when they think no one is watching.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èmi-ò-níí-ṣu-imí-le-imí, olúwarẹ̀ ó rìn jìnnà ààtàn.
english_literal: I-will-not-defecate-on-existing-excrement will walk a good distance into the bush.
interpretation_gold: People who are too finicky will pay in effort and delay for their habits.
deepseek_translation: I do not defecate on excrement, the owner of the farm walks far to the dung heap.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches the importance of respecting others' property and not taking advantage of their kindness or resources.
claude_translation: I-will-not-cook-yam-for-you-to-eat, your master will walk far in the evening
claude_interpretation: When you refuse to help someone or show kindness, they will seek assistance elsewhere, often going to great lengths to find what you denied them.
gemini_translation: I will not defecate on feces, the person will walk far from the dump.
gemini_interpretation: It is wise to avoid repeating past mistakes or engaging in futile actions, as doing so only prolongs the problem or effort.
mistral_translation: I will not sniff the scent of a fart, let the owner of the fart walk far away from the refuse dump
mistral_interpretation: Avoid unnecessary involvement in others' shameful or unpleasant situations, allowing them to bear their own consequences
llama_translation: The one who does not know how to swim, the king's servant will lead to the riverbank.
llama_interpretation: A leader should guide and support those who are inexperienced or lack knowledge in a particular area.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èpè la fi ńwo èpè sàn.
english_literal: Curses are the antidote for curses.
interpretation_gold: One matches the remedy to the affliction.
deepseek_translation: It is with a curse that we watch a curse heal.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb teaches that sometimes the solution to a problem comes from the same source that caused it.
claude_translation: It is with a curse that we use to heal a curse.
claude_interpretation: Sometimes you must use the same method or approach that created a problem to solve it.
gemini_translation: It is with a curse that a curse is healed.
gemini_interpretation: Sometimes, a problem or negative situation can only be resolved by using a similar or equally strong measure.
mistral_translation: It is with curses that one counts curses as being plentiful.
mistral_interpretation: People often focus on and amplify negativity, making problems seem worse than they are.
llama_translation: It is with curse that one looks at a curse.
llama_interpretation: One should not respond to evil with evil.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Epo lojú ọbẹ̀.
english_literal: Palm-oil is the countenance of stew.
interpretation_gold: One should be particularly attentive to that one ingredient or thing whose absence mars the entire project.
deepseek_translation: Palm oil is in the eye of the soup.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns against greed or excess, as too much palm oil (a key ingredient) can ruin a dish just as excess can spoil any situation.
claude_translation: Oil is the eye of soup.
claude_interpretation: The most essential or valuable element gives life and beauty to the whole, just as oil makes soup appetizing and complete.
gemini_translation: Palm oil is the eye of the soup.
gemini_interpretation: Palm oil is an essential ingredient that gives soup its characteristic color and appeal, symbolizing that some elements are crucial for the completeness or identity of something.
mistral_translation: Palm oil is in the soup.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the obvious presence or involvement of something or someone essential in a situation.
llama_translation: Palm oil is on the stew
llama_interpretation: Good things are about to happen or a pleasant surprise is coming.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Elékuru kì í kiri lóko.
english_literal: The seller of steamed ground beans does not hawk her wares on a farm.
interpretation_gold: One wastes one's time attempting to sell things to those who produce them.
deepseek_translation: The guinea fowl does not roam the farm.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb warns against meddling in affairs that do not concern you.
claude_translation: The corn seller does not wander around in the farm.
claude_interpretation: People should focus on their own area of expertise rather than interfering in matters outside their profession or knowledge.
gemini_translation: The seller of ekuru does not hawk in the farm.
gemini_interpretation: One should not offer goods or services where there is no demand or appropriate audience.
mistral_translation: The cassava meal does not go around the farm.
mistral_interpretation: One should not waste limited resources on unnecessary or overly ambitious tasks.
llama_translation: The elephant does not sleep in the farm
llama_interpretation: One should not take advantage of a situation or place where they are a guest or have been given permission to stay.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ewúrẹ́ ò ṣe-e fiṣu ṣọ́.
english_literal: A goat is not a wise choice as the guard over yams.
interpretation_gold: Do not entrust your affairs to your enemy.
deepseek_translation: A goat does not use its beard to cover itself.
deepseek_interpretation: One should not rely on insignificant things for important matters.
claude_translation: A goat cannot be trusted to guard yam
claude_interpretation: You should not put someone in charge of something they are naturally inclined to destroy or consume.
gemini_translation: A goat cannot be used to guard yam. (Or, A goat cannot be used to watch over yams.)
gemini_interpretation: It is unwise to entrust something valuable to someone or something that has a natural inclination to destroy or consume it.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "A goat cannot be used to guard yam. (Or, A goat cannot be used to watch over yams.)", "interpretation": "It is unwise to entrust something valuable to someone or something that has a natural inclination to destroy or consume it."}
mistral_translation: The goat does not use yam to tie a knot.
mistral_interpretation: One should not attempt a task beyond their capability or use unsuitable tools for a purpose.
llama_translation: Goat does not use its horn to kill itself
llama_interpretation: One should not use one's own strength or abilities to harm oneself.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Èló là ńra adìẹ òkókó, tí à ńgba ọmọ-ọ rẹ̀ sìn?
english_literal: How much does a hen cost that one would contract to raise chicks for the owner?
interpretation_gold: Certain obligations are not worth the trouble.
deepseek_translation: How much are we buying the rooster, that we are taking its chick for free?
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb criticizes unfairness or illogical actions, especially when someone takes advantage of a situation without proper compensation.
claude_translation: How much do we buy a hen for, that we would accept its chick in return?
claude_interpretation: One should not accept something of lesser value as compensation for something of greater worth.
gemini_translation: How much does one buy a mature hen, that one would take its chick as a gift?
gemini_interpretation: This proverb questions the logic of accepting a small, insignificant gift when the main, more valuable item is already acquired or expected.
mistral_translation: How much is the price of a hen that lays eggs, when one is raising its chicks?
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the immeasurable value of something or someone that brings continuous benefits or blessings.
llama_translation: The elephant is eating the okoko tree, and you are asking for its child?
llama_interpretation: One should not ask for something that is not yet available or not yet born.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ètò lòfin kìn-ín-ní lóde ọ̀run.
english_literal: Order is the first law in heaven.
interpretation_gold: Whatever one does, one must be orderly.
deepseek_translation: Order is the law that governs heaven.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the importance of order and structure in all aspects of life, as even the heavens are governed by it.
claude_translation: Order is the law that exists in heaven.
claude_interpretation: Divine order and proper organization are fundamental principles that should guide all aspects of life.
gemini_translation: Order is the first law in heaven.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes the fundamental importance of order and structure, suggesting that even in the divine realm, organization is paramount.
mistral_translation: Order is the everlasting law outside in heaven
mistral_interpretation: The proverb emphasizes that divine or natural order governs all things, and humans should follow established rules or systems.
llama_translation: Customs are what make the world thick
llama_interpretation: Cultural practices and traditions are what give life depth and richness.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ète lẹ̀gbọ́n; ìmọ̀ràn làbúrò; bí-a-ó-ti-ṣe lẹ̀kẹta wọn.
english_literal: Intention is the eldest, contemplation is the next, and plan of action is the third.
interpretation_gold: First there is the goal, next a contemplation of it, and finally a plan for attaining it.
deepseek_translation: Deceit is the elder; wisdom is the younger; how-we-do-it is their third sibling.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb warns that deceit may appear superior, but true wisdom and proper conduct ultimately prevail.
claude_translation: Cunning is the first; wisdom is the second; how-we-will-do-it is the third of them.
claude_interpretation: Success requires three elements: cleverness to identify opportunities, wisdom to make good decisions, and practical planning to execute effectively.
gemini_translation: Thought is the elder sibling; advice is the younger sibling; how-it-will-be-done is their third.
gemini_interpretation: Careful planning and consideration (thought) precede seeking counsel (advice), and both are essential before taking action (how-it-will-be-done).
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Thought is the elder sibling; advice is the younger sibling; how-it-will-be-done is their third.", "interpretation": "Careful planning and consideration (thought) precede seeking counsel (advice), and both are essential before taking action (how-it-will-be-done)."}
mistral_translation: The elder is a chair; the wise one is a bag; what shall we do with the third one?
mistral_interpretation: Respect for elders and wisdom are essential, but the third person's role or value must also be carefully considered.
llama_translation: The partridge is in the bush; the hunter is outside; if they do not meet, they will not fight.
llama_interpretation: Avoiding a confrontation can prevent conflict.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Epo ló ṣeé jẹṣu; àkàsọ̀ ló ṣeé gun àká; obìnrín dùn-ún bá sùn ju ọkùnrin lọ.
english_literal: It is palm oil that goes best with yams; it is a ladder that is best for climbing granaries; a woman is more pleasant to make love to than a man.
interpretation_gold: Certain things are fit for certain purposes; not anything will do anytime.
deepseek_translation: Oil is what is used to eat yam; cloth is what is used to cover the body; a woman is sweeter to sleep with than a man.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb highlights the natural and essential roles or preferences in life, emphasizing that certain things are inherently better suited for specific purposes.
claude_translation: Palm oil is what makes yam delicious; a ladder is what makes it possible to climb a palm tree; a woman is sweeter to sleep with than a man.
claude_interpretation: Each thing has its proper complement or partner that makes it complete and fulfilling.
gemini_translation: Palm oil is what makes yam edible; a ladder is what makes a barn climbable; a woman is more pleasant to sleep with than a man.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb uses three distinct examples to emphasize that certain things are inherently better or more suitable for specific purposes.
mistral_translation: It is palm oil that makes yam tasty; it is the wrapper that makes the load climb the shoulder; a woman is sweeter when she sleeps than a man.
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the unique and irreplaceable value each person or thing brings to a situation, emphasizing that certain qualities or roles enhance outcomes in their own way.
llama_translation: Palm oil is used to eat jẹṣu; a cloth is used to cover the body; a woman's beauty surpasses that of a man.
llama_interpretation: A woman's inner qualities and character are more important than a man's physical appearance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Fi ìjà fún Ọlọ́run jà, fọwọ́ lérán.
english_literal: Leave the fighting to God, sit back and watch.
interpretation_gold: One should leave those who have injured one to God's judgement and punishment.
deepseek_translation: Leave the fight for God to fight, fold your arms.
deepseek_interpretation: The proverb advises against taking matters into one's own hands and instead trusting in divine justice.
claude_translation: Fight God's battle and wash your hands clean.
claude_interpretation: When you fight for a righteous cause or defend what is morally right, you remain blameless and pure in your actions.
gemini_translation: Give the fight to God to fight, and cross your arms.
gemini_interpretation: It is best to entrust difficult situations to a higher power and remain calm, rather than engaging in conflict yourself.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Give the fight to God to fight, and cross your arms.", "interpretation": "It is best to entrust difficult situations to a higher power and remain calm, rather than engaging in conflict yourself."}
mistral_translation: Fight for God with fighting, but wash your hands with meat
mistral_interpretation: Do not hypocritically claim to serve God while engaging in unethical or harmful actions.
llama_translation: Make war for God and run away
llama_interpretation: One should not take credit for a task that requires divine intervention or assistance.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Fimí-pamọ́-kí-npa-ọ́ làrùn ńjẹ́.
english_literal: Hide-me-and-I-will-kill-you is the name a disease answers to.
interpretation_gold: A concealed disease is a deadly thing.
deepseek_translation: The one who keeps silent about their pain is the one who suffers.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that withholding one's troubles leads to prolonged suffering, emphasizing the importance of speaking up about one's problems.
claude_translation: It is the hidden-and-kill-you type that the stomach eats
claude_interpretation: Hidden or internal problems are often more dangerous than obvious ones because they cause harm without being detected.
gemini_translation: Hide me so I can hide you is what sickness is called.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb highlights the reciprocal and often hidden nature of illness, where symptoms may be concealed while the disease itself progresses and affects the individual.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "Hide me so I can hide you is what sickness is called.", "interpretation": "This proverb highlights the reciprocal and often hidden nature of illness, where symptoms may be concealed while the disease itself progresses and affects the individual."}
mistral_translation: Hide-me-so-that-I-will-not-die is what the sick person says
mistral_interpretation: The proverb highlights the desperate measures people take to avoid death or difficult situations, even when such efforts are futile or unrealistic.
llama_translation: It is the one who is not at home that the wind blows on
llama_interpretation: One who is not in their comfort zone or familiar environment is more vulnerable to challenges.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: “Gba ọmọ fún mi kí nrèdí”; bí ìdí ò bá ṣe-é re ká gbọ́mọ fọ́lọ́mọ.
english_literal: “Hold my child for me so I may wiggle my buttocks”; if one cannot wiggle one's buttocks one should return the child to its mother.
interpretation_gold: One should not place oneself in difficulty in order to help others out of difficulty.
deepseek_translation: "Take a child for me to tie the waist"; if the waist is not suitable, we reject the child.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb advises careful evaluation before accepting responsibilities or commitments.
claude_translation: Take the child for me so I can defecate; if the buttocks cannot be wiped clean, let us throw the child away
claude_interpretation: One should not make hasty decisions or abandon responsibilities when facing temporary difficulties that can be resolved.
gemini_translation: “Take the child for me to dance”; if the dancing is not possible, let us take the child from the child.
gemini_interpretation: One should not make promises or commitments that cannot be fulfilled, and if a task becomes impossible, it is better to retract the offer than to fail.
mistral_translation: Take a child for me so I can nurse; if the reason is not genuine, we will hear the child crying for its mother
mistral_interpretation: One should not take on responsibilities without a sincere or valid reason, as it will lead to complications.
llama_translation: Take my child for me to raise; if the head is not good, the child will not be good
llama_interpretation: A child's upbringing and character are shaped by the values and behavior of their caregivers.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbọ̀nwọ́ ti kékeré yọké.
english_literal: The elbow develops a hump right from its youth.
interpretation_gold: Said of a precocious person.
deepseek_translation: The young squirrel climbs up.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb emphasizes that even the young or inexperienced can achieve great things with determination.
claude_translation: The elbow has removed itself from being small.
claude_interpretation: Someone who was once humble or insignificant has now become proud or arrogant due to their changed circumstances.
gemini_translation: The elbow, though small, protrudes.
gemini_interpretation: Even something seemingly insignificant can be prominent or have a noticeable impact.
gemini_raw: {"translation": "The elbow, though small, protrudes.", "interpretation": "Even something seemingly insignificant can be prominent or have a noticeable impact."}
mistral_translation: The wisdom of a child surpasses that of an elder.
mistral_interpretation: Age does not always guarantee superior knowledge or judgment; wisdom can come from unexpected sources.
llama_translation: The forest that is small is the one that is cleared.
llama_interpretation: Even the most daunting tasks can be accomplished when broken down into smaller, manageable parts.

part_theme: perspicaciousness, reasonableness, sagacity, savoir-faire, wisdom, worldly wisdom
yoruba: Ìgbín ìbá má mọ̀-ọ́ jẹ̀ kò tó okòó.
english_literal: Had the snail been careless in its foraging it would not “have grown large enough to” be worth twenty cowries.
interpretation_gold: With caution one can offset the effects of any handicap.
deepseek_translation: The snail that will not know hunger is not up to a yam heap.
deepseek_interpretation: This proverb teaches that one must endure hardship to appreciate abundance.
claude_translation: If the snail did not know how to eat, it would not be as big as a cob of corn.
claude_interpretation: Everyone has natural abilities and instincts that enable them to survive and thrive in their own way.
gemini_translation: If the snail knew how to eat, it wouldn't be worth twenty cowries.
gemini_interpretation: This proverb suggests that if something or someone were more capable or valuable, it would not be easily obtainable or cheap.
mistral_translation: If a snail had not known its way, it would not have reached the farm.
mistral_interpretation: Consistent effort and familiarity with one's path lead to success.
